reference.label: 3(d) Your employer or other organisation associated with your email address

exposures.title: Collaborators see your email, access times and behaviour
exposures.whatItMeans: Anyone with edit access to a design you interact with — including people outside your Team — receives your name, avatar, email, and usage metrics covering time of access and insights about how you interacted with the design. A privacy setting can anonymise the email and usage metrics but not the name and avatar.
exposures.whyItMatters: Opening a shared link reports back when you looked and what you did to whoever owns the design, which is analytics on the reader rather than the document. The toggle exists but is off by default in the sense that it must be found and changed.

exposures.title: Retention is a commercially reasonable time
exposures.whatItMeans: After termination or deactivation, Canva retains profile information and User Content for a commercially reasonable time and for as long as it has a valid purpose, including legal and audit obligations and backup and archival purposes.
exposures.whyItMatters: Neither 'commercially reasonable' nor 'valid purpose' yields a date, and both are Canva's judgement. The contrast is inside the same document: the COPPA schedule for US children is written down, and dormant student accounts are deleted after twelve months plus a three-month warning.

reference.label: 8. How long we keep your information

exposures.title: Objecting to legitimate-interest processing can cost you the service
exposures.whatItMeans: European users may object to processing based on legitimate interests, and the policy states that doing so may diminish the quality of the service received or prevent you from using the service.
exposures.whyItMatters: The legitimate-interest basis here covers advertising, marketing messages, and machine learning on usage data — none of which is required to make a design tool work. Attaching loss of access to the objection makes the right expensive to use.

exposures.title: Data goes to authorities and to intelligence sharing services
exposures.whatItMeans: Canva accesses, preserves and shares information with regulators, law enforcement, police, intelligence sharing and take down services and others under its Authority Request Policy, or on a good-faith belief that it is necessary to address fraud, terms breaches, or harmful or illegal activity.
exposures.whyItMatters: 'Intelligence sharing services' is a category that appears in no other document in this corpus, and it sits alongside the good-faith-belief route that does not require legal process.

availableActions.action: Turn off AI training and clear Memories
availableActions.howTo: Two separate settings: the privacy controls page governs whether your data trains Canva's models and those of the third-party providers it engages, and AI personalisation settings govern Memories — the derived data Canva generates and stores about you.

reference.label: 7(d) Managing how Canva analyses your data

availableActions.action: Opt out of third-party enrichment
availableActions.howTo: A dedicated opt-out stops Canva collecting further data about you from third-party providers to tailor your experience and the messages it sends. It is separate from the marketing unsubscribe and from the AI setting.

reference.label: 7(c) Opting out of enrichment using third-party data

availableActions.action: Opt out of LiveRamp email matching specifically
availableActions.howTo: The policy links a LiveRamp opt-out directly. This is the mechanism by which your email address is matched against other networks to target you on Facebook, Google and connected televisions.

availableActions.action: Turn off 'Share my design usage with collaborators'
availableActions.howTo: In privacy settings. It anonymises your email address and usage metrics — access times and interaction insights — to people with edit access to designs you open. Your name and avatar stay visible regardless.

availableActions.action: Keep link sharing on the default
availableActions.howTo: 'Only people added can access' is the default and the most private option. 'Anyone with the link' lets non-Canva users open the design anonymously and see the full names, avatars, cursors and comments of logged-in collaborators.

availableActions.action: Use a personal email address
availableActions.howTo: An organisation-issued address makes the account administrable by that organisation and is itself disclosed back to them. The policy's own advice for Team members is to keep anything you want to own in a separate personal account with an email address not issued by your employer.

availableActions.action: Use the 'Do not sell or share' banner if you are in a covered US state
availableActions.howTo: California, Colorado, Connecticut, Utah and Virginia residents can opt out of sale and of sharing for cross-context behavioural advertising through the banner or by contacting Canva, and can appeal a refusal to act on any rights request.

availableActions.action: Withdraw consent rather than objecting, where you can
availableActions.howTo: Processing based on consent — including machine learning and predictive analysis on User Content — can be withdrawn through the privacy settings page with no stated consequence. Objecting to legitimate-interest processing is the route the policy warns may cost you access to the service.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: A real and specifically located control covering activity, content and media uploads, plus a separate Memories setting, with Canva Education content excluded from AI training outright. Operates as an opt-out rather than an opt-in.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: A commercially reasonable time and for as long as Canva has a valid purpose. The exceptions are written down: a COPPA retention schedule for US under-13s, and deletion of dormant student accounts after twelve months plus a three-month email warning.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Unusually complete. Advertising partners are named — Facebook, Google, LiveRamp, Outbrain, Taboola, Appsflyer, TikTok — and all twenty-one subprocessors touching student data are listed with their purposes, including OpenAI for Canva AI products.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: Available through a banner or by contacting Canva, covering advertising-partner sharing and the disclosure to an employer of whether their email domain is in use. Student data is expressly never sold or shared.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Material changes to collection, use, storage or sharing are notified on the website or by email to the account address, alongside a revised Last Updated date and an archive of previous versions.

requiredDisclosures.name: Lawful basis for processing
requiredDisclosures.note: Four bases set out with worked examples, and unusually candid about what legitimate interests covers — advertising, marketing, and predictions built from spending, platform usage, occupation and employer.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named data controller
requiredDisclosures.note: Canva Pty Ltd, 110 Kippax St, Surry Hills, NSW 2010, Australia, with the processor/controller split explained by reference to the Data Processing Addendum.

requiredDisclosures.name: International transfer safeguards
requiredDisclosures.note: EU Model Clauses and the UK International Data Transfer Addendum for non-adequate countries, plus EU-U.S., Swiss-U.S. and UK Extension Data Privacy Framework adherence by Canva's US subsidiary. Storage locations are enumerated, then extended to any other country where Canva or its providers operate.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data subject rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Access, correction, deletion, restriction, portability and objection, with an explanation that requests may be refused and why, and a route to the local data protection authority.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children under 13
requiredDisclosures.note: The most detailed children's section in the corpus: iKeepSafe COPPA and FERPA certification, a toll-free number, a written retention schedule, a named subprocessor list, institutional control of student data, and dormant-account deletion after twelve months.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data protection officer contact
requiredDisclosures.note: No DPO is named. Contact is through a general form and the section 14 details; the controller entity and its registered address are given instead.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent withdrawal mechanism
requiredDisclosures.note: Withdrawal available through the privacy settings page or by contacting Canva, with the usual carve-out for processing already carried out. Marketing opt-out sits separately in Message Preferences.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: No consent interface is described in this document. Users are directed to browser and device settings and to a separate Cookies Policy, with a warning that disabling tracking may disable many features.

analyses.summary: Zerodha's privacy policy is unusually restrained for an Indian broker on the things that matter most — Aadhaar is genuinely voluntary with a working offline alternative, Zerodha does not store it, and the policy states flatly that it will never sell or rent personal information. What it gives up elsewhere is notice and duration. The policy can be rewritten at Zerodha's sole discretion with no notification at all, leaving users to check the page periodically; no retention period is stated for anything; and persistent cookies are described as permanently placed and as storing profiling information including income. The legal frame is the IT Act 2000 and the 2011 SPDI Rules, with a GDPR annexe — the DPDP Act 2023 is not mentioned, and no grievance officer is named.

exposures.title: The policy can change with no notice at all, and checking is your job
exposures.whatItMeans: Zerodha may revise this policy at any time without telling you, and expressly puts the burden on you to re-read the page to discover what changed.
exposures.whyItMatters: Consent to a privacy policy is only meaningful if you know what you consented to. A policy that can be rewritten silently means the terms you agreed to at account opening are not the terms you are held to now, and the only way to find out is to keep re-reading a page you have no reason to revisit.

reference.label: Subject to Change
reference.quote: This Privacy Policy is subject to change and may be updated or revised from time to time, without any prior notification to the User, at the sole discretion of Zerodha. It is the responsibility of the User to periodically review the Privacy Policy

exposures.title: Nothing has a retention period
exposures.whatItMeans: Data is kept for regulatory and audit purposes and also for unspecified 'business purposes', with no period given for any category — including KYC documents, PAN, Aadhaar-derived fields, passport and licence scans.
exposures.whyItMatters: A broker holds the identity documents that open bank accounts and take loans. Without a stated period there is no point at which that file is destroyed, so the breach exposure from an account you closed years ago is the same as for an active one.

reference.label: Collection and use of your personal information
reference.quote: We would save such information as required by the law, and as directed by the regulators along with such intermediaries regulated by them, for the purpose of offering You our services, and for such further regulatory, audit, and business purposes.

exposures.title: Permanent cookies that profile your income
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy describes persistent cookies as permanently placed on your computer and as storing profiling information including age, gender and income, while calling that information non-personal because the cookie holds no name or account number.
exposures.whyItMatters: An income bracket tied to a unique cookie identifier is a profile of a person whatever it is labelled, and the classification matters: calling it non-personal is what removes it from the consent, access and correction rights the rest of the policy grants over personal information.

reference.label: Usage of Cookies
reference.quote: Zerodha may use persistent cookies which are permanently placed on your computer to store non-personal (Browser, ISP, OS, Clickstream information etc) and profiling information (age, gender, income etc).

exposures.title: Cookies are set unless you go and change your browser
exposures.whatItMeans: There is no consent banner or in-product control. Cookies are issued on login by default, and the only refusal route offered is a browser setting that the policy warns may make parts of the site unusable.
exposures.whyItMatters: Refusal that costs you access to your own trading account is not a real choice, and pushing the control into browser settings puts it where most people will never find it.

reference.label: Privacy Statement as per EU-GDPR
reference.quote: Unless you have adjusted your browser setting so that it will refuse cookies, our system will issue cookies when you log on to our site.

exposures.title: The fuller set of rights is reserved for people covered by GDPR
exposures.whatItMeans: Deletion, correction, access and portability are set out in a section that opens by saying it applies to those subject to the GDPR. Indian users get a correction and deletion route by email, but no stated portability right and no supervisory authority to complain to.
exposures.whyItMatters: Almost every user of an Indian broker regulated by SEBI is in India, so the section granting the clearest rights is the one that covers almost none of them. India's DPDP Act 2023 grants comparable rights and is not referenced anywhere in the policy.

reference.label: Privacy Statement as per EU-GDPR
reference.quote: In case You are subjected to the above stated Regulation, You would have the below stated rights

exposures.title: Marketing runs until you object
exposures.whatItMeans: Keeping customers informed about relevant services is listed as a legitimate interest that continues unless you indicate you do not want it.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is opt-out rather than opt-in, so the default is that your contact details are used for marketing, and the burden of stopping it sits with you.

reference.label: Privacy Statement as per EU-GDPR
reference.quote: to keep our customers informed about relevant services, unless you have indicated at any time that you do not wish us to do so

exposures.title: The policy covers you before you are a customer
exposures.whatItMeans: 'Covered Persons' is defined to include anyone who has merely visited the website or enquired about opening an account, and browsing is allowed without registering while IP address, ISP, referring URL, pages clicked and time spent are collected via Google Analytics.
exposures.whyItMatters: A record is built about people who never became customers and never had an opportunity to decline, which is the same pattern the corpus has found at several other sites — collection that begins before any relationship exists.

reference.label: Scope of this Policy
reference.quote: any natural or legal person who has visited this website/platform and/or has agreed to or has enquired open an account

exposures.title: Security risk is transferred to you in the same breath as the assurances
exposures.whatItMeans: After describing SSL, HTTPS and industry best practice, the policy states that perfect security does not exist and that you use the website and app at your own risk.
exposures.whyItMatters: The disclaimer sits alongside detailed security promises, so the practical effect is that the promises carry no consequence if they fail. For a demat account the asset at stake is the securities portfolio itself.

reference.label: Security
reference.quote: “Perfect security” does not exist on the Internet, and therefore You use the website and mobile application at your own risk.

availableActions.action: Open the account offline and never share Aadhaar at all
availableActions.howTo: Ask for the physical account-opening route and sign the forms by hand. The policy states this alternative exists and requires no Aadhaar information whatsoever; Aadhaar may also be replaced by a driving licence or passport as address proof.

reference.label: Aadhaar user consent policy — Voluntary Act

availableActions.action: Demand a readable copy of everything held about you
availableActions.howTo: Write to india@zerodha.com and legal@zerodha.com. The policy acknowledges Zerodha is obliged under Regulation 5 of the SPDI Rules 2011 to provide every registered user a readable copy of the personal information provided.

reference.label: Collection and use of your personal information
reference.quote: Zerodha is obliged to provide every registered user of Zerodha with a readable copy of the personal information you have provided us

availableActions.action: Correct or delete your details in writing
availableActions.howTo: Email both india@zerodha.com and legal@zerodha.com, or write to the Bangalore registered office at #153/154, 4th Cross, Dollars Colony, JP Nagar 4th Phase. The policy names both addresses for modification, deletion and access requests.

reference.label: Correction/Updating or Access to Personal Information

availableActions.action: Stop the marketing
availableActions.howTo: Tell Zerodha you do not wish to receive service updates — the policy makes this a standing objection, effective 'at any time', rather than a per-campaign unsubscribe.

availableActions.action: Refuse profiling cookies in the browser, knowing the cost
availableActions.howTo: Set the browser to refuse cookies. Expect parts of the site to stop working — the policy says so explicitly — so test this before you need to place a trade.

availableActions.action: Check the policy yourself, on a schedule
availableActions.howTo: There is no notification of changes, so the only way to track them is to re-read the page and compare against the last-updated date. This is exactly what the policy says is your responsibility.

availableActions.action: If you are covered by GDPR, ask for your data to be ported
availableActions.howTo: Send written notice to legal@zerodha.com. The named Data Protection Officer is Somnath Mukherjee. Portability is promised only 'to the maximum extent possible'.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Expressly disclaimed. The policy may be revised without any prior notification, at Zerodha's sole discretion, with the duty to check placed on the user.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period is stated for any category. Data is held for legal, regulatory, audit and unspecified business purposes, which sets no end point even after an account is closed.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: No grievance officer is named, though the SPDI Rules 2011 the policy relies on require one. A Data Protection Officer is named, but only for GDPR purposes.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: No consent interface. Cookies including profiling cookies are issued on login unless the user has already configured the browser to refuse them.

requiredDisclosures.name: Aadhaar Act compliance and alternatives
requiredDisclosures.note: Unusually complete. Aadhaar is stated to be voluntary, an offline signing route is offered, Zerodha states it stores no Aadhaar information, and what it receives via DigiLocker is enumerated as six fields including only the last four digits.

requiredDisclosures.name: No sale of personal information
requiredDisclosures.note: Stated without qualification — no sale or rental to anyone, for any reason, at any time.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data protection officer contact
requiredDisclosures.note: Somnath Mukherjee is named as DPO, contactable at legal@zerodha.com.

requiredDisclosures.name: Lawful basis for processing
requiredDisclosures.note: Eight grounds are enumerated, covering consent, contract, legal obligation and legitimate interest.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data subject rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Deletion, correction, access and portability are set out, but the section is scoped to users subject to the GDPR.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent withdrawal mechanism
requiredDisclosures.note: Correction, deletion and unsubscribe are available by email to india@zerodha.com and legal@zerodha.com, or by post to the registered office.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: DigiLocker, Digiotech Solutions Pvt. Ltd. (e-Sign ASP) and Google Analytics are named. Other vendors are described only as authorised third-party vendors.

requiredDisclosures.name: Company identification details
requiredDisclosures.note: Zerodha Broking Limited, CIN U65929KA2018PLC116815, SEBI registration INZ000031633, with the registered Bangalore address.

analyses.summary: American Express India's online privacy statement discloses that card applications may collect biometric information, that automated systems make decisions about those applications, and that online behaviour is combined with credit-bureau records and transaction history into one profile. Marketing opt-outs are real and specific. What is missing is any stated retention period, any right to contest an automated decision, and any advance notice of changes — those take effect the moment they are posted.

exposures.title: Card applications may collect biometric information
exposures.whatItMeans: Applying for an American Express card online may involve collecting your employment details, your income, and your biometric information.
exposures.whyItMatters: Biometrics are the one category you cannot change after a breach. The statement names the collection but not what is retained, for how long, or whether the application can proceed without it.

reference.label: A. INFORMATION WE COLLECT
reference.quote: If you apply for an American Express Card online, we may collect more detailed personal information such as: Your employment details. Your income. Biometric information.

exposures.title: Automated systems decide on your application
exposures.whatItMeans: Automated systems are used to make certain decisions, process card applications, manage fraud and assess security risk.
exposures.whyItMatters: A machine can decline your application or flag your account, and the statement offers no right to an explanation, no human review, and no route to contest the outcome.

reference.label: B. USE OF INFORMATION
reference.quote: We may use automated systems to help us make certain decisions, process card applications, manage fraud, and assess security risks.

exposures.title: Online behaviour is merged with credit-bureau and transaction records
exposures.whatItMeans: Information from card transactions, public records and third-party sources such as credit bureaus may be combined with the browsing and device data collected under this statement.
exposures.whyItMatters: Your page views and searches stop being website analytics and become part of a financial profile. Few people reading a cookie disclosure expect it to join their credit file.

reference.label: Other Sources of Information
reference.quote: we may collect information from your Card transactions, publicly available records and databases, or third-party sources, such as credit bureaus. We may combine this other information with the information we collect under this statement.

exposures.title: Data is shared with advertising and loyalty partners
exposures.whatItMeans: Disclosure extends to other financial institutions, loyalty programs, travel partners and certain advertising partners, as well as to any buyer in a sale of the business.
exposures.whyItMatters: The recipients are described by category rather than named, so you cannot review who actually holds your data or what their own terms allow.

exposures.title: Changes take effect the moment they are posted
exposures.whatItMeans: The statement may change at any time, advance notice is discretionary, and continued use after an update is treated as acceptance.
exposures.whyItMatters: 'Depending what we change, we may let you know in advance' leaves the decision entirely with the company. The only reliable signal is the effective date at the top of the page.

reference.label: H. CHANGES TO THIS STATEMENT
reference.quote: Any changes to this statement will become effective immediately when posted.

exposures.title: Retention is defined by purpose, not by time
exposures.whatItMeans: Information is kept for as long as necessary for legal or regulatory requirements or legitimate business purposes.
exposures.whyItMatters: No period is stated for any category, including biometrics. 'Legitimate business purposes' is defined by the company, so retention has no external limit you can check.

availableActions.action: Update marketing and data-sharing choices in your account
availableActions.howTo: Log in at americanexpress.com/communications to change marketing and data sharing preferences, or americanexpress.com/preferences to unsubscribe from email.

availableActions.action: Opt out of WhatsApp service messages
availableActions.howTo: The statement offers a specific WhatsApp opt-out separate from other channels. SMS and email alerts continue regardless.

availableActions.action: Register on the TRAI Do Not Call list for phone marketing
availableActions.howTo: The statement directs phone opt-outs to India's National Do Not Call registry rather than handling them internally.

availableActions.action: Raise privacy issues with the Grievance Officer
availableActions.howTo: A Grievance Officer is named as a contact route, which is the escalation path Indian IT Rules require and which most peers in this corpus omit.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: Required of intermediaries under India's IT Rules. Named here with a contact route.

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of personal data collected
requiredDisclosures.note: Detailed and specific, including biometrics, income and employment for applications.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period is stated for any category. Retention is bounded only by 'legitimate business purposes', which the company defines.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automated decision-making rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Automated decisions on card applications are disclosed, but no right to explanation, human review or contest is described.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children's data
requiredDisclosures.note: States the services are not intended for under-18s and that it does not knowingly collect from or market to them.

analyses.summary: Apple's website terms were last updated in November 2009 and remain in force. They cap Apple's liability to you at the greater of six months of subscription fees or one hundred dollars, bar recovery of anything beyond out-of-pocket expenses, give you one year to bring any claim, and require you to indemnify Apple without limit for third-party claims arising from your use of the site. You also agree in advance that any violation causes Apple irreparable harm and consent to injunctive relief.

exposures.title: Apple's liability to you is capped at one hundred dollars
exposures.whatItMeans: If Apple is found liable for damage connected to your use of the site, its liability cannot exceed the greater of subscription fees paid in the prior six months — expressly excluding hardware, software and AppleCare purchases — or US$100.
exposures.whyItMatters: The cap is not proportionate to any harm; it is a fixed floor with hardware and software purchases carved out of the calculation. Combined with the bar on non-out-of-pocket damages below, the maximum realistic recovery is very small.

reference.label: Limitation of Liability
reference.quote: Apple’s liability shall in no event exceed the greater of (1) the total of any subscription or similar fees ... or (2) US$100.00

exposures.title: You indemnify Apple without limit, but Apple's exposure to you is capped
exposures.whatItMeans: You agree to hold Apple, its officers, directors, shareholders, employees, agents, subsidiaries and affiliates harmless from any third-party demand, loss, liability, claim or expense including attorneys' fees arising from your use of the site.
exposures.whyItMatters: The asymmetry is the point: your obligation to Apple has no cap and no exclusions, while Apple's to you stops at a hundred dollars.

exposures.title: You consent in advance to being injuncted
exposures.whatItMeans: You agree that any violation of these terms constitutes an unlawful and unfair business practice, causes irreparable harm for which money would be inadequate, and you consent to Apple obtaining whatever injunctive or equitable relief it deems appropriate.
exposures.whyItMatters: Irreparable harm is normally something a court decides. Agreeing to it in advance concedes the hardest element of an injunction before any dispute exists, and you also agree to pay Apple's legal costs if it sues you.

reference.label: Violation of These Terms of Use
reference.quote: any violation by you of these Terms of Use will constitute an unlawful and unfair business practice, and will cause irreparable harm to Apple, for which monetary damages would be inadequate, and you consent to Apple obtaining any injunctive or equitable relief

exposures.title: One year to sue, and only out-of-pocket losses count
exposures.whatItMeans: Any claim must be brought within one year of the cause of action arising or it is barred, and no recovery may be sought for damages other than out-of-pocket expenses.
exposures.whyItMatters: It shortens statutory limitation periods and removes whole categories of loss from the table. Claims under separate purchase terms are carved out, so this bites on site-related disputes.

exposures.title: You are liable if someone else uses your Apple ID
exposures.whatItMeans: You may be held liable for losses incurred by Apple or by any other user or visitor caused by someone else using your Apple ID, password or account as a result of your failing to keep it confidential.
exposures.whyItMatters: The exposure extends to losses suffered by third parties, not just Apple, and the standard is your failure to keep information secure rather than any deliberate act.

exposures.title: Feedback you send becomes Apple's to use freely
exposures.whatItMeans: Any feedback provided at the site is deemed non-confidential and Apple is free to use it on an unrestricted basis.
exposures.whyItMatters: There is no limit on purpose or duration and no compensation. Sending a suggestion through the site gives it away.

reference.label: Feedback and Information
reference.quote: Any feedback you provide at this site shall be deemed to be non-confidential. Apple shall be free to use such information on an unrestricted basis.

exposures.title: Terms from 2009, changeable at any time, with checking left to you
exposures.whatItMeans: The document is dated 20 November 2009 with a 1997–2009 copyright line, and states Apple may change it at any time with your continued use constituting acceptance — it is your responsibility to check periodically.
exposures.whyItMatters: A seventeen-year-old document still binding by access, with no notification mechanism, means the terms you agreed to and the terms you have read are unlikely to be the same set.

reference.label: Ownership of Site; Agreement to Terms of Use

exposures.title: Deep linking and automated access are prohibited
exposures.whatItMeans: You may not use any deep-link, page-scrape, robot, spider or other automatic device or equivalent manual process to access, copy or monitor any part of the site.
exposures.whyItMatters: Prohibiting deep links restricts ordinary web behaviour, and the ban on 'equivalent manual process' reaches activity a person could do by hand.

availableActions.action: Bring any site-related claim within one year
availableActions.howTo: The contractual limitation period is one year from when the cause of action arises. Claims under separate purchase terms for goods and services are excluded from this limit.

availableActions.action: If you are an EU consumer, sue in your own country
availableActions.howTo: The Santa Clara County venue clause expressly does not apply to consumers based in the European Union, who may make a claim in the courts where they reside.

reference.label: Governing Law; Dispute Resolution
reference.quote: If you are a consumer based in the European Union, you may make a claim in the courts of the country where you reside.

availableActions.action: Do not send ideas or feedback through the site
availableActions.howTo: Feedback is deemed non-confidential and freely usable. Apple maintains a separate Unsolicited Idea Submission Policy referenced by these terms; read it before submitting anything you value.

availableActions.action: Use mediation before litigating
availableActions.howTo: The terms require a good-faith attempt to resolve disputes within thirty days, after which either party may go to mediation. Only if mediation fails are other remedies available.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: California law, Santa Clara County venue, with an express carve-out preserving EU consumers' right to sue at home.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Apple may change the terms at any time; the document places the burden of checking on the user and treats continued use as acceptance.

requiredDisclosures.name: Arbitration clause
requiredDisclosures.note: These website terms use mediation then courts rather than binding arbitration — notably less restrictive than the US consumer norm, and there is no class-action waiver here.

analyses.summary: One page carrying three policies — India, EU/UK/US, and MyBiz for corporate travel — and the Indian one is the weakest of the three. It claims aggregated data derived from you as MMT's property, sellable to third parties at its sole discretion with no compensation. It permits disclosure 'to conduct our business', states that disclosure may happen without your knowledge, and disclaims liability for it. The Android app takes SMS, contacts, IMEI and SIM serial with the note that there is no option to customise the list, and synced contacts are used to tell you which hotels your friends have stayed at. Withdrawing consent may compel MMT to cancel a booking you have already made. The EU/UK/US half is a different document with real legal bases and GDPR rights — and it carries, near-verbatim, the same guest scorecard Booking.com hands to hotels.

exposures.title: Aggregated data about you is MMT's property, and it may be sold
exposures.whatItMeans: Personal information used in aggregated format is claimed as MMT's property, usable at its sole discretion, without compensation to you, for any legitimate purpose — the clause names commercial sale to third parties as an included example.
exposures.whyItMatters: Most policies that aggregate say they do it for analytics. This one asserts ownership of the result and reserves the right to sell it, and it sits in the same document as a statement that personal information as defined by California law has not been sold — two claims that only coexist because 'aggregated' is doing the work.

reference.label: Business partners and third-party vendors
reference.quote: Any Personal Information which we collect and which we may use in an aggregated format is our property. We may use it, in our sole discretion and without any compensation to you, for any legitimate purpose including without limitation the commercial sale thereof to third parties.

exposures.title: The app permission list cannot be customised
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy states that on install a list of permissions appears, that they are needed for the app to function effectively, and that there is no option to customise the list. The list includes reading your SMS, your contacts, IMEI/IMSI, SIM serial number, Bluetooth, calendar, camera, microphone and location.
exposures.whyItMatters: IMEI and SIM serial are hardware identifiers that survive reinstalling the app, clearing data and changing accounts. Presenting them as an all-or-nothing condition of using a travel app removes the per-permission control the operating system otherwise provides.

reference.label: Permissions required for using our mobile applications
reference.quote: a list of permissions appear and are needed for the app to function effectively. There is no option to customize the list.

exposures.title: Your contacts are synced to MMT's servers, and used to tell you where your friends stayed
exposures.whatItMeans: Contacts permission on both Android and iOS enables sharing and referral features, and the policy states the information will be stored on MMT's servers and synced from your phone. It is also used to make recommendations for hotels where your friends have stayed.
exposures.whyItMatters: That last use discloses one customer's travel history to another. The friend never consented to their stays being surfaced to whoever has their number saved, and has no account or setting through which to find out.

reference.label: Contacts
reference.quote: We may also use this information to make recommendations for hotels where your friends have stayed. This information will be stored on our servers and synced from your phone.

exposures.title: Withdrawing consent can get a booking you already made cancelled
exposures.whatItMeans: Consent may be withdrawn by email, but the policy states that doing so may severely inhibit MMT's ability to serve you, may unreasonably restrict servicing of a booking already made, and may compel MMT to cancel that booking.
exposures.whyItMatters: A data-protection right whose exercise cancels a paid trip is not a right most people can use. Whether any refund follows is not addressed here. This is the second document in the corpus where exercising a privacy right costs the user a service they paid for.

reference.label: Users outside the geographical limits of India
reference.quote: unreasonably restrict us to service your booking (if a booking is already made) which may further affect your trip or may compel us to cancel your booking

exposures.title: Disclosure 'to conduct our business', possibly without your knowledge, with liability disclaimed
exposures.whatItMeans: Beyond legal process, the grounds for disclosing personal information include conducting MMT's business, regulatory and internal audit, securing systems, and protecting MMT's rights or property. The policy then states such disclosure and storage may take place without your knowledge, and that MMT will not be liable to you or any third party for damages arising from it.
exposures.whyItMatters: 'To conduct our business' is not a limit — it covers anything MMT does. Pairing an unbounded ground with a secrecy clause and a liability waiver means the disclosure is unreviewable in practice as well as in principle.

reference.label: Disclosure of information
reference.quote: Such disclosure and storage may take place without your knowledge. In that case, we shall not be liable to you or any third party for any damages howsoever arising from such disclosure and storage.

exposures.title: The hotel is told your cancellation percentage and that no misconduct has been reported about you
exposures.whatItMeans: In the EU/UK/US policy, MMT states it provides booking agencies with historical information about you: whether you have booked with them before, the number of completed bookings with MMT, a confirmation that no misconduct has been reported about you, the percentage of bookings you have cancelled, and whether you leave reviews.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is a traveller reputation score disclosed to a business you have no relationship with, in wording close to identical to Booking.com's. Two of the largest online travel agencies carrying the same clause makes it the norm of the vertical rather than one company's choice.

reference.label: Data sharing with third parties
reference.quote: a confirmation that no misconduct has been reported about you, the percentage of bookings you've cancelled in the past or whether you've given reviews about past bookings

exposures.title: Which policy protects you depends on where you are, and the Indian one is thinner
exposures.whatItMeans: The Indian policy takes consent from the act of using the site, gives no legal bases, and offers access, correction and deletion through the account. The EU/UK/US policy sets out GDPR lawful bases per purpose, Article 21 objection rights, restriction, portability, standard contractual clauses for transfers, and an under-16 floor. The Indian section instead sets an 18-year threshold for transacting.
exposures.whyItMatters: The same company, the same booking, materially different protections decided by IP address. This is the second pattern of its kind in the corpus after Uber and LinkedIn, and here it is not marked with an asterisk — you have to notice you are reading a different policy.

exposures.title: Aadhaar, PAN, passport, bank statements and vaccination certificates, then passed on
exposures.whatItMeans: Visa services take passport copies and bank statements; contactless hotel check-in takes Aadhaar, driving licence or election card; international bookings take PAN or passport under the RBI's Liberalised Remittance Scheme; and Covid-19 vaccination status may be taken. MMT commits to redacting sensitive content, to never processing the beneficiary ID inside a vaccination certificate, and to never sharing any of it without prior consent except under legal process.
exposures.whyItMatters: The commitments are specific and unusually careful for this corpus, and they are the reason this is not rated higher. What remains is the concentration: a single travel account holding the identity documents that open bank accounts and cross borders, with no retention period attached to any of them.

exposures.title: Your creditworthiness is assessed and shared to offer bookings on credit
exposures.whatItMeans: MMT states it may verify customers' information on a selective basis including their credit information, and may share personal data with third parties engaged to assess creditworthiness for offering bookings on credit.
exposures.whyItMatters: A credit assessment is run on selected customers without a described trigger, notice, or route to see or contest the result, in service of a lending product the customer has not applied for.

exposures.title: Reviews carry a public profile and travel to other platforms
exposures.whatItMeans: Anyone who posts a review, rating, answer or photograph gets a profile other users can open, showing the number of trips taken, reviews written, questions asked and answered, and photographs posted. Reviews may also appear on other travel platforms.
exposures.whyItMatters: A trip count attached to a name is a travel-frequency signal about a real person, published by default as a consequence of leaving one review, and republished somewhere the reviewer did not choose.

availableActions.action: Deny contacts permission — it is the one that exposes other people
availableActions.howTo: Contacts are stored on MMT's servers and synced from the phone, and used to surface where your contacts have stayed. Denying it at the operating-system level after install is the only control described; the in-app list offers none.

availableActions.action: Book on the website rather than the app
availableActions.howTo: The permission set — SMS reading, contacts sync, IMEI/IMSI, SIM serial, Bluetooth, calendar — applies to the mobile app and is stated to be non-customisable. The website collects session data and cookies but none of the device identifiers.

reference.label: Permissions required for using our mobile applications

availableActions.action: Withdraw consent only when you have no live booking
availableActions.howTo: Withdrawal goes to privacy@go-mmt.com, but the policy states it may compel cancellation of a booking already made. Time any withdrawal for after travel is complete, and ask in the same email what happens to money already paid.

reference.label: Users outside the geographical limits of India

availableActions.action: Decline car-rental and contactless check-in extras that move your ID documents
availableActions.howTo: Contactless hotel check-in sends Aadhaar, driving licence or election card to the property. These are convenience features rather than conditions of booking, and each one you skip keeps a government identity document out of a third party's system.

availableActions.action: Use the Data Protection Officer, not the general privacy mailbox, for rights requests
availableActions.howTo: dpo@makemytrip.com is named as the DPO contact across all three policies and is the address the California and European sections point to for targeted-advertising opt-out and rights requests. privacy@go-mmt.com handles consent withdrawal and general concerns.

availableActions.action: Opt out of targeted advertising if a US state law covers you
availableActions.howTo: The California section offers an opt-out from processing for targeted advertising, exercised through browser settings or by emailing dpo@makemytrip.com, plus a right to appeal a denied request on a form MMT will supply. No equivalent opt-out is offered in the Indian policy.

reference.label: The Data Rights of the Citizens of California

availableActions.action: Turn on two-factor authentication
availableActions.howTo: Recommended in the European policy and available in the Security section of account settings. The account can hold passport scans, Aadhaar copies, bank statements and stored card details, which makes it a higher-value target than a travel login appears to be.

reference.label: What security and retention procedures does MMT put in place to safeguard your personal data?

availableActions.action: Opt out of reward programmes in writing if you do not want your data passed to fulfilment partners
availableActions.howTo: Winning a reward means MMT may share your personal information with the third party fulfilling it. The policy states you can opt out of such programmes by writing to MMT.

availableActions.action: Delete your account when you are done, and expect some fields to survive
availableActions.howTo: A deletion link is provided, and the account also allows direct correction and deletion of most fields — the policy notes some mandatory fields are excluded and gives no retention period for what remains.

reference.label: How long do we keep your personal information?

availableActions.action: Tell your co-travellers, because MMT makes it your job
availableActions.howTo: Booking for others means representing that each of them agreed to their information being disclosed to MMT and onward to service providers. For international trips that can include passport details, dietary requirements and medical conditions passed to hotels and tour managers in each city.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: Four separate retention headings across the three policies — India, EU/UK/US, and MyBiz — and not one states a period. Every formulation is 'as long as reasonably necessary' plus legal, tax and accounting extensions.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: India's IT Rules require a named grievance officer with contact details for an intermediary of this kind. The document names a Data Protection Officer reachable at dpo@makemytrip.com and a general privacy mailbox, but no grievance officer and no physical address for grievances.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent withdrawal mechanism
requiredDisclosures.note: Available by email to privacy@go-mmt.com — qualified by the statement that withdrawal may compel cancellation of an existing booking.

requiredDisclosures.name: Lawful basis for processing
requiredDisclosures.note: Set out per activity in the European section: contract for service delivery and support, consent or legitimate interest for marketing and partner sharing, legitimate interest for personalization, research and business transfers. The Indian section states no legal bases and takes consent from use of the site.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data protection officer contact
requiredDisclosures.note: dpo@makemytrip.com, named as responsible for monitoring compliance, and repeated at the foot of both the EU/UK/US and MyBiz policies.

requiredDisclosures.name: International transfer safeguards
requiredDisclosures.note: EU standard data protection clauses or an adequacy decision for processing outside the EU/EEA. The Indian section states only that data is processed in India and other jurisdictions where MMT's vendors operate, and that those regimes may differ from the user's own.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: States that personal information as defined by the CPRA has not been sold as of now, that sensitive personal information is not used or disclosed beyond what the CPRA authorises, and that exercising rights will not lead to discrimination. Read against the separate claim of ownership over aggregated data with a right of commercial sale.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children's data
requiredDisclosures.note: Two different floors in one document: the Indian policy requires you to be at least 18 to transact and to consent, while the European policy sets under-16 with parental consent and deletion on discovery. The California section adds that consent is required before under-16s see cross-context behavioural advertising.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automated decision-making rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Profiling is referenced in the Article 21 objection rights, and creditworthiness assessment is described, but no disclosure of automated decision-making logic, significance or consequences appears, and no right to human review is offered.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: The Indian policy describes advertising and third-party cookies and directs users to browser settings rather than offering a consent mechanism. A separate MakeMyTrip cookie policy is analysed under its own hash and does honour Do Not Track.

analyses.summary: X's privacy policy is unusually specific about retention — 18 months for your emails to support, 13 for cookies, 12 for ad and partner data — and unusually vague about the one thing it concedes twice: that your data trains AI models. X trains its own models on what it collects, and third-party collaborators may train theirs, on a condition the policy writes as 'if you do not opt out' without ever saying where that opt-out lives. Direct message contents are collected, biometric information is collected on consent and appears nowhere in the retention list, and if your account is suspended X keeps your email and phone number indefinitely. The document says X does not sell your personal information and, four sections earlier, that it may share, sell or transfer it in a merger.

exposures.title: X trains its models on your data, and this policy names no way to decline
exposures.whatItMeans: Section 2.1 states X may use the information it collects, plus publicly available information, to help train its machine learning or artificial intelligence models. The Take Control section offers access, correction, portability, deletion and settings, and none of them is described as reaching model training.
exposures.whyItMatters: The terms of service put the same right inside the content licence you grant by posting, so the two documents agree that it happens and neither locates a control. Across this corpus, AI training opt-out is the disclosure most often recorded absent; X is a case where the practice is admitted plainly and the opt-out simply is not there.

reference.label: 2.1 Operate, improve, and personalize our services
reference.quote: We may use the information we collect and publicly available information to help train our machine learning or artificial intelligence models

exposures.title: An opt-out mentioned only as a condition, never as an instruction
exposures.whatItMeans: Under Third-party collaborators, X may share or disclose your information with third parties who, if you do not opt out, may use it for their own independent purposes — including, in the policy's own example, training their artificial intelligence models, generative or otherwise. The sentence is the only place this opt-out appears. It is not named, located, or linked.
exposures.whyItMatters: The clause makes your inaction the legal basis for someone else's training corpus while telling you nothing about how to act. A reader who wants to exercise the right the sentence assumes they have cannot find it in the document that assumes it.

reference.label: 3.2 With third parties and third-party integrations — Third-party collaborators
reference.quote: If you do not opt out, in some instances the recipients of the information may use it for their own independent purposes

exposures.title: Break the rules once and your email and phone are kept forever
exposures.whatItMeans: Where your account is suspended for violating the Rules, X may keep the identifiers you used to create it — email address or phone number — indefinitely, to stop you making a new account.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the one retention period in a carefully itemised list with no end. It also has no stated appeal: an account restored on appeal does not obviously undo an indefinite retention record, and the policy does not say it does.

reference.label: 4. How Long We Keep Information
reference.quote: we may keep the identifiers you used to create the account (such as your email address or phone number) indefinitely

exposures.title: Direct message contents are collected, not just their metadata
exposures.whatItMeans: The usage information X collects includes, for Direct Messages, the contents of the messages, the recipients, and the date and time. Encrypted Messages contribute metadata rather than content. Anything you sent to someone who reads X through a third-party service may reach that service too.
exposures.whyItMatters: Private messages sit in the same collected pool that feeds personalisation, safety systems and, under section 2.1, model training. The distinction that protects you is whether you used the encrypted product, which the policy states without explaining when it applies.

reference.label: 1.2 Information we collect when you use X — Usage information
reference.quote: when you use Direct Messages, including the contents of the messages, the recipients, and date and time of messages

exposures.title: X links devices and browsers you never signed in on to your account
exposures.whatItMeans: Signing in once associates that device with the account. Beyond that, subject to settings, X may associate your account with other browsers and devices, associate a signed-out device with other devices, and infer your identity by matching hashes of email addresses that merely share common components with the one you gave X. When you are not signed in at all, X may still infer who you are.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is identity inference rather than identity collection, and it reaches people in a signed-out state who never agreed to anything. The cookie policy adds that once a device has been used to log in, the association continues whether or not you are logged in.

reference.label: 1.2 Information we collect when you use X — Inferred identity
reference.quote: When you access X and are not signed in, we may infer your identity based on the information we collect.

exposures.title: A Professional Account makes your street address and phone number always public
exposures.whatItMeans: Professional Accounts may carry a street address, contact email and contact phone number, and the policy states all of which will always be public. There is no described setting to make them private while keeping the account type.
exposures.whyItMatters: Creators and small businesses switch to a Professional Account for analytics and monetisation. The words 'always public' mean a home address entered by a sole trader is not retractable through settings, only by deleting the data.

reference.label: 1.1 Information you provide us — Professional Accounts
reference.quote: including street address, contact email address, and contact phone number, all of which will always be public

exposures.title: Biometric information is collected with no retention period stated for it
exposures.whatItMeans: Based on your consent, X may collect and use biometric information for safety, security and identification. Section 4 itemises retention for profile data, usage data, payment data, communications, cookies and ad data, and does not mention biometrics at any point.
exposures.whyItMatters: Biometric identifiers are the category people cannot reissue after a breach, and state biometric statutes generally require a written retention and destruction schedule. The one collection that most needs a clock is the one the retention section skips.

reference.label: 1.1 Information you provide us — Biometric information
reference.quote: Based on your consent, we may collect and use your biometric information for safety, security, and identification purposes.

exposures.title: "We don't sell your personal information", and section 3.5 says X may sell it
exposures.whatItMeans: Section 6.1 closes with a flat statement that X does not sell personal information. Section 3.5 states X may share, sell, or transfer information about you in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization, sale of assets, or bankruptcy, and that this policy will apply to data transferred to the new entity.
exposures.whyItMatters: Both sentences can be true under the CCPA's definition of a sale, which exempts corporate transactions. A reader who takes the plain-English promise at face value will not expect their data to move with the company, and the assurance that this policy follows it is worth exactly as much as the new owner's power to amend it.

reference.label: 3.5 As a result of a change in ownership
reference.quote: We may share, sell, or transfer information about you in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization, sale of assets, or bankruptcy.

exposures.title: Your job-search activity goes to potential employers
exposures.whatItMeans: X may collect biographical information, employment and educational history, employment preferences, skills, and job search activity and engagement, and use it to share with potential employers when you apply, to enable professional connections, and to show you more relevant advertising. Applicant tracking system providers are named as a category of service provider receiving applicant and job data.
exposures.whyItMatters: Job-search activity is combined with the advertising system by the same sentence that offers the recruiting benefit, so looking for work makes you a better-targeted ad audience as a by-product.

reference.label: 1.1 Information you provide us — Job applications / recommendations

exposures.title: The legal bases for processing are not in the policy
exposures.whatItMeans: Section 6.1 says X has carefully considered the legal reasons it is permitted to process your information, and refers readers who want to understand the nuances to a separate page. No lawful basis is stated for any processing operation in this document.
exposures.whyItMatters: For a controller established in Dublin serving EU users, the lawful basis is exactly the disclosure the transparency obligation exists to produce. A sentence saying the analysis has been done, with the result somewhere else, is not that disclosure.

reference.label: 6.1 We have specific legal bases to use your information
reference.quote: X has carefully considered the legal reasons it is permitted to collect, use, share and otherwise process your information.

exposures.title: Deletion is a queue with no stated end
exposures.whatItMeans: Following the deletion instructions deactivates the account and queues the data for deletion. For up to 30 days the account can be restored. The policy does not say how long deletion then takes, or what survives it, and separately notes that search engines and third parties may keep copies of public posts indefinitely.
exposures.whyItMatters: Erasure requests are answered with a queue rather than a deadline, and the indefinite retention of suspended-account identifiers shows the queue has exceptions the deletion section does not mention.

reference.label: 5.2 Deleting your information
reference.quote: your account will be deactivated and your data will be queued for deletion

availableActions.action: Turn off data sharing with business partners
availableActions.howTo: Privacy and Safety settings carry a 'Data sharing with business partners' option that controls the partner sharing in section 3.1. The policy warns it does not control sharing described elsewhere, including service providers — so it is narrower than it sounds.

reference.label: 3.1 When you post and share — With partners

availableActions.action: Turn off off-X activity and inferred identity linking
availableActions.howTo: Settings and privacy > Privacy and safety > Off-X activity controls both the storage of where you see X content across the web and whether X links your account to browsers and devices you did not sign in on. Data already learned from stored history may keep being used.

reference.label: 1.2 Information we collect when you use X — Inferred identity

availableActions.action: Read what X has inferred about you before deciding anything
availableActions.howTo: Your X Data shows collected and inferred information, and a separate request route exists for more. The download archive covers posts. Both are the only way to see what the inference described in section 1.2 actually produced.

availableActions.action: Restore within 30 days if you deactivate by mistake
availableActions.howTo: Deactivation queues data for deletion but the account can be restored for up to 30 days afterwards. After that the policy describes no route back.

deadline.description: Up to 30 days after deactivation to restore an account that was deactivated accidentally or wrongfully.

availableActions.action: Do not put an address you would not publish into a Professional Account
availableActions.howTo: The professional category, street address, contact email and contact phone are stated to be always public. A personal account keeps profile information to display name and username.

reference.label: 1.1 Information you provide us — Professional Accounts

availableActions.action: Use the state-specific request pages, which are not in this document
availableActions.howTo: Section 10 links separate handling pages for California CCPA requests, Washington's My Health My Data Act consumer health data, and Oregon's Consumer Privacy Act appeals. The rights and the mechanisms live there, not here.

availableActions.action: In the EU, EFTA or UK, write to the named controller and escalate to the Irish DPC
availableActions.howTo: The controller is X Internet Unlimited Company, One Cumberland Place, Fenian Street, Dublin 2, marked for the attention of the Data Protection Officer. Its lead supervisory authority is the Irish Data Protection Commission, and standard contractual clauses can be requested by contacting X.

availableActions.action: Assume anything sent through unencrypted Direct Messages is collected in full
availableActions.howTo: The policy collects DM contents and only metadata for Encrypted Messages. Use the encrypted product, or another service, for anything you would not want inside the pool that feeds personalisation and model training.

reference.label: 1.2 Information we collect when you use X — Usage information

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: Two distinct training practices are disclosed — X's own models in 2.1, and third-party collaborators' models in 3.2 — and no opt-out is named for either. Section 3.2 goes as far as conditioning the third-party use on 'if you do not opt out' without saying what the opt-out is or where it is. The terms of service put the same training right inside the content licence and also offer no opt-out, so the two documents are consistent and consistently silent.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: Among the most itemised in this corpus: 18 months for communications with X, 13 months for cookies and cookie-derived data, 12 months for ad interaction data and for data shared by ad and business partners, duration of the account for profile and usage data. Two gaps: biometrics appear in no retention line, and identifiers from suspended accounts are kept indefinitely.

requiredDisclosures.name: Biometric data consent
requiredDisclosures.note: Collection is expressly conditioned on consent and limited to safety, security and identification purposes.

requiredDisclosures.name: Biometric data retention
requiredDisclosures.note: Section 4 enumerates retention for six categories of data and omits biometric information entirely. No destruction schedule, trigger or maximum period is stated anywhere in the document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Lawful basis for processing
requiredDisclosures.note: Section 6.1 asserts that legal bases have been considered and links out to 'additional information about data processing'. No basis is stated for any processing purpose in this document, which is the transparency obligation the section is answering.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named data controller
requiredDisclosures.note: Split by residence and given with postal addresses: X Corp., Bastrop TX for the US and rest of world; X Internet Unlimited Company, Dublin for the EU, EFTA States and UK; X Switzerland GmbH, Bern as the Swiss representative.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data protection officer contact
requiredDisclosures.note: Reachable by post only — 'Attn: Data Protection Officer' at the Dublin and Bern addresses. No name and no direct email address for the DPO; general contact runs through a Privacy Policy Inquiries page.

requiredDisclosures.name: International transfer safeguards
requiredDisclosures.note: Standard contractual clauses where applicable, obtainable on request, plus participation in the EU-US, Swiss-US and UK Extension Data Privacy Frameworks with JAMS as the independent recourse body and FTC enforcement.

requiredDisclosures.name: No sale of personal information
requiredDisclosures.note: Stated flatly in 6.1 — 'And no, we don't sell your personal information' — but as an aside inside a paragraph about legal bases, and sitting alongside 3.5, which permits sharing, selling or transferring data in a merger, acquisition, reorganisation, asset sale or bankruptcy.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: No opt-out link or mechanism appears in this document. Section 10 points California residents to a separate CCPA handling page; this analysis covers only this document's text.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Every recipient is a category — service providers, ad partners, advertisers, corporate affiliates, third-party collaborators, video partners, applicant tracking system providers. Not one is named, including the affiliate that would receive data under 3.4 and the collaborators said in 3.2 to train their own AI models on it.

requiredDisclosures.name: Sensitive personal information categories
requiredDisclosures.note: The policy collects biometric information, precise location, and direct message contents without enumerating them as sensitive personal information or describing any right to limit their use. That right is left to the linked state-specific pages.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children under 13
requiredDisclosures.note: Minimum age 13, no knowing collection from under-13s, removal and account termination on discovery, plus a reporting route for parents. The paragraph appears twice verbatim in the captured text, which is a rendering artefact rather than a substantive difference.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automated decision-making rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Recommendation, ad targeting, identity inference and age estimation are all described as automated, and no right to human review, explanation or objection to a solely automated decision appears anywhere in the document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data subject rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Access, correction, portability, deletion, objection, restriction and consent withdrawal are all offered through settings and the Your X Data tool, with an authorised-agent route and a stated right to complain to a local supervisory authority. X reserves the right to reject requests where identity cannot be verified.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Stronger than most in this corpus: for changes X determines to be material, notice and an opportunity to review the revised policy before you continue to use X — a pre-use commitment rather than a post-hoc 'check this page' clause.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: X operates in India, where the IT Rules 2021 require a named Resident Grievance Officer with contact details. The policy names controllers for the US, the EU/EFTA/UK and Switzerland and no Indian officer or address.

analyses.summary: Bank of America's CCPA notice is well built — three opt-out routes, browser preference signals honoured as valid requests, opt-outs processed in 15 calendar days, requests in 45, and metrics published under section 7102. The catch is who it covers. It states that it does not apply to information collected about California residents who apply for or obtain the bank's financial products for personal, family or household purposes, because that information is exempt under the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, and routes those people to a separate U.S. Consumer Privacy Notice. So the rights described here reach prospects, event attendees and website visitors, and stop at the bank's own retail customers — while Bank of America's online privacy notice sends California residents to this document for their additional rights. The other material fact is dated: as of April 2025 the bank commenced sharing browsing and search history, geolocation, employment information and inferences from its webpages with third-party advertisers and data aggregation services for cross-context behavioural advertising, having previously sold and shared nothing.

exposures.title: The notice excludes the bank's own retail customers
exposures.whatItMeans: The CCPA does not cover information subject to the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, and this notice states plainly that it does not apply to information collected about California residents who apply for or obtain Bank of America's financial products and services for personal, family or household purposes. Those individuals are directed to the U.S. Consumer Privacy Notice, a different document.
exposures.whyItMatters: Everything the notice grants — access to specific pieces, correction, deletion, opt-out of sharing, freedom from retaliation — is unavailable to the population it is most natural to assume it covers. Bank of America's online privacy notice tells California residents covered by the CCPA that they may have additional rights and to reference this notice. Whether you are covered is the very thing the qualifier turns on, and it is settled only by opening this document and finding yourself excluded — so a retail customer following the pointer arrives at a door already closed to them.

reference.label: Applicability
reference.quote: this Notice does not apply with respect to information that we collect about California residents who apply for or obtain our financial products and services for personal, family, or household purposes

exposures.title: In April 2025 the bank began sharing your browsing with advertisers
exposures.whatItMeans: The notice records that from April 2025 Bank of America commenced sharing personal information collected from its webpages with non-affiliated third-party websites and advertisers for cross-context behavioural advertising. The categories shared are purchasing and consuming histories, internet browsing and search history, geolocation including device and IP location, professional or employment information, and inferences about preferences and interests.
exposures.whyItMatters: In the same document the bank confirms it sold and shared nothing in the preceding twelve months, so this is a change of practice with a date on it rather than a standing disclosure. Browsing on a bank's website reveals which products you were considering, and it now leaves the bank.

reference.label: Notice of Right to Opt-Out from Sale/Sharing
reference.quote: Beginning in April 2025, we have commenced sharing Personal Information collected from our webpages with non-affiliated, third-party websites and advertisers

exposures.title: One of the two recipient categories is data aggregation services
exposures.whatItMeans: The categories of third parties receiving shared information are given as websites and advertisers that contract for cross-context behavioural advertising, and data aggregation services. No company is named in either category.
exposures.whyItMatters: Data aggregation services exist to join data from many sources into one profile, which is the opposite of the containment a bank relationship implies. With only a category given, there is no way to find out who holds the resulting profile or to approach them directly.

reference.label: Categories of third parties to whom we may share your information for commercial purposes
reference.quote: Data aggregation services

exposures.title: The contents of your mail, email and texts are a collected category
exposures.whatItMeans: Sensitive personal information collected and disclosed for business purposes includes the contents of a California resident's mail, email and text messages where the bank is not the intended recipient, biometric information processed to identify you uniquely, racial or ethnic origin, citizenship or immigration status, religious beliefs and union membership, and information analysed concerning your health.
exposures.whyItMatters: These are the categories a person would least expect a bank to hold about them, and the worked example given for using them is investigating discrimination claims using ethnicity and message contents. The notice offers no way to limit any of it — see the next entry.

reference.label: Personal Information We Collect and Disclose for a Business Purpose
reference.quote: Personal Information collected and analyzed concerning a California resident's health

exposures.title: The right to limit sensitive information is answered by exemption, not offered
exposures.whatItMeans: Rather than providing a limit control, the notice states it only uses or discloses sensitive personal information for purposes consistent with the CCPA regulations, then enumerates the exempt purposes — providing expected services, security incidents, resisting fraud, physical safety, short-term transient use, account servicing and quality assurance.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the lawful way to avoid offering the limit right, and the enumeration is honest, but the consumer still ends up with a category of highly sensitive data and no control over it. The rights list in this same notice omits the limit right entirely, so nothing tells the reader that a right they may have heard of has been handled by exemption.

reference.label: How We Use Sensitive Personal Information
reference.quote: We only use or disclose Sensitive Personal Information for the following purposes consistent with CCPA Regulations

exposures.title: Consumer data resellers and credit bureaus are collection sources
exposures.whatItMeans: The categories of sources include service providers, consumer data resellers, credit reporting agencies, public record sources, affiliates, website and mobile app activity, social media, and corporate clients supplying information about their employees and board members.
exposures.whyItMatters: Two of these mean information arrives about you without any interaction with the bank at all — bought from a reseller, or handed over by your employer. Neither route gives you a moment at which to decline, and the notice-at-collection this document constitutes is the only notice you get.

reference.label: From Whom We Collect Personal Information
reference.quote: Service Providers, Consumer Data Resellers, Credit Reporting Agencies and other similar persons or entities

exposures.title: No retention period for any category
exposures.whatItMeans: Retention is described as depending on three criteria — legal and regulatory requirements, how long the business purpose needs, and whether you exercise a deletion right. No duration is given for anything, including biometric information and government identifiers.
exposures.whyItMatters: Two of the three criteria are set by the bank, and the third requires the consumer to act. Since retail customers are excluded from this notice, the deletion lever that would end retention is unavailable to most people reading it.

reference.label: How Long We Retain Personal Information
reference.quote: The length of time that we intend to retain each category of Personal Information will depend on several criteria

exposures.title: Changes are published by editing a date
exposures.whatItMeans: The only stated change mechanism is posting the revised notice on the same page with a new Last Updated date. There is no notification, no advance period and no version history.
exposures.whyItMatters: The April 2025 commencement of advertising sharing is exactly the kind of change this mechanism delivers silently — a practice that did not exist appeared in the document, and the only signal was a date. Bank of America's online privacy notice uses the same mechanism, so both of the bank's consumer-facing privacy documents change without telling anyone.

reference.label: Changes to This California Consumer Privacy Act Notice
reference.quote: We may change or update this Notice from time to time.

availableActions.action: Turn on a browser opt-out preference signal
availableActions.howTo: Enable Global Privacy Control or an equivalent. Bank of America states it treats opt-out preference signals as valid requests to opt out of sale and sharing for that browser, with no individualised request needed. Repeat it on every browser and device.

deadline.description: All opt-out requests are stated to be processed within 15 calendar days of receipt.

reference.label: How We Process Opt-Out Preferences
reference.quote: Bank of America treats opt-out preference signals as valid requests to opt-out of sale/sharing for the browser.

availableActions.action: Set the sharing preference in your account
