availableActions.howTo: Click Your Privacy Choices at the bottom of the web or mobile pages, then the 'Sharing and Selling of Personal Data' tab in the left column. Preferences can be changed at any time and each adjustment overrides the previous one.

reference.label: How to opt-out of sharing your information

availableActions.action: Opt out by phone if you would rather not use the web tool
availableActions.howTo: Call 888.341.5000. The same number handles rights requests generally, alongside the online Personal Information Request Form and IndividualRightsRequests@bofa.com.

availableActions.action: If you bank with them, use the U.S. Consumer Privacy Notice instead
availableActions.howTo: Anyone who applies for or holds a Bank of America product for personal, family or household purposes falls outside this notice. The document that governs them is the U.S. Consumer Privacy Notice, referenced here and published separately. Read that one before relying on any right described in this document.

reference.label: Applicability
reference.quote: The CCPA, however, does not apply to certain information, such as information subject to the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act

availableActions.action: Send an authorised agent, with signed permission
availableActions.howTo: An authorised agent may submit an opt-out request on your behalf where you have given them signed permission. For access requests on behalf of another person the bank may require proof of authorisation such as a power of attorney plus verification of identity directly from that person.

reference.label: How to opt-out of sharing your information

availableActions.action: Check the published request metrics before you file
availableActions.howTo: www.bankofamerica.com/ccpa-metrics carries the reporting required by section 7102 of the CCPA regulations — how many requests were received, complied with and denied, and how long they took. It is the only public evidence of how the routes above actually perform.

availableActions.action: Expect 45 days, and an explanation if it slips
availableActions.howTo: Verified requests are processed within 45 days, extendable once by a further 45 with an explanation for the delay. Requests for specific pieces need extra identity verification, and the bank will not return Social Security or licence numbers, financial account numbers, biometric data, passwords or security answers in any case.

deadline.description: 45 days to process a verified request, extendable by up to a further 45 days with an explanation.

reference.label: Rights under the CCPA
reference.quote: We will work to process all verified requests within 45 days pursuant to the CCPA.

requiredDisclosures.name: Scope of covered individuals
requiredDisclosures.note: Disclosed, and the disclosure is the document's most consequential sentence. Five legal entities are named — Bank of America, Merrill, BofA Securities, Managed Account Advisors LLC and BAL Investment & Advisory — and the notice then excludes information collected about California residents who apply for or obtain financial products for personal, family or household purposes, on the GLBA exemption, routing them to the U.S. Consumer Privacy Notice. Clear, lawful, and it removes the bank's retail customers from every right below.

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of personal data collected
requiredDisclosures.note: Twelve categories enumerated with examples, including Social Security, driver's licence and passport numbers, biometric information, geolocation, call and video recordings, education information, and inferences forming a profile of preferences, psychological trends, predispositions, intelligence and aptitudes.

requiredDisclosures.name: Sensitive personal information categories
requiredDisclosures.note: Separately enumerated: government identifiers, account log-in and card numbers with security codes, precise geolocation, racial or ethnic origin, citizenship or immigration status, religious or philosophical beliefs, union membership, the contents of mail, email and text messages, biometric processing for unique identification, health information, and the personal information of Californians under 16.

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of personal information sold or shared
requiredDisclosures.note: Five categories listed for sharing — purchasing histories, browsing and search history, geolocation, professional or employment information, and inferences — with the two recipient categories and the single commercial purpose stated, and April 2025 given as the start date.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: Three routes: the Your Privacy Choices link with a Sharing and Selling tab, browser opt-out preference signals honoured as valid requests, and a phone number. Processed within 15 calendar days, with an authorised-agent route. Among the better-specified opt-outs in this corpus.

requiredDisclosures.name: No sale of personal information
requiredDisclosures.note: Stated twice and dated: no personal or sensitive personal information was sold in the twelve months preceding the notice, and no personal information of children under 16 is sold or shared. 'Sold' and 'shared' are each defined.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data subject rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Notice at collection, request to know including specific pieces, correction, deletion, opt-out and freedom from retaliation, each with the verification requirements and the grounds for refusal set out, and 45 days plus one 45-day extension for a verified request. The circumstances in which a request will be refused are described rather than left implicit.

requiredDisclosures.name: Right to limit use of sensitive personal information
requiredDisclosures.note: Not offered and not listed among the rights. The notice instead enumerates the purposes under the CCPA regulations for which sensitive personal information is used, which is the lawful route to not providing the control — but a reader is never told that this is what has happened, and the categories at stake include health data, ethnicity and the contents of communications.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No duration for any category. Three criteria are given, two of which the bank sets and the third of which requires the consumer to exercise a deletion right that the scope section has already removed from most readers.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: The only mechanism is reposting with a new Last Updated date. No notification, no advance period, no version history — which is how the April 2025 start of advertising sharing arrived.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Recipients are categories throughout: affiliates, service providers and contractors described by function, government agencies, and for sharing, 'certain third parties, such as websites and advertisers' and 'data aggregation services'. Not one company is named in either the business-purpose disclosure or the sharing disclosure.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automated decision-making rights
requiredDisclosures.note: The notice describes inferences that build a profile covering psychological trends, predispositions, intelligence and aptitudes, and then says nothing about automated decision-making technology — no pre-use notice, no access right, no opt-out. Walmart's California notice, captured in this corpus, carries all three.

requiredDisclosures.name: Shine the Light disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: California Civil Code section 1798.83 gives residents an annual right to a list of personal information disclosed to third parties for their direct marketing, or requires the business to disclose an opt-out policy instead. Neither appears anywhere in this document. Both Walmart's and eBay's California notices in this corpus carry one.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children's data
requiredDisclosures.note: Personal information of California residents under 16 is classified as sensitive personal information, and the notice states such information is neither sold nor shared. No separate description of collection from children appears; Bank of America publishes a Children's Privacy Policy referenced from its online privacy notice.

requiredDisclosures.name: GLBA consumer privacy notice
requiredDisclosures.note: This is the CCPA notice, not the GLBA privacy notice. It relies on the GLBA exemption and points the covered population to the separate U.S. Consumer Privacy Notice, which is not part of this capture. Recording an absence here would be a claim about a document that was not read.

analyses.summary: JioHotstar's terms state that live sports will show advertisements even on an advertisement-free plan — the thing many subscribers are paying to avoid. Fees are non-refundable whether or not you used the service, you cannot downgrade before expiry or change your payment method mid-term, and there is no guarantee that any specific content, or any minimum amount of content, stays available. Together with its privacy policy, which cancels your subscription without refund if you exercise erasure, the pattern is consistent: the money is not coming back.

exposures.title: Ad-free plans still show ads on live sports
exposures.whatItMeans: The terms state that some content, such as live sports or shows, will show advertisements even where the subscription plan selected is an advertisement-free plan.
exposures.whyItMatters: Live cricket is the main reason many people subscribe in India, and removing advertising is the main reason they pay more. The exception is stated once, in a paragraph about packaging models, rather than at the point of purchase.

reference.label: Description of Service and Acceptance of Terms of Use
reference.quote: some Content such as live sports or shows, when accessed, will show advertisements even where the subscription plan selected is an advertisement free plan

exposures.title: Fees are non-refundable even if you never watched anything
exposures.whatItMeans: Subscription and add-on fees are non-refundable irrespective of whether the subscription or add-on has been availed by you or not, and cancelling before the period ends brings no refund for the unexpired portion.
exposures.whyItMatters: Paying and never using the service returns nothing, and neither does cancelling early. The only exception is upgrading to a more expensive plan.

exposures.title: You can upgrade instantly but cannot downgrade at all
exposures.whatItMeans: Changing to a higher tier takes effect immediately on paying the pro-rata difference. Downgrading an existing plan or add-on before it expires is not permitted.
exposures.whyItMatters: Movement is one-directional and only in the direction that costs more. You also cannot change your payment method during the subscription term at all.

exposures.title: The content you subscribed for can be removed
exposures.whatItMeans: Jiostar reserves the right to change, supplement, alter or remove any content subject to a subscription fee as it deems fit, and does not guarantee the availability of any specific content or any minimum amount of content.
exposures.whyItMatters: You can pay for a year to watch one series and have it withdrawn, with no refund available under the clause above.

exposures.title: Prices and plans change on posting, and using the service is acceptance
exposures.whatItMeans: Jiostar may change, terminate or amend subscription plans, add-on benefits, fees and billing cycles at its sole discretion at any time, effective on posting to the site, with continued use deemed conclusive acceptance. Separately it commits to advance notice of a fee change for a plan you already hold.
exposures.whyItMatters: The two statements sit in tension: advance notice is promised for your existing plan's fee, while the broader right to amend takes effect on posting alone.

exposures.title: The Social Feed wants your contacts
exposures.whatItMeans: To invite friends to the Social Feed you must permit access to your contacts list. Anyone who has your number in their phonebook, or who accepted your invitation, can see your social posts and your scores and progress in contests.
exposures.whyItMatters: Visibility is granted by other people having your number, not by you choosing them, and contact-list access exposes people who are not users.

exposures.title: Agreeing to the terms is agreeing to marketing from partners
exposures.whatItMeans: You specifically consent to Jiostar, its affiliates and partners contacting you at any time during your association, including to offer new products or services, by email and other electronic means. Notices sent to the contact details held are deemed adequate service.
exposures.whyItMatters: Marketing consent for an unnamed set of partners is bundled into acceptance of the terms rather than sought separately, and no opt-out is described here.

exposures.title: Free trials can be withdrawn without notice
exposures.whatItMeans: Eligibility, duration and content available during a free trial are at Jiostar's discretion, and the trial can be modified, suspended or terminated at any time without notice. Billing starts automatically at the end of the trial unless you cancel first.
exposures.whyItMatters: The trial can end early on the company's decision while the automatic charge that follows it stays scheduled.

availableActions.action: Cancel before the free trial ends, not after
availableActions.howTo: Billing starts automatically at the end of the trial. Cancellation is in the My Account section, and cancelling early forfeits the remaining trial with no compensation — but avoids the charge.

availableActions.action: Do not expect an ad-free plan to be ad-free during sport
availableActions.howTo: If live sport is why you are subscribing, the advertisement-free tier does not remove advertising from it. Budget for the cheaper plan instead.

reference.label: Description of Service and Acceptance of Terms of Use

availableActions.action: Pick your tier deliberately — you cannot come back down
availableActions.howTo: Upgrades take effect immediately; downgrades are not permitted until the plan expires. Choose the lower tier first if you are unsure.

availableActions.action: Check your payment method has time left on it
availableActions.howTo: You cannot change the payment method during the subscription term, and if it expires or fails you remain liable for uncollected amounts and the subscription may be terminated.

availableActions.action: Decline contacts access for the Social Feed
availableActions.howTo: The feature is optional. Declining keeps your contest scores and posts out of view of everyone who happens to hold your number.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automatic renewal disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: States clearly that billing recurs automatically each period until cancelled, and that cancellation is available in My Account with notification on cancellation.

requiredDisclosures.name: Advance notice of fee changes
requiredDisclosures.note: Commits to advance notice of a change in the subscription fee for a plan already held — though the general amendment right takes effect on posting.

requiredDisclosures.name: Electronic record status
requiredDisclosures.note: Identifies itself as an electronic record under India's Information Technology Act 2000, requiring no physical or digital signature.

requiredDisclosures.name: Refund and cancellation rights
requiredDisclosures.note: No refund is available in any circumstance described, including for a service never used, an unexpired period, or content withdrawn after purchase.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: Not present in the captured text. Payment complaints are stated to be forwarded to the third-party gateway provider rather than handled by a named officer.

analyses.summary: Flipkart's privacy policy shares personal data with credit bureaus and lending partners for credit underwriting, collects health and prescription information, and asks for access to your SMS, contacts, camera and photo gallery — with the note that refusing may affect your access to products and services. Insights about your buying behaviour go to group companies, business partners and third parties for their own commercial purposes. The captured text ends mid-section, so the rights and grievance provisions could not be read.

exposures.title: Your data goes to credit bureaus and lending partners
exposures.whatItMeans: Personal data is shared with Flipkart group companies including credit bureaus and business partners, for credit underwriting behind personal loans, insurance and the PayLater deferred-payment product. Those recipients may share it onward with their own affiliates and partners, and may market to you as a result.
exposures.whyItMatters: Shopping on a retail platform feeds a credit assessment. The onward-sharing chain is explicitly open-ended, so the eventual holders of your data are not knowable from this document.

exposures.title: Refusing device permissions can cost you the service
exposures.whatItMeans: With consent, Flipkart may access your SMS, instant messages, contacts directory, location, camera, photo gallery and device information, and may request PAN, credit information report, GST number, government ID and KYC details. The policy states your access to products and services may be affected if consent is not given.
exposures.whyItMatters: Consent that carries a service penalty is not freely given in the sense the word implies. SMS and contacts access in particular reveal data about people who are not Flipkart users.

reference.label: Use of Demographic / Profile Data / Your Information
reference.quote: You understand that your access to these products/services may be affected in the event consent is not provided to us.

exposures.title: Health and prescription data is collected and routed to third parties
exposures.whatItMeans: Medical or health-related information may be collected, and for prescription products you may be connected through third-party vendors to medical practitioners or teleconsultants to validate or issue a prescription.
exposures.whyItMatters: Health data is the most sensitive category most people hold, and it enters a platform whose main business is retail advertising and credit. The policy does not separate its handling from the general sharing provisions.

exposures.title: Behavioural insights are passed on for others' commercial purposes
exposures.whatItMeans: Insights derived from your buying behaviour and browsing patterns may be shared with group companies, affiliates, business partners and third parties, who may use them for promotions, advertising, marketing, product development and other commercial purposes, including on their own platforms.
exposures.whyItMatters: 'Other commercial purposes' has no boundary, and the policy states that any processing by those third parties is governed by their own policies rather than this one.

exposures.title: Membership benefits share your contact details for outreach
exposures.whatItMeans: For Plus members with bundled third-party benefits such as streaming subscriptions, your name, email address and mobile number are shared with service partners to activate the benefit and to contact you by SMS, email and WhatsApp.
exposures.whyItMatters: Taking a bundled perk hands your phone number to another company with an express purpose of outreach, and WhatsApp contact is named specifically.

reference.label: Sharing of Personal Data for Plus Membership Benefits and Partner Services

exposures.title: Data may be sold in a corporate transaction
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy states Flipkart and its affiliates will share or sell some or all of your personal data with another business entity in a merger, acquisition, reorganisation or restructuring.
exposures.whyItMatters: The word used is 'sell', not 'transfer'. The successor is required to follow this policy, which limits the exposure but does not remove it.

exposures.title: Agreement is asserted from visiting the site
exposures.whatItMeans: Visiting the platform, providing information, or using a product is expressly agreeing to the privacy policy, the terms of use and applicable product terms.
exposures.whyItMatters: Three documents are accepted by one act, and the act is arriving on the page.

availableActions.action: Deny SMS, contacts and gallery permissions at the OS level
availableActions.howTo: These are separate from the core shopping function. Denying them at the operating-system level is the only reliable control, since the policy frames them as consent-based rather than as settings.

reference.label: Use of Demographic / Profile Data / Your Information

availableActions.action: Turn on 'Opt out of Ads Personalization' in device settings
availableActions.howTo: The policy states Flipkart will have no access to your advertising ID once this device setting is enabled — a stronger effect than a website-level toggle.

availableActions.action: Unsubscribe from promotional messages in notification preferences
availableActions.howTo: The policy links a communication-preferences page for opting out of non-essential promotional and marketing messages. It does not affect the data sharing described above.

availableActions.action: Opt out of Google Analytics separately
availableActions.howTo: The policy names Google Analytics as a third-party cookie partner and links Google's own opt-out tool, which is outside Flipkart's control.

availableActions.action: Read the Ultra-Partner's own policy before being redirected
availableActions.howTo: Ultra-Partners for travel, movie tickets and bill payments are entered using your Flipkart login, and Flipkart disclaims responsibility for their practices.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data localisation
requiredDisclosures.note: States personal data is primarily stored and processed in India and that no product or service is offered outside India.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period is stated. Retention is bounded by purpose, with open-ended exceptions for fraud prevention, legal claims and indefinite retention in anonymised form.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: Not present in the captured text. Important caveat: the capture ends mid-document at the 'Your Rights' heading with no content following it, so this section may exist on the live page but be rendered only on expansion. Treat as unverified rather than confirmed missing.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children's data
requiredDisclosures.note: States it does not knowingly collect from under-18s, and places the representation of authority on the adult who shares a child's data.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent withdrawal mechanism
requiredDisclosures.note: The only opt-out described is for promotional communications and ads personalisation. No route to withdraw consent for the credit-bureau, lending-partner or insight-sharing disclosures appears in the captured text.

analyses.summary: LinkedIn's Professional Community Policies are the mildest acceptable-use document you could reasonably write: a graduated enforcement ladder that limits visibility or labels content before removing it, a stated appeal right for both content and account actions, and a published newsworthiness carve-out. Two things weaken it. It carries no effective date or version anywhere, so a member cannot tell whether the rules have changed since they last read them, and the enforceable detail sits in roughly a dozen linked sub-policies that are not part of this document. It also never says what happens to your posts, connections or messages when an account is restricted — the one question a professional network's users most need answered.

exposures.title: Account restriction is defined by severity, not by a countable threshold
exposures.whatItMeans: Content can be made less visible, labelled or removed; repeated or egregious offences can restrict the account. What counts as egregious, and how many repeats is repeated, is not stated.
exposures.whyItMatters: For someone whose job search or client pipeline runs through LinkedIn, the loss is a professional network rather than a hobby account, and the document gives no way to know how close to that outcome you are.

reference.label: Violating our community policies can result in action against your account or content
reference.quote: Repeated or egregious offenses can result in account restriction.

exposures.title: The policy never says what happens to your content when the account is restricted
exposures.whatItMeans: The enforcement section describes actions against content and against accounts but is silent on whether posts, articles, connections and messages remain, become inaccessible to you, or are deleted.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the document where a user would look for it, and the answer determines whether an enforcement action costs you a week of visibility or a decade of professional record. Nothing here tells you to export first.

reference.label: Violating our community policies can result in action against your account or content

exposures.title: The enforceable detail lives in about a dozen policies that are not in this document
exposures.whatItMeans: Nine of the rules end in a 'Learn more about our ... policies' pointer — harassment, violent and graphic content, restricted goods, dangerous organisations, false or misleading content, scams, hate, sexual harassment, nudity, spam — each a separate undated page.
exposures.whyItMatters: What you actually agreed to is the union of a dozen documents, none of which is reproduced or dated here, so the summary you read is not the standard you are held to.

exposures.title: Automated systems remove content and the appeal is not promised to a human
exposures.whatItMeans: LinkedIn states that automated systems identify potentially violating content alongside trained reviewers, and that violating content can be removed. The appeal route is offered but the document does not say a person reviews it.
exposures.whyItMatters: Automated classifiers produce false positives on exactly the content this policy carves out as educational or newsworthy, and a user cannot tell from this document whether contesting one reaches a human.

reference.label: Tell us if you see abusive content
reference.quote: In addition to LinkedIn's trained content reviewers, we use automated systems to identify potentially violative content.

exposures.title: Real identity is mandatory and pseudonymity is prohibited
exposures.whatItMeans: Members must use their true identity, may not use a profile photo that is not their own likeness, may not create a profile for anyone else, and may not share an account.
exposures.whyItMatters: There is no compliant way to participate under a pseudonym. For a whistleblower, a person changing careers away from an abusive employer, or anyone at risk from being findable, the only options are a rule violation or absence.

reference.label: Do not create a fake profile or falsify information about yourself
reference.quote: Do not use an image of someone else, or any other image that is not your likeness, for your profile photo.

exposures.title: One rule's content is set by outside organisations and can change without notice
exposures.whatItMeans: Content that directly contradicts guidance from leading global health organizations and public health authorities is prohibited. Neither the organisations nor the guidance are named.
exposures.whyItMatters: The prohibited set moves whenever those bodies revise their guidance, and a post that complied when published can become a violation without the policy changing a word.

reference.label: Do not share false or misleading content
reference.quote: Do not share content that directly contradicts guidance from leading global health organizations and public health authorities

exposures.title: The document states no effective date or version
exposures.whatItMeans: Unlike LinkedIn's copyright policy, which is dated, this one carries no effective date, no last-updated line and no version marker.
exposures.whyItMatters: A member cannot establish which version of the rules applied when they posted something, which matters precisely when an old post is enforced against.

availableActions.action: Appeal any content removal or account restriction
availableActions.howTo: The policy states an appeal is available where you believe the action was an error. It is the only remedy named, so use it rather than reposting, which reads as a repeat offence.

reference.label: Violating our community policies can result in action against your account or content
reference.quote: If you believe action taken on your content or your account was in error, you can submit an appeal.

availableActions.action: Export your LinkedIn data before you need it
availableActions.howTo: This policy does not say what survives an account restriction, so keep your own copy of posts, articles and connections. LinkedIn's data export exists outside this document.

availableActions.action: Read the linked sub-policies for anything close to the line
availableActions.howTo: The nine 'Learn more' pages carry the operative definitions. The summaries here are shorter than the rules they stand for.

availableActions.action: Label paid endorsements and altered media in the post itself
availableActions.howTo: The policy requires a clear and conspicuous notice of any personal benefit received, and disclosure of synthetic or manipulated media. Both are conditions on otherwise permitted content, so the disclosure is what keeps the post up.

reference.label: Do not share false or misleading content

availableActions.action: Report content through the three-dots menu rather than by messaging LinkedIn
availableActions.howTo: The in-product report on the content itself is the named channel, and the policy warns that misuse of the reporting tools is itself a violation.

reference.label: Tell us if you see abusive content

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: The document carries no effective date, no last-updated line, no version and no clause about how changes to these policies will be communicated. LinkedIn's copyright policy, by contrast, states an effective date.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consequences of account restriction for user content
requiredDisclosures.note: A new name: none of the existing vocabulary covers content loss on termination, which is the social_ugc rubric item an acceptable-use policy is where you would find it. The document sets out a graduated enforcement ladder ending in account restriction without stating what becomes of the member's posts, connections or messages.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automated decision-making rights
requiredDisclosures.note: The use of automated systems to identify violating content is disclosed, and an appeal against content and account actions is offered — the substance of a right to contest. The document does not state that the appeal receives human review.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer complaint route
requiredDisclosures.note: In-product reporting via the three-dots menu is described for any surface, with the Transparency Center referenced for detail and an appeal route for the reported-against member.

requiredDisclosures.name: Synthetic content declaration
requiredDisclosures.note: Members must disclose the fake or altered nature of synthetic or manipulated media depicting a person saying or doing something they did not. This is an obligation placed on users rather than a statement of LinkedIn's own labelling practice.

requiredDisclosures.name: Minimum age
requiredDisclosures.note: The policy addresses child exploitation content and NCMEC reporting but sets no age condition for using the service; that sits in the User Agreement, which is captured separately, so it could not be verified from this document.

analyses.summary: Amazon's Conditions of Use bind you by use, and bind everyone in your household through your account. Disputes go to binding arbitration with a class-action waiver, applied to claims regardless of when they arose, and — unlike OpenAI's equivalent clause — there is no opt-out window at all. Anything you post carries a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, sublicensable licence to Amazon, plus your indemnity for any claim arising from it.

exposures.title: Binding arbitration and a class-action waiver, with no way out
exposures.whatItMeans: All disputes relating to any Amazon service or product are resolved by binding arbitration rather than in court, on an individual basis only, covering claims regardless of when they arose. Small claims court, intellectual-property injunctions and disputes about the pre-arbitration procedure are the only carve-outs.
exposures.whyItMatters: No opt-out appears anywhere in the document. OpenAI's terms in this same corpus give thirty days to decline arbitration; here the waiver attaches on use and is permanent. Public injunctive relief and any representative capacity are expressly excluded.

reference.label: DISPUTES
reference.quote: All other disputes, claims, and requests for relief must be arbitrated, regardless of when they arose, which means you and we are each waiving our right to sue in court and have a judge or jury trial.

exposures.title: You agree on behalf of your whole household
exposures.whatItMeans: By using Amazon Services you agree to the conditions on behalf of yourself and all members of your household and anyone else who uses an Amazon Service under your account.
exposures.whyItMatters: The arbitration clause and class-action waiver above are imposed on people who never read the document, never clicked anything, and may not know the account exists.

reference.label: Conditions of Use
reference.quote: you agree, on behalf of yourself and all members of your household and others who use any Amazon Service under your account, to the following conditions

exposures.title: Reviews and photos become Amazon's, permanently
exposures.whatItMeans: Posting content grants Amazon a nonexclusive, royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable and fully sublicensable right to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, publish, translate, create derivative works from, distribute and display it worldwide in any media, plus the right to use your name with it.
exposures.whyItMatters: Perpetual and irrevocable means deleting the review does not end the licence, and sublicensable means it can be passed to parties Amazon never names. On top of that, you indemnify Amazon for all claims resulting from content you supply.

reference.label: REVIEWS, COMMENTS, COMMUNICATIONS, AND OTHER CONTENT

exposures.title: A failed payment lets Amazon charge a different card
exposures.whatItMeans: If there is a problem charging your selected payment method, Amazon may charge any other valid payment method associated with your account.
exposures.whyItMatters: The card you chose for a purchase is not necessarily the card that gets charged, and no notice or confirmation step is described before the substitution happens.

exposures.title: Accounts and orders can be ended at sole discretion
exposures.whatItMeans: Amazon reserves the right to refuse service, terminate accounts, terminate your rights to use Amazon Services, remove or edit content, or cancel orders in its sole discretion.
exposures.whyItMatters: No cause is required and no appeal route is described, in a document that also governs access to purchased digital content and devices.

exposures.title: Terms change at any time, and using the site is agreement
exposures.whatItMeans: Amazon reserves the right to change the site, policies, Service Terms and these Conditions at any time, and using Amazon Services after a change is agreement to it.
exposures.whyItMatters: There is no notification and no effective date beyond the Last Updated line, and the arbitration clause reaches claims that arose before the current version existed.

exposures.title: Service-specific terms override these ones
exposures.whatItMeans: Alexa, Amazon Music, Gift Cards, Prime Video and other services carry their own Service Terms, and where they conflict with these Conditions the Service Terms control.
exposures.whyItMatters: Reading this document does not tell you what governs the service you actually use. The controlling document changes depending on which part of Amazon you are in.

availableActions.action: Use small claims court instead of arbitration
availableActions.howTo: If your dispute qualifies for small claims court where you live, that route stays open. It is the only general-purpose court remedy the document preserves.

availableActions.action: Complete the pre-arbitration procedure carefully
availableActions.howTo: Contact customer service first, then submit a Notice of Dispute on the Claim Form and negotiate in good faith for 60 days. This is a condition precedent, and whether it was met is decided by a court rather than an arbitrator.

deadline.description: 60 days of good-faith negotiation after a Notice of Dispute before arbitration can be initiated.

availableActions.action: Do not post anything you may want to remove later
availableActions.howTo: The content licence is perpetual and irrevocable, so deleting a review or photo does not end Amazon's rights in it or its ability to sublicense it.

reference.label: REVIEWS, COMMENTS, COMMUNICATIONS, AND OTHER CONTENT

availableActions.action: Keep only one payment method on the account if substitution concerns you
availableActions.howTo: Amazon may charge any other valid method on your account if the selected one fails. Removing spare methods in Your Payments removes that possibility.

availableActions.action: Read the Service Terms for the part of Amazon you use
availableActions.howTo: Alexa, Prime Video, Gift Cards and Amazon Music each have terms that override these on conflict. The Conditions of Use are the floor, not the whole agreement.

requiredDisclosures.name: Arbitration opt-out right
requiredDisclosures.note: No opt-out window of any kind appears. Compare OpenAI in this corpus, which offers 30 days from account creation and a renewed window on each update to its arbitration terms.

requiredDisclosures.name: Pre-arbitration dispute procedure
requiredDisclosures.note: A defined route — customer service, Notice of Dispute, 60 days of good-faith negotiation — with compliance disputes reserved to a court rather than the arbitrator.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent to electronic communications
requiredDisclosures.note: Consent to receive notices electronically and agreement that they satisfy any legal writing requirement. This is E-SIGN-shaped consent, presented inside general site terms rather than as a separate disclosure.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Washington state law, with a carve-out routing personal-injury and property-damage claims to the law of the state where the harm occurred.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Changes may be made at any time with no notification; continued use is agreement.

analyses.summary: HDFC Bank's website usage terms claim ownership of everything you submit through the site — including your ideas and know-how, usable 'in any manner whatsoever' — and treat merely visiting the site as express authorisation to profile and track you with cookies. The force majeure clause suspends the bank's obligations for computer hacking and unauthorised access to data, which places the consequences of a security failure on the customer. Thirty days' notice of changes is genuinely better than several peers here.

exposures.title: Everything you submit becomes the bank's property
exposures.whatItMeans: All information submitted through the website is deemed HDFC Bank's property, and the bank is free to use any ideas, concepts, know-how or techniques you provide in any manner whatsoever.
exposures.whyItMatters: There is no purpose limit, no time limit and no compensation. Note that the near-identical clause appears in American Express India's site rules — this is a pattern in Indian financial website terms, not a quirk of one bank.

reference.label: Website Usage Terms
reference.quote: all information submitted by me through the HDFC Bank website shall be deemed the property of HDFC Bank, and the Bank shall be free to use any ideas, concepts, know-how or techniques provided by me at the Site, in any manner whatsoever

exposures.title: The bank is not liable if it is hacked
exposures.whatItMeans: The force majeure definition includes computer hacking, unauthorised access to computer data and storage devices, and virus or malicious code in the payment or delivery mechanism. During such an event the bank's obligations are suspended.
exposures.whyItMatters: Force majeure is meant for events outside anyone's control, like floods. Classifying a breach of the bank's own systems as force majeure moves the consequences of a security failure onto the customer, and it does so inside a website-terms document.

reference.label: Force Majeure Event
reference.quote: computer hacking, unauthorised access to computer data and storage devices, computer crashes, malfunctioning in the computer terminal or the systems getting affected by any malicious, destructive or corrupting code

exposures.title: Contacting the bank consents to contact from its partners
exposures.whatItMeans: Initiating any contact through the website is agreement to be contacted by the bank or by any other entity with which the bank has an arrangement.
exposures.whyItMatters: Filling in an enquiry form opens you to marketing from an unnamed and open-ended set of third parties, and the consent is bundled into the act of asking a question.

reference.label: Website Usage Terms
reference.quote: On initiating a contact through the Bank website I agree to being contacted by the bank or any other entities with whom the bank has entered into an arrangement.

exposures.title: Visiting the site is express authorisation to profile you
exposures.whatItMeans: The terms state that cookies are used for storing preferences, profiling visitors and tracking visitor behaviour, and that by visiting you acknowledge, accept and expressly authorise their placement.
exposures.whyItMatters: 'Expressly authorize' is asserted from an act — loading a page — that involves no express anything. Profiling and behavioural tracking are named outright, so what is being consented to is not in doubt; whether it was consented to is.

reference.label: Website Usage Terms
reference.quote: By visiting the website I acknowledge, accept and expressly authorize the Bank for the placement of cookies on my computer.

exposures.title: Disputes go to Mumbai courts only
exposures.whatItMeans: Courts in Mumbai have exclusive jurisdiction over any claim arising from dealings with the bank.
exposures.whyItMatters: For a customer anywhere else in India, pursuing a claim means litigating in another city. The clause covers 'any claims or matters arising out of dealings with HDFC Bank', which reads more broadly than website use.

reference.label: Website Usage Terms
reference.quote: the Courts in Mumbai alone shall have exclusive jurisdiction

exposures.title: Binding by use, with acceptance of future changes built in
exposures.whatItMeans: Use of the site constitutes acceptance of the terms and of changes to them from time to time.
exposures.whyItMatters: You agree in advance to terms that do not yet exist. The 30-day notice period below softens this considerably, but the acceptance mechanism is still continued use rather than a decision.

availableActions.action: Use the 30-day notice window
availableActions.howTo: The bank commits to 30 days' prior notice of changes, communicated on the website and by other modes. That is a real window to read a change before it binds you — most peers in this corpus give none at all.

reference.label: Website Usage Terms
reference.quote: HDFC Bank has the absolute discretion to amend or supplement any of the Website Usage Terms at any time and will give prior notice of 30 days for such changes

availableActions.action: Do not submit ideas or proposals through the website
availableActions.howTo: The ownership clause attaches to everything submitted through the site. Use a channel governed by a different agreement for anything you want to keep.

availableActions.action: Read the service-specific terms separately
availableActions.howTo: These terms are stated to be in addition to, not in place of, the terms for NetBanking and other services. The protections that matter for your money are in those documents, not this one.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: 30 days' prior notice is committed to, communicated on the website and by other modes.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Indian law, with exclusive jurisdiction in Mumbai courts.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: India's IT Rules require a named grievance officer with contact details. None appears in this document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: Profiling and behavioural tracking cookies are described, but consent is asserted from the act of visiting rather than obtained. No opt-out or preference control is described here.

analyses.summary: Zoom's Cookie Statement, updated June 2023, is a competent mid-tier cookie notice: six categories with real purpose descriptions, a working per-category and per-cookie consent tool in the page footer, a named Data Privacy Officer with a postal address, and a commitment to notify and let you review material changes before you continue. Two disclosures cost more than they first read. The analytics category includes session recording and replay capturing mouse movements and clicks, and clearing your cookies silently deletes the advertising opt-out you set. No cookie is named and no duration is given anywhere except the six-month preference cookie.

exposures.title: The analytics category includes session recording and replay
exposures.whatItMeans: Performance cookies gather usage data using session recording and replay technology, capturing mouse movements, clicks and other actions.
exposures.whyItMatters: This reconstructs what you did on the page, not just that you visited it — a materially different thing from the visit counts the same paragraph mentions in the next sentence, and it sits in the bucket most people accept as ordinary metrics.

reference.label: Performance Cookies
reference.quote: Zoom uses Cookies, including session recording and replay technology, to gather usage and performance data (including mouse movements, clicks and other actions)

exposures.title: Clearing your cookies deletes your advertising opt-out
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy states that deleting cookies deletes the settings and preferences those cookies controlled, advertising preferences included, and they must be recreated.
exposures.whyItMatters: Clearing cookies is the standard privacy hygiene step, and here it silently reverses a privacy choice you already made. Nothing prompts you afterwards, so the opt-out lapses without notice.

reference.label: How to Control Cookies
reference.quote: If you choose to delete Cookies, settings and preferences controlled by those Cookies, including advertising preferences, will be deleted and may need to be recreated.

exposures.title: Whether you are asked or merely allowed to opt out depends on where you live
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy repeats three times that consent, opt-out and the default cookie setting all vary by jurisdiction, including for advertising cookies.
exposures.whyItMatters: In one country the advertising cookies are off until you agree; in another they are on until you find the footer tool. The document never says which country is which, so a reader cannot tell which regime they are in without testing it.

reference.label: Targeting
reference.quote: Depending on your jurisdiction, the default setting for cookies differs.

exposures.title: Cookies you cannot refuse may send personal data to the United States
exposures.whatItMeans: A footnote to the Strictly Necessary category states that some of those cookies may transfer personal data to the US, and that third parties deploying them have signed processor agreements.
exposures.whyItMatters: The one category exempt from consent is also the one carrying an international transfer. The processor agreement is a contractual control over what the vendor may do, not a transfer safeguard, and no Standard Contractual Clauses or Data Privacy Framework participation is named.

reference.label: Strictly Necessary Cookies
reference.quote: Some Strictly Necessary Cookies may transfer personal data to the United States.

exposures.title: No cookie is named and no lifetime is disclosed
exposures.whatItMeans: The six categories are described by purpose only. The single duration in the entire document is the preference cookie, stored for at least six months; specifics are deferred to the cookie management tool.
exposures.whyItMatters: You can see what the categories are for but not how long any of them persist or which companies operate them — YouTube is the only third party named in the whole statement.

reference.label: What are Cookies and How Does Zoom Use Them?
reference.quote: Zoom stores a “preference” cookie on your device for at least six (6) months to prevent repeatedly asking you to set your cookie preferences

exposures.title: Global Privacy Control is honoured for two US states and Do Not Track for nobody
exposures.whatItMeans: Zoom responds to the GPC signal for residents of California and Connecticut, and states its websites are not set up to respond to Do Not Track.
exposures.whyItMatters: The browser signal with legal force works, but only for people in the two states whose statutes compel it. Everyone else is back to the footer tool, which is per-browser and lost when cookies are cleared.

reference.label: Global Privacy Control
reference.quote: We respond to the Global Privacy Control signal for residents of California and Connecticut.

availableActions.action: Use the Cookie management tool in the page footer
availableActions.howTo: It accepts or declines categories and individual cookies at any time, for everything except Strictly Necessary. It is a real per-category control, not an email request — but it is per-browser, so repeat it on each device.

reference.label: How to Control Cookies
reference.quote: you can accept or decline categories or individual cookies at any time by visiting our Cookie management tool at the footer of this webpage

availableActions.action: Re-set your cookie preferences after clearing your browser
availableActions.howTo: Deleting cookies wipes the advertising opt-out along with them. Treat the footer tool as something to revisit whenever you clear site data.

availableActions.action: Turn on Global Privacy Control if you are in California or Connecticut
availableActions.howTo: Zoom states it responds to GPC for residents of those two states. Unlike Do Not Track, which it ignores, this signal takes effect and needs no account.

availableActions.action: Decline Targeting cookies to stop social sharing tracking as well
availableActions.howTo: The policy states social media companies cannot tell whether you are logged in once Targeting cookies are off. The cost is that the share buttons stop working.

availableActions.action: Write to the named Data Privacy Officer
availableActions.howTo: Zoom Communications, Inc., Attention: Data Privacy Officer, 55 Almaden Blvd, Suite 600, San Jose, CA 95113, or privacy@zoom.us. A postal address plus a role is more than most cookie notices in this corpus publish.

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of cookies and their purposes
requiredDisclosures.note: Six categories — Strictly Necessary with three sub-types, Functional, Performance, Targeting and Social Media — each with a substantive purpose description and worked examples. Purposes are clear; cookie names and lifetimes are deferred to the management tool.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: A footer cookie management tool accepts or declines by category and by individual cookie at any time, and the policy states consent is sought before setting certain cookies. The default state, and whether consent or opt-out applies, varies by jurisdiction.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No expiry or lifetime is given for any cookie category. The only duration in the document is the preference cookie's 'at least six (6) months', which is the retention of the choice rather than of any tracking identifier.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Advertising partners, analytics providers and social media companies are described by role only. YouTube is the single named third party, mentioned as an example of embedded video.

requiredDisclosures.name: International transfer safeguards
requiredDisclosures.note: The transfer is disclosed — some Strictly Necessary cookies may send personal data to the United States — but no Article 46 mechanism is identified. The processor agreement described is a limit on the vendor's processing, not a transfer safeguard, and neither Standard Contractual Clauses nor the EU-US Data Privacy Framework is named.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data protection officer contact
requiredDisclosures.note: A Data Privacy Officer is addressed by role with a full postal address in San Jose and privacy@zoom.us. Better than most cookie notices in this corpus, which give an email at best.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: No dedicated link, but the footer cookie tool provides the opt-out from advertising cookies and Zoom states it honours the Global Privacy Control signal — limited to residents of California and Connecticut.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Changes take effect on posting, but material changes carry a commitment to notify and to give an opportunity to review before you continue using the sites or keep your cookie preferences. Stronger than the posting-only clause typical of this docType.

analyses.summary: One page carrying two documents: a U.S. States Privacy Notice for eighteen states and a California Privacy Notice, both effective 1 July 2025. The California half does the work — full category lists, sale and share tables, per-right response times, and, uniquely in this corpus, the section 7102 request metrics printed inline rather than linked. Those metrics are the finding: of 58,311 deletion requests, 30,521 were complied with in whole or in part and 27,766 were not, which eBay footnotes as mostly user cancellations during a grace period. The eighteen-state half does almost none of the work — its sections on categories, purposes and third-party sharing each say to go read Section 4 or 5 of the User Privacy Notice instead. eBay states it both shares and sells personal information, with identifiers, network activity and inferences sold to advertising networks and financial service providers, and it collects from data brokers and credit bureaus. Retention has no figures at all here, only a pointer to internal regional guidelines, while eBay's global privacy notice does state six to ten years for Europe.

exposures.title: eBay sells your identifiers and inferences to financial service providers
exposures.whatItMeans: The notice states without qualification that eBay both shares and sells personal information under California law. The sale table lists identifiers, internet and other electronic network activity information, and inferences, going to advertising networks and to financial service providers. The share table is the same categories, to advertising networks only.
exposures.whyItMatters: Sale means transfer for monetary or other valuable consideration, and 'financial service providers' appear only in the sale table, not the share table — so a category of recipient with an interest in your creditworthiness receives inference data on commercial terms. Inferences here explicitly include the user segment you have been placed in.

reference.label: Categories of Personal Information Shared and Sold
reference.quote: We share and sell personal information under California Privacy Laws.

exposures.title: The eighteen-state notice sends you somewhere else for the substance
exposures.whatItMeans: For residents of Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Maryland, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Oregon, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Texas, Utah and Virginia, the three sections covering the categories of personal data processed, the purposes for processing, and the data shared with third parties each consist of a sentence directing the reader to Section 4 or Section 5 of the User Privacy Notice.
exposures.whyItMatters: These state statutes require the privacy notice to contain those disclosures, and the supplemental notice a resident is pointed to contains only cross-references. Everything specific in this capture — the category lists, the sale and share tables, the metrics — sits in the California half and is scoped to California by its own terms.

reference.label: U.S. States Privacy Notice — 1. Categories of Personal Data Processed
reference.quote: To understand the categories of personal data, including sensitive data, that we collect and process about States consumers, please review Section 4 of our User Privacy Notice.

exposures.title: Nearly half of deletion requests were not complied with
exposures.whatItMeans: The published metrics for June 2024 to May 2025 record 58,311 deletion requests received, 30,521 complied with in whole or in part, and 27,766 denied, at a median 14 days. Access requests ran 63,449 received against 4,145 denied at a median of 7 days, and all 661,520 opt-out requests were honoured in a median of one day. A footnote states most denied deletion and access requests were withdrawn or cancelled by users during a grace period.
exposures.whyItMatters: Forty-eight per cent is the number, the explanation for it is eBay's own and unverifiable from the document, and the grace period the footnote relies on is not described anywhere else in the notice. eBay is the only company in this corpus that prints these figures in the document rather than behind a link, which is why the question can be asked of eBay at all.

exposures.title: Guests get an opt-out that dies when they clear cookies
exposures.whatItMeans: Non-registered users and users with suspended accounts can set the Your Privacy Choices toggle, but eBay states it cannot permanently opt out anyone without a registered account: the choice applies only to that browser and only for as long as that browser's cookies are not erased.
exposures.whyItMatters: Guest checkout is a mainstream way to buy on eBay, and the people using it are the ones who chose not to create an account. Their opt-out is stored in the same mechanism that ordinary browser hygiene deletes, so the right expires without notice and its expiry looks exactly like nothing having happened.

reference.label: How to Exercise Your Rights — Non-registered eBay users
reference.quote: eBay is unable to permanently opt-out consumers who do not have a registered eBay account.

exposures.title: Retention points to a document you cannot read
exposures.whatItMeans: The retention section gives three factors — necessity for providing the services, consent-based processing, and statutory or contractual obligations — and states that the specific periods are documented in eBay's regional data retention guidelines, which are internal and not published.
exposures.whyItMatters: eBay's global User Privacy Notice does carry a figure, generally six to ten years for European contracts and business records, and that figure is not carried into the U.S. notice. So an actual retention number exists in one of this company's documents and stops at the American border, leaving U.S. readers with a reference to an internal file.

reference.label: 2.2 Data Retention
reference.quote: The specific retention periods for personal information are documented in our regional data retention guidelines.

exposures.title: Biometrics, ethnicity and message contents are collected as sensitive data
exposures.whatItMeans: Sensitive personal information is enumerated as government ID numbers including Social Security, driver's licence and passport, financial account and log-in information, precise geolocation, information about ethnic or racial origin, the contents of communications, and biometric information. The limit right is then answered by stating that eBay does not use sensitive information to infer characteristics, or limits its use to purposes authorised by CPRA section 1798.121(a).
exposures.whyItMatters: That statement is the lawful route to not offering a limit control, and it is written as an either-or without saying which applies. The categories at stake are the ones a marketplace has no obvious need for, and the sentence that would explain why they are held instead explains why no control is needed.

reference.label: 5. Your Privacy Rights — Right to Limit the Use of Sensitive Personal Information
reference.quote: eBay does not use your sensitive personal information to infer characteristics about you or limits its use to purposes authorized by CPRA Section 1798.121(a).

exposures.title: Data brokers and credit bureaus are listed sources
exposures.whatItMeans: The categories of sources include data brokers and other data providers, credit agencies or bureaus, government entities and public sources, advertising networks, social networks, operating systems and platforms, and other eBay customers.
exposures.whyItMatters: Data brokers and credit bureaus mean information about you arrives without you doing anything, and neither is a source you can switch off. Combined with the sale of identifiers and inferences to financial service providers, information moves in both directions between eBay and the credit-data industry.

reference.label: 1.2 Categories of sources of personal information that we collect
reference.quote: Data brokers and other data providers

exposures.title: A mismatch in your own details ends the request
exposures.whatItMeans: Where an authorised agent submits on your behalf, eBay requires proof of identity and proof of address for you as well as proof of the agent's authority, and states that if the name, address or email address given does not match eBay's records the request cannot be processed. eBay also reserves the right to charge a reasonable fee or decline to act where a request is excessive or overly burdensome.
exposures.whyItMatters: The people most likely to need an agent — someone who has moved, someone locked out of the account email, someone whose account was suspended — are exactly the people whose details will not match. There is no stated route to correct the mismatch first, so the failure mode is a closed loop.

reference.label: How to Exercise Your Rights — Authorized agents
reference.quote: If the name, address, or email address you provide does not match our records, we will not be able to process the request.

exposures.title: Do Not Track signals are ignored
exposures.whatItMeans: eBay discloses, as California law requires it to, that because there is no industry or legal standard for recognising or honouring Do Not Track signals it does not respond to them.
exposures.whyItMatters: The disclosure obligation is met and the position is common. It is worth recording alongside the fact that the Global Privacy Control signal is honoured where legally required, so the two browser signals a person might send get opposite treatment and the notice does not put them side by side.

reference.label: 7. Do Not Track
reference.quote: Because there currently isn't an industry or legal standard for recognizing or honoring DNT signals, we don't respond to them at this time.

exposures.title: The California notice changes the moment it is posted
exposures.whatItMeans: The California half reserves the right to change from time to time and states that changes become effective on the date they are posted. The eighteen-state half is slightly better: it commits to appropriate measures to inform users of material changes in accordance with applicable law.
exposures.whyItMatters: eBay's User Privacy Notice notifies registered users through My Messages and email and publishes the previous version for comparison. Neither of those commitments appears in the state and California documents, so the company's weakest change mechanism is attached to the documents that describe statutory rights.

reference.label: California Privacy Notice — introduction
reference.quote: Changes shall become effective on the date they are posted.

availableActions.action: Ask for the specific list of third parties by name
availableActions.howTo: Go to the Privacy Request Webform, select Other Privacy Request, and describe it as 'Right to Request a Specific List of Third Parties'. eBay gives that exact wording twice. It is the only route in either document that produces named recipients rather than categories.

reference.label: How to Exercise Your Rights
reference.quote: Right to Request a Specific List of Third Parties

availableActions.action: Opt out while logged in, not while browsing as a guest
availableActions.howTo: Use the State Opt-out Rights page or Your Privacy Choices in the footer and set the toggle to out, but sign in to your eBay account first — that is what makes the choice permanent rather than tied to one browser's cookies.

availableActions.action: Send Global Privacy Control as well
availableActions.howTo: Enable GPC in your browser. Where legally required eBay honours it, and associates it with your eBay account when you are logged in on that device. Not logged in, it applies to that browser and device only.

availableActions.action: Correct your data in Account Settings rather than by webform
availableActions.howTo: Corrections made directly in eBay Account Settings take effect immediately; the same correction submitted through the webform can take up to 45 days. Suspended accounts can still use Account Settings for most fields.

reference.label: 5. Your Privacy Rights — Right to Correct

availableActions.action: Request your data through My eBay
availableActions.howTo: Account tab in My eBay, then 'Request your eBay data'. Identity is verified by your existing username and password, so no documents are needed. Access is targeted at 45 days, and the published median for the last reporting year was 7.

deadline.description: 45 days for access and correction requests; deletion requests are stated to take between 30 and 60 days.

reference.label: 5. Your Privacy Rights — Right to Access

availableActions.action: Expect deletion to take up to sixty days if you have sold recently
availableActions.howTo: Use the Deleting your data help page and select Delete My Data. eBay states 30 to 60 days depending on whether you have sold recently, because of its Money Back Guarantee commitment. Do not resubmit inside that window — resubmission is one of the things that shows up as a cancelled request.

deadline.description: Deletion requests are stated to take between 30 and 60 days, longer where you have recently sold on eBay.

reference.label: 5. Your Privacy Rights — Right to Delete
reference.quote: Deletion requests may take between 30 and 60 days to fulfill

availableActions.action: Appeal a refusal — the right exists and is easy to miss
availableActions.howTo: Depending on your state, you can appeal a denied request by following the instructions in the denial email. eBay commits to explaining the reasons for any denial, which is the material you appeal on.

reference.label: 4. Your Privacy Rights — Right to Appeal Denials

availableActions.action: Use the Shine the Light route if you want direct-marketing disclosure
availableActions.howTo: California residents can ask once a year, free, what personal information was disclosed to third parties for those third parties' own direct marketing. eBay states it does not make such disclosures without consent or an opt-out, so this is a route to confirming that in writing.

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of personal data collected
requiredDisclosures.note: Fully enumerated in the California half — identifiers including tax and social security numbers for payment-enabled sellers, protected classifications, commercial and financial information, professional data, network activity, geolocation, audio recordings of customer service calls, inferences including the advertising segment you are placed in, and sensitive personal information. The eighteen-state half carries none of this and cross-references the User Privacy Notice instead.

requiredDisclosures.name: Sensitive personal information categories
requiredDisclosures.note: Six categories named: government ID numbers, financial account and log-in information, precise geolocation, ethnic or racial origin, contents of communications, and biometric information.

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of personal information sold or shared
requiredDisclosures.note: Two tables with recipient categories. Sold: identifiers, network activity and inferences, to advertising networks and financial service providers. Shared: the same three categories, to advertising networks. A third table covers business-purpose disclosure to service providers, credit agencies where required by law, VeRO programme participants, financial institutions, government authorities and other eBay users.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: Your Privacy Choices footer link, a dedicated State Opt-out Rights page, the Privacy Request Webform, and Global Privacy Control honoured where legally required and bound to the account when logged in. Every one of the 661,520 opt-out requests in the reporting year was honoured, at a median of one day. The gap is guest users, for whom the opt-out cannot be made permanent.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data subject rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Access, portability, correction, deletion, opt-out of sale, opt-out of sharing and targeted advertising, non-discrimination, and a right to appeal a denial, each with a route for registered users, guests, suspended accounts and authorised agents, and with response times attached — 45 days for access and correction, 30 to 60 for deletion. The most operationally specific rights section in this corpus.

requiredDisclosures.name: Right to limit use of sensitive personal information
requiredDisclosures.note: Stated as a right, then answered rather than provided: eBay says it does not use sensitive personal information to infer characteristics, or limits its use to purposes authorised by CPRA section 1798.121(a). Written as an either-or, so which of the two positions applies is not settled by the document. No limit control is offered because on either reading none is required.

requiredDisclosures.name: Shine the Light disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: The annual free request right under California Civil Code section 1798.83 is described, together with a statement that eBay does not share personal information for third parties' own direct marketing without consent or an opt-out.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Track response disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: CalOPPA requires a business to disclose how it responds to browser Do Not Track signals. eBay discloses that it does not respond to them, citing the absence of an industry or legal standard. A new name in this vocabulary: it is a distinct statutory disclosure from the CCPA opt-out and from cookie consent, and eBay's cookie notice carries the same text.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children's data
requiredDisclosures.note: eBay states it does not knowingly collect, disclose or sell the personal information of consumers under 16, and that its User Agreement does not permit anyone under 18 to use the services, with a route for a parent or guardian who discovers otherwise.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No figure for any category. Three determining factors are described and the periods themselves are said to live in eBay's regional data retention guidelines, an internal document. eBay's global User Privacy Notice states generally six to ten years for European contracts and business records; nothing equivalent is given here.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automated decision-making rights
requiredDisclosures.note: The eighteen-state notice lists seven rights and profiling is not among them. Several of the states it names — Colorado, Connecticut, Virginia, Texas, Oregon and Montana among them — grant a right to opt out of profiling in furtherance of decisions producing legal or similarly significant effects. eBay's User Privacy Notice does address automated decisions; this supplemental notice, which is where a resident of those states is sent, does not.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Recipients are categories throughout — advertising networks, financial service providers, service providers, credit agencies, government authorities. No company is named. eBay does, unusually, tell you how to obtain the specific list on request, giving the exact wording to use on the webform, so the identities exist and are reachable but are not in the document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: The California half states that changes take effect on the date they are posted, with no notification. The states half is better — appropriate measures to inform users of material changes in accordance with applicable law — but names no method and no period. eBay's User Privacy Notice commits to My Messages and email notice and publishes the previous version; neither commitment is carried into these documents.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer complaint route
requiredDisclosures.note: The escalation described ends inside eBay: reasons given for a denial, and an appeal by replying to the denial email where your state provides one. No supervisory authority, attorney general or privacy agency is named as the route beyond that, and no contact is given other than a Privacy Contact page reference.

analyses.summary: Meta's privacy policy is unusually well presented — highlights, examples, a Privacy Checkup, real download and delete tools, notice before material changes, and a flat commitment never to sell your information. What it discloses inside that presentation is the widest processing in the corpus: collection from people with no account, message content and metadata, camera-roll and voice input, mouse movement, and public content used to develop AI at Meta both for Meta and for third parties. Retention is decided case by case with no period stated for anything.

exposures.title: Information is collected about you with no account at all
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy states plainly that when you use Meta products, some information about you is collected even if you do not have an account, and separately that content others share or reshare about you is processed.
exposures.whyItMatters: None of the controls this policy describes — Privacy Checkup, ad preferences, download, delete — exist for someone without an account. The tools and the collection are not offered to the same set of people.

reference.label: What information do we collect?
reference.quote: When you use our products, we collect some information about you even if you don't have an account.

exposures.title: Your public content develops Meta's AI, and third parties' too
exposures.whatItMeans: Under 'Developing and improving AI at Meta', the information used includes public content that you or others create or share — posts, comments, audio — and your interactions with AI features and their metadata. The stated purpose is to develop and improve AI at Meta for Meta Products and for third parties.
exposures.whyItMatters: Content posted years before generative AI existed is training material now, and the benefit extends beyond Meta. No opt-out for this appears in the policy text itself.

reference.label: Developing and improving AI at Meta

exposures.title: Message content and metadata are processed
exposures.whatItMeans: Information used for personalisation, product provision and safety includes messages you send and receive, including their content, and metadata about content and messages — each qualified with 'subject to applicable law'. Manual human review is used in some cases.
exposures.whyItMatters: Private messaging is named alongside public posts as an input to personalisation and to safety review, and the limit is whatever local law imposes rather than a commitment made here.

exposures.title: One Accounts Centre merges your WhatsApp identity
exposures.whatItMeans: Adding a WhatsApp account to an Accounts Centre with other Meta accounts associates them and shares your information with WhatsApp. Information, infrastructure and systems are shared across the Meta Companies for safety, personalisation of ads and offers, feature development and usage analysis.
exposures.whyItMatters: The separation people assume between their messaging app and their social profile is a settings choice, and joining them is presented as a convenience feature.

exposures.title: Behavioural signals down to mouse movement
exposures.whatItMeans: Device information collected includes what you are doing on your device — whether the app is in the foreground, whether your mouse is moving — alongside device identifiers, device signals, GPS location and network information.
exposures.whyItMatters: The stated purpose is telling humans from bots, but a continuous record of cursor behaviour is a fine-grained behavioural signal held against your identity.

exposures.title: Camera roll, voice and support selfies
exposures.whatItMeans: Collected content includes what you provide through the camera feature or your camera roll settings, through voice-enabled features, and a photo or video selfie if you supply one when contacting support.
exposures.whyItMatters: A selfie given to prove identity to support enters the same processing described for personalisation and safety, and no separate handling or retention is stated for it.

exposures.title: Retention is case by case, with no period for anything
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy states information is kept as long as needed, that the decision is made on a case-by-case basis, and that in some instances information is kept for an extended period.
exposures.whyItMatters: Not one category — not messages, not AI interactions, not the selfie — has a stated end date, and the criteria are all defined by Meta.

reference.label: How long do we keep your information for?

availableActions.action: Run Privacy Checkup
availableActions.howTo: A guided walkthrough of the Facebook privacy settings, linked directly from the policy. It is the fastest route to the settings that actually change what is collected and shown.

availableActions.action: Keep WhatsApp out of your Accounts Centre
