availableActions.howTo: The merge is opt-in. Not adding WhatsApp to an Accounts Centre with your other Meta accounts is what keeps the two identities separate.

availableActions.action: Download your information, then delete what you do not need
availableActions.howTo: The policy links tools to port, download and delete your information or account. Download first — deletion is not reversible and the policy notes extended retention in some cases.

reference.label: Port, download or delete your information

availableActions.action: Review Manage apps and websites for integrated partners
availableActions.howTo: Integrated partners receive information about you and your activity when you connect them, and can always access what is public. This is where those connections are revoked.

availableActions.action: Use the material-change notice window
availableActions.howTo: Meta commits to notifying you before material changes and giving you the opportunity to review the revised policy before continuing to use the products — a real window, and better than most peers here.

reference.label: How will you know that the Policy has changed?

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Commits to notice before material changes with an opportunity to review the revised policy before continuing — stronger than the 'effective when posted' standard common in this corpus.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data subject tools
requiredDisclosures.note: Access, portability, download and deletion are each offered as in-product tools rather than as email requests.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data protection officer and supervisory authority
requiredDisclosures.note: A DPO for Meta Platforms is contactable in some countries, and the policy points users to their local data protection authority.

requiredDisclosures.name: No sale of personal information
requiredDisclosures.note: States it does not sell any information to anyone and never will, and that partners are contractually restricted in how they may use what is provided.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period is given for any category. Retention is decided case by case, with extended preservation in unspecified instances.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: Public content and AI-feature interactions are used to develop AI at Meta for Meta and for third parties. No opt-out is described in the policy text.

analyses.summary: Meta's cookie policy states plainly that it collects data through cookies on third-party websites and apps that embed Meta technology, and that this happens whether or not you hold an account and whether or not you are logged in. It describes categories of use rather than specific data, defers the substance of processing to the Privacy Policy, and offers controls that are largely gated behind having an account.

exposures.title: You are tracked on other companies' sites even with no account
exposures.whatItMeans: Any website or app that embeds Meta technology — a Like button, a pixel, a login widget — sends Meta information about your device and activity when you visit it.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the one collection channel you cannot opt out of by declining to use the product. The policy states it applies to people who have never signed up, so account settings and account deletion do not reach it.

reference.label: Where do we use cookies?
reference.quote: This occurs whether or not you have a Facebook or Instagram account or are logged in.

exposures.title: Collection happens without any action from you
exposures.whatItMeans: Merely loading a page that includes Meta technology triggers collection. You do not have to click the Like button or interact with anything.
exposures.whyItMatters: It removes the intuition most people rely on — that data is shared when you choose to share it — and makes exposure a property of the pages you visit rather than of what you do on them.

reference.label: Where do we use cookies?
reference.quote: including device information and information about your activity, without any further action from you

exposures.title: Data moves across the Meta group and to outside firms
exposures.whatItMeans: Cookies are used across products of other Meta companies, and outside companies also place cookies on Meta products for advertising, measurement, marketing and analytics.
exposures.whyItMatters: It means the recipients of your data are not a fixed list you can inspect, and the policy points you to those third parties' own policies rather than binding them here.

reference.label: Do other Companies use cookies in connection with the Meta Products?
reference.quote: other companies use cookies on the Meta Products to provide advertising, measurement, marketing and analytics services to us

exposures.title: The document defines the technology, not the limits
exposures.whatItMeans: "Cookies" is defined to include identifiers, device data and other storage technologies, and the rules for what is actually done with that data are deferred to the Privacy Policy.
exposures.whyItMatters: Reading this document does not tell you what Meta may do with what it collects. The binding limits live in a separate document that can change independently of this one.

reference.label: What are cookies and what does this policy cover?
reference.quote: Except as otherwise stated in this policy, the Privacy Policy will apply to our processing of the data that we collect via cookies.

availableActions.action: Turn off cookie-based ad personalisation in Meta's ad settings
availableActions.howTo: Open Settings → Ads → Ad preferences on Facebook or Instagram and review the ad-topic and activity controls the policy points to.

reference.label: How can you control your information?

availableActions.action: Block third-party cookies in your browser
availableActions.howTo: Browser cookie settings block the off-site channel this policy describes. The policy names this as a control but notes it is separate from Meta's own settings.

availableActions.action: Use the controls published for people with no account
availableActions.howTo: The policy separates controls into 'If you have a Facebook account', 'If you have an Instagram account' and 'Everyone'. The 'Everyone' set is the only route available without signing up.

reference.label: How can you control your information?

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: This document describes advertising, analytics and measurement cookies but names no lawful basis and no consent mechanism for them. It may be handled by a separate banner or the Privacy Policy; it is not disclosed here.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: No opt-out of sale or sharing appears in this document. It may be published elsewhere on the site; this analysis covers only the text of this document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of cookies and their purposes
requiredDisclosures.note: Seven purpose categories are listed — authentication, security and integrity, advertising and measurement, features, performance, analytics, third-party sites.

analyses.summary: LinkedIn's cookie policy, effective June 2022, is the only document in this corpus where a cookie notice carries the heaviest disclosure on the page. Outside what it calls Designated Countries, LinkedIn collects device information about people who have never engaged with its services at all, and it states that logging out of your account does not stop it logging your browsing on that browser until the cookie expires. Consent is asserted from continued use rather than any affirmative act, and no preference centre is described. It names no cookie, no duration and no third party — the tables it refers to are not in the document.

exposures.title: Device data is collected about people who have never used LinkedIn
exposures.whatItMeans: Outside the undefined set of Designated Countries, LinkedIn collects — or relies on others to collect — ad ID, IP address, operating system and browser information about devices whose owners have not engaged with its services.
exposures.whyItMatters: Never signing up is not a way out. The information is gathered to target and measure ads for LinkedIn members, so a non-user's device becomes an input to a product they declined. The document does not define Designated Countries, so a reader cannot tell whether they are in the protected set.

reference.label: Advertising
reference.quote: outside Designated Countries, we also collect (or rely on others who collect) information about your device where you have not engaged with our Services

exposures.title: Logging out does not stop the logging
exposures.whatItMeans: A member who signs out on a browser continues to have their interaction with LinkedIn's services logged on that browser until the cookie expires, and the resulting analytics are shared in aggregate with LinkedIn's customers.
exposures.whyItMatters: Signing out is the action most people take when they want to stop being tracked. This states it does not work, and the policy gives no cookie lifetime, so there is no way to know how long the logging continues.

reference.label: Analytics and research
reference.quote: If you are a LinkedIn member but logged out of your account on a browser, LinkedIn may still continue to log your interaction with our Services on that browser until the expiration of the cookie

exposures.title: Consent is taken from continued use, and no preference control is offered
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy states that by continuing to visit or use the services you agree to cookies for every purpose described, including advertising. The Your Choices section offers only targeted-advertising settings and browser controls — no per-category consent tool.
exposures.whyItMatters: Continued browsing is not an affirmative act, which is what the GDPR and the ePrivacy rules require for non-essential cookies. Peers with far less tracking in their policies — Dropbox and Zoom — both publish a working per-category preference tool.

reference.label: Cookie Policy
reference.quote: By continuing to visit or use our Services, you are agreeing to the use of cookies and similar technologies for the purposes described in this policy.

exposures.title: Plugins recognise you on sites that are not LinkedIn
exposures.whatItMeans: The Apply with LinkedIn and Share buttons, plus LinkedIn tags on customer and partner sites, use cookies to recognise you on third-party sites — and cookies may be placed in your browser on non-LinkedIn sites that merely display ads or host those tags.
exposures.whyItMatters: You do not have to visit LinkedIn to be identified by it. A recruitment page or a vendor blog carrying a LinkedIn tag is enough, and the set of such sites is not knowable to a visitor.

reference.label: Cookies
reference.quote: We or third parties may also place cookies in your browser when you visit non-LinkedIn sites that display ads or that host our plugins or tags.

exposures.title: No cookie is named and no duration is given
exposures.whatItMeans: The document describes seven purposes but lists no cookie names, no expiry times and no retention. It points to cookie tables that are not part of this policy, and adds that the names may change over time.
exposures.whyItMatters: Every consequence in this policy — how long logged-out logging continues, how long a persistent identifier survives — depends on a duration that is not stated anywhere. Dropbox and OpenAI both publish per-cookie expiry.

reference.label: What technologies are used?
reference.quote: Please note that the names of cookies and similar technologies may change over time.

exposures.title: No third party is named
exposures.whatItMeans: Recipients are described only as customers, partners and service providers, who may set their own cookies on and off LinkedIn for their own marketing purposes.
exposures.whyItMatters: You cannot identify who holds data collected about you, review their terms, or exercise rights against them. The nearest thing to a list is a pointer to the Help Center.

reference.label: What third parties use these technologies in connection with our Services?
reference.quote: third parties may use cookies in their LinkedIn pages, job posts and their advertisements on and off LinkedIn for their own marketing purposes

exposures.title: Do Not Track is ignored and Global Privacy Control is not mentioned
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy explains what Do Not Track is and then declines to honour it, and says nothing about Global Privacy Control, which several US states give legal effect to.
exposures.whyItMatters: Both browser-level signals a person might rely on are either refused or unaddressed, leaving the account-level advertising settings as the only working control — and those do not stop the analytics logging described elsewhere in the document.

reference.label: What is Do Not Track (DNT)?
reference.quote: LinkedIn does not generally respond to “do not track” signals.

exposures.title: Two summary boxes are unfilled authoring placeholders
exposures.whatItMeans: Where the technologies table and the purposes table each promise a summary, the captured text carries the literal strings 'ENTER A SUMMARY' and 'ENTER SUMMARY'.
exposures.whyItMatters: The document opens by claiming to be clear and open and to provide detailed information, and the two plain-language summaries it set out to give are empty. It has stood since June 2022 in that state.

reference.label: What technologies are used?
reference.quote: ENTER A SUMMARY

availableActions.action: Set advertising preferences as a member or as a visitor
availableActions.howTo: The policy provides separate controls for LinkedIn members and for visitors without an account. These limit ad personalisation; they do not stop the analytics logging or the plugin recognition described in the same document.

availableActions.action: Reset or limit the mobile advertising ID on Android
availableActions.howTo: The policy points to the operating system's own controls for ads personalisation and states that iOS advertising IDs are not used for targeted advertising, so this only matters on Android.

reference.label: Opt out of targeted advertising
reference.quote: We do not use iOS mobile advertising IDs for targeted advertising.

availableActions.action: Block third-party cookies and clear LinkedIn cookies in the browser
availableActions.howTo: This is the only control the policy offers against off-site plugins and tags, and against the continued logging after sign-out — that logging is stated to run until the cookie expires, so deleting the cookie ends it.

availableActions.action: Avoid the Apply with LinkedIn and Share buttons on other sites
availableActions.howTo: Interacting with a plugin causes it to identify you. Applying through the employer's own form instead keeps that interaction off LinkedIn's record.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: The only basis stated is continued use of the services, which is not the affirmative act the GDPR and ePrivacy rules require for advertising and analytics cookies. No consent banner, preference centre or per-category control is described anywhere in the document; the choices offered are advertising settings and browser controls.

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of cookies and their purposes
requiredDisclosures.note: Seven purposes are described in a table — authentication, security, preferences, customized content, plugins, advertising, analytics and research — and four technology types are distinguished. The purposes are clear; nothing beneath them is.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No expiry, duration or retention appears for any cookie or identifier. The cookie tables the policy refers to are not part of the document, and it warns that the names may change over time.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Third parties are identified only by role — customers, partners, service providers — while being permitted to set cookies on and off LinkedIn for their own marketing purposes. No company is named.

requiredDisclosures.name: Scope of covered individuals
requiredDisclosures.note: Present, and adverse: the policy states that outside Designated Countries it collects device information about people who have not engaged with its services. Designated Countries is not defined in this document, so the reader cannot place themselves inside or outside the exclusion.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: No opt-out link and no Global Privacy Control statement, in a document that describes cross-context advertising and off-site tracking. Do Not Track is addressed only to say it is not honoured.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Effective 3 June 2022 with no clause stating how changes to the cookie policy will be notified, in a document that already says the cookies it covers may change names over time.

analyses.summary: PayPal's privacy statement is unusually candid about scale. It names data brokers among its sources, infers your income and creditworthiness from how you shop, collects face scans and voiceprints, and takes precise geolocation from anyone logged into a financial account — using a Gramm-Leach-Bliley exemption to avoid offering Americans the right to limit that last one. Personal information trains its AI models and feeds automated decisions that can refuse you service, and in the United States those decisions carry no opt-out. It does state a retention period, which most of this corpus does not: the length of the relationship plus ten years, and three years past account closure for biometrics. Served from PayPal's India legal hub, it has jurisdiction sections for the US, UK/EEA, Mexico and Singapore, and none for India.

exposures.title: Data brokers are a named source of information about you
exposures.whatItMeans: Alongside service providers, payment networks, credit reporting agencies and government entities, the list of sources PayPal obtains personal information from names data brokers outright. Every category listed above — including sensitive information — may come from these sources rather than from you.
exposures.whyItMatters: You cannot correct, withdraw or even see what a broker sold about you, and nothing you do at PayPal governs how it was gathered. Naming them is more honest than most peers manage; it also means the profile does not start from your account.

reference.label: Categories of Personal Information We Collect
reference.quote: Third parties, including service providers, Partners and Merchants, payment partners... government entities, data brokers, and financial institutions.

exposures.title: Your income and creditworthiness are inferred from how you shop
exposures.whatItMeans: Inferred data is its own collected category: gender, income, browsing and purchasing habits, creditworthiness, fraud and risk assessment, preferences and shopping behaviour, derived from your transactions and your interactions with PayPal's partners and merchants.
exposures.whyItMatters: Inferences are treated as collected data and flow into the automated decisions that can limit or refuse your account. Unlike a credit file, there is no bureau to query and no statutory route to dispute an inference you were never shown.

reference.label: Categories of Personal Information We Collect
reference.quote: Inferred data: Such as gender, income, browsing and purchasing habits, creditworthiness, fraud and risk assessment

exposures.title: Precise location is taken from anyone logged into a financial account, and a banking law removes your right to limit it
exposures.whatItMeans: Precise geolocation is collected from users while they are logged into their financial account, and is classified as sensitive personal information. Where US privacy law would normally give you a right to limit the use of sensitive information, PayPal states it relies on a Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act exemption for precise geolocation.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the sharpest instance in the corpus of a financial-sector carve-out being used to switch off a consumer privacy right: the data is sensitive by the law's own definition, and the control the law attaches to it does not apply.

reference.label: Your rights related to Sensitive Personal Information
reference.quote: The exemption we rely on for precise geolocation is based on the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act.

exposures.title: Face scans and voiceprints, kept for three years after you leave
exposures.whatItMeans: Biometric data — voice identification, photo identification and face scans — is collected with in-experience consent to authenticate account actions such as recovering passwords, lifting account limitations and initiating cryptocurrency transfers. It is retained for no more than three years after your account closes, unless law requires longer.
exposures.whyItMatters: Biometrics cannot be reissued after a breach. Three years past closure is a stated limit, which is better than the silence most of this corpus offers, but it still means your face is on file long after you stopped being a customer.

reference.label: How Long We Store Your Personal Information
reference.quote: We retain biometric data for as long as needed or permitted given the purpose for which it was collected and no more than 3 years after your account closes

exposures.title: Automated decisions can cut off your account, and in the US there is no opt-out
exposures.whatItMeans: Automated Decision Making profiles your economic situation, reliability and behaviour to assess credit, fraud and money-laundering risk, and may result in PayPal refusing new services, stopping services you use, or imposing limits. In other jurisdictions you may seek review or object; in the United States, PayPal states these are exempt practices or do not trigger an opt-out right.
exposures.whyItMatters: The decision that freezes your money is made by a model, and the review right that exists in the EEA and UK does not exist for US users. The safeguards offered instead are internal — model overviews and random sampling.

reference.label: AI and Automated Decision Making
reference.quote: In the United States, these are either exempt practices or do not trigger an opt-out right under applicable United States privacy laws.

exposures.title: Your information trains PayPal's AI, and its agentic tools read your purchase and payment history
exposures.whatItMeans: Personal information may be used to train the AI models powering PayPal's services. Agentic AI tools, which can initiate actions on your behalf, are given access to your queries, preferences, interests, purchase history and payment information.
exposures.whyItMatters: No opt-out from model training is described anywhere in the statement — unlike the personalized-shopping and marketing choices, which have named settings. Payment information reaching a tool designed to act autonomously is a materially different exposure from the same data sitting in an account record.

reference.label: AI and Automated Decision Making
reference.quote: When you use these tools, they will have access to your Personal Information, including queries, preferences, interests, purchase history, and payment information.

exposures.title: Ten years of retention after the relationship ends
exposures.whatItMeans: Information used for the ongoing relationship is kept for its duration plus ten years, or longer where local law, litigation, investigations, audit or compliance require it. Closing the account or exercising deletion does not clear what PayPal is permitted to keep for transactions, fraud prevention, legal compliance and internal business processes.
exposures.whyItMatters: A stated period is a genuine improvement — twelve documents in this corpus state none at all — but a decade is a long time for a file that includes biometric authentication history, inferred income and every transaction you made.

reference.label: How Long We Store Your Personal Information
reference.quote: stored for the duration of the relationship plus a period of 10 years or such period as mandated by any applicable local law

exposures.title: Sharing your data with merchants for personalized shopping is on unless you turn it off
exposures.whatItMeans: Unless law requires consent, PayPal discloses information collected after 27 November 2024 to partners and merchants for personalized shopping in the United States by default. Opting out is a preference in the Data and Privacy setting, and existing pre-2024 history can additionally be swept in if you affirmatively consent.
exposures.whyItMatters: The date is the tell: a defined start point means the default was switched on for accounts that already existed, and the disclosure continues until the account holder finds the setting.

reference.label: Choose what we share with Partners and Merchants for Personalized Shopping

exposures.title: Under US financial privacy law, most of the sharing cannot be limited — and it continues after you leave
exposures.whatItMeans: The Gramm-Leach-Bliley notice shows PayPal shares for everyday business purposes, its own marketing, and joint marketing with other financial companies, with no right to limit any of them. Only creditworthiness sharing with affiliates, affiliate marketing and non-affiliate marketing can be limited. The notice states that sharing continues when you are no longer a customer.
exposures.whyItMatters: The three categories you can switch off are the three federal law requires; everything else is outside your control by design. Ending the customer relationship does not end the sharing.

reference.label: Notice for Consumers of Financial Products and Services
reference.quote: When you are no longer our customer, we continue to share your information as described in this notice.

exposures.title: In the EEA, saying nothing for 30 days counts as agreeing to new recipients
exposures.whatItMeans: PayPal publishes a third-party recipient list and may update it on the first business day of each quarter. Transfers to new entities begin 30 days after publication, and if you do not object within those 30 days you are deemed to have accepted the additions. Your remedy for disagreeing is to close the account.
exposures.whyItMatters: The disclosure itself is better than any peer here — Luxembourg bank secrecy law is why the recipient list exists at all — but it puts the burden on the user to check a webpage every quarter, and treats silence as consent to new data recipients.

reference.label: Banking Regulations Notice for Users in the EEA
reference.quote: If you do not object to the new Personal Information disclosure, within 30 days after the publication of the updated list of third parties, you are deemed to have accepted the changes

exposures.title: You are collected on before you have an account, and it is joined up if you open one later
exposures.whatItMeans: Personal information is collected from non-account holders using guest checkout, Fastlane profiles, unbranded Braintree processing, Visa+ and Hyperwallet payouts. If you create a PayPal account afterwards, those earlier transactions may be linked to it.
exposures.whyItMatters: Choosing not to have an account does not keep you out of the dataset, and the record assembled while you had no account and no settings becomes part of the account you eventually open.

reference.label: Non-Account Holders
reference.quote: If you Pay without a PayPal account, we may link your transaction information with your PayPal account if you create a PayPal account later.

exposures.title: Do Not Track is ignored, and refusing cookies may lock you out
exposures.whatItMeans: PayPal states it does not respond to Do Not Track browser settings because many of its services will not function without tracking data. It also states that certain features are only available through cookies, so declining them may make the sites and services limited or unusable.
exposures.whyItMatters: For a payment service, 'decline cookies and you may not be able to use it' is not a real choice — it puts access to your own money on one side of the trade.

reference.label: Do Not Track
reference.quote: Because many of our services won't function without tracking data, we do not respond to DNT settings.

availableActions.action: Turn off personalized-shopping sharing with partners and merchants
availableActions.howTo: Log into your PayPal account and edit the preferences in the Data and Privacy setting. Transactions you initiate still go through; what stops is the disclosure of your preferences, sizes and styles to merchants for personalization. Do not separately consent to sweeping in pre-27-November-2024 history.

reference.label: Choose what we share with Partners and Merchants for Personalized Shopping

availableActions.action: US customers: limit the three categories of sharing federal law lets you limit
availableActions.howTo: Edit preferences in the Data and Privacy setting, or call 1-888-221-1161 to limit all sharing where permitted. This covers creditworthiness shared with affiliates, affiliates marketing to you, and non-affiliates marketing to you. New customers should act promptly — sharing may begin 30 days after the notice is sent.

deadline.description: For a new customer, PayPal may begin sharing 30 days from the date the privacy notice was sent.

availableActions.action: Do not link bank, card, investment, social or mail accounts
availableActions.howTo: Linked accounts are collected from periodically until you unlink them, and PayPal states it is not responsible for protecting information shared with a third party through a link you authorized. Manage or revoke these under Security settings in your account.

reference.label: Choose how linked accounts collect and use Personal Information

availableActions.action: Refuse contacts sync, and keep the profile private
availableActions.howTo: Importing contacts hands PayPal other people's names, addresses, phone numbers, images and usernames, and you are made to certify you had their permission. Declining still leaves the apps usable. Separately, account profile information can include sensitive details — the profile can be set to Private at any time.

reference.label: Choose how we collect Personal Information

availableActions.action: Decline precise geolocation at the device level
availableActions.howTo: PayPal collects precise geolocation from users logged into a financial account and relies on a GLBA exemption rather than the usual right to limit sensitive information, so the control that works is your operating system's location permission. Address-based recommendations continue regardless.

reference.label: Send you locally relevant options and for security

availableActions.action: EEA and UK: request review of an automated decision, and complain to a regulator
availableActions.howTo: You can seek review of, object to, or revoke consent for an automated decision with legal or similarly significant effects, and be told the logic and consequences involved. Complaints go to your local supervisory authority — the CNPD in Luxembourg is PayPal's lead authority, the ICO for the UK. Neither right is offered to US users.

reference.label: UK and EEA Data Protection Rights

availableActions.action: Ask for the list of specific third parties your data went to
availableActions.howTo: Distinct from a data access request: PayPal offers a right to request a list of the specific third parties it disclosed your information to, by phone or contact form in the US and through the Help Center elsewhere. EEA and UK users additionally get the standing quarterly recipient list.

reference.label: Your right to request a list of specific third parties

availableActions.action: Check the EEA third-party recipient list each quarter if you want to object
availableActions.howTo: The list is updated on the first business day of January, April, July and October, and new transfers start 30 days later. Silence across that window is treated as acceptance, so an objection has to be raised inside it.

deadline.description: 30 days from publication of each quarterly update to the third-party list, after which non-objection is deemed acceptance.

reference.label: Banking Regulations Notice for Users in the EEA

availableActions.action: Unsubscribe from marketing, but expect service messages regardless
availableActions.howTo: Use the unsubscribe link in marketing email, reply STOP to texts, or turn off device notifications and change account notification settings. Digital receipts and account-status alerts cannot be switched off, though you may be able to choose the channel. Nevada residents can join an internal Do Not Call list on 1-888-221-1161.

reference.label: Choose how we communicate with you

availableActions.action: Appeal a refused privacy request
availableActions.howTo: If a request is denied in whole or part, you may have the right to be told why and to appeal, and PayPal states it will provide information about the appeals process. An authorized agent can act for you with a power of attorney or equivalent written authority.

reference.label: How you can exercise your rights

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: A rare positive in this corpus: relationship duration plus ten years, with biometric data capped at three years after account closure. Extensions for legal obligation, litigation and audit are named rather than left open.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: States PayPal does not sell personal information, nor share it for cross-context behavioral advertising subject to non-exempt practices, and has not in the prior 12 months. The qualifier matters — GLBA-exempt financial data sits outside that statement.

requiredDisclosures.name: GLBA consumer privacy notice
requiredDisclosures.note: Full model-form notice dated 17 November 2025, with the sharing table, the limitable and non-limitable categories, a 30-day window for new customers, and California, Vermont and Nevada supplements.

requiredDisclosures.name: Right to limit use of sensitive personal information
requiredDisclosures.note: PayPal states this right is not necessary because it uses sensitive information only per consent or permitted purposes, and expressly relies on a Gramm-Leach-Bliley exemption for precise geolocation. The category is collected; the statutory control over it is not offered.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: Personal information is used to train AI models powering the Services, and agentic tools are given purchase and payment information. No opt-out, objection route or exclusion is described, in contrast to the named settings for personalized shopping and marketing.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automated decision-making rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Available in the EEA and UK as review, objection and consent withdrawal. For US users PayPal states these practices are exempt or do not trigger an opt-out right, leaving only internal safeguards — model overviews and random sampling.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: This statement is served from PayPal's India legal hub and India's IT Rules require a named grievance officer with contact details. India appears only as an entry in the corporate contact table; there is no India section, no grievance officer and no reference to India's data protection law, while the US, UK/EEA, Mexico and Singapore each get their own disclosures.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children's data
requiredDisclosures.note: Services are not directed to under-18s, no knowing collection, and prompt deletion on actual knowledge unless retention is legally required. A higher age floor than the COPPA minimum.

requiredDisclosures.name: International transfer safeguards
requiredDisclosures.note: Binding Corporate Rules approved by supervisory authorities for intra-group EU transfers, and adequacy decisions, Standard Contractual Clauses, the UK IDTA or a derogation for anything else.

requiredDisclosures.name: Lawful basis for processing
requiredDisclosures.note: Set out per purpose in a dedicated table, with special-category conditions where relevant, and applied to other regimes with equivalent requirements.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: 30 days' prior notice where applicable law requires notice; otherwise the revised statement is effective on its published date. New users are bound by upcoming changes already posted at the time they first receive the statement.

analyses.summary: DoorDash disclaims responsibility for the food itself — including whether the allergen and ingredient information shown to you is accurate, and it notes that information may have been generated or enhanced by artificial intelligence. It then disclaims damages for personal injury and caps its total liability at whatever you paid it in the previous six months. Completed orders are final and non-refundable; refunds are gratuitous and at DoorDash's sole discretion. Arbitration is mandatory and retroactive, the agreement tells you outright that accepting it removes you from class actions already filed, and the 30-day opt-out is open only to accounts created after the current version took effect — updates never reopen it. DashPass has more automatic on-ramps into a recurring charge than any subscription in this corpus, and DoorDash may retry a failed renewal against every payment method on your account.

exposures.title: Allergen information may be AI-generated, and DoorDash is not responsible if it is wrong
exposures.whatItMeans: DoorDash states it is not responsible for whether menu listings, item descriptions or nutrition, ingredient and allergen information accurately reflect what the merchant sells, and that such information may not have come from the merchant and may have been generated or enhanced with the assistance of artificial intelligence.
exposures.whyItMatters: Allergen information is the one field on a food listing where being wrong can hospitalise someone. This says it may be machine-written, may not be the merchant's, and carries no accountability — and the same agreement disclaims damages for personal injury.

reference.label: Contractors and Merchants Are Independent
reference.quote: may not have been provided directly by the Merchant and/or may have been generated or enhanced with the assistance of artificial intelligence

exposures.title: Personal injury damages disclaimed, and liability capped at six months of your fees
exposures.whatItMeans: Aggregate liability is limited to the amounts you paid or owe DoorDash in the six months before the event. Indirect, punitive, special, incidental and consequential damages are disclaimed, and personal injury, pain and suffering and emotional distress are named inside that disclaimer. New Jersey residents and Québec consumers are carved out of the personal-injury and punitive parts; nobody else is.
exposures.whyItMatters: For a service that puts prepared food in your hands, this caps the consequences of getting it wrong at the value of your recent orders. That two jurisdictions are carved out shows the drafters knew the disclaimer would not survive everywhere — and left it applying everywhere else.

reference.label: Breach and Limitation of Liability
reference.quote: DOORDASH'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF AMOUNTS ACTUALLY PAID BY AND/OR DUE FROM YOU TO DOORDASH IN THE SIX (6) MONTH PERIOD IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT

exposures.title: Accepting the terms elects you out of class actions already filed against DoorDash
exposures.whatItMeans: Arbitration applies to all claims that arose before, on or after the effective date. The agreement states in capitals that cases attempting to assert class claims have been filed against DoorDash, and that by accepting the arbitration agreement you elect not to participate in them.
exposures.whyItMatters: Retroactive arbitration clauses are common; naming live litigation and telling you that clicking through withdraws you from it is not. It is candid, and it means the cost of accepting is a specific claim you may already have, not a hypothetical future one.

reference.label: Scope of Arbitration Agreement
reference.quote: CASES HAVE BEEN FILED AGAINST DOORDASH—AND OTHERS MAY BE FILED IN THE FUTURE—THAT ATTEMPT TO ASSERT CLASS ACTION CLAIMS, AND BY ACCEPTING THIS ARBITRATION AGREEMENT YOU ELECT NOT TO PARTICIPATE IN SUCH CASES.

exposures.title: The arbitration opt-out is only for brand-new accounts, and updates never reopen it
exposures.whatItMeans: A 30-day opt-out by email to opt-out@doordash.com exists, but only for people creating a DoorDash or Caviar account for the first time on or after the current version's effective date. The agreement states expressly that updates to the terms do not give existing users a new opportunity to opt out.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the middle point of a three-way contrast in the corpus. OpenAI reopens its opt-out window on every update; Amazon offers none at all; DoorDash offers one that closes permanently 30 days after signup and is never reopened. The clause exists, and almost nobody who has it can still use it.

reference.label: Opt Out
reference.quote: DoorDash's updates to these Terms and Conditions do not provide a new opportunity to opt out of the Arbitration Agreement

exposures.title: Completed orders are final, and any refund is a gift DoorDash may choose not to give
exposures.whatItMeans: For United States, Canada and New Zealand orders, charges for completed and delivered orders or orders confirmed by a merchant are final and non-refundable. DoorDash states it has no obligation to provide refunds or credits and may grant them gratuitously at its sole discretion in each case. Where it does refund, it is under no obligation to do so again.
exposures.whyItMatters: Combine this with the independence clause — DoorDash is not the restaurant, not the courier, and not responsible for either — and a wrong or inedible order has no party who owes you anything. The remedy exists only as a discretionary favour.

reference.label: Refunds
reference.quote: Charges paid by you for completed and delivered orders, or for orders confirmed by a Merchant, are final and non-refundable.

exposures.title: A refused alcohol delivery forfeits the whole order, including everything else in it
exposures.whatItMeans: If an alcohol or age-restricted delivery cannot be completed — no valid ID, visibly intoxicated, or nobody physically present — the purchase is non-refundable, you may receive no part of the order including the items that were not age-restricted, and a non-refundable Undeliverable Item Fee may be charged on top.
exposures.whyItMatters: Being out when the courier arrives costs you the groceries as well as the wine, plus a fee. The refusal grounds are ones the courier judges on the doorstep, and the forfeiture is total rather than proportionate to the restricted item.

reference.label: Transactions Involving Alcohol and Other Age-Restricted Products
reference.quote: your purchase is non-refundable and you or the intended recipient may not receive any part of the applicable order, including any non-alcohol items

exposures.title: DashPass renewal will be retried against every payment method on your account
exposures.whatItMeans: By subscribing you authorise DoorDash to store your designated payment method and any other payment method associated with the account, and to retry a failed renewal using various payment methods on file. If your card details change, the card provider may supply updated details, which DoorDash may use to keep the subscription running.
exposures.whyItMatters: Removing or letting a card expire is how most people stop a subscription they have lost track of. This authorises a fallback to every other card on the account and a refresh of details from the issuer, so the usual passive cancellation does not work.

reference.label: DashPass Subscriptions
reference.quote: retrying payment using various payment methods you have on file if payment fails when attempting a renewal

exposures.title: Eight different free DashPass on-ramps, all of which convert to a paid plan by themselves
exposures.whatItMeans: Free trials, gift subscriptions, and complimentary subscriptions via Chase, RBC, Amazon Prime in Canada and Australia, T-Mobile, Lyft, Chegg and Disney+ Perks each convert automatically into a paid monthly or annual DashPass plan at the then-current fee unless cancelled first. Cancellation takes effect only at the end of the current period and must be made at least one day before the renewal date.
exposures.whyItMatters: Every one of these begins as somebody else's perk, often months or years earlier — the Amazon Prime Australia offer runs 24 months before it starts charging. The person being charged did not choose DoorDash as a subscription; they accepted a benefit from their bank, phone carrier or streaming service.

exposures.title: A perpetual, irrevocable licence to your reviews and photos, with your name attached, surviving your account
exposures.whatItMeans: User content — reviews, ratings, photos, video, feedback — is licensed to DoorDash and its service providers perpetually, irrevocably, transferably, royalty-free, worldwide and sublicensably, to use, modify, translate, create derivative works from and distribute, without notification to or approval by you. A separate licence covers your username, first name and last initial, profile photo and ratings history for attribution. The licence survives termination of your account.
exposures.whyItMatters: Deleting your account does not withdraw the licence, and DoorDash states it has no obligation to attribute the content to you when it uses it. Reviews may also be summarised by AI and displayed as summaries.

reference.label: User Content
reference.quote: the license granted to DoorDash herein shall survive termination of the Services or your account

exposures.title: Disputing a charge is a rule violation if DoorDash decides it was unfounded
exposures.whatItMeans: The rules prohibit falsely or fraudulently claiming an order was missing, incorrect, poor quality or never delivered, and falsely or fraudulently disputing a card charge or requesting a chargeback. Breach permits suspension or permanent deactivation of your account at DoorDash's sole discretion.
exposures.whyItMatters: The qualifier is 'falsely or fraudulently', so an honest dispute is not barred — but DoorDash decides which is which, refunds are already discretionary, and the penalty for guessing wrong is losing the account. A chargeback is the remedy a card network gives you precisely for when the merchant says no.

exposures.title: Mass arbitration is grouped 100 claims to an arbitrator
exposures.whatItMeans: Where 100 or more similar arbitration demands are filed within 30 days, they are randomised into groups of up to 100, one set of filing and administrative fees is assessed per group, and one arbitrator is assigned per group. Each claim is still decided individually and no award has preclusive effect on another.
exposures.whyItMatters: Filing fees are what makes coordinated individual arbitration a real threat once class actions are waived. Charging one fee per hundred claims removes that pressure while keeping the formal promise that each claim is heard on its own.

availableActions.action: New accounts only: opt out of arbitration within 30 days
availableActions.howTo: Email opt-out@doordash.com with your name and address, DoorDash username, the email on the account, and a clear statement that you want to opt out of the Arbitration Agreement. Only available if you created the account on or after this version's effective date, and it will never be offered again.

deadline.description: 30 days after first becoming subject to the Arbitration Agreement — available only to accounts created on or after the current version's effective date.

availableActions.action: Cancel DashPass at least one full day before the renewal date
availableActions.howTo: Cancellation is initiated through the app or site and takes effect at the end of the current period — cancel by 11:59:59pm on the day before renewal. Benefits continue to the end of the period. Removing your card does not work: DoorDash may charge any other payment method on file.

deadline.description: At least one day before the next scheduled renewal date, or the next period is charged.

availableActions.action: Claim the 48-hour DashPass refund window if you have not ordered
availableActions.howTo: Cancelling within the first 48 hours of your first paid subscription period, having placed no DashPass-eligible order, may get the fee refunded at DoorDash's discretion. After a free trial, cancelling within the first 48 hours of the first paid period gets a full refund as of right. Québec annual subscribers can request a prorated refund on 855-431-0459; British Columbia annual subscribers get one automatically within 15 days.

deadline.description: 48 hours from the start of your first paid DashPass subscription period.

availableActions.action: Diarise the end date of any complimentary DashPass from a bank, carrier or streaming perk
availableActions.howTo: Chase, RBC, Amazon Prime, T-Mobile, Lyft, Chegg and Disney+ Perks subscriptions all roll into a paid plan at the then-current fee when the perk ends — the Australian Amazon Prime one after 24 months, T-Mobile 30 days after you leave the qualifying plan. Cancelling the perk does not cancel DashPass.

availableActions.action: Be present with ID for anything age-restricted, or lose the entire order
availableActions.howTo: The courier must see valid government identification and you must be physically present and not visibly intoxicated. Failing any of those forfeits the whole order — non-restricted items included — plus an Undeliverable Item Fee. Ordering alcohol together with groceries puts the groceries at that risk too.

reference.label: Transactions Involving Alcohol and Other Age-Restricted Products

availableActions.action: Verify allergens with the restaurant directly, not from the listing
availableActions.howTo: DoorDash disclaims accuracy for nutrition, ingredient and allergen information and states it may be AI-generated. For anyone with a serious allergy, the listing is not a source — call the merchant.

availableActions.action: Use the informal resolution conference — it is a required step, and it tolls the clock
availableActions.howTo: Before arbitration either side must meet by phone or video in good faith. Notify DoorDash at Informal.Resolution@doordash.com with your name, account phone and email, and a description of the claim; the conference happens within 60 days. Limitation periods and filing deadlines are tolled while it runs, and an arbitration filed without completing it will be dismissed.

deadline.description: The informal conference must occur within 60 days of the other party receiving notice, unless extended by agreement.

availableActions.action: Use small claims court instead — US and New Zealand consumers keep that option
availableActions.howTo: Qualifying claims may be brought in small claims court or tribunal so long as they stay there and proceed individually. If the arbitrator finds you cannot afford the fees and no waiver is available, DoorDash pays them; for Australian claims under AUD $10,000 it reimburses them outright.

availableActions.action: Restrict your public profile so reviews are counted but not displayed
availableActions.howTo: DoorDash aggregates publicly viewable user content into a profile anyone can view. Setting it to restricted means only the number of reviews and photos you have submitted is shown, not their contents.

availableActions.action: Opt out per channel — and know that deleting the account is the only full stop
availableActions.howTo: Marketing email has an unsubscribe link; marketing texts stop with STOP to 63758; transactional texts with STOP to 87424 or a toggle in settings; push notifications toggle in the app; phone calls via an internal do-not-call request on 855-431-0459. Opting out of one channel does not affect the others, courier MMS delivery confirmations cannot be stopped at all, and the terms state that opting out of everything requires deleting your account.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automatic renewal disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: Set out in capitals: automatic renewal by default, the then-current fee charged at renewal, $9.99/month or $96/year named for trial conversions, and a linked cancellation flow. Prior notice of each renewal is given only to the extent applicable law requires it.

requiredDisclosures.name: Arbitration opt-out right
requiredDisclosures.note: 30 days by email to opt-out@doordash.com — but only for accounts created on or after the current version's effective date, and the terms state expressly that updates never reopen the window for existing users.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Material changes are notified by email or another means; other changes take effect on posting, and continued use is agreement. Material changes to the arbitration agreement itself do not apply to claims already noticed.

requiredDisclosures.name: Refund and cancellation rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Disclosed and almost entirely negative: completed orders final and non-refundable, refunds gratuitous at sole discretion, subscription fees non-refundable. Statutory floors are named and preserved for Australia, New Zealand, Québec and British Columbia consumers.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Delaware law with the Federal Arbitration Act for US orders, Ontario for Canada, Victoria for Australia, New Zealand for New Zealand — with exclusive venue in San Francisco for Californians and the user's home district for other US consumers.

requiredDisclosures.name: Designated DMCA agent
requiredDisclosures.note: A copyright-infringement claims procedure is set out with contact details for notices.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer complaint route
requiredDisclosures.note: Customer Support page for general complaints, plus the California Civil Code § 1789.3 disclosure naming the Complaint Assistance Unit of the California Department of Consumer Affairs with its address and telephone number.

requiredDisclosures.name: Limitation on indemnity
requiredDisclosures.note: The indemnity requires you to pay for DoorDash's defence, but expressly does not extend to DoorDash's own unconscionable commercial practice, negligence, fraud, deception, false promise, misrepresentation or concealment of a material fact.

requiredDisclosures.name: Pre-arbitration dispute procedure
requiredDisclosures.note: Mandatory individualised informal conference by phone or video within 60 days of notice, with limitation periods tolled and dismissal of any arbitration filed without it. Both the party and any counsel must attend, and multiple claimants cannot share a conference.

analyses.summary: X's cookie notice describes nine categories of use, including advertising and cross-device personalisation, and offers no consent gate for any of them — the controls it lists are browser settings, industry opt-out tools and in-product toggles that all act after collection has started. Two limits are geographic rather than universal: off-X browsing history is only default-off in the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, and everyone else has to find the setting. It also states plainly that logging in once ties that device to your account whether or not you are signed in afterwards, and that you will always see ads based on your X activity regardless of what you turn off.

exposures.title: No consent gate — every control acts after the fact
exposures.whatItMeans: The notice lists advertising, marketing, analytics, research and cross-device personalisation as purposes, then offers browser cookie settings, the Digital Advertising Alliance tool, mobile OS ad-tracking settings and in-product toggles. None is described as a choice made before cookies are set, and turning cookies off entirely is said to break logging in to x.com.
exposures.whyItMatters: Where consent is legally required for non-essential cookies, a control that only stops future collection is not one. Here the alternative to accepting the advertising and analytics set is being unable to sign in.

reference.label: What are my privacy options?
reference.quote: if you turn off cookies entirely, X services may not work correctly or you might have trouble logging into x.com

exposures.title: Off-X browsing history is default-off only inside Europe
exposures.whatItMeans: X stores the other websites where you have seen X content. Users in the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland get that storage switched off by default. Everyone else keeps it until they find Settings and privacy > Privacy and safety > Off-X activity and turn it off themselves.
exposures.whyItMatters: The same product treats the same data differently by where you live, and the protection travels with the regulator rather than with the user. This is the mirror image of the pattern already recorded in this corpus, where collections are disclosed as not happening in the EEA — here the safeguard, not the collection, stops at the border.

reference.label: What are my privacy options?
reference.quote: If you’ve turned this off, or are in the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway or Switzerland, we won't store or use these web page visits

exposures.title: Turning it off does not undo what was already learned
exposures.whatItMeans: The same paragraph states that if X has previously stored your web browsing history, it may continue to personalise your experience based on what it already learned from that history.
exposures.whyItMatters: The switch stops collection and not use. Years of stored browsing can keep shaping what you are shown after you opt out, and the notice describes no way to delete the inferences that history produced.

reference.label: What are my privacy options?
reference.quote: if we've previously stored your web browsing history, we may continue to personalize your experience based on information we've already learned from that history

exposures.title: One login binds that device to your account permanently
exposures.whatItMeans: If you ever log in to X on a device, X associates and will continue to associate that device with your account. From then on it receives information about the device when a partner shares data, when you visit x.com or third-party sites carrying X services, or when you visit an advertiser's site or app — signed in or not. IP address and timestamp are named as the most common linking signals.
exposures.whyItMatters: Logging out is not a reset. A shared or borrowed device stays attached to whoever signed in on it, and the association is described as continuing rather than expiring.

reference.label: Personalization across devices
reference.quote: if you ever log in to X with your device, we associate and will continue to associate that device with your account

exposures.title: Ads based on your X activity cannot be turned off at all
exposures.whatItMeans: The notice states flatly that you will always see ads on X based on your X activity. The six controls it then lists — personalised ads, DAA opt-out, iOS and Android limits, inferred identity, browser cookies — all address off-X data or cross-device linking.
exposures.whyItMatters: The commitment to meaningful privacy options is made two paragraphs above a sentence that removes on-platform ad targeting from the set of things you can decline.

reference.label: What are my privacy options?
reference.quote: You will always see ads on X based on your X activity.

exposures.title: Paying for a feature can override the setting you chose
exposures.whatItMeans: Even where you have turned off storage of where you see X content across the web, X states it will still store certain information for certain paid subscription features where that is necessary for the feature to work, and will tell you about it at sign-up.
exposures.whyItMatters: A privacy setting that a later purchase silently reopens is not a standing choice. The disclosure is made at the point of subscribing rather than in the setting itself, so the toggle keeps reading as on.

reference.label: What are my privacy options?
reference.quote: for certain paid subscription features, even if you make this adjustment we will still store certain information

exposures.title: Your preferences are per-browser, and only count while logged in
exposures.whatItMeans: To view or change web settings for the account you must be logged in to that browser. Changing settings while logged out affects only that browser's logged-out behaviour.
exposures.whyItMatters: A person who uses two browsers, or a phone and a laptop, has to repeat every choice, and a choice made in a logged-out state does not attach to the account it was meant to protect.

reference.label: More privacy options
reference.quote: Changing your X settings in the web browser when you’re logged out will only affect behavior on that browser while you aren't logged in to X.

availableActions.action: Turn off off-X activity and inferred identity
availableActions.howTo: Settings and privacy > Privacy and safety > Off-X activity carries both 'Allow use of where you see X content across the web' and 'Personalize based on your inferred identity'. The second is what stops X linking your account to browsers and devices other than the ones you sign in on.

availableActions.action: Turn off personalised ads for off-X data
availableActions.howTo: Settings and privacy > Privacy and safety > Ads preferences > Personalized ads controls the use of off-X data for advertising. On-platform targeting from your X activity continues regardless.

availableActions.action: Use the device-level ad-tracking controls, which reach what the app settings do not
availableActions.howTo: The notice points to Limit Ad Tracking on iOS 13 and earlier, the Allow apps to request to track setting on iOS 14 and later, and ads personalisation in Android device settings. These act on the advertising ID rather than on X's own toggles.

availableActions.action: Run the industry opt-out tools, per browser
availableActions.howTo: optout.aboutads.info and networkadvertising.org/choices are both named, and Google's Ads Settings separately, because Google is named as an advertising partner. Each opt-out is stored in the browser it was set in, so it must be repeated on every browser and does not survive clearing cookies.

availableActions.action: Repeat every setting in each browser you use, while logged in
availableActions.howTo: The notice states you must be logged in to the browser for account-level web settings to apply, and that logged-out changes affect only that browser's logged-out behaviour.

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of cookies and their purposes
requiredDisclosures.note: Nine categories — authentication and security, functionality, user preferences, analytics, research and development, personalized content, advertising, marketing, and personalization across devices — each with the purposes it serves, plus separate explanations of cookies, pixels and local storage. The per-cookie chart the notice says describes individual cookies is referenced by link and is not part of this captured text, so its contents could not be verified here.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: No prior consent gate, banner or granular acceptance is described for advertising, analytics, marketing or cross-device personalisation. The controls offered are in-product toggles, browser settings and industry opt-out tools, all of which operate after collection has begun, and the notice states that blocking cookies outright may break logging in.

requiredDisclosures.name: Lawful basis for cookie processing
requiredDisclosures.note: No lawful basis is stated for any category, and no distinction is drawn between cookies strictly necessary to deliver the service and the advertising and analytics categories that ordinarily require consent.

requiredDisclosures.name: Equal treatment regardless of jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Off-X browsing history is stated to be not stored or used for users in the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, and stored by default for everyone else. The document discloses the split rather than hiding it, but it is a protection scoped to a regulator's territory rather than to users.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Google is named twice — once as an analytics provider and once as an advertising partner. Everyone else is a category: 'third-party advertising partners', 'ad partners' websites', third parties that have integrated X services. Snap's cookie policy in this corpus names eleven partners individually, so the category-level description is a choice rather than a constraint.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: Partial. The notice states cookie lifespans are capped at 13 months 'in certain areas', which is a qualified commitment rather than a maximum; the privacy policy states the same 13-month figure for cookie-derived data without the qualifier.

requiredDisclosures.name: Version history
requiredDisclosures.note: The document carries no last-updated or effective date and no archive link, unlike X's terms and privacy policy, which both carry effective dates. It says the cookie chart is updated from time to time without saying when this text was.

analyses.summary: eBay's privacy notice is the most institutionally serious in the corpus — Binding Corporate Rules, data protection officers appointed by country, named advertising partners, an actual retention figure of six to ten years in Europe, and a right to object to AI training. It is also the only document here that says out loud it reads your private messages to stop you trading off-platform: every message sent through eBay's tools is received by eBay first, filtered automatically, reviewed by staff when flagged, and may be blocked, expressly to enforce the prohibition on purchases and sales outside eBay. Sellers hand over government ID, selfies, bank account numbers and, with consent, biometric data, and eBay separately obtains records of their previous convictions from government sources. Credit bureau data flows both ways — in for risk modelling and credit limits, out when you pay late. And the advertising split repeats a pattern the corpus has now seen three times: personalised advertising rests on consent in the EEA, Switzerland and the UK, and on legitimate interest for everyone else.

exposures.title: Every message is read, and one purpose is protecting eBay's commission
exposures.whatItMeans: All messages sent through eBay's tools, including chat and emails to eBay alias addresses, are received by eBay first and automatically filtered, with conspicuous ones checked manually by customer service. eBay may block transmission and restrict or block the account. Among the stated purposes, alongside fraud and phishing, is enforcing the prohibition on purchases and sales outside eBay.
exposures.whyItMatters: Filtering for fraud is one thing; the same interception also polices whether two people arrange a deal that would avoid eBay's fees. That is a commercial interest, disclosed in the same sentence as the safety interests, and it applies to every private message between buyer and seller.

reference.label: 11. Filtering of messages sent via our messaging tools
reference.quote: including but not limited to enforcing the prohibition of purchases and sales outside of eBay

exposures.title: Advertising consent depends on where you live
exposures.whatItMeans: Advertising and content personalisation, measurement and analytics on and off eBay's sites is processed with consent for users within the EEA, Switzerland and the United Kingdom, and under legitimate interest for users outside them.
exposures.whyItMatters: The same processing, the same data, a different legal footing decided by residence. It is the third instance of this pattern in the corpus after Uber and LinkedIn, and unlike theirs it is not marked with an asterisk or buried — it is simply two bullets in adjacent subsections. Outside Europe the control is an objection you must raise rather than a consent you must give.

exposures.title: Sellers' criminal records are obtained from government sources
exposures.whatItMeans: In connection with payment services for sellers, eBay collects data from government or other sources concerning any previous convictions of that seller. Sellers also provide government-issued ID including social security number, date of birth, identification documents, selfie photos and bank account numbers, and with consent biometric data for identity verification.
exposures.whyItMatters: Conviction data is a special category almost everywhere, and it is gathered from third parties rather than declared by the person. Combined with biometrics and identity documents, a seller's file here is closer to a financial institution's than a marketplace's — which is what the payments business makes it.

reference.label: 4.4 Personal data from other sources and 5.5

exposures.title: Credit bureau data flows in and your defaults flow out
exposures.whatItMeans: eBay obtains credit reports and checks from credit agencies for identity confirmation, risk modelling and setting credit limits. It also transmits information about payment delays, payment defaults and other irregularities to credit agencies, bureaus and collections agencies where relevant to your credit report.
exposures.whyItMatters: A dispute over an eBay transaction can reach your credit file, which affects borrowing far outside the marketplace. The outbound flow is listed among the recipients rather than presented as a consequence, and no threshold or notice before reporting is stated.

reference.label: 5.2 and 5.4 recipients — Credit agencies, bureaus, or associations

exposures.title: Anyone at your computer can bid, buy and check out
exposures.whatItMeans: The stay-signed-in option lets you or any other user of that computer or browser bid, buy or make an offer, check out or add to cart, purchase with PayPal Faster Checkout if enabled, view My eBay and order details, send member-to-member messages, and conduct after-sale activities including cancelling orders and submitting claims — all without re-entering a password.
exposures.whyItMatters: The list is enumerated frankly, and it includes committing money. Only changing the password, username or other account information triggers re-authentication, so the protected actions are the ones that protect eBay's account integrity rather than the ones that spend your money.

exposures.title: Personal data on a blockchain cannot be erased
exposures.whatItMeans: Certain marketplace features deploy tokens, smart contracts and digital assets to a public blockchain — eBay Authenticity Certificates are given as an example. The notice states that it is not possible to erase data from the blockchain, that blockchain transaction details are immutable, and that neither eBay Inc. nor any affiliate is the controller for activities you conduct via the blockchain or public wallets.
exposures.whyItMatters: The right to erasure set out elsewhere in the same document has a hole in it that no one can close, and responsibility for the data placed there is disclaimed at the same time. Whether a user understood that when requesting an authenticity certificate is a different question.

exposures.title: AI training runs on legitimate interest, opt-out only
exposures.whatItMeans: Where law permits, eBay uses personal data collected from users to train, test, validate and align its own AI models and third-party models, potentially covering any of the data categories it collects, combined with data from external sources. The legal basis is legitimate interest, and the notice grants a right to object.
exposures.whyItMatters: Legitimate interest means the processing happens unless you act, and objecting requires knowing the right exists and finding the link. The mitigation described — filtering, data masking, differential privacy, impact assessments — is more specific than most documents offer, and the right to object is a genuine control that Google, Walmart and Netflix do not provide at all.

reference.label: 12. eBay and AI — AI development and training

exposures.title: You are placed in an advertising segment and told what it looks like
exposures.whatItMeans: Cookie-derived data includes the user segment or category into which you fall, with the worked example 'female, 20-49 years old, interested in sneakers'. Named advertising partners include Google, Meta, Microsoft, Pinterest and TikTok.
exposures.whyItMatters: Segments are inferences about a person that they never supplied and cannot correct at source. The candour is unusual and useful — most documents describe segmentation abstractly — but declining third-party advertising cookies stops personalisation rather than the segmentation itself.

reference.label: 4.3 Personal data we collect in connection with the use of cookies

exposures.title: Your counterparty becomes a data controller over your details
exposures.whatItMeans: On completing a transaction — including one that was cancelled, failed or subsequently invalidated — eBay provides the other user with your name, username, email address, contact information, shipping and billing information or return address. That user then becomes an independent controller of your data, responsible for their own compliance.
exposures.whyItMatters: Your address ends up with a stranger under rules eBay can only recommend, not enforce, and the transfer happens even where the transaction fell through. eBay does prohibit reuse for marketing and tells sellers to honour access and erasure requests, but enforcement is a User Agreement matter after the fact.

reference.label: 11. Your responsibilities over transactional information you receive through eBay

exposures.title: Camera settings travel with the photos you list
exposures.whatItMeans: Among the data collected automatically is certain metadata recording the settings of your camera, included in images of items you upload for sale.
exposures.whyItMatters: Image metadata is a category most people do not know they are sending, and it links listings across accounts and over time by the device that took the pictures. eBay limits the disclosure to camera settings, which is narrower than the location data such metadata often carries.

availableActions.action: Object to AI training
availableActions.howTo: The notice provides a specific right to object to processing for AI development and training, linked from section 12. Because the basis is legitimate interest rather than consent, the training continues until you exercise it.

reference.label: 12. eBay and AI — AI-related individual rights

availableActions.action: Manage advertising preferences on the right page for where you live
availableActions.howTo: Users in the EEA, Switzerland and the UK use the Advertising and related preferences page, where personalisation rests on consent. Everyone else uses the AdChoice page to object. Both are separate from the cookie controls in the User Cookie Notice.

availableActions.action: Do not stay signed in on a shared computer
availableActions.howTo: The notice lists what anyone using that browser can then do without a password, including bidding, checking out and paying with Faster Checkout. Sign out and clear cookies when finished; some browser privacy settings end the session when the browser closes.

availableActions.action: Choose a username that does not identify you
availableActions.howTo: The public username is shown with all public eBay activity — bids, purchases, items for sale, saved interests, sellers and searches, feedback and reviews — and appears in notices sent to other users about suspicious activity. The notice states that a username allowing others to identify you lets them identify your eBay activity.

reference.label: 11. What happens when you share your personal data on our sites

availableActions.action: Contact your country's data protection officer directly
availableActions.howTo: eBay has appointed DPOs in several countries and publishes the list in its Privacy Center. The notice states you may also contact the eBay Privacy Team or your regional controller regardless of whether a DPO exists in your country — the controller for India is eBay Singapore Services Private Limited, for the EU eBay GmbH in Kleinmachnow.

reference.label: 2. Controller and 3. Data protection officer and contact

availableActions.action: Exercise the full rights set, free of charge
availableActions.howTo: Access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, withdrawal of consent, objection to legitimate-interest processing including profiling, and complaint to a supervisory authority — through the Privacy Contact page. The notice confirms these are generally free, with a fee only for manifestly unfounded or repetitive requests, capped at actual cost.

availableActions.action: Withhold precise location and keep general location
availableActions.howTo: Precise mobile location is consent-based and can be disabled per application in device settings. General location from IP address is used for radius search and other location-based features and is not optional.

availableActions.action: Think before requesting an Authenticity Certificate
availableActions.howTo: Blockchain-deployed features carry data that cannot be erased by anyone, and eBay disclaims controllership for activity you conduct on the blockchain or through public wallets. The erasure right does not reach it.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: Rare in this corpus: an actual figure. Retention periods in Europe are stated as generally between six and ten years for contracts, notifications and business letters, with the factors determining variation set out and regional retention guidelines referenced.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: A stated right to object to processing for AI development and training, with the legal basis identified as legitimate interest and the mitigation measures — filtering, data masking, differential privacy, impact assessments — described.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Registered users are notified of material changes via My Messages in My eBay and/or by email, with the effective date posted and the previous version published for comparison.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data protection officer contact
requiredDisclosures.note: DPOs appointed in several countries with a published list, plus the eBay Privacy Team and the responsible regional controller as alternatives regardless of whether a DPO exists locally.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named data controller
