requiredDisclosures.note: Twelve entities named with full addresses, split by region and by whether the service is general or seller payments — eBay Inc. in San Jose, eBay GmbH in Kleinmachnow, eBay S.à r.l. in Luxembourg, eBay Singapore Services for India, and others.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Advertising partners named as Google, Meta, Microsoft, Pinterest and TikTok; shipping companies named by example as DHL and UPS; the VeRO and PROACT programmes identified. Other recipients are given as categories.

requiredDisclosures.name: Lawful basis for processing
requiredDisclosures.note: The most detailed in the corpus: five bases, each with an enumerated purpose list and, for every purpose group, the specific categories of recipients that receive data under it.

requiredDisclosures.name: International transfer safeguards
requiredDisclosures.note: Binding Corporate Rules for intra-group transfers, European Commission standard contractual clauses (2021/914/EU) for others, and the current adequacy list enumerated country by country.

requiredDisclosures.name: Rights over automated decision-making
requiredDisclosures.note: States that no automated decision significantly affecting you will be made unless necessary for a contract, consented to, or legally required, and cross-references the right to object.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data subject rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, consent withdrawal, objection including to profiling, and complaint to a supervisory authority, each described in detail with its statutory limits. Erasure is expressly qualified for data on a blockchain.

requiredDisclosures.name: Biometric data consent
requiredDisclosures.note: Seller biometric processing for identity verification, fraud prevention and KYC is placed under the consent basis rather than legitimate interest.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children's data
requiredDisclosures.note: Services are stated not to be intended for children, no knowing collection from children under applicable national law, and children are not permitted to use the services under the User Agreement.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: Handled through the User Cookie Notice and the regional preferences pages, with the distinction drawn between technically necessary cookies and advertising cookies, and the consequence of declining stated plainly.

requiredDisclosures.name: Equal treatment regardless of jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Advertising personalisation, measurement and analytics rests on consent inside the EEA, Switzerland and the UK and on legitimate interest everywhere else. Storing financial information for future transactions is likewise consent-based only in the EEA.

analyses.summary: Reddit's privacy policy is the strongest in this corpus on the things that are usually vague. It deletes IP addresses after 100 days, does not track precise location, does not require a real name, does not sell to data brokers, and extends the same privacy rights to every user rather than only those in jurisdictions that mandate them. The trade is publicity: your posts are public by construction, appear in search engines and AI chatbot answers, and are licensed in bulk to third parties who pay for access.

exposures.title: Your posts are licensed in bulk to companies training AI
exposures.whatItMeans: Public content is accessible through Reddit's developer services and APIs, and the policy states third parties are required to pay licensing fees for access to larger quantities of content. It also states your content may appear in responses from an AI chatbot such as OpenAI's ChatGPT.
exposures.whyItMatters: Your comments are an asset Reddit sells access to. The policy is unusually direct about this — most platforms describe AI training without naming the commercial arrangement — but naming it does not give you a share or an opt-out.

reference.label: Reddit Is a Public Platform
reference.quote: That content and information may also be available in search results on internet search engines like Google or in responses provided by an AI chatbot like OpenAI’s ChatGPT

exposures.title: Public means permanently public, beyond Reddit's control
exposures.whatItMeans: Posts, comments, username and timestamps can be seen and reshared by anyone, including without permission and where Reddit has no control. Using the Services is stated to be directing Reddit to share this publicly and freely.
exposures.whyItMatters: Deleting a post does not retrieve the copies. The policy is honest that this is structural rather than a setting, which is more than most say.

exposures.title: Age, gender and language are inferred about you
exposures.whatItMeans: Reddit infers attributes such as age range, gender and preferred languages from the information it holds, and collects an interest selection at account creation for recommendations and advertising.
exposures.whyItMatters: Attributes you deliberately did not provide are derived anyway, on a platform whose main privacy proposition is not requiring your real identity.

exposures.title: Advertiser data is matched to you by hashed email
exposures.whatItMeans: Demographic or interest information is received from third parties including advertisers and combined with your Reddit data using a common identifier such as a hash of an email address or a mobile device ID.
exposures.whyItMatters: A hashed email is still a stable identifier for one person, so activity on other services is joined to a pseudonymous Reddit account.

exposures.title: Drafts and private messages are collected
exposures.whatItMeans: Non-public content collected includes saved drafts of posts and comments, private messages, private chats, modmail, and your reports and communications with moderators.
exposures.whyItMatters: A draft you never posted is held, and modmail — often about harassment or account problems — sits in the same collection.

exposures.title: Moderator bots and third-party tools reach your content
exposures.whatItMeans: Moderators access content and information using bots and tools, and third parties access public content through Embeds, APIs and the Developer Platform.
exposures.whyItMatters: The set of parties reading your posts includes volunteers running their own software, which no setting on your account controls.

availableActions.action: Browse without an account, or without a real name
availableActions.howTo: No account is required to read, and an account needs no real name — a username, and either a password, SSO or a phone number. This is a genuine structural choice, not a setting to find.

availableActions.action: Exercise your rights wherever you live
availableActions.howTo: Reddit states anyone can request a copy of their personal data, account deletion, or information about its policies — not only users in jurisdictions that require it.

reference.label: Introduction
reference.quote: All of our users get privacy rights - not just those in select countries.

availableActions.action: Turn off advertiser data matching in User Settings
availableActions.howTo: The policy states you can control how information received from advertisers is used to personalise ads, through the User Settings menu.

availableActions.action: Leave Location Customization off
availableActions.howTo: Reddit does not track precise location; approximate location comes from logs. Location Customization and tagging content with a place are the two ways you would add more.

availableActions.action: Treat drafts as submitted
availableActions.howTo: Saved drafts are collected as non-public content. If you would not post it, do not leave it in a draft.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: A specific, verifiable commitment that is rare in this corpus: IP addresses are deleted after 100 days, except the one used to create the account.

requiredDisclosures.name: Universal data subject rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Access, deletion and policy information are offered to all users regardless of jurisdiction, rather than only where law compels it.

requiredDisclosures.name: No sale to data brokers
requiredDisclosures.note: States personal data is not sold to third parties including data brokers, distinct from the paid licensing of public content it also discloses.

requiredDisclosures.name: Version history
requiredDisclosures.note: Twelve dated prior revisions are published on the page, back to December 2017 — the only document in this corpus that lets a reader see what changed and when.

requiredDisclosures.name: Precise location tracking
requiredDisclosures.note: The policy states plainly that precise location is not tracked; approximate location is derived from logs data.

analyses.summary: Dropbox writes clearly and gives real notice — thirty days before a terms change or a fee rise, a prorated refund if you leave over one, an annual renewal reminder, and an arbitration regime that reimburses your fees under $75,000 and pays a $1,000 bonus if you beat their settlement offer. The exposure is concentrated in two places instead. Liability for a service whose entire purpose is holding your files is capped at the greater of $20 or what you have paid on your current plan, and once Dropbox suspends or terminates access you cannot export your files at all. Dropbox also accesses, stores and scans everything you upload, with that permission extending to affiliates and unnamed trusted third parties. US users are in mandatory individual arbitration unless they opted out within 30 days of registering — and unlike OpenAI, a later version of the terms does not reopen that window.

exposures.title: Liability for your files is capped at twenty dollars
exposures.whatItMeans: Except where the law forbids limiting liability, Dropbox's total liability is the greater of $20 or the amount you have paid under your current service plan. Loss of data, loss of use, business interruption and lost profits are separately excluded outright.
exposures.whyItMatters: The service exists to hold your files, and loss of data is the specific harm excluded by name. A free user's remedy for Dropbox destroying everything they have stored is twenty dollars; a paying user's is one plan's fees.

reference.label: Limitation of Liability
reference.quote: WE LIMIT OUR LIABILITY TO YOU TO THE GREATER OF $20 USD OR 100% OF ANY AMOUNT YOU'VE PAID UNDER YOUR CURRENT SERVICE PLAN WITH DROPBOX

exposures.title: Suspension locks you out of your own files permanently
exposures.whatItMeans: In the ordinary case Dropbox gives advance notice and a chance to export. But where it believes you are in material breach, that export opportunity is removed — and once access is suspended or terminated, the terms state you will not be able to access or export your content, with no refund.
exposures.whyItMatters: Material breach includes any violation of the Acceptable Use Policy, judged by Dropbox on a reasonable-belief standard. For a storage product, losing the ability to retrieve your own files is a more severe outcome than losing the service, and there is no stated appeal or grace period.

reference.label: Termination
reference.quote: Once we suspend or terminate your access to the Services, you will not be able to access or export Your Stuff. Dropbox does not provide refunds if we suspend or terminate your access to the Services, unless required by law.

exposures.title: Everything you upload is scanned, and the permission travels
exposures.whatItMeans: To deliver previews, search, OCR, thumbnails and personalisation, Dropbox accesses, stores and scans your files, and you grant that permission not only to Dropbox but to its affiliates and to trusted third parties it works with.
exposures.whyItMatters: The scanning covers document contents, not metadata — OCR reads text out of images and scans. 'Trusted third parties' is not defined or enumerated in these terms, so the set of parties permitted to process your files is determined by Dropbox after you agree.

reference.label: Your Stuff & Your Permissions
reference.quote: To provide these and other features, Dropbox accesses, stores, and scans Your Stuff. You give us permission to do those things, and this permission extends to our affiliates and trusted third parties we work with.

exposures.title: Arbitration for US users, and the opt-out never reopens
exposures.whatItMeans: US residents must arbitrate individually before a single arbitrator, with class actions, class arbitrations, consolidation and private attorney general actions all barred. The opt-out is a form submitted within 30 days of first registering, and the terms state that a choice made under a previous version remains binding.
exposures.whyItMatters: The window runs from registration, so for anyone already a user it has closed and cannot be reopened by a later version of the terms. This is the same posture DoorDash takes and the opposite of OpenAI's, which reopens on every update — the corpus now has both ends of that spectrum and Dropbox at the closed end.

reference.label: Resolving Disputes — Opt out of Agreement to Arbitrate
reference.quote: if you agreed to a previous version of these Terms that allowed you to opt out of arbitration, your previous choice to opt out or not opt out remains binding

exposures.title: Your employer's admin controls the account you may have started yourself
exposures.whatItMeans: If you join a Dropbox Team, administrators may access, disclose, restrict or remove information in your account and may restrict or terminate your access. If you converted an existing personal account into a team account, administrators may prevent you from later disassociating it.
exposures.whyItMatters: A personal account converted into a team account can carry years of personal files into an employer's control, and the terms say the administrator may block you from separating it again. Signing up with a work email address alone can trigger the organisation's ability to block your use until you convert.

reference.label: Dropbox Teams — Using Dropbox Teams
reference.quote: If you convert an existing Dropbox account into part of a Dropbox Team, your administrators may prevent you from later disassociating your account from the Dropbox Team.

exposures.title: A free account is deleted after twelve months of not logging in
exposures.whatItMeans: Dropbox reserves the right to suspend or terminate access where you do not have a Paid Account and have not accessed the service for 12 consecutive months. Advance notice by email and an export opportunity apply in this case.
exposures.whyItMatters: Free storage is often used as long-term backup — the use that involves not logging in. The notice goes to the email address on the account, which is the address most likely to be stale for a dormant account.

exposures.title: Free features can disappear without notice
exposures.whatItMeans: Features added at no additional charge to enhance the storage service may be withdrawn without further notice, in contrast to the 30-day notice that governs fee and terms changes.
exposures.whyItMatters: The generous notice provisions elsewhere in these terms do not reach the functionality itself. A workflow built on a free feature can stop working the day Dropbox decides to remove it.

reference.label: Additional Features
reference.quote: these free features may be withdrawn without further notice

exposures.title: Using a beta feature puts you under a confidentiality obligation
exposures.whatItMeans: Beta, alpha, preview, early access and evaluation services are confidential until official launch, and by using them you agree not to disclose any information about them to anyone without Dropbox's permission. Using them also means agreeing Dropbox may contact you for feedback.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is a one-way confidentiality duty imposed on a consumer by clicking into a feature, with no time limit stated and no carve-out for ordinary discussion or public complaint about a product you are using.

reference.label: Beta Services
reference.quote: Beta Services are confidential until official launch. If you use any Beta Services, you agree not to disclose any information about those Services to anyone else without our permission.

exposures.title: Refunds exist only where a law compels them
exposures.whatItMeans: Paid accounts can be cancelled at any time, but refunds are issued only if required by law. The EU's 14-day cancellation right is named as the example; users elsewhere are left with the default of no refund.
exposures.whyItMatters: Cancelling a just-renewed annual plan recovers nothing outside the jurisdictions that mandate it, and renewal is automatic. The annual renewal reminder email is what makes this manageable.

exposures.title: Suggestions you make carry no obligation back to you
exposures.whatItMeans: Dropbox states it welcomes feedback but may use comments or suggestions without any obligation to you.
exposures.whyItMatters: The mildest version of a clause the corpus has now seen six times. Unlike Paytm's irrevocable assignment or the HDFC and Amex formulations, this claims no ownership and waives no moral rights — it disclaims obligation rather than taking title.

availableActions.action: Opt out of arbitration within 30 days of registering
availableActions.howTo: Submit the opt-out form linked from the 'Opt out of Agreement to Arbitrate' paragraph. This only works within 30 days of first registering your account or agreeing to the Terms, and the terms state a choice made under an earlier version stays binding — so a later update will not give you a fresh window.

deadline.description: 30 days from first registering the account or agreeing to these Terms. Expressly not reopened by later versions of the terms.

reference.label: Resolving Disputes — Opt out of Agreement to Arbitrate

availableActions.action: Export your files before any dispute escalates
availableActions.howTo: Keep an independent copy. Export is available while your account is in good standing, and Dropbox commits to notice and an export window in the ordinary case — but not where it believes you are in material breach, and not at all once access is suspended.

availableActions.action: Use the 30-day window when terms or fees change
availableActions.howTo: Dropbox notifies by email or in-product notification before the effective date, and updates take effect no less than 30 days after. Cancel before that date and, where applicable, Dropbox states it will offer a prorated refund of prepaid amounts.

deadline.description: Updated terms take effect no less than 30 days after notice; fee changes on renewal carry no less than 30 days' advance notice by email.

availableActions.action: Send a Notice of Dispute and use the fee-shifting
availableActions.howTo: Email dispute-notice@dropbox.com with your name, a description of the dispute and the relief you seek. This is required before a formal proceeding, and doing it in time is the condition for Dropbox reimbursing arbitration filing fees on non-frivolous claims under $75,000. If your award beats Dropbox's offer, the terms promise $1,000 on top.

reference.label: Resolving Disputes — Arbitration Fees and Incentives

availableActions.action: Use small claims court instead
availableActions.howTo: Either party may bring qualifying claims in small claims court in San Francisco or any US county where you live or work, without arbitrating first.

availableActions.action: Keep a personal account off your work email
availableActions.howTo: Signing up with an organisation-provisioned email address lets that organisation block your use until you move to a team account. Converting an existing account into a team may then be irreversible without administrator consent.

availableActions.action: In the EU, claim the 14-day refund
availableActions.howTo: EU users may cancel and obtain a refund within 14 days of signing up for, upgrading to, or renewing a paid account, through the link in the Cancellation paragraph.

deadline.description: 14 days from signup, upgrade or renewal, for EU residents.

availableActions.action: Log in to a free account at least once a year
availableActions.howTo: Twelve consecutive months without access is a stated ground for terminating a free account. If you use Dropbox as long-term backup, a single sign-in resets that clock.

deadline.description: 12 consecutive months without accessing the Services is a ground for termination of a non-paid account.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Email or in-product notification before the effective date, with updates effective no less than 30 days after notice, and a prorated refund offered where applicable if you cancel instead.

requiredDisclosures.name: Advance notice of fee changes
requiredDisclosures.note: No less than 30 days' advance notice by email of renewal fee changes, with an opportunity to cancel before the new fee applies.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automatic renewal disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: Billing recurs from conversion to a paid account until cancellation, and annual plans receive a reminder email a reasonable period before the renewal date.

requiredDisclosures.name: Arbitration opt-out right
requiredDisclosures.note: Disclosed with its limits stated plainly: 30 days from first registration, by form, and expressly not reopened by agreeing to a later version of the terms.

requiredDisclosures.name: Pre-arbitration dispute procedure
requiredDisclosures.note: Written Notice of Dispute to dispute-notice@dropbox.com, with a 60-day informal resolution period before either side may bring a formal proceeding. The EU online dispute resolution platform is also linked.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: California law and the courts of San Francisco County, expressly subject to local consumer-forum rights in the EU and elsewhere, with a North Carolina carve-out for Template claims.

requiredDisclosures.name: Designated DMCA agent
requiredDisclosures.note: Copyright Agent, Dropbox, Inc., 1800 Owens St, San Francisco, CA 94158, copyright@dropbox.com, alongside a Copyright Complaint Form.

requiredDisclosures.name: Repeat infringer policy
requiredDisclosures.note: Dropbox reserves the right to delete or disable allegedly infringing content and to terminate accounts of repeat infringers.

requiredDisclosures.name: Minimum age
requiredDisclosures.note: 13 in the United States, 16 elsewhere, rising to whatever higher age local law requires for processing without parental consent.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer rights preservation
requiredDisclosures.note: Repeatedly and specifically: EU statutory warranties, non-waivable consumer rights, liability for fraud, local consumer forums, and mandatory local cancellation laws are each carved out of the corresponding limitation.

requiredDisclosures.name: Limitation on indemnity
requiredDisclosures.note: These terms impose no user indemnity obligation at all, which is unusual for a SaaS agreement in this corpus.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No retention period appears in the terms. Deletion is addressed only through termination, where the stated outcome is that you can no longer access or export your files.

analyses.summary: This is Robinhood's statement for website visitors, and it says outright that it does not cover people who apply for or hold Robinhood's financial products — so the document a customer needs is a different one. Within its own scope it discloses two things worth knowing: it collects information about you from other people's contact lists, and it shares identifiers and browsing activity with advertising partners and social networks in a way state law classifies as a sale.

exposures.title: This document does not cover you if you are a customer
exposures.whatItMeans: The statement excludes information collected about individuals who apply for or obtain Robinhood's financial products for personal, family or household purposes, and excludes Robinhood Social users and Sherwood Media.
exposures.whyItMatters: It is the privacy document reachable from the site, and it is the wrong one for anyone with an account. The rules governing a brokerage customer's data live in a separate User Privacy Statement that this one only links to.

reference.label: Robinhood Markets US Web Visitor Privacy Statement
reference.quote: This Privacy Statement does not apply to information that we collect about individuals who apply for or obtain our financial products and services for personal, family, or household purposes

exposures.title: You are profiled from other people's contact lists
exposures.whatItMeans: If you appear in another user's contacts and that user shares the list, Robinhood collects your contact information and your association with that user.
exposures.whyItMatters: This builds a record about people who never visited the site, never agreed to anything, and have no way to know the record exists. It is the clearest shadow-profile disclosure in this corpus.

reference.label: Information We Collect from Other Sources
reference.quote: If you are in another user’s contact list and they choose to disclose that list with us, then we will collect the contact information and your association with that user.

exposures.title: Your data is shared with social networks in a way the law calls a sale
exposures.whatItMeans: The state-rights table discloses that identifiers, internet activity information and inferences have been 'sold' or 'shared' with advertising and marketing partners and social networks in the past twelve months.
exposures.whyItMatters: A brokerage passing behavioural data to social networks connects your interest in financial products to your social identity, and the disclosure is a legal admission rather than a hypothetical.

exposures.title: Fraud-risk inferences are bought from outside firms
exposures.whatItMeans: Information obtained from vendors includes inferences about your preferences and attributes, and inferred fraud risk, from identity verification and fraud prevention partners.
exposures.whyItMatters: A third party's judgement about your fraud risk enters Robinhood's record about you, and the statement gives no way to see, correct or contest that inference specifically.

exposures.title: The opt-out lives in your browser and quietly expires
exposures.whatItMeans: Opting out of targeted advertising, sharing and sales works through a browser signal such as Global Privacy Control, and must be renewed on a new device, a new browser, or after clearing cookies. Do Not Track is not honoured.
exposures.whyItMatters: The refusal is stored in the same place as the tracking it refuses, so the act of clearing tracking data also clears the opt-out — and nothing tells you it has lapsed.

reference.label: EXERCISING YOUR RIGHTS
reference.quote: You will need to renew your opt-out choice if you visit our website from a new device or browser or if you clear your cookies because your opt-out choice will be linked to your browser only.

exposures.title: No retention period is stated
exposures.whatItMeans: Retention is described as based on business needs and legal requirements, for as long as necessary for the purposes described.
exposures.whyItMatters: Purpose-bounded retention with no stated maximum means the period is whatever the company decides, and there is no figure you could hold it to.

availableActions.action: Read the User Privacy Statement instead if you have an account
availableActions.howTo: This statement links the Robinhood US User Privacy Statement, which is the document that actually governs customer data. Do not rely on this one for your account.

reference.label: Robinhood Markets US Web Visitor Privacy Statement

availableActions.action: Enable Global Privacy Control in your browser
availableActions.howTo: Robinhood states it acts on GPC as a legally recognised opt-out signal for targeted advertising, sharing and sales. It does not act on Do Not Track.

availableActions.action: Email privacy@robinhood.com to access, correct or delete
availableActions.howTo: State privacy rights — confirm, access, correct, delete, and appeal a refusal — are exercised by email. An authorised agent can act for you with proof.

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of personal information sold or shared
requiredDisclosures.note: A table names the categories and the recipient categories — advertising and marketing partners, social networks — for the past twelve months.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: Offered via Global Privacy Control, with an email route for access, correction and deletion, and an appeal route if a request is refused.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children under 13
requiredDisclosures.note: States it does not knowingly collect from under-13s and gives a contact for suspected cases; also states no knowing sale or share for under-16s.

requiredDisclosures.name: GLBA consumer privacy notice
requiredDisclosures.note: This statement expressly excludes customers of the financial products. The GLBA notice obligation attaches to the separate User Privacy Statement, which is not this document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period or criteria beyond 'business needs and legal requirements' is given for any category.

analyses.summary: Coinbase publishes the most rigorous privacy disclosure in this corpus: a legal basis stated for every processing purpose, named regulators, a published DPO address, a rights dashboard, and an explicit commitment not to retain the contacts of friends you invite. The collection itself is correspondingly deep — biometrics from identity selfies, social security number, wealth verification, tax residency in every jurisdiction, and your spouse's name and tax identification number.

exposures.title: Your spouse's tax identification number is collected
exposures.whatItMeans: Supplemental identification information includes spouse name and spouse tax identification number, alongside your own social security or social insurance number, passport or licence, utility bills, visa information, employment and salary details.
exposures.whyItMatters: Your spouse is not the customer, did not agree to this policy, and has no account through which to exercise any of the rights it describes — yet their government tax identifier is held.

exposures.title: Biometric data is generated from your verification selfie
exposures.whatItMeans: Electronic identification information consists of biometric information generated from photos or videos you provide, and the verification process compares your selfie against your submitted identity documents.
exposures.whyItMatters: A faceprint is permanent in a way a password is not. The purpose — anti-money-laundering verification — is legitimate and legally required, but no separate retention period or deletion route for the biometric data appears.

exposures.title: Your full financial position is on file
exposures.whatItMeans: Financial information includes bank account number, payment card number, trading and investment experience, tax identification number for every tax residency, all countries of tax residence, and income, net assets or wealth verification statements.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is a complete financial profile in one place, and the policy states that if you do not provide what the law requires, the account will be closed — so it is not optional.

exposures.title: Automated systems decide about your account
exposures.whatItMeans: Automated decision-making is used to verify accounts and their activities, detect suspicious or fraudulent behaviour, and prevent account takeovers, drawing on identification, financial, transaction and usage data.
exposures.whyItMatters: An automated system can freeze or restrict access to your funds. The policy discloses the practice and points to the rights section, but describes no dedicated route to contest a specific automated outcome.

reference.label: To promote the safety, security and integrity of our Services

exposures.title: You are screened against public databases and the blockchain
exposures.whatItMeans: Information is obtained from public databases including the United Nations Sanctions List, the US ITA Consolidated Screening List and SEC EDGAR, and public blockchain data is analysed — timestamps, transaction IDs, digital signatures, amounts and wallet addresses.
exposures.whyItMatters: Blockchain analysis links your verified real-world identity to on-chain activity that is otherwise pseudonymous, and that association is durable.

exposures.title: Analytics data is collected before you have an account
exposures.whatItMeans: Analytics providers supply information about your usage, interactions, age group and survey responses — in some cases prior to account creation. Marketing partners supply your name, contact details and what you did on and off Coinbase's own sites.
exposures.whyItMatters: The profile begins before you sign up, and is assembled partly from what other companies observed about you.

exposures.title: Some communications cannot be declined
exposures.whatItMeans: Critical service communications sent for legal or security purposes cannot be opted out of, by email or mobile notification.
exposures.whyItMatters: Reasonable for a regulated financial service, but it means the contact details you supply remain a permanent channel for as long as the account exists.

availableActions.action: Use the Privacy Rights Dashboard
availableActions.howTo: Access and deletion requests are self-service through a dedicated dashboard rather than an email queue — one of the few in this corpus that is a tool rather than a request form.

availableActions.action: Contact the DPO directly
availableActions.howTo: dpo@coinbase.com is published in the policy itself, alongside the support portal.

reference.label: 10. How to Contact Us With Questions

availableActions.action: In the EEA or UK, object to legitimate-interest processing
availableActions.howTo: Customisation, marketing and promotional processing all rely on legitimate interests, and the policy states you have the right to object to and seek restriction of that processing.

reference.label: Data use for our Legitimate Interests

availableActions.action: Invite friends without worrying about their data
availableActions.howTo: Referral information — your contacts' phone numbers or email addresses — is collected to send the invitation and expressly not retained. This is stated twice in the policy.

availableActions.action: Consider whether you need to nominate a trusted contact
availableActions.howTo: Nominating a guardian or trusted contact means their email address is collected too. It is optional and worth a deliberate decision rather than a default.

requiredDisclosures.name: Lawful basis for processing
requiredDisclosures.note: The strongest in this corpus: contract, legal obligation and legitimate interests are each named per purpose, with the specific interest relied on and jurisdiction-specific carve-outs for Brazil, Australia and Singapore.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data protection officer contact
requiredDisclosures.note: dpo@coinbase.com published in the policy body.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named regulators and legal bases for disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: Names the CFTC, SEC, NFA, FINTRAC, Central Bank of Ireland, FCA, BaFin, MAS, CySEC and ASIC, plus the specific statutes under which disclosure may be compelled.

requiredDisclosures.name: Non-retention of referral contacts
requiredDisclosures.note: A direct counter-example to the shadow-profile pattern found elsewhere in this corpus: contacts collected to send an invitation are expressly not retained.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automated decision-making rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Automated decision-making affecting account access is disclosed, but no route to obtain human review or contest a specific outcome is described.

requiredDisclosures.name: Biometric data retention
requiredDisclosures.note: Biometric information generated from verification photos is disclosed with a security commitment, but no retention period or deletion route specific to it appears.

analyses.summary: eBay's cookie notice is unusually candid and unusually stale. It says outright that these technologies exist to track your behaviour and identify you across devices, names Meta and Google as the partners with their full legal entities and addresses, discloses that data goes to Meta both through the pixel and server-to-server, and gives a real retention figure — Google Analytics data deleted after 14 months. It also describes device fingerprinting, and notes that such techniques work without local storage and are not fully managed by your browser, which is the only control it offers most readers. That is the split: users in the EEA, Switzerland and the UK get a consent settings page with withdrawal at any time, and everyone else gets an advertising preferences page that adjusts how eBay activity is used, not whether third-party partners may set cookies. It was last updated on 23 February 2022, three document generations behind the User Privacy Notice it says it must be read with.

exposures.title: Consent exists in Europe; everyone else gets a preference toggle
exposures.whatItMeans: Users in the EEA, Switzerland and the UK are sent to a dedicated settings page to decide whether they consent to third-party advertising, personalisation, measurement and analytics cookies, with withdrawal at any time. All other users are sent to the AdChoice advertising preferences page, which adjusts whether eBay activity is used for customised advertising. The notice is explicit that the choices depend on the purposes and, in practice, on where you live.
exposures.whyItMatters: A consent gate decides whether the data is collected; a preference page decides what is done with data already collected. eBay's privacy notice already splits advertising between consent inside Europe and legitimate interest outside it, and this document is where that split becomes a concrete difference in the interface a user is given.

reference.label: Your options at a glance
reference.quote: to determine whether you consent to the use of cookies and similar technologies by our third-party partners

exposures.title: Device fingerprinting, and it escapes the control the notice offers
exposures.whatItMeans: Among the similar technologies described are ones that function without local storage on your device and instead use browser functions to create a fingerprint of your system serving as a unique identifier. The notice adds that these may work across all your browsers and in some cases are not fully managed by your browser, needing to be managed from installed applications or the device itself.
exposures.whyItMatters: Every control this document offers non-European users — clearing cookies, browser settings, opt-out cookies — operates on stored files. A fingerprint is derived rather than stored, so it survives all of them, and the notice says so without offering any alternative route to switch it off.

reference.label: 1.1 Similar technologies
reference.quote: These technologies may function across all your browsers and in some cases are not fully managed by your browser

exposures.title: The stated purpose is identifying you across devices
exposures.whatItMeans: The notice states in plain terms that in general these technologies enable eBay to track your user behaviour and identify you, even across devices. Google Signals is then described as extending that to devices linked to your Google account, and Google Analytics in Universal Analytics mode as assigning sessions and interactions across multiple devices to a pseudonymous user ID.
exposures.whyItMatters: Cross-device identification joins a work laptop, a home tablet and a phone into one person, which is the step that turns browsing into a profile. The candour is genuinely better than most documents here; the practice is still the most consequential thing in it.

reference.label: 1.2 Why do we use these technologies?
reference.quote: these technologies enable us to track your user behavior and identify you

exposures.title: Data goes to Meta server-to-server, and Meta then answers for it alone
exposures.whatItMeans: eBay transmits information about your use of its services, including additional personal data, through the Meta Pixel and by sending data directly to Meta from its own servers. Where eBay and Meta are joint controllers for ad targeting and measurement, Meta subsequently processes the data as an independent controller and assumes exclusive responsibility, and it is Meta's job to honour your rights over what Meta holds.
exposures.whyItMatters: Server-to-server transmission is invisible to ad blockers and browser controls in a way a pixel is not. And the joint-control arrangement means the company you have a relationship with hands responsibility for your data to one you may not, with the remedy relocated to Meta's own opt-out settings.

reference.label: 2.1 Meta
reference.quote: Meta will subsequently process the data as an independent controller and assumes exclusive responsibility.

exposures.title: reCAPTCHA reads your mouse movements before you do anything
exposures.whatItMeans: Google reCAPTCHA analyses user behaviour to distinguish humans from bots, evaluating IP address, the duration of the visit and mouse movements. The analysis begins automatically as soon as the user connects to the online service, runs entirely in the background, and the data collected is forwarded to Google.
exposures.whyItMatters: This starts on page load, not when you submit a form, and there is no control offered for it anywhere in the notice — not in the European consent page, which covers advertising and analytics, and not in AdChoice. Mouse movement is behavioural, which makes it identifying in the same way typing rhythm is.

reference.label: Google reCAPTCHA: Prevention of automated access
reference.quote: duration of the user's visit to the online service or the user's mouse movements

exposures.title: Necessary cookies cannot be refused, and refusing the rest breaks the cart
exposures.whatItMeans: Operationally necessary cookies are stated to be unrefusable. Analytics cookies are first-party and the only route offered for them is browser settings, which must be configured separately for every browser, and which the notice warns will stop you using services such as adding an item to the cart and will make you enter your password more often.
exposures.whyItMatters: The one category with no in-product control is analytics, and the fallback for it is the setting that also disables the shop. It is the pattern Amazon's cookie notice shows too: the control that exists is the one that removes the service rather than the tracking.

reference.label: 3.1 Technologies which are necessary for the provision of our Services
reference.quote: Because these cookies are necessary to deliver our Services to you, you cannot refuse them.

exposures.title: Clearing cookies deletes the opt-outs you set
exposures.whatItMeans: The notice states that deleting all cookies on your device also deletes any opt-out cookies already set, so every opt-out already declared must be declared again.
exposures.whyItMatters: Clearing cookies is the standard privacy hygiene advice, and here it reverses the privacy choices you made. The document is honest about it and offers no mechanism that survives, so the opt-out is only as durable as the least privacy-conscious thing you do to your browser.

reference.label: 3.2 Technologies which are used for advertising
reference.quote: If you delete all cookies on your device, any opt-out cookies that have already been set will also be deleted

exposures.title: Four years old, and the documents it must be read with are not
exposures.whatItMeans: The notice states it was updated on 23 February 2022 and that it must be read in conjunction with the User Privacy Notice. On the same captured page, the User Privacy Notice is dated 21 April 2025 and the User Agreement 28 June 2026.
exposures.whyItMatters: A cookie notice describes which third parties receive data through which technologies, and that changes with every advertising vendor a company adds. Four years without a revision either means nothing changed across three generations of the surrounding documents, or means the notice no longer describes what runs on the page.

reference.label: Cookie Notice header
reference.quote: This Cookie Notice was updated on February 23, 2022.

availableActions.action: In the EEA, Switzerland or the UK, refuse third-party cookies outright
availableActions.howTo: Use the dedicated settings page linked at the top of the notice to decide whether third-party partners may use cookies for advertising, personalisation, measurement and analytics. Consent can be withdrawn at any time with effect for the future, through the same page.

reference.label: Your options at a glance — Users in the EEA, Switzerland and the UK

availableActions.action: Everywhere else, set AdChoice and then the industry opt-outs
availableActions.howTo: AdChoice, at the eBay Advertising Preferences page or via the link in any eBay advertisement, controls whether your eBay activity is used for customised advertising. That is not a cookie consent, so follow it with youronlinechoices.com, aboutads.info/choices and networkadvertising.org/choices, each of which the notice links.

reference.label: 3.2 Technologies which are used for advertising — All other users

availableActions.action: Install the Google Analytics opt-out add-on
availableActions.howTo: The notice links Google's browser plugin, which stops collection of your use of the services including your IP address, and separately disables Google Signals cross-device tracking. Turning off personalised ads in your Google account settings closes the other half.

availableActions.action: Opt out of the Meta Pixel inside Meta, not inside eBay
availableActions.howTo: eBay directs you to log into your Meta account and change your privacy or advertising settings per Meta's opt-out instructions. Because Meta acts as an independent controller for the targeting data, this is the only place the choice can be made.

availableActions.action: Block third-party cookies rather than all cookies
availableActions.howTo: The notice links per-browser instructions for Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Internet Explorer and Safari and warns that deactivating cookies stops functions such as adding items to the cart. Blocking third-party cookies only keeps the cart working while cutting the advertising vendors.

reference.label: 3.1 Technologies which are necessary for the provision of our Services
reference.quote: The settings must be made separately for each browser you use.

availableActions.action: Redo your opt-outs after any cookie clear
availableActions.howTo: Opt-out choices are themselves stored in cookies. After clearing browser data, changing device or switching browser, set AdChoice and the industry opt-outs again. There is no account-level equivalent for these in this document.

reference.label: 3.2 Technologies which are used for advertising

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: Present for the EEA, Switzerland and the UK: a dedicated settings page for third-party advertising, personalisation, measurement and analytics cookies, with withdrawal at any time with effect for the future, and the consequence of declining stated plainly. It exists for that region only — everywhere else the notice offers the AdChoice preferences page, which governs use of eBay activity rather than whether cookies are set.

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of cookies and their purposes
requiredDisclosures.note: Cookies, web beacons, SDKs and similar technologies are each defined; session versus persistent and first- versus third-party are distinguished; and four purposes plus four functional categories are given — operationally necessary, analytics, advertising and social media. What is missing is the table most cookie notices of this length carry: no individual cookie is named and no individual duration is given.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Unusually good for a cookie notice. Meta and Google are each named with the correct legal entity and registered address for the reader's region — Meta Platforms Ireland Ltd, Block J, Serpentine Avenue, Dublin 4 and Meta Platforms Inc., 1601 Willow Road, Menlo Park; Google Ireland Ltd, Gordon House, Barrow Street, Dublin 4 and Google LLC, 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway. The specific products are identified too: Meta Pixel, Google Ad Manager, Google Ads, Google Analytics, Google Signals and reCAPTCHA.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: Partially, and rare for a cookie notice: Google Analytics data is automatically deleted after 14 months, with data reaching that age purged monthly. No period is given for eBay's own first-party cookies or for the advertising cookies, so the one figure covers the processor rather than the controller.

requiredDisclosures.name: International transfer safeguards
requiredDisclosures.note: Described in operational rather than legal terms: IP addresses are shortened on a Google server in the EEA before being sent to Google servers in the USA, so what crosses is already truncated, and the transmitted IP is not combined with other Google data. The Meta arrangement cites the Meta Data Processing Terms and the Meta European Data Transfer Addendum by name. No standard contractual clauses or adequacy decision is cited directly.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named data controller
requiredDisclosures.note: The joint controllership with Meta is set out with unusual precision — when eBay is sole controller and Meta a processor, when the two are joint controllers, that a joint control agreement exists, and that under it Meta is responsible for safeguarding data subject rights over data Meta holds while eBay is responsible for providing this information.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Track response disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: The CalOPPA disclosure of how the business responds to browser Do Not Track signals. eBay states it does not respond to them, citing the absence of an industry or legal standard, in identical wording to its California privacy notice.

requiredDisclosures.name: Lawful basis for cookie processing
requiredDisclosures.note: No legal basis is stated for any category. Operationally necessary cookies are asserted to be unrefusable without identifying the ground, analytics cookies are set as first-party with no basis given, and outside Europe the notice never says on what footing third-party advertising cookies are set — eBay's User Privacy Notice answers that with legitimate interest, and this document does not.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: No change mechanism of any kind. The document carries a single 'updated on February 23, 2022' line, no version history, no notification commitment, and no effective date for anything since. eBay's User Privacy Notice, dated April 2025, does commit to notifying registered users and publishing the prior version.

requiredDisclosures.name: Granular consent control for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: Even in the European settings page, the choice described is a single decision covering advertising, content personalisation, measurement and analytics together. Nothing in the notice offers separate control per purpose or per vendor, and the reCAPTCHA collection that begins on page load has no control at all in any region.

analyses.summary: JioHotstar's privacy notice ties your data rights to your money. Asking for erasure terminates your subscription with no refund, and if you object to personalised advertising and no preference toggle exists, the notice tells you to stop using the platform and have your subscription cancelled. Marketing profiles built from your watch history are retained not for as long as needed but for the maximum period the law allows.

exposures.title: Erasing your data cancels your subscription and you get no refund
exposures.whatItMeans: Requesting erasure of your personal information closes your account, and the notice states this results in your subscription being terminated without any refunds.
exposures.whyItMatters: A data-protection right is priced: exercising it forfeits money you have already paid. That converts a legal entitlement into a paid choice, and it is the only instance of this in the corpus.

reference.label: 7.6 Data Retention and Erasure
reference.quote: Erasure of your information from the Platform will result in your subscription being terminated without any refunds.

exposures.title: Marketing profiles are kept for the maximum period the law allows
exposures.whatItMeans: Data collected to build an advertising profile — your watch history and platform activity — and the phone number used for direct marketing are both retained for the maximum period permitted by law in your territory.
exposures.whyItMatters: Retention is normally framed as the minimum needed for a purpose. Framing it as the legal maximum inverts that, and it applies specifically to the advertising profile rather than to records the company must keep.

exposures.title: Objecting to personalised advertising means leaving
exposures.whatItMeans: If you want processing for personalised content or interest-based advertising stopped and the platform does not offer a preference for it, the notice says you should cease using the platform and it can arrange to cancel your subscription.
exposures.whyItMatters: The stated remedy for exercising a right to object is to stop being a customer. Combined with the no-refund erasure clause, both routes out cost money.

exposures.title: A failed location lookup falls back to your last known position
exposures.whatItMeans: Location is derived from your SIM card and IP address, and with permission from GPS. If IP detection fails, the notice states the last cached location is collected as your current location.
exposures.whyItMatters: You are assigned a location you are not actually at, and it enters the same profile used for content and advertising decisions.

reference.label: 3.2 Information we collect automatically
reference.quote: In the event IP detection fails, we will collect the last cached location as your current location

exposures.title: Social login hands over your friends' information too
exposures.whatItMeans: Linking or logging in through Facebook, Twitter, Instagram or Google may send JioHotstar your profile and social information including your friend list and your friends' social information.
exposures.whyItMatters: One convenience click discloses data about people who are not customers and never made a choice about this platform.

reference.label: 3.4. Information we collect through third party sources

exposures.title: Which apps you use, and your support calls, are collected
exposures.whatItMeans: With permission, information about the applications you frequently use on your device is collected. Customer support interactions include chat transcripts and call recordings.
exposures.whyItMatters: Your installed and frequently used apps describe far more about you than viewing habits do, and it is collected by a streaming service for purposes the notice does not separately justify.

exposures.title: Consenting to the notice consents to worldwide transfers
exposures.whatItMeans: By consenting to the notice you consent to transfer of your personal information to affiliated companies, group companies, service providers or third-party recipients in locations around the world.
exposures.whyItMatters: No destination or safeguard is named beyond 'reasonable steps', and the consent is bundled into acceptance of the notice as a whole.

availableActions.action: Use the in-app advertising preference before considering erasure
availableActions.howTo: The notice describes interest-based advertising controls and consent withdrawal through in-app or device preferences. Exhaust those first — the escalation path it offers instead is cancelling your subscription.

availableActions.action: Withdraw location and microphone permission at the device level
availableActions.howTo: GPS location and microphone consent can be revoked from your device settings at any time, without contacting the company.

reference.label: 7.7 Withdrawing Consent and Restriction of Processing

availableActions.action: Do not use social login
availableActions.howTo: Registering with an email address instead of Facebook, Twitter, Instagram or Google keeps your friend list and your friends' information out of the platform entirely.

reference.label: 3.4. Information we collect through third party sources

availableActions.action: If you subscribed through Apple, cancel there separately
availableActions.howTo: The notice states that erasure or objection on the platform does not stop Apple billing you. Unsubscribing and requesting erasure on iTunes are separate processes you must complete yourself.

availableActions.action: Request access and portability before erasing
availableActions.howTo: Data access and portability are offered as separate rights that do not close the account. Use them first, since erasure ends the subscription without refund.

requiredDisclosures.name: Payment data handling
requiredDisclosures.note: States card details are held by payment processors and never stored or processed by JioStar, which is a stronger position than most peers here take.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data subject rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Rectification, access, portability, erasure, consent withdrawal and objection are each described with a route — though erasure and objection carry the subscription consequences above.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: India's IT Rules require a named grievance officer with contact details. The notice gives only a generic address, hello@jiohotstar.com, with no name, designation or resolution timeline.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period is stated. For advertising profiles the stated standard is the maximum the law allows, which is a ceiling rather than a limit, and data is anonymised rather than deleted at the end.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children's data
requiredDisclosures.note: Under-18s may not register, verified parental consent is required, and a Kids mode is provided — though the notice also permits under-18 use under guardian supervision.

analyses.summary: LinkedIn's copyright policy sets out the DMCA notice and counter-notice process. Two things in it cost the user rather than the platform: filing a complaint discloses your contact details to the person you are complaining about, and contesting a wrongful takedown requires consenting to a United States federal court — the Northern District of California if you live anywhere outside the US. It has been effective since March 2014.

exposures.title: Your contact details are forwarded to the person you report
exposures.whatItMeans: When you file a copyright complaint, LinkedIn may pass your written notice — including your contact information — to the member who posted the content.
exposures.whyItMatters: Reporting infringement is not anonymous. The notice form requires your mailing address and phone or email, and those can reach the party you are in dispute with.

reference.label: Complaints regarding content posted on the LinkedIn website
reference.quote: LinkedIn may make a good faith attempt to forward the written notification, including the complainant’s contact information, to the Member who posted the content

exposures.title: Contesting a takedown means consenting to a US court
exposures.whatItMeans: A counter-notice requires you to consent to the jurisdiction of a US federal district court — the Northern District of California if your address is outside the United States — and to accept service of process from the complainant.
exposures.whyItMatters: For a user outside the US, recovering wrongly removed content requires accepting litigation in California. That is a far higher price than the takedown itself, and it is the only route the policy offers.

reference.label: Counter-Notice
reference.quote: you consent to the jurisdiction of the Federal District court ... located in the Northern District of California (Santa Clara County), if your address is located outside the United States

exposures.title: Both notice and counter-notice carry personal legal liability
exposures.whatItMeans: Every notice and counter-notice must be submitted under penalty of perjury, and the policy states a false one may create personal liability.
exposures.whyItMatters: The policy explicitly suggests obtaining legal advice before using either process, which places a real cost on the ordinary user who believes their content was removed by mistake.

reference.label: Complaints regarding content posted on the LinkedIn website
reference.quote: A false notice or counter-notice may give rise to personal liability.

exposures.title: Account termination is discretionary
exposures.whatItMeans: LinkedIn may disable or terminate accounts of members who infringe or repeatedly infringe, or who otherwise post unlawful content, at its discretion.
exposures.whyItMatters: The trigger is 'appropriate circumstances and in our discretion' rather than a defined threshold, so the number of complaints that costs you a professional network is not stated.

reference.label: Complaints regarding content posted on the LinkedIn website
reference.quote: in appropriate circumstances and in our discretion, to disable and/or terminate the accounts of Members

exposures.title: Effective March 2014
exposures.whatItMeans: The stated effective date is over a decade old.
exposures.whyItMatters: The named postal address and process have not been restated since 2014, which is weak evidence that the operational detail is current.

reference.label: Copyright Policy
reference.quote: Effective March 26, 2014

availableActions.action: File a counter-notice if your content was wrongly removed
availableActions.howTo: Use LinkedIn's Counter-Notice form. Read the jurisdiction clause first — submitting it means consenting to a US federal court and accepting service of process from the complainant.

availableActions.action: Use the non-copyright reporting routes for other complaints
availableActions.howTo: Trademark, false-profile and inappropriate-content complaints go through the Help Center, not this process, and do not carry the perjury declaration.

reference.label: Claims regarding content other than copyright infringement

requiredDisclosures.name: Designated DMCA agent
requiredDisclosures.note: A named copyright agent and postal address are published, as 17 U.S.C. § 512 requires.

requiredDisclosures.name: Counter-notice procedure
requiredDisclosures.note: The § 512(g) counter-notice route is set out with its required elements.

requiredDisclosures.name: Repeat-infringer policy threshold
requiredDisclosures.note: A repeat-infringer policy is asserted, but no threshold, strike count or appeal route is disclosed — only 'appropriate circumstances and in our discretion'.

analyses.summary: Paytm's privacy statement is written to India's DPDP framework and does several things well — it promises not to sell personal data, offers in-app account deletion, commits to notifying significant changes, and bars behavioural tracking of children. The cost is the breadth of what the app takes from your phone: contacts and call logs, SIM serial and IMEI, location, SMS, camera, microphone and files. And consent is all-or-nothing — decline and the statement says you may get no products or services at all.

exposures.title: The app collects your contacts and call logs
exposures.whatItMeans: Mobile device information collected through the Paytm app includes your phone number, SIM serial number, contacts and call logs, device location, IMEI, network carrier and your transactional and promotional SMS.
exposures.whyItMatters: Contacts and call logs are data about other people who never agreed to anything. This is among the broadest device collection in the corpus, and it sits in a payments app where the stated purpose does not obviously require it.

reference.label: 3. WHAT PERSONAL DATA DOES PAYTM COLLECT?
reference.quote: device location, communication information including phone number, SIM Serial Number, contacts and call logs, device information (including storage, model, IMEI, Network Carrier information), transactional and promotional SMS

exposures.title: Refusing any of it can mean no service at all
exposures.whatItMeans: The statement asserts that using the products constitutes free, specific, informed and unconditional consent, and that if you decline to share data as required, Paytm may not be able to provide you with any products or services.
exposures.whyItMatters: Consent that is a precondition of access is not really a choice, and the statement describes it as 'free' and 'unambiguous' in the same paragraph that makes it mandatory.

reference.label: 1. WHAT ASPECTS DOES THE PRIVACY STATEMENT COVER?
reference.quote: in case you choose not to share your Personal Data as required, with us, we may not be able to provide you with any products or services

exposures.title: Full government identity set plus signature and voice
exposures.whatItMeans: Collected data includes Aadhaar details, PAN, Voter ID, passport and driving licence, specimen signatures, and voice recordings of your customer care calls.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the complete identity package needed to impersonate someone in India, held in one place. The statement gives no retention period for it beyond 'until the purpose exists'.

reference.label: 3. WHAT PERSONAL DATA DOES PAYTM COLLECT?

exposures.title: Data is used to target advertising and third-party pages
exposures.whatItMeans: Processing purposes include showing you advertisements, selective offers, promotions and location-based services, and auto-populating third-party pages when you click through an advertisement.
exposures.whyItMatters: Auto-populating a third-party page means your details reach that third party as a result of a click, which most users would read as browsing rather than sharing.

reference.label: 4. HOW DOES PAYTM PROCESS YOUR PERSONAL DATA?
reference.quote: To auto populate such Third-Party pages based on your click on advertisement instances on our website and proceeding to such pages.

exposures.title: Security is qualified by an explicit carve-out
exposures.whatItMeans: The statement says absolute protection cannot be guaranteed due to factors beyond its control such as hacking, viruses, force majeure and breach of firewall.
exposures.whyItMatters: It is an honest caveat, but it also places the residual risk of a breach with the customer, in a document holding Aadhaar, PAN and financial history.

reference.label: 9. HOW DOES PAYTM KEEP YOUR PERSONAL DATA SAFE?

availableActions.action: Deny contacts, call log and SMS permissions at the OS level
availableActions.howTo: Android and iOS permission settings control these independently of the app. The app may degrade, but the statement does not condition core payments on contact access.

reference.label: 3. WHAT PERSONAL DATA DOES PAYTM COLLECT?

availableActions.action: Delete your account from within the app
availableActions.howTo: Deletion is offered on the website, WAP site and app, and the statement says external processing ceases on deletion. That is a real self-service route, which several peers here do not offer.

reference.label: 10. HOW LONG DOES PAYTM KEEP YOUR DATA?

availableActions.action: Withdraw consent to trigger erasure
availableActions.howTo: The statement ties retention to the earlier of purpose ending, consent withdrawal, or an erasure request — so withdrawal is an actual lever, subject to five stated exceptions including legal proceedings.

reference.label: 10. HOW LONG DOES PAYTM KEEP YOUR DATA?

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: A grievance email is published, as India's IT Rules and DPDP framework require.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children's and disabled persons' data
requiredDisclosures.note: Verifiable parental or guardian consent is committed to for under-18s and persons with disability, with an explicit bar on behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising for children — stronger than most peers here.

requiredDisclosures.name: Right to erasure and consent withdrawal
requiredDisclosures.note: Both are named and tied to retention, with in-app account deletion available.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Commits to email or an on-site notice for significant changes, and to an opportunity to review before continuing — materially better than the 'effective when posted' standard elsewhere in this corpus.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Sharing is described as 'need-to-know' with affiliates, subsidiaries and service providers, with payment gateways as the only example. No recipient is named.

analyses.summary: Flipkart's terms of use forbid customers from making any negative or denigrating statement about Flipkart or its sellers — a non-disparagement clause binding buyers, sitting in the same list as the rules against hacking and spam. Ownership of what you bought passes to you the moment the seller hands it to the courier, and accepting the parcel is deemed approval that it arrived intact, so loss and damage in transit fall on you. Flipkart may sue you in any court it chooses; you may only sue in Bengaluru. Consent to share your information with third parties is granted in a bullet headed 'Service Interruptions'. Terms change with no prior notice and take effect on posting. The Grievance Officer is named in full, with a 24-to-48-hour response guarantee.

exposures.title: You agree not to say anything negative about Flipkart
exposures.whatItMeans: Among the binding principles governing your use of the platform, you undertake not to make any negative, denigrating or defamatory statement or comment about Flipkart, its brand or domain names, or otherwise engage in conduct that might tarnish the image or reputation of Flipkart or of sellers on the platform.
exposures.whyItMatters: Defamation is already unlawful; this reaches past it to anything merely negative, about sellers as well as the platform. A customer who posts a critical review of a bad delivery is inside the literal wording, and breach is a ground for suspending the account.

reference.label: Use of the Platform
reference.quote: You shall not make any negative, denigrating or defamatory statement(s) or comment(s) about Us or the brand name or domain name used by Us

exposures.title: The parcel becomes yours when the courier collects it, not when you receive it
exposures.whatItMeans: Ownership transfers to you immediately when the seller hands the products to the transporter. The transporter is not a buyer or seller and is only a logistics provider, and it is not liable for delay, mis-delivery, non-delivery, loss or damage caused by any cause reasonably beyond its control.
exposures.whyItMatters: Risk usually follows title, so passing title at the warehouse door puts the loss of a parcel that never arrives on the customer rather than the seller. The customer has no visibility of, and no contract with, the leg of the journey where the loss happens.

reference.label: Charges
reference.quote: Once the Seller hands over the products to the Transporter for delivery, the ownership of, products is immediately transferred to you.

exposures.title: Taking the parcel is deemed to confirm it arrived complete and undamaged
exposures.whatItMeans: Once you accept delivery at the delivery location, the transporter is deemed to have completed all its contractual obligations, and your acceptance constitutes deemed approval that the consignment was received in full and in intact condition.
exposures.whyItMatters: A sealed box cannot be checked at the door, and this makes taking it an acknowledgement of contents you have not seen. Paired with title passing at the seller's premises, both ends of the transit risk sit with the buyer.

reference.label: Charges
reference.quote: Your acceptance of delivery of products shall constitute deemed approval of the fact that the consignment has been received in full and intact condition.

exposures.title: Flipkart can sue you anywhere; you can only sue in Bengaluru
exposures.whatItMeans: Indian law governs. Flipkart expressly reserves the right to bring proceedings before any court or forum of competent jurisdiction, and you irrevocably submit to that forum. Any proceeding you bring must be exclusively before the courts in Bengaluru.
exposures.whyItMatters: The asymmetry is the finding. A customer anywhere in India must travel to Karnataka to be heard, while the company may choose the venue most convenient to it. Cost of forum is often what decides whether a small consumer claim is brought at all.

reference.label: Governing laws
reference.quote: (i) Flipkart has the right to bring any proceedings before any court/forum of competent jurisdiction... and (ii) any proceeding brought by you shall be exclusively before the courts in Bengaluru, India.

exposures.title: Consent to third-party data sharing is granted under a heading about service interruptions
exposures.whatItMeans: A bullet headed 'Service Interruptions' — otherwise about maintenance and downtime — opens with the sentence that you consent to sharing your information with third parties unless you specifically opt out. No opt-out mechanism is described anywhere in the terms.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the broadest data provision in the document and it is placed where nobody reading for its subject would look. An opt-out right with no stated route to exercise it is not a control.

reference.label: Service Interruptions
reference.quote: You hereby consent to sharing your information with third parties unless you specifically opt out.

exposures.title: Terms and fees change with no prior notice and bite immediately
exposures.whatItMeans: Flipkart may revise the terms from time to time without prior notice to you, and revisions are effective immediately on posting; you are recommended to check periodically, and continued use is deemed acceptance. Fee policy changes work the same way, and Flipkart reserves the right to charge a fee for browsing as well as buying.
exposures.whyItMatters: Two separate clauses put the burden of monitoring on the customer with nothing promised in return. The fee clause is the sharper of the two, because it can attach a charge to an activity — browsing — that is free today.

reference.label: Amendments
reference.quote: We may revise these Terms from time to time, without prior notice to you... and will be effective immediately after such posting

exposures.title: A perpetual, irrevocable licence over your information, sublicensable through multiple tiers
exposures.whatItMeans: You grant Flipkart a non-exclusive, worldwide, perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, multi-tier sublicensable right to exercise the copyright, publicity, database rights and any other rights you have in your information, in any media now known or not yet known.
exposures.whyItMatters: Publicity rights cover your name and likeness. The grant is perpetual and irrevocable, so it outlives the account, and 'sublicensable through multiple tiers' means it can travel to parties Flipkart never names.

exposures.title: Flipkart may hand your information to law enforcement whenever it thinks appropriate
exposures.whatItMeans: You expressly authorise Flipkart to disclose any information about you to law enforcement or other government officials whenever it believes, in its sole discretion, that this is necessary or appropriate in connection with the investigation or resolution of possible crimes.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is disclosure on Flipkart's own judgement rather than on legal compulsion, and the authorisation is pre-given so there is no point at which you are asked or told.

reference.label: Use of the Platform
reference.quote: You hereby expressly authorize Us to) disclose any information about You to law enforcement or other government officials, as we, in Our sole discretion, believe necessary or appropriate

exposures.title: The seller can cancel your order for buying too much, on a limit that varies per person
exposures.whatItMeans: Placing an order is only an offer; the seller may cancel it at sole discretion, including where quantities exceed typical individual consumption — measured across a single order or several orders for the same product. What counts as typical is at the seller's sole discretion and the terms state it may vary from individual to individual.
exposures.whyItMatters: A rule that is explicitly different for different customers, applied after payment, with no published threshold. Payment is refunded, but the purchase is not honoured and the reason cannot be checked against anything.

exposures.title: Flights convenience fee is never refunded, whatever goes wrong
exposures.whatItMeans: The convenience fee charged on travel bookings is non-refundable under any circumstances whatsoever — including cancellation, a no-show, an itinerary change, or any failure or default by the service provider. Where an under-charge occurs for a technical or other reason, Flipkart may claim the balance and cancel the booking if it is not paid before the travel date.
exposures.whyItMatters: 'Any failure or default on the part of the service provider' is the case where the customer did nothing wrong and the fee is kept anyway, for a booking that did not happen.

availableActions.action: Escalate to the named Grievance Officer with a guaranteed response window
availableActions.howTo: Karthik R, Associate Director, grievance.officer@flipkart.com, 044-45614709, Monday to Saturday 9:00-18:00, at Block B (Begonia), 7th Floor, Embassy Tech Village, Bengaluru 560103. Use it when the support team has not addressed an order concern within its promised timeframe. Flipkart guarantees a response within 24 to 48 hours of receipt.

deadline.description: Flipkart guarantees a Grievance Officer response within 24 to 48 hours of receiving the email.

availableActions.action: Open the box in front of the courier where the value justifies it
availableActions.howTo: Accepting delivery is deemed approval that the consignment arrived in full and intact, and title passed to you back at the seller's premises. Opening at the door, or refusing a visibly damaged parcel, is the only moment where the deeming provision has not yet operated.

availableActions.action: Ask how to exercise the third-party sharing opt-out — the terms grant it but do not explain it
availableActions.howTo: The consent to share your information with third parties applies 'unless you specifically opt out', with no route given. Raise it through the Help Centre and, if that fails, with the Grievance Officer, and ask for the mechanism in writing.

availableActions.action: Get GST invoice details right the first time — no revision is entertained
