availableActions.howTo: Delivery and billing addresses must match and must be the registered place of business, or input tax credit is denied where the GSTIN and delivery address are in different states. Flipkart does not verify the GSTIN or entity name, will not revise an issued invoice, and you indemnify it for anything arising from the details you supplied.

availableActions.action: Read the Consignment Note — it carries its own terms
availableActions.howTo: The transporter issues a Consignment Note containing separate terms and conditions governing carriage, made available on your order page. Those terms apply in addition to the terms of use and are where the delivery leg is actually governed.

availableActions.action: Treat delivery time estimates as non-binding on the courier
availableActions.howTo: Any arrival or delivery time given at booking is an estimate provided by Flipkart, and the terms state the transporter has no role in it and is not bound by time commitments Flipkart makes to you.

availableActions.action: Know that one login covers every Flipkart group app
availableActions.howTo: The terms state you agree to single login access across all apps owned by Flipkart group companies, and that anyone you give account access to — including via separate profiles under your account — can view and access your account information. Treat the credentials as covering more than one service.

availableActions.action: Skip the voice shopping feature if you do not want voice data retained
availableActions.howTo: Using voice command shopping means Flipkart and its affiliates collect, store and use your voice inputs, including to improve their products and services. The feature is optional and restricted to India.

availableActions.action: Check the English listing before relying on a translated one
availableActions.howTo: Translations into eleven Indian languages are provided on a reasonable-effort basis with no warranty of accuracy, Flipkart disclaims all liability arising from them, and the English version prevails in any conflict. Delivery addresses entered in another language are transliterated into English for fulfilment.

availableActions.action: Report infringement to infringement@flipkart.com
availableActions.howTo: Trademark complaints go to infringement@flipkart.com or ss@flipkart.com. Offensive or unlawful content on the platform is reported through customer care.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: Karthik R, Associate Director, with designation, full postal address, email, phone and working hours, cited as compliance with the Information Technology Act 2000 and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020 — plus a guaranteed 24-to-48-hour response. The third document in the corpus to name one properly.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Expressly none: terms may be revised without prior notice and are effective immediately on posting, with continued use deemed acceptance. Fee policy changes follow the same rule.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Indian law with exclusive jurisdiction in Bengaluru for proceedings brought by the user — and an express reservation for Flipkart to sue in any competent court or forum. No arbitration clause.

requiredDisclosures.name: Company identification details
requiredDisclosures.note: Flipkart Internet Private Limited named with its incorporation statute, registered office and two branch office addresses, published under Rule 3(1) of the IT (Intermediary Guidelines) Rules 2021.

requiredDisclosures.name: Electronic record status
requiredDisclosures.note: Declared an electronic record under the Information Technology Act 2000, computer-generated and requiring no physical or digital signature.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent withdrawal mechanism
requiredDisclosures.note: Consent to third-party data sharing is stated to apply unless you specifically opt out, but no opt-out route, form or address is given anywhere in the document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Refund and cancellation rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Disclosed and adverse in parts: the seller may cancel at sole discretion with a refund, delivery charges are refunded on return, but the flights convenience fee is non-refundable in every circumstance including service-provider default.

requiredDisclosures.name: Repeat infringer policy
requiredDisclosures.note: Trademark and copyright complaint addresses are given, with a stated right to remove content that violates the terms or applicable law.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: A terms of use rather than a privacy notice; retention is deferred to Flipkart's privacy policy, analysed under its own hash.

analyses.summary: This is the Robinhood statement that actually covers account holders, and it is far more consequential than the visitor one the site surfaces. It extracts facial geometry from your selfies, makes your Pay & Request profile — including transaction history with whoever is looking — visible to anyone on Robinhood by default, and passes your name, address and securities positions to the companies whose shares you hold. It also explains that because your data is governed by federal financial privacy law, your state deletion and access rights may simply not apply.

exposures.title: Your state privacy rights may not apply at all
exposures.whatItMeans: Because personal information held by the financial entities is generally governed by the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act rather than state privacy laws, the statement says Robinhood may have no obligation to accept a data subject request, or no obligation to honour a particular one.
exposures.whyItMatters: Access, correction and deletion are the rights most people believe they have. For a brokerage relationship this says plainly that they may not exist — and it is the clearest statement of that carve-out in this corpus.

reference.label: Additional US State Privacy Rights
reference.quote: in some cases, we may have no obligation to accept any Data Subject Requests (“DSRs”), and in other cases, we may have no obligation to honor a particular DSR

exposures.title: Facial geometry is extracted from your selfies
exposures.whatItMeans: Biometric data in the form of facial geometry is extracted from selfies, photographs and videos to verify identity and detect fraud, and vendors such as Persona may collect biometric data from your photo and your voice.
exposures.whyItMatters: The purpose is legitimate and clearly stated, but a faceprint and a voiceprint now sit with a third-party vendor as well as with Robinhood, and no separate retention period is given for them.

exposures.title: Your payment profile and transaction history are public by default
exposures.whatItMeans: Your Pay & Request profile — profile picture, username, full name, the year you joined, and the transaction history between you and whoever is viewing — is visible to anyone on Robinhood unless you change your visibility settings. It may be disclosed to users of a service you have not yet enrolled in.
exposures.whyItMatters: Financial transaction history between two people is exposed by default rather than by choice, and the default reaches users of a product you never signed up for.

reference.label: With other users of our Services

exposures.title: Companies you invest in receive your name and holdings
exposures.whatItMeans: Robinhood may provide your name, address, email address and securities positions to companies in which you hold securities, on request.
exposures.whyItMatters: Your position size in a specific company reaches that company's investor-relations function, tied to your name and contact details.

reference.label: Companies in which you hold securities

exposures.title: Chatbot conversations train the AI
exposures.whatItMeans: Inputs and conversations with chatbots and AI features may be used to train, test, improve or enhance AI functionality, with notice and consent obtained only where applicable law requires it.
exposures.whyItMatters: People describe money problems to a support chatbot in ways they would not write down elsewhere, and consent here tracks the legal floor rather than being sought as a matter of course.

exposures.title: You are collected from other people's contact lists
exposures.whatItMeans: If you appear in another user's contact list and that user shares it, Robinhood processes your contact information and, on a referral, your association with that user.
exposures.whyItMatters: The same shadow-profile pattern as the visitor statement, now inside the product that holds financial accounts.

exposures.title: Precise location can be a condition of trading
exposures.whatItMeans: Approximate or precise geolocation is collected per device permissions, and to trade Events Contracts you may be required to enable precise geolocation for regulatory compliance.
exposures.whyItMatters: Location becomes non-optional for a specific product rather than a preference, which is worth knowing before enabling it.

availableActions.action: Turn off Pay & Request profile visibility
availableActions.howTo: Profile visibility can be opted out of at any time in settings. Until you do, your name, photo and shared transaction history are visible to anyone on Robinhood.

availableActions.action: Use the GLBA affiliate-sharing opt-out
availableActions.howTo: Sharing between Robinhood affiliates can be limited through the GLBA financial privacy notices for each entity; email privacy@robinhood.com to exercise it. This is the opt-out that survives the state-law carve-out above.

availableActions.action: Disable marketing-partner data sharing
availableActions.howTo: Account holders can switch off sharing with marketing partners in Managing your privacy choices, which stops hashed email and device ID going out for cross-site advertising.

availableActions.action: Withdraw contacts and photo gallery access at the device level
availableActions.howTo: The statement notes you can withdraw app permission for your contact list or photo gallery through device settings. That also protects the people in your contacts.

reference.label: Access to your device data and precise location

availableActions.action: Reply STOP to end text messages
availableActions.howTo: Texts stop on replying STOP; promotional email stops via unsubscribe. Service and transactional messages continue either way.

reference.label: How to control your communications preferences

requiredDisclosures.name: GLBA consumer privacy notice
requiredDisclosures.note: Separate GLBA notices are named and linked for each of the ten financial entities, and this statement is positioned as supplementing rather than replacing them.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: An actual figure: up to 5 years after the relationship ends for regulated-institution obligations. One of the few specific retention periods in this corpus.

requiredDisclosures.name: Biometric data consent
requiredDisclosures.note: Facial geometry extraction is disclosed and the vendor is named, but no separate consent, retention period or deletion route for biometric data is described.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children under 13
requiredDisclosures.note: No knowing collection except for authorised credit card users added by a parent or guardian, with a separate Children's Privacy Notice and a parental representation requirement.

requiredDisclosures.name: State privacy rights (access, deletion, correction)
requiredDisclosures.note: Expressly qualified: where GLBA governs, Robinhood states it may have no obligation to accept or honour a data subject request. The rights exist for non-financial products such as Social, not for the brokerage relationship.

analyses.summary: Coinbase's cookie policy grants a real right to refuse everything except strictly necessary cookies and points to a working Cookie Preferences Manager, but it names only three cookies in the whole document and gives no vendor list and no expiry table — durations are described as "a few days, weeks or months". It also states that cookie data may become personal information once combined, and that disabling cookies can lock you out of secure areas of a financial account. Effective 12 July 2023, with no commitment to notify you of changes: you are told to revisit the page.

exposures.title: Advertising cookies follow you off Coinbase onto the rest of the internet
exposures.whatItMeans: Targeting cookies are used to serve Coinbase advertising on third-party sites and to measure how you respond to it, using both first-party and third-party cookies.
exposures.whyItMatters: The fact that you looked at a crypto exchange becomes an advertising signal carried by other companies. For a financial account this is a category of browsing most people would not choose to broadcast.

reference.label: 2. What do we use cookies for? — Targeting purposes
reference.quote: after you have been to our Services, you may see advertisements about our Services elsewhere on the Internet

exposures.title: No cookie inventory, no vendor list, and no expiry table
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy names exactly three cookies across the entire document — JSESSIONID, cm_default_preferences and _gat_gtag — as illustrations. No third-party recipient is named other than Google, and retention is described only in general terms.
exposures.whyItMatters: You are asked to decide per category without being told which companies are in each category or how long their identifiers persist. Stripe's equivalent page itemises 273 cookies with host, party and duration, so the information is producible.

reference.label: 3. How long will cookies stay on my browsing device?
reference.quote: Persistent cookies are set to automatically expire after a defined duration (for example, a few days, weeks or months).

exposures.title: Refusing cookies at the browser can lock you out of secure areas of your account
exposures.whatItMeans: Strictly necessary cookies cannot be switched off in the preferences manager, and blocking them at browser level is stated to cut off access to secure areas of the Services.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is an exchange and custodian holding customer funds. The practical floor of consent is higher than on a content site, because the alternative to accepting is losing access to money you already hold there.

reference.label: 4. How to manage cookies
reference.quote: if you set your browser to disable cookies, you may not be able to access secure areas of our Services

exposures.title: Cookie data becomes personal information once combined
exposures.whatItMeans: Coinbase states cookies may collect personal information, or information that becomes personal information when combined with other data, in which case the Global Privacy Policy applies on top of this one.
exposures.whyItMatters: The reassuring framing of cookies as anonymous identifiers does not hold here by Coinbase's own account. Which combinations happen, and what governs them, is settled in a second document this one only links to.

reference.label: Introduction
reference.quote: we may use cookies and similar technologies to collect personal information, or information that becomes personal information if we combine it with other information

exposures.title: The policy can change with no notice and the burden of checking is yours
exposures.whatItMeans: Coinbase reserves the right to update the policy for operational, legal or regulatory reasons and offers no notification mechanism — only an invitation to revisit the page.
exposures.whyItMatters: A consent choice recorded under one set of purposes carries forward into a different set without anything telling you the set changed. The document is dated 12 July 2023 and there is no version history to compare against.

reference.label: 5. Will this Cookie Policy be updated?
reference.quote: You can also revisit this page if you wish to keep yourself informed.

exposures.title: The claim that advertising partners cannot identify you is stated without qualification
exposures.whatItMeans: Coinbase asserts that the information collected through targeting cookies does not enable third-party service providers to identify your name, contact details or other directly identifying information.
exposures.whyItMatters: The assertion is unconditional and covers partners Coinbase does not name. It sits two paragraphs from the statement that cookie data becomes personal information once combined, and the two are not reconciled.

reference.label: 2. What do we use cookies for? — Targeting purposes
reference.quote: The information collected through this process does not enable these third party service providers to identify your name, contact details or other personal information that directly identifies you.

availableActions.action: Reject every category except strictly necessary in the Cookie Preferences Manager
availableActions.howTo: The policy states an explicit right to reject all cookies except strictly necessary ones, and the manager covers both first-party and third-party cookies. This is a real control, not an email request.

reference.label: 4. How to manage cookies
reference.quote: You have the right to decide whether to accept or reject cookies (except strictly necessary cookies).

availableActions.action: Block third-party cookies in the browser rather than all cookies
availableActions.howTo: The policy warns that disabling cookies wholesale can cut off secure areas of the Services. Blocking only third-party cookies targets the advertising and measurement layer while leaving login intact.

availableActions.action: Use the industry opt-out portals the policy links for third-party advertising
availableActions.howTo: The DAA (optout.aboutads.info), DAA Canada, NAI and, in the EU, EDAA (youronlinechoices.eu) portals are named, along with the DAA AppChoices app for mobile. These reach partners the preferences manager may not.

availableActions.action: Read the Coinbase Global Privacy Policy for what happens to the combined data
availableActions.howTo: This policy states the Global Privacy Policy applies in addition wherever cookie data is or becomes personal information. Retention, recipients and deletion rights are settled there, not here.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: A Cookie Preferences Manager offers per-category enable/disable covering first-party and third-party cookies, and the policy states an express right to reject everything except strictly necessary cookies.

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of cookies and their purposes
requiredDisclosures.note: Four purposes are described in prose — strictly necessary, performance, functional and targeting — each with one named example cookie. Present but the thinnest form of the disclosure: no per-category inventory.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No per-cookie expiry is given except for three examples (session, 6 months, 1 minute). Section 3 explains the persistent/session distinction and then describes duration as 'a few days, weeks or months', which is not a retention period.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Google is the only third party named anywhere in the document. Advertising, measurement and security partners are referred to only as 'companies we work with' and 'our third-party service providers', so the set of recipients cannot be determined from this policy.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: No sale-or-share opt-out and no statement that personal information is not sold appear in this document. The only opt-outs offered for advertising are the DAA, NAI and EDAA industry portals, which are self-regulatory and not the CCPA right.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: Captured from coinbase.com/en-in/legal/cookie, the edition served to Indian users. The IT Rules 2021 require a named grievance officer with contact details; the only route offered here is an unnamed Support Portal link.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Section 5 reserves the right to update the policy and commits to no notification of any kind — the reader is asked to revisit the page. No version history is published, so a change cannot be detected by comparison either.

analyses.summary: MakeMyTrip's user agreement takes consent to call and message you that expressly overrides your registration on India's national Do Not Disturb register, then makes you indemnify MakeMyTrip for any losses it suffers if you complain to the telecom regulator about those messages and the complaint is judged erroneous. Its liability is limited to producing a confirmed booking; everything after that belongs to the airline or hotel, and service providers have absolute control over whether you get a refund. Force majeure is drafted to include MakeMyTrip's own insolvency and 'business exigencies'. Terms change with no notice at all. Against that, the recommendation-system and sponsored-listing disclosures are among the most candid in this corpus, and the Grievance Officer is named in full — Manav Narula, with address, email and hours.

exposures.title: Your consent to be called overrides the national Do Not Disturb register
exposures.whatItMeans: By using the site you authorise MakeMyTrip's representatives to contact you by phone, message and email, and the agreement states that this consent supersedes any preference you set through India's National Customer Preference Register.
exposures.whyItMatters: The NCPR is the statutory register a person uses to stop marketing calls. A term of use that claims to override it turns a regulator-run opt-out into something a booking cancels. PhonePe's privacy notice does the same thing, which makes it two documents in this corpus rather than one company's drafting.

reference.label: User's responsibility
reference.quote: This consent shall supersede any preferences set by such User through national customer preference register (NCPR) or any other similar preferences.

exposures.title: Complain to the telecom regulator and you may have to pay for it
exposures.whatItMeans: You indemnify MakeMyTrip against all losses and damages it incurs from any action taken by TRAI, access providers or any other authority because of an erroneous complaint you raised about its communications — or because a wrong number or email was provided, for any reason.
exposures.whyItMatters: This attaches a personal financial risk to using a consumer-protection complaint channel. Whether a complaint was 'erroneous' is decided after the fact, so the exposure exists at the moment of complaining, which is where deterrence works.

reference.label: Usage of the mobile number, communication details of the User by MMT
reference.quote: The User will indemnify MMT against all types of losses and damages incurred by MMT due to any action taken by TRAI... due to any erroneous complaint raised by the User

exposures.title: MakeMyTrip's own insolvency and business exigencies are force majeure
exposures.whatItMeans: The force majeure clause lists acts of God, labour unrest, a pandemic, terrorist activity and government decisions — and alongside them, insolvency and 'business exigencies'. Where it applies, MakeMyTrip says it cannot be held responsible and directs you to the service provider for any resolution or refund.
exposures.whyItMatters: Force majeure exists for events outside a party's control. A company's own insolvency and its own business decisions are not that. Including them converts the clause from a shared allocation of unforeseeable risk into a general excuse.

reference.label: Force majeure
reference.quote: due to various reasons like act of God, labor unrest, insolvency, a pandemic, an epidemic, business exigencies, government decisions

exposures.title: Terms change with no notice — reviewing them is your responsibility
exposures.whatItMeans: MakeMyTrip reserves the right to change the user agreement from time to time and states that the user is responsible for regularly reviewing it. No notice, notice period or effective date is committed to.
exposures.whyItMatters: The second Indian travel and delivery platform in this corpus to make the customer the change-monitoring mechanism, after Zomato. Every clause here — including the indemnities and the liability limits — is revisable without anyone telling you.

reference.label: Miscellaneous
reference.quote: MMT reserves the right to change the User Agreement from time to time. The User is responsible for regularly reviewing the User Agreement.

exposures.title: The service provider decides whether you get a refund, and MakeMyTrip only forwards it
exposures.whatItMeans: All refunds — user-initiated, provider-initiated or force majeure — follow the service provider's policy, and the agreement states that service providers have absolute control over the refund policy and are solely responsible for determining the amount. MakeMyTrip processes refunds only after receiving the money from the provider, within 24 hours, or 96 hours for transactions over six months old.
exposures.whyItMatters: You paid MakeMyTrip and MakeMyTrip charged you a convenience fee, but the party that decides your refund is one you never contracted with directly. The service-level promise is on forwarding money already received, not on getting it.

reference.label: Fees and payment
reference.quote: Service providers have absolute control over the refund policy, and the service provider is solely responsible for determining the amount of refund to be provided.

exposures.title: Your booking can be cancelled without being told, on a suspicion or an authority's request
exposures.whatItMeans: If MakeMyTrip discovers or has reason to believe that a request is unauthorised, that information about you or any traveller is incorrect, or that a fact was misrepresented, it may cancel the booking without prior intimation and accepts no responsibility for the resulting loss. Separately, if any judicial, quasi-judicial, investigation or government authority asks it to cancel a booking, it will do so without approaching you at all.
exposures.whyItMatters: A cancelled flight discovered at the airport is the worst-case version of this. The trigger for the first branch is MakeMyTrip's own belief, and the second removes even the chance to correct a mistaken identification before you travel.

reference.label: Right to cancel
reference.quote: MMT will cancel the same without approaching the concerned User whose booking has been cancelled

exposures.title: Retrospective tax and fee increases are yours to pay, without notice
exposures.whatItMeans: Any increase from a change in tax rates or new government levies must be borne by you, and the agreement states this may be without prior notice and may be retrospective. Separately, where MakeMyTrip under-charged because of a technical error or any other reason, it may claim the balance from you and cancel the booking if you do not pay before the travel date.
exposures.whyItMatters: A booking you paid for in full is not a settled price. Both branches let the amount owed rise after the transaction, and the second attaches cancellation of the trip to non-payment of a shortfall that was not your error.

exposures.title: Your data goes to law enforcement without your consent, and your credit is checked
exposures.whatItMeans: The agreement states your data may be shared with law enforcement agencies for any lawful or investigation purpose without your consent. It also states MakeMyTrip may verify your credit score for fraud detection and for offering bookings on credit, and may share personal information with third parties engaged to assess creditworthiness.
exposures.whyItMatters: 'Any lawful or investigation purpose' is broader than compulsion by legal process, and the credit check runs on selected customers with no described trigger for a lending product they have not applied for.

exposures.title: MakeMyTrip's liability stops at issuing the confirmation
exposures.whatItMeans: Except where it acts as a reseller, MakeMyTrip states its liability is limited to providing you with a confirmed booking. It assumes no liability for the standard of the service provided, gives no guarantee of quality or fitness as represented, and cannot be held liable if the information the provider supplied about the service is inaccurate, inadequate or obsolete.
exposures.whyItMatters: The hotel description you chose from and the price you compared were supplied by the provider and disclaimed by the platform, so the accuracy of everything you actually decided on is nobody's contractual responsibility.

exposures.title: Reviews are auto-moderated by AI, may be edited, and can be withdrawn when a hotel changes hands
exposures.whatItMeans: All reviews pass through AI-powered automated moderation. The guidelines state reviews are accepted exactly as written, and separately that MakeMyTrip may make minimal edits to mask profane or inappropriate wording. Reviews are rejected on a long list of grounds including any that appear suspicious in the company's reasonable opinion, and MakeMyTrip may cease showing a property's reviews if its management changes.
exposures.whyItMatters: Withdrawing a property's review history on a change of management removes exactly the record a traveller would use to judge whether anything has actually changed, and it is a decision the platform makes rather than the reviewers.

reference.label: Guest review moderation guidelines
reference.quote: We may also cease showing reviews of a property if the management of the property changes.

availableActions.action: Escalate to the named Grievance Officer, but budget sixty days
availableActions.howTo: Manav Narula, grievanceofficer@makemytrip.com, 19th Floor Tower B Building No. 5, DLF Epitome, DLF Phase 3, Cybercity, Gurugram 122001, Monday to Friday 9:00-18:00 IST, in English. You must first have raised a ticket and either had it unresolved to your satisfaction or waited 30 days from ticket generation; the officer then aims to respond within 30 days of escalation. Have the booking reference and ticket ID ready.

deadline.description: 30 days from ticket generation before escalation is invited, then 30 days for the Grievance Officer to respond.

availableActions.action: Opt out of feedback contact in writing — it is the only stated carve-out
availableActions.howTo: The agreement authorises MakeMyTrip to contact you for feedback by email, phone, SMS and other channels, and states that a user who chooses not to be contacted must write to privacy@go-mmt.com for specific exclusion. There is no equivalent opt-out from the consent that overrides your NCPR registration.

availableActions.action: Read the service provider's cancellation policy, not MakeMyTrip's
availableActions.howTo: Refund amount and eligibility are entirely the airline's or hotel's decision, set out on the booking page or in the confirmation. That document, not the user agreement, is what determines whether you get money back.

availableActions.action: Check names, ages and documents against the passports before you pay
availableActions.howTo: A misrepresented or incorrect fact about you or any traveller entitles MakeMyTrip to cancel without prior intimation and with no liability for the loss. Infant fares require the child to be under 24 months for the whole itinerary including the return leg, or a separate child-fare booking is needed.

availableActions.action: Confirm baggage allowance with the airline — some fares include none
availableActions.howTo: Some fares in the booking flow are hand-baggage fares carrying no free check-in allowance, priced differently by each airline. Baggage terms are set by the airline and MakeMyTrip states it has no role in them.

availableActions.action: Sort past the default, and watch for the 'sponsored' badge
availableActions.howTo: Results are sorted by popularity by default, computed from gross and net bookings, reviews, location, price, property type and click rate. You can re-sort by user rating or price. Properties badged 'sponsored' have paid for that position. This disclosure is unusually candid — use it.

availableActions.action: Arrange your own travel insurance
availableActions.howTo: Unless MakeMyTrip explicitly provides it, obtaining sufficient cover is stated to be your obligation and no claim arising from its absence will be accepted. Where insurance is sold through the platform, MakeMyTrip is only a facilitator — claims and disputes go directly to the insurer.

availableActions.action: Report a suspected fraud call to riskcontrol@go-mmt.com
availableActions.howTo: MakeMyTrip states its staff will never ask for card numbers, CVV, OTP, net banking credentials, or a transfer to a personal account, and will never ask you to install screen-sharing software. Money sent to an account not held by MakeMyTrip is expressly not recoverable from it.

reference.label: Fake calls and other similar phishing, spamming or fraudulent activities

availableActions.action: Report objectionable or infringing content to ipr@go-mmt.com — and expect it to be forwarded
availableActions.howTo: Complaints need the violation identified, the location or link, proof of IP ownership where relevant, and your contact details. Note that by complaining you consent to MakeMyTrip sharing the contents of your complaint with third parties including the accused party.

availableActions.action: Verify visa and travel-document requirements yourself
availableActions.howTo: MakeMyTrip states its guidance on travel documents is advisory only and not conclusive, and that for visa services it will not advise on the merit, completeness or suitability of documents or the likelihood of approval. Being unable to travel for want of valid documents is expressly your risk.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: Manav Narula, with email, full postal address and working hours, cited as compliance with the Information Technology Act 2000 and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020. A self-declaration to the Central Consumer Protection Authority is also linked. The second document in the corpus to name one properly.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: None. The agreement may be changed from time to time and the user is made responsible for regularly reviewing it.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Indian law with unresolved disputes referred to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts in Delhi. No arbitration clause and no class-action waiver.

requiredDisclosures.name: Refund and cancellation rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Disclosed and deferred: the service provider's policy governs, the provider decides the amount, and MakeMyTrip commits only to forwarding refunds within 24 hours of receiving them — 96 hours for transactions over six months old.

requiredDisclosures.name: Sponsored listing disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: Sponsored properties carry a badge and the agreement states plainly that the provider paid for that position. Among the clearest paid-placement disclosures in the corpus.

requiredDisclosures.name: Recommendation system transparency
requiredDisclosures.note: The ranking inputs are enumerated — search-form entries, past platform usage, and the property's gross bookings, net bookings, reviews, location, price, type and click rate — with the default sort named and alternatives offered.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent withdrawal mechanism
requiredDisclosures.note: Only a narrow carve-out for feedback contact, by writing to privacy@go-mmt.com. No mechanism is offered to withdraw the consent that the agreement states supersedes a user's NCPR registration.

requiredDisclosures.name: Content moderation policy
requiredDisclosures.note: Unusually detailed for this corpus: AI auto-moderation with manual review, enumerated acceptance and rejection grounds for text and image reviews, the extent of permitted editing, translation handling, and a statement that no warranty is given as to any review's accuracy or genuineness.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data localisation
requiredDisclosures.note: For UPI, the agreement records that both the PSP bank and the third-party application provider must store all payment and UPI transaction data only in India, and sets out the full NPCI escalation chain up to the Banking Ombudsman and the Ombudsman for Digital Complaints.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: A user agreement rather than a privacy notice; retention is deferred to MakeMyTrip's privacy policy, which is analysed under its own hash and states none.

analyses.summary: LinkedIn's privacy policy states outright that if you are outside the EU, EEA or Switzerland it collects device information about you even where you have never engaged with its services — a protection it extends to Europeans and withholds from everyone else. It infers your gender from your first name or pronouns, your age from graduation dates and your compensation bracket from job titles, collects calendar meeting attendees from other people's synced calendars, and trains AI models on your data. Its terms were the most balanced in this corpus; its data practices are not.

exposures.title: Outside Europe, you are tracked without ever using LinkedIn
exposures.whatItMeans: If you are outside the Designated Countries, LinkedIn collects — or relies on others including Microsoft to collect — your ad ID, IP address, operating system and browser information on devices where you have not engaged with its services at all.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is a two-tier privacy policy stated in one sentence. The same company, the same technology, and the protection turns on where you live. Someone in India or Brazil is tracked for ad targeting on the basis of never having used the product.

reference.label: 1.4 Cookies and Similar Technologies
reference.quote: If you are outside the Designated Countries, we also collect (or rely on others, including Microsoft, who collect) information about your device where you have not engaged with our Services

exposures.title: Your gender is guessed from your first name
exposures.whatItMeans: Inferences used for ad targeting include using first names or pronoun usage to infer gender, graduation dates to infer age, and job titles to infer industry, seniority and compensation bracket.
exposures.whyItMatters: Attributes you deliberately withheld are assigned anyway, and then used to decide which jobs and opportunities you are shown. Inferring gender from a name is also simply unreliable, and the error is invisible to the person it is applied to.

exposures.title: Other people's calendars put you in the system
exposures.whatItMeans: When others sync their calendar, LinkedIn receives meeting information including times, places, attendees and contacts. It also receives contact data when others import contacts, scan business cards, or sync email accounts — from which it collects email header information and associates it with member profiles.
exposures.whyItMatters: Being in someone's meeting invite is enough. This reaches people with no account, and no setting of yours controls what a colleague chooses to sync.

exposures.title: Your data trains AI models
exposures.whatItMeans: Personal data may be used to develop and train artificial intelligence models, alongside generating inferences with AI and automated systems.
exposures.whyItMatters: The policy names the practice and links external principles pages, but describes no opt-out in its own text — so the document that announces the use does not tell you how to decline it.

exposures.title: Your messages are scanned to draft and summarise
exposures.whatItMeans: If your settings allow, LinkedIn scans messages to provide bots and tools that schedule meetings, draft responses, summarise messages and recommend next steps. It also collects who you communicate with and when.
exposures.whyItMatters: Professional messages often carry salary discussions, job searches and grievances. The scan is settings-gated, which is better than most, but the metadata of who you talk to and when is collected regardless.

exposures.title: Recruiters can export your profile unless you opt out
exposures.whatItMeans: Premium customers can export limited profile information — name, headline, current company, current title, general location — unless you opt out, and can store their own data about you such as a resume or sales history, governed by their policies rather than LinkedIn's.
exposures.whyItMatters: The default is export-permitted, and once exported the data leaves LinkedIn's policy entirely and lives under the customer's.

exposures.title: Employers and applicant tracking systems supply data about you
exposures.whatItMeans: LinkedIn receives personal data such as your job title and work email address when you use the services of its customers and partners, including employers, prospective employers and applicant-tracking systems providing job application data.
exposures.whyItMatters: Applying for a job through a company's own system can feed LinkedIn, which is not a party most applicants think they are dealing with.

availableActions.action: Opt out of profile export by premium customers
availableActions.howTo: Export by recruiters and sales customers is on by default and the policy states it happens 'unless you opt-out'. The setting is the only thing preventing it.

availableActions.action: Do not sync your calendar or contacts
availableActions.howTo: Calendar sync hands over meeting times, places and attendees — including people who are not members. Declining it protects them as well as you.

availableActions.action: Turn off off-site ad tracking
availableActions.howTo: The policy provides an opt-out from use of cookie data that tracks your behaviour on other sites for ad targeting, with separate controls for visitors who have no account.

availableActions.action: Check the inference settings for age and gender
availableActions.howTo: The policy links a page describing the inferences made about age and gender and how they are used. Reviewing what has been assumed about you is the only way to find an error in it.

availableActions.action: Turn off message scanning in settings
availableActions.howTo: Scanning for drafting, summarising and scheduling is conditioned on your settings, so it can be switched off — unlike the communication metadata, which is collected either way.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named data controller
requiredDisclosures.note: LinkedIn Ireland Unlimited Company for the EU, EEA and Switzerland; LinkedIn Corporation elsewhere, with a separate European Regional Privacy Notice.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Notice through the Services or by other means, with an opportunity to review before the changes take effect.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automated decision-making disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: Unusually specific about what is inferred and from what — gender from names and pronouns, age from graduation dates, compensation bracket from job titles.

requiredDisclosures.name: Equal treatment regardless of jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Expressly not equal. Device data collection on people who have never engaged with the Services applies only outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland — the policy states the geographic condition in terms.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: Training of AI models on personal data is disclosed; no opt-out is described in the policy text, which points instead to external principles and approach pages.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No retention period appears in the captured text for any category of data.

analyses.summary: Chase's website terms bind you by access alone and contain an uncapped indemnity that you are deemed to accept the moment you look at account data you do not own — covering forensic investigators, customer notification and credit monitoring, and expressly overriding any contrary agreement you have with the account owner. They also carry a full AI-agent regime requiring any agent acting for you to identify itself and answer truthfully when asked whether it is human, with you liable for what it gets wrong.

exposures.title: Uncapped indemnity, accepted by looking at the page
exposures.whatItMeans: If you access account data you are not the owner or authorised user of, you indemnify JPMorgan Chase and every subsidiary, officer and agent for all losses — expressly including law firms, forensic firms, restoring lost data, notifying affected customers and providing credit monitoring. Assent is manifested by accessing the data.
exposures.whyItMatters: There is no cap and no negotiation. The clause states it applies notwithstanding any agreement you have with the account owner saying otherwise, so a contrary arrangement with the customer does not protect you. It also reaches breaches of your systems and of anyone you shared the data with.

reference.label: Terms of use
reference.quote: You manifest your assent to this indemnity by accessing account data through JPMorgan Chase’s Website or systems, notwithstanding the terms of any agreement you have with a customer or an account owner stating otherwise.

exposures.title: You are bound by opening the page
exposures.whatItMeans: Access to the website is agreement to the terms, and the terms may change at any time by being posted, with no notice.
exposures.whyItMatters: The indemnity above is accepted by the same mechanism. Nothing asks you to agree, and nothing tells you when the terms move.

reference.label: Terms of use
reference.quote: BY ACCESSING THIS WEBSITE YOU AGREE TO BE BOUND BY THE TERMS AND CONDITIONS BELOW. THESE TERMS AND CONDITIONS ARE SUBJECT TO CHANGE.

exposures.title: AI agents acting for you must identify themselves, and you carry their mistakes
exposures.whatItMeans: Any software taking autonomous or semi-autonomous action on your behalf must identify itself as an AI agent, label its traffic deterministically, and answer truthfully when asked whether it is human. You are responsible for its errors, misinterpretations, unintended actions, or anything exceeding the authority you gave it.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is one of the few clauses in this corpus written for automated tools rather than people, and it assigns their failures to you without limit. Chase may also block or terminate agent access at its sole discretion.

reference.label: AI Agent or Agentic AI Notices
reference.quote: you are responsible for any actions or errors that may result from the Agent’s incorrect interpretation or implementation of your instructions, if it performs unintended actions or exceeds the authority you gave it

exposures.title: Everything you do on the site may be recorded, and you consent by being there
exposures.whatItMeans: Use of the website, including patterns and characteristics of your interaction with it, may be monitored, tracked and recorded, and anyone using the site expressly consents to that.
exposures.whyItMatters: Behavioural monitoring of how you move through a banking site is broader than page analytics, and consent is asserted rather than requested.

reference.label: Terms of use
reference.quote: Anyone using this Website expressly consents to such monitoring, tracking and recording.

exposures.title: Your data may be sent to any country Chase considers appropriate
exposures.whatItMeans: You consent to transmission, transfer or processing of information through any country in the world, expressly including outside the EEA, as Chase deems necessary or appropriate.
exposures.whyItMatters: No destination is named and no standard is set beyond the company's own judgement, and using the site is treated as agreement to it.

exposures.title: No liability, including for malicious code on their own site
exposures.whatItMeans: The site is provided as-is with all warranties disclaimed, including freedom from viruses or harmful code, and Chase will not be liable for computer viruses or malicious code in the website.
exposures.whyItMatters: It disclaims responsibility for harm originating on Chase's own infrastructure. The terms do preserve Chase's regulatory obligations to clients, so this bounds website liability rather than banking duties.

exposures.title: The revision date does not match the content
exposures.whatItMeans: The document is marked 'Rev. Aug. 2016' but contains an agentic-AI section that cannot date from 2016.
exposures.whyItMatters: The only version signal on the page is wrong, so a reader cannot tell what changed or when — and these terms bind on access with no other notice.

reference.label: Patent Notice
reference.quote: Rev. Aug. 2016

availableActions.action: Do not access accounts you do not own through Chase's systems
availableActions.howTo: The indemnity triggers on accessing account data where you are not the owner or an authorised user as reflected in Chase's own records. Being authorised by the customer is not enough — the record in Chase's systems is what counts.

availableActions.action: Get yourself recorded as an authorised user before acting for someone
availableActions.howTo: If you manage an account for a family member or client, have Chase's systems reflect that authorisation. The clause turns on their record, not on your arrangement with the account owner.

availableActions.action: Check whether any automation you use meets the AI-agent conditions
availableActions.howTo: Any tool acting semi-autonomously on your behalf must identify itself and label its traffic. Non-compliant automation puts you in breach and makes you liable for its errors.

reference.label: AI Agent or Agentic AI Notices

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: New York law governs access to and use of chase.com.

requiredDisclosures.name: FDIC insurance status of investment products
requiredDisclosures.note: States that securities, annuities and insurance products are not bank deposits, not FDIC insured, and carry risk of loss of value.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Changes are incorporated by being posted, with no notification and no reliable effective date — the stated revision, August 2016, predates content in the document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Limitation on indemnity
requiredDisclosures.note: No cap, no exclusion for Chase's own negligence, and no carve-out for consumers. The indemnity is stated to be in addition to all other rights and remedies.

analyses.summary: Chase's online privacy policy discloses that what you do in your accounts shapes what you are sold: the advertising you see — including pre-screened credit offers — is targeted using the types of accounts you hold, your transaction information and where you bank. Browsing data is combined with credit-reporting-agency records. The only opt-out offered is an industry cookie mechanism that must be repeated on every browser and device, and which by the policy's own admission does not stop the ads.

exposures.title: Your transactions decide which credit offers you are shown
exposures.whatItMeans: Advertisements — expressly including pre-screened offers of credit — are selected using information about your relationships with Chase, such as the types of accounts you hold, transactional information and the location of your banking activity.
exposures.whyItMatters: Account activity is the most sensitive category a bank holds, and here it is an advertising input. Pre-screened credit offers are a financial product, so the targeting decides who gets offered credit and on what basis.

reference.label: Online advertising
reference.quote: Which advertisements you see is often determined using the information we or our affiliates, service providers and other companies that we work with have about you, including information about your relationships with us (e.g., types of accounts held, transactional information, location of banking activity).

exposures.title: Browsing data is merged with credit agency records
exposures.whatItMeans: Information is collected from co-branded partner sites and commercially available third-party sources including credit reporting agencies, and combined with everything collected under this policy.
exposures.whyItMatters: The policy also states that usage information collected online may later be associated with personal information about you — so anonymous-feeling browsing becomes attributable after the fact.

reference.label: Additional Sources of Information
reference.quote: We may combine this information with the personal and other information we have collected about you under this Online Privacy Policy.

exposures.title: The advertising opt-out must be redone on every browser and device
exposures.whatItMeans: Opting out of behavioural advertising works by setting a cookie, so it applies only to the browser it was set in, and the policy states you will still receive advertisements — just not customised ones.
exposures.whyItMatters: A cookie-based opt-out is erased by clearing cookies, does not exist on a new device, and is invisible when it lapses. The burden of maintaining it sits entirely with you.

reference.label: Opting Out of "Online Behavioral Advertising" (OBA)
reference.quote: you will need to opt out of OBA from each browser on each of the computers and devices that you use

exposures.title: Flash cookies are used and are not cleared by browser settings
exposures.whatItMeans: Local Shared Objects — flash cookies — may be stored on your hard drive by a media player or other installed software, and the policy notes these may not be managed in your browser in the same way as cookies.
exposures.whyItMatters: It is a tracking store that survives the action most people take to clear tracking, and the policy discloses this without offering a way to remove it.

reference.label: Understanding Cookies, Web Beacons and Other Tracking Technologies
reference.quote: Local Shared Objects are similar to cookies in terms of their operation, but may not be managed in your browser in the same way.

exposures.title: Messages you send the bank may not be secure
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy warns that information you send electronically may not be secure in transmission and recommends not using unsecure channels for sensitive data such as your tax identification number.
exposures.whyItMatters: The warning is useful, but the policy does not say which of the bank's own channels are secure, which leaves you to judge that yourself.

exposures.title: Changes take effect on posting
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy may change at any time, with notice given by posting a revised version and a new Last Updated date; changes become effective when posted.
exposures.whyItMatters: There is no advance notice and no re-acceptance. The Last Updated date — September 2023 at capture — is the only signal that anything moved.

reference.label: Changes to this Online Privacy Policy

availableActions.action: Opt out of behavioural advertising at youradchoices.com
availableActions.howTo: The policy directs you to the Digital Advertising Alliance opt-out, or the Advertising Options Icon on Chase ads. Repeat it on every browser and device, and again after clearing cookies.

availableActions.action: Use the U.S. Consumer Privacy Notice choices, not this policy
availableActions.howTo: If you hold a financial product with Chase, the policy states that the separate U.S. Consumer Privacy Notice governs and offers actual choices over use and sharing. That is the document with the opt-outs that matter.

availableActions.action: Exercise CCPA rights if you are a California resident
availableActions.howTo: The policy links a separate CCPA rights page, which carries deletion and opt-out rights this document does not itself provide.

availableActions.action: Deny precise location to the Chase Mobile app
availableActions.howTo: The policy says permission may be asked before collecting precise geo-location through the app. Denying it at the OS level removes one input to the advertising targeting described above.

requiredDisclosures.name: GLBA consumer privacy notice
requiredDisclosures.note: Referenced rather than reproduced — the separate U.S. Consumer Privacy Notice is named as governing for customers holding a financial product, and is said to carry the sharing choices.

requiredDisclosures.name: CCPA rights
requiredDisclosures.note: California residents are pointed to a separate CCPA rights page.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children under 13
requiredDisclosures.note: States the services are not intended for under-13s without parental consent, with a carve-out and separate policy for the Chase First Banking program.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No retention period is stated for any category of information collected under this policy.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: No sale-or-share opt-out appears in this document; it is deferred to the linked CCPA page. The policy does state it may share collected information with others for advertising where permitted by law.

analyses.summary: Uber India's terms disclaim the thing the service is actually for. Uber does not guarantee the quality, suitability, safety or ability of drivers, states that drivers may not be professionally licensed, excludes personal injury and property damage from liability, and caps total liability at five hundred euros — in a contract governed by Indian law. Disputes go to confidential mediation and then confidential arbitration, and anything you post carries a perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable licence.

exposures.title: Personal injury is excluded from liability
exposures.whatItMeans: Uber states it shall not be liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive or consequential damages including personal injury or property damage related to any use of the Services, or arising from any transaction or relationship between you and a driver.
exposures.whyItMatters: Physical safety is the entire risk of taking a car ride. Placing personal injury inside the excluded categories, and stating that the entire risk remains solely with you, is the most consequential exclusion in this corpus.

reference.label: LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
reference.quote: UBER SHALL NOT BE LIABLE FOR INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, PUNITIVE OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOST PROFITS, LOST DATA, PERSONAL INJURY OR PROPERTY DAMAGE

exposures.title: Total liability is capped at five hundred euros
exposures.whatItMeans: Uber's total liability for all damages, losses and causes of action in connection with the Services cannot exceed €500.
exposures.whyItMatters: The cap is roughly forty-five thousand rupees for every claim a rider could ever bring, and it is denominated in euros inside a contract governed by Indian law and signed with an Indian company — which suggests it was carried over from another jurisdiction's template rather than set for this market.

exposures.title: Driver safety and licensing are expressly not guaranteed
exposures.whatItMeans: Uber makes no representation, warranty or guarantee regarding the quality, suitability, safety or ability of Third Party Providers, and states that drivers on some request brands may not be professionally licensed or permitted.
exposures.whyItMatters: Riders reasonably assume the platform vets drivers. This says plainly that it does not warrant that it has, while also positioning itself as a technology platform rather than a transport carrier.

exposures.title: Arbitration is confidential, so patterns stay invisible
exposures.whatItMeans: Disputes go first to mandatory mediation, then after sixty days to binding arbitration before a single arbitrator under India's Arbitration and Conciliation Act. The existence and content of the proceedings, all documents, orders and awards must remain strictly confidential.
exposures.whyItMatters: Confidentiality binds the rider, not just the process. A systemic safety or billing problem affecting thousands of people cannot become visible through the only dispute channel available.

exposures.title: You indemnify Uber for Uber's own use of your content
exposures.whatItMeans: You indemnify Uber and its officers, directors, employees and agents against all claims, losses, liabilities and legal costs arising from your use of the Services, your breach of the Terms, your violation of third-party rights, and — expressly — Uber's use of your User Content.
exposures.whyItMatters: Clause (iii) makes you pay for consequences of Uber's own decisions about how to exploit what you posted, under a licence that is perpetual, irrevocable and sublicensable.

exposures.title: Surge charges apply whether or not you knew
exposures.whatItMeans: Charges may increase substantially during high demand. Uber will use reasonable efforts to inform you, but you are responsible for charges incurred under your account regardless of your awareness of them or their amount. Charges are final and non-refundable unless Uber decides otherwise.
exposures.whyItMatters: 'Reasonable efforts' to inform, paired with liability regardless of awareness, puts the risk of a pricing surprise entirely on the rider, with refunds at Uber's discretion.

exposures.title: Cleaning and repair fees are charged on a driver's report
exposures.whatItMeans: If a driver reports a need for repair or cleaning and Uber verifies it in Uber's reasonable discretion, Uber may charge your payment method for the cost. Those amounts are non-refundable.
exposures.whyItMatters: The counterparty reports it, Uber judges it, your card pays it, and it cannot be refunded. No appeal route is described.

exposures.title: Terms change on posting, and Uber can terminate at any time for any reason
exposures.whatItMeans: Amendments are effective as soon as Uber posts them, and continued use is consent. Uber may immediately terminate the Terms or deny access to the Services at any time, for any reason.
exposures.whyItMatters: No notice on either side. Losing account access can strand someone who relies on the service, and no cause or appeal is described.

availableActions.action: Use the sixty-day mediation window before arbitration
availableActions.howTo: Disputes must go to mediation first, and only after sixty days without settlement can arbitration be started. Mediation is the cheaper stage and the one where a refund is realistically obtainable.

deadline.description: Mediation must run 60 days from the request before the dispute can be referred to arbitration.

availableActions.action: Request a lower charge from the driver at the time of the ride
availableActions.howTo: The terms expressly preserve your right to request lower charges from the driver at the point of service, and Uber will respond to a driver's request to modify them. That is far easier than disputing afterwards.

availableActions.action: Keep only one payment method on the account
availableActions.howTo: If the primary method fails, Uber may charge a secondary method on file — including for repair and cleaning fees you are contesting.

availableActions.action: Opt out of SMS by emailing support
availableActions.howTo: Text messages can be stopped by emailing support@uber.com with the phone number receiving them. Uber notes this may affect your use of the service.

availableActions.action: Do not post content you want to keep control of
availableActions.howTo: User Content carries a worldwide, perpetual, irrevocable, transferable, sublicensable, royalty-free licence usable on third-party sites, with no notice, consent or payment — and you indemnify Uber for its use of it.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Indian law, mediation then arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996, seated in India, conducted in English or in the user's native language where they do not speak English.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer rights preservation
requiredDisclosures.note: States the limitations do not purport to limit liability or alter consumer rights that cannot be excluded under applicable law — which is what may make the €500 cap and the personal-injury exclusion unenforceable in India in practice.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: India's IT Rules require a named grievance officer with contact details for an intermediary of this kind. None appears in this document; only a general legal page and a copyright agent are referenced.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Amendments are effective on posting, with continued use treated as consent. No notification is provided.

requiredDisclosures.name: Refund and cancellation policy
requiredDisclosures.note: Charges are stated to be final and non-refundable unless Uber determines otherwise, and repair or cleaning fees are expressly non-refundable. No criteria, timeline or appeal route is published.

analyses.summary: Snapchat's privacy policy, effective 21 September 2026, is genuinely more restrained than its social peers on one axis and hollow on another. It carves private Snaps and Chats with friends out of personalisation and advertising and out of service providers' own use, and it deletes Chats from its servers by default 24 hours after they are opened — real commitments no other social document in this corpus makes. Against that it states no retention period for anything else, admits it cannot promise deletion by any specific time, offers no opt-out from having your My AI conversations feed its machine learning models, describes face grouping in Memories with no consent step or biometric retention schedule, infers your age from your content and activity, and builds a record of you from other people's uploaded contact lists whether or not you are a user. Its commitment on changes is that it will let you know 'one way or another', sometimes by changing the date at the top — weaker than the advance notice the Terms of Service promise for themselves.

exposures.title: No retention period for anything, and no promise deletion will ever finish
exposures.whatItMeans: The retention section gives factors rather than periods: as long as you tell us to, as long as we need it, as required by law, as needed to prevent harm or investigate. The one concrete number is the 24-hour default deletion of opened Chats. Everything else is routed to a Privacy by Product page and a Support Site outside this document, and the section closes by disclaiming any timing commitment.
exposures.whyItMatters: A retention schedule is what makes a deletion right checkable. Without one, 'we deleted it' and 'we still hold it' are indistinguishable from the outside, and the policy has already said it cannot promise otherwise.

reference.label: How Long We Keep Your Information
reference.quote: we cannot promise that deletion will take place by a specific time

exposures.title: Your My AI conversations train the models, and there is no way off
exposures.whatItMeans: Content shared with My AI is collected as Inputs, used to generate Outputs, and fed into the algorithms and machine learning models Snap develops. The policy states directly that its models take My AI conversations into account. No opt-out, no setting and no exclusion is offered.
exposures.whyItMatters: The policy protects private messages to friends from personalisation but places no equivalent fence around messages to My AI, which sit in the same chat list and read the same way. The Terms of Service compound this by treating those Inputs as licensed content.

reference.label: Develop & Improve Features, Algorithms & Machine Learning Models
reference.quote: take into account the conversations Snapchatters are having with My AI

exposures.title: Faces are grouped in Memories with no consent step and no retention schedule
exposures.whatItMeans: Where face grouping features are enabled, Snap uses information about faces detected in your Memories to improve search, organisation and personalisation, including suggesting Memories containing the same person. The policy names no consent mechanism for this processing, no separate retention period for the face data, and no deletion route for it distinct from deleting the Memory. Apple's TrueDepth camera data is handled better and said so: used in real time, not stored on Snap's servers, not shared.
exposures.whyItMatters: Face grouping operates on everyone who appears in your camera roll, including people who have never used Snapchat and cannot consent or object. Biometric statutes generally require written consent and a published retention and destruction schedule, and neither appears in this policy.

reference.label: Personalize Your Experience & Give Context
reference.quote: we may use information about faces detected in your Memories

exposures.title: Snap infers how old you are from what you post
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy states Snap may infer your age or interests based on your content or activity, may use age-assurance measures including automated tools to decide whether you meet minimum age requirements or should receive age-appropriate protections, and may estimate or infer your age or ask you to verify it depending on region. Age inference sits in the same sentence as interest inference, under the personalisation heading.
exposures.whyItMatters: An automated inference about a minor's age is a decision with consequences — which protections apply, which content is shown, which ads are served — and the policy gives no accuracy standard, no notice when the inference is made, and no route to contest a wrong one. On a platform whose users skew young, this is the mechanism most of the child-safety promises rest on.

reference.label: Personalize Your Experience & Give Context
reference.quote: infer your age or interests based on your content or activity

exposures.title: Someone else's address book puts you in Snap's records
exposures.whatItMeans: If another Snapchatter uploads a contact list containing your information, Snap may combine it with other information it holds about you to work out who you may want to communicate with. Separately, if you provide contact details Snap may use them to reach you by SMS, email or other messaging services. Contacts already shared persist until removed in app settings, and the policy warns that changing device permissions may not remove them.
exposures.whyItMatters: You are described here as a person Snap builds a profile about because of a decision someone else made. Nothing in this section is conditioned on you having an account, and there is no notice or deletion route offered to a non-user whose details are already held.

reference.label: Data We Receive From Others
reference.quote: we may combine that with other information we have about you

exposures.title: Notice of change is 'one way or another', sometimes just a new date
exposures.whatItMeans: The updates section commits to a heads-up about changes Snap thinks you should know about, then explains that sometimes this means revising the date at the top of the policy and other times an additional notice such as a homepage statement or in-app notification. No advance period, no materiality threshold, and the choice between the two is Snap's.
exposures.whyItMatters: Revising a date is not notice; it is a record that a change happened, findable only by someone already re-reading the policy. Snap's own Terms of Service, effective the same day, commit to reasonable advance notice of material changes — so the weaker promise is the one attached to the document about your data.

reference.label: Updates to the Privacy Policy
reference.quote: we’ll let you know by revising the date at the top of the Privacy Policy

exposures.title: Your data is an asset in a sale of the business
exposures.whatItMeans: If Snap sells or negotiates to sell its business, it may transfer your information to a successor or affiliate as part of that transaction. The clause covers negotiation as well as completion, and no notice, consent or deletion opportunity is offered at either point.
exposures.whyItMatters: Nothing in this policy binds the buyer to it, and the privacy commitments that make the document unusual — the private-content carve-out in particular — are Snap's promises, not the successor's.

reference.label: Recipients & Reasons for Sharing
reference.quote: we may transfer your information to a successor or affiliate

exposures.title: The people your data reaches are described by category, not by name
exposures.whatItMeans: Recipients include service providers, business and integrated partners, anti-fraud industry partners, advertisers, affiliates, and legal, safety and security partners. Only OpenTable and Apple are named in the text; the actual identities live on two maintained lists linked out of the document. Snap states it is not responsible for how integrated partners collect or use your information.
exposures.whyItMatters: A reader of this policy cannot find out who holds their data without leaving it for pages that can change without the policy changing, and the disclaimer means the party you would complain to is not the party that took the data.

reference.label: Integrated Partners
reference.quote: We are not responsible for how those partners collect or use your information

exposures.title: Cross-border safeguards are asserted without naming one
exposures.whatItMeans: Personal information may be collected from, transferred to, stored and processed in the United States or other countries outside where you live. The policy says safeguards are in place as required by law where you live, and points to the Region Specific Information section, which is a list of eight country links rather than substance.
exposures.whyItMatters: No transfer mechanism is named — no standard contractual clauses, no adequacy decision, no framework — so there is nothing in this document to check the assertion against. The Terms of Service go the other way and state Snap may route content to EU authorities without contesting potential conflicts of law.

reference.label: International Data Transfers
reference.quote: we ensure safeguards are in place to protect the data as required by law where you live

exposures.title: Under-18 protections are stated as a possibility, not a commitment
exposures.whatItMeans: The audience section says Snap may also limit how it collects, uses and stores some of the information of Snapchatters under 18, and that in some cases this means certain functionality will be unavailable to under-18s. Which information, which limits and which functionality are not specified anywhere in this policy.
exposures.whyItMatters: Snapchat's user base skews young, so this paragraph is doing more work than any other in the document, and it is written entirely in 'may' and 'some'. A parent reading it cannot learn what is actually treated differently for their fifteen-year-old.

reference.label: Our Audience
reference.quote: we may also limit how we collect, use, and store some of the information of Snapchatters under 18

availableActions.action: Keep sensitive conversations with friends, not with My AI
availableActions.howTo: The policy commits that private content and communications sent to your friends are not used for personalisation, recommendations or ads, and are not shared with service providers for their own purposes. My AI is outside that carve-out and its conversations feed the machine learning models. The distinction is invisible in the app; it is only in this document.

reference.label: Personalize Your Experience & Give Context
reference.quote: We do not use the private content and communications you send to people who are your friends

availableActions.action: Download your data to see what is actually held, including location history
availableActions.howTo: Use the Download My Data tool from in-app settings. The policy points to it specifically as the way to see the location data Snap retains about you, which is the one place it offers verification rather than description.

reference.label: How Long We Keep Your Information

availableActions.action: Withdraw contacts you previously shared, in app settings rather than device settings
availableActions.howTo: Snap keeps a shared contact list until you remove it in app settings, and warns that changing your phone's permissions may not remove contacts already uploaded. Revoking the OS permission alone leaves the data in place.

reference.label: How Long We Keep Your Information

availableActions.action: Turn off findability by phone number and email
availableActions.howTo: The policy states that by default you are findable to others through the phone number and email address you provided, and that this can be changed in settings. It is a default-on setting, not an opt-in.

reference.label: Control Over Your Information
reference.quote: by default you are findable to others through your phone number and/or email address that you provided

availableActions.action: Reduce ad personalisation in the app's advertising settings
availableActions.howTo: Snap offers advertising settings for a less personalised experience, plus separate handling for iOS 14.5+ tracking. This limits ad targeting; it does not stop the collection or the content-based inferences that feed recommendations.

availableActions.action: Check your region's notice before relying on any right in this document
availableActions.howTo: Australia, Brazil, Canada, Europe, Mexico, South Korea, Turkey and the United States each have separate notices linked from the Region Specific Information section, and the US notice applies only to residents of states with their own privacy laws. The lawful bases for processing are also on a separate linked page. The rights you actually hold are in those documents, not this one.

availableActions.action: Set up Family Center knowing what it does and does not show
availableActions.howTo: With Family Center enabled, a parent or guardian is shown information about the connected teen's account — who their friends are and who they share location with. Snap states the content of private communications is not shared.

availableActions.action: Delete the account, accepting that deletion has no completion date
availableActions.howTo: Account deletion is available and individual items can be deleted separately — saved Memories, My AI content, Spotlight submissions. Legal holds, abuse reports, flagged content and backups are named as reasons data survives the request, and the policy makes no timing commitment.

reference.label: How Long We Keep Your Information

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of personal data collected
requiredDisclosures.note: Thorough and well organised into what you provide, what Snap generates, what it receives from others, and what needs permission. Names device sensors, compass and microphone data, headphone connection state, installed apps, advertising identifiers, phonebook contents, precise GPS location and content-derived labels.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
