requiredDisclosures.note: No period is stated for any category except the 24-hour default deletion of opened or expired Chats. The section offers five factors instead of durations, routes actual periods to a Privacy by Product page and Support Site outside this document, and expressly disclaims any timing commitment for deletion.

requiredDisclosures.name: Biometric data consent
requiredDisclosures.note: Face grouping in Memories is described as a feature that uses information about detected faces, with no consent mechanism, no separate notice and no reference to biometric statutes anywhere in the policy. Contrast the same section's handling of Apple's TrueDepth data, which is expressly used in real time, not stored and not shared — Snap knows how to write this commitment and did not write it for face grouping.

requiredDisclosures.name: Biometric data retention
requiredDisclosures.note: No retention or destruction schedule for face data. The only retention rule that touches it is the general one that location associated with a Snap is kept as long as the Snap is kept, which implies faces detected in Memories persist for the life of the Memory with no independent limit.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: Neither the phrase, the link, nor any opt-out from sale or sharing appears in this policy or in the page footer captured with it, which carries Cookie Settings, Privacy Policy and Terms of Service only. US state rights are routed to a separate U.S. State Privacy Notice linked from the Region Specific Information list, and the policy states that notice applies only to residents of certain states. A reader of the main Privacy Policy is never told whether Snap sells or shares their data.

requiredDisclosures.name: No sale of personal information
requiredDisclosures.note: The policy contains no statement that Snap does not sell personal information. It discloses sharing with advertisers, business and integrated partners, and anti-fraud industry partners, and describes receiving data from advertisers to target and measure ads, without characterising any of it against the sale or share definitions.

requiredDisclosures.name: Sensitive personal information categories
requiredDisclosures.note: Precise GPS location, phonebook contents, microphone audio and face data from Memories are all collected and none are identified as sensitive personal information, nor is a right to limit their use offered. The word does not appear in the policy.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children under 13
requiredDisclosures.note: Stated clearly: Services are directed to 13 and over, users must confirm they are 13 or older, and on actual knowledge that a user is under 13 or under a higher local minimum Snap will stop providing Services and delete the account and data. The trigger is actual knowledge, not reasonable belief, and no parental-consent route exists because no under-13 use is contemplated.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children's data
requiredDisclosures.note: Present but thin, and it is the load-bearing paragraph for this platform. Under-18 handling is 'we may also limit how we collect, use, and store some of the information' with no specifics; age assurance including automated tools is announced without accuracy standard, notice or appeal; and Family Center sharing with a parent is described. Age inference from content and activity appears under personalisation rather than here.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: Snap states its algorithms and machine learning models take My AI conversations into account and that it develops generative AI using collected information. No opt-out, exclusion or setting is offered anywhere in the policy. The only limit stated is that private content sent to friends is excluded from personalisation, recommendations and ads — a narrower carve-out than model development.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data subject rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Access, correction, deletion, portability via Download My Data, and objection to processing are all listed with in-app routes, in a Control Over Your Information section placed before the collection disclosures. The objection right is qualified by 'depending on where you live and the particular data' and is explained on a linked page rather than here.

requiredDisclosures.name: Lawful basis for processing
requiredDisclosures.note: Acknowledged and then delegated in a single line: some jurisdictions require Snap to state its legal basis and that information is 'here', on a page outside this document. No basis is stated for any purpose in the policy itself, including for the advertising and model-development uses.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data protection officer contact
requiredDisclosures.note: A DPO is acknowledged and reachable, but only through a contact form link — no name, no email address, no postal address. The Terms of Service by contrast give full registered addresses, company numbers and VAT IDs for all three Snap entities.

requiredDisclosures.name: International transfer safeguards
requiredDisclosures.note: Present in assertion only. Transfers to the United States and other countries are disclosed and safeguards are said to be in place as required by local law, but no mechanism is named — no standard contractual clauses, adequacy decision or framework — and the reader is sent to the Region Specific Information list.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Recipients are given as categories — service providers, business and integrated partners, anti-fraud industry partners, affiliates, legal and safety partners. Only OpenTable and Apple are named in the text; the identities sit on two maintained lists linked out of the policy, which can change without the policy changing.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent withdrawal mechanism
requiredDisclosures.note: Partial but real: unsubscribe from promotional email and SMS, change device-level permissions, remove previously shared contacts in app settings, adjust advertising settings, and object to processing. Withdrawal is not offered for the model-development or age-inference uses, and the Terms make personalisation a condition of the contract unless you opt to receive less of it.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Present but the weakest form in the corpus: a commitment to let you know 'one way or another', where one of the two named ways is revising the date at the top of the page. No advance period and no materiality threshold, against the Terms of Service's commitment to reasonable advance notice of material changes made effective the same day.

requiredDisclosures.name: Minimum age
requiredDisclosures.note: Thirteen, or the higher local minimum where one applies, stated in the Our Audience section and consistent with the Terms of Service.

analyses.summary: Netflix's privacy statement protects one thing fiercely and treats the rest as ordinary advertising inventory. What you watched is genuinely ring-fenced: Netflix states it does not share title selections with its marketing providers and uses contractual and technical measures to stop them reaching that data. Everything around it flows freely. Advertisers supply Netflix with demographic information and interests they inferred from your activity on their own sites, Netflix collects information on advertiser sites and apps in return, and partners — your TV manufacturer, ISP, or mobile carrier — hand over personal details, payment details and the Netflix voice commands you gave their devices. No retention period is stated for anything. Netflix does not respond to Do Not Track and offers no universal opt-out signal, so every control is a per-profile or per-device setting you must find. And where the terms of use promise a month's notice before material changes, the privacy statement promises only what the law requires, with continued use counting as acceptance.

exposures.title: Advertisers tell Netflix what they inferred about you elsewhere
exposures.whatItMeans: Advertising information includes demographic data and likely interests that Advertisers collected or inferred from your interactions and purchases on their own and other websites and apps. Netflix also states it collects information on Advertiser websites and apps, and buys general location and demographic supplements from online and offline information providers.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is a profile assembled from your behaviour outside Netflix entirely, arriving from companies you never gave anything to. The behavioural advertising setting controls how ads are selected on Netflix; it is not described as stopping the ingestion of this data.

reference.label: The Categories of Personal Information We Collect — Advertising information
reference.quote: information provided by Advertising Companies (such as your demographic information, likely interests they have collected or inferred from your interactions and purchases through their own and other websites and apps)

exposures.title: Your TV maker, ISP and carrier feed data back to Netflix
exposures.whatItMeans: Partners including TV manufacturers, internet service providers, streaming device makers and mobile carriers may provide Netflix with personal details, payment details, usage information, and device and network information — expressly including search queries and commands you make through partner devices or voice assistance platforms.
exposures.whyItMatters: A voice command spoken to a television remote reaches Netflix through the manufacturer, and the relationship that authorises it is the one you have with the manufacturer rather than with Netflix. The statement gives no way to sever these flows short of not using the device.

reference.label: Where We Collect Personal Information From — From Partners whose products and services you use

exposures.title: Voice recordings, not just transcripts
exposures.whatItMeans: Usage information includes voice inputs, specified as including both transcripts and recordings, when using voice-related features. In Netflix games, text and voice chat may be monitored and recorded by Netflix and its service providers.
exposures.whyItMatters: A recording carries the voice itself, which is identifying in a way a transcript is not, and no retention period applies to it. Walmart's comparable disclosure states expressly that it takes a transcript and does not use voice for biometric analysis; Netflix's does not draw that line.

reference.label: The Categories of Personal Information We Collect — Usage information

exposures.title: Nothing has a retention period
exposures.whatItMeans: Retention is described as as long as necessary for a list of purposes that covers every use in the statement, with duration depending on factors including your relationship with Netflix and the need to defend anticipated legal claims.
exposures.whyItMatters: The list of purposes is the same list that authorises the collection, so the retention limit is coextensive with the collection itself and sets no end point. Viewing history and voice recordings are both inside it.

exposures.title: No universal opt-out signal is honoured
exposures.whatItMeans: The statement says Netflix does not currently respond to web browser Do Not Track signals, and describes no support for Global Privacy Control. Every control offered is a per-profile setting, a per-device identifier setting, or an industry self-regulatory tool.
exposures.whyItMatters: A universal signal is the only control that works across browsers and devices without being re-set each time. Its absence means the behavioural advertising, matched identifier and resettable device identifier choices each have to be found and repeated separately, and the device-level one is expressly specific to that device.

reference.label: How can I exercise choice regarding these technologies?
reference.quote: We do not currently respond to web browser "do not track" signals.

exposures.title: The privacy statement promises less notice than the terms of use do
exposures.whatItMeans: Changes to the privacy statement carry notice only as required by law, and continued use of the service after they take effect constitutes acknowledgement and acceptance. The remedy offered for disagreeing is cancelling the account.
exposures.whyItMatters: Netflix's terms of use commit to at least one month's notice before material changes — one of the strongest such commitments in the corpus. The document governing what happens to your data commits to nothing beyond the statutory minimum, and the two were last updated on the same day.

exposures.title: Anyone on the account sees your viewing and your game chat
exposures.whatItMeans: Anyone with access to the account may see viewing information, account information, and game-related information including text chat contents and saved games. Profiles are available to everyone on the account and can be used, edited or deleted by any of them; a Profile Lock PIN restricts streaming access to a profile.
exposures.whyItMatters: Household sharing is the normal way the product is used and the account holder cannot compartmentalise it by default. Viewing history also surfaces through partner interfaces integrated with the service, so it can appear on a shared television's home screen.

reference.label: Section C: Access to Account and Profiles

exposures.title: Game data reaches other players and civil litigants
exposures.whatItMeans: In Netflix games, your game handle, gameplay, text and voice chat, user-generated content including uploaded photos and selfies, and your online status may be publicly available to other players — including players on non-Netflix versions of the same game. Netflix states it may access, preserve and disclose game communications in response to legal requests from government agencies and civil litigants.
exposures.whyItMatters: Civil litigants is a broader category than law enforcement, and chat content is retained long enough to answer such a request. The statement also warns that removing a message does not recover it from players who already saved it.

reference.label: Netflix Games Supplemental Privacy Disclosures — Compliance with law

exposures.title: Hashed contact matching with third-party platforms
exposures.whatItMeans: Netflix sends pseudonymised versions of your email address or phone number to third-party services, which compare them against their own databases to find you and let Netflix market to you there and measure the result.
exposures.whyItMatters: Hashing means the third party learns nothing new about someone it does not already have, but for anyone it does have, the match confirms they are a Netflix user. The opt-out exists under Matched Identifier Communications in per-profile settings, which is not where most people would look for it.

reference.label: Communication and Marketing Preferences — Matched Identifier Communications

availableActions.action: Turn off Behavioural Advertising in the profile's privacy settings
availableActions.howTo: Account section, then Privacy and data settings for the relevant profile. Turning it off means you still see advertisements but they are non-behavioural. There is no such setting on Kids profiles because Netflix states it does not run behavioural advertising there at all.

availableActions.action: Switch off Matched Identifier Communications
availableActions.howTo: Same place — Privacy and data settings for the relevant profile, under Matched Identifier Communications. This is what stops Netflix sending hashed versions of your email or phone number to third-party platforms to target you there.

availableActions.action: Reset and limit the advertising identifier on every device
availableActions.howTo: Device settings, usually under privacy or ads. Netflix states the choice is specific to that device, so it must be repeated on each television, phone and streaming stick you use.

reference.label: How can I exercise choice regarding these technologies?

availableActions.action: Download everything Netflix holds about you
availableActions.howTo: netflix.com/account/getmyinfo provides both the access copy and the portable export. The statement also grants correction, deletion, objection, restriction, consent withdrawal, a right to complain to a data protection authority, and a right not to be subject to solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effect.

availableActions.action: Set a Profile Lock PIN
availableActions.howTo: Restricts streaming access to a profile so that others on the account cannot open it. Without it, anyone with account access can view, edit or delete any profile and see its viewing information and game chat.

reference.label: Section C: Access to Account and Profiles

availableActions.action: Sign out of all devices when you sell or return one
availableActions.howTo: Account section, 'Sign out of all devices'. The statement warns that a device logged into the account stays logged in indefinitely unless you sign it out, and that email or text-based login features make this easier to overlook.

reference.label: Removing device access to your Netflix account

availableActions.action: Turn off profile transfers
availableActions.howTo: The profile transfer feature lets anyone with account access move an eligible profile — including viewing history and recommendations — to a separate account. The setting is in the Account section.

availableActions.action: Contact the Data Protection Officer directly
availableActions.howTo: privacy@netflix.com is given as the address for the Data Protection Officer and Privacy Office, for rights requests and for anything the self-service routes do not cover.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period for any category. Retention is tied to the same list of purposes that authorises collection, with detail deferred to a help-centre page outside this document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data protection officer contact
requiredDisclosures.note: privacy@netflix.com, given for the Data Protection Officer and Privacy Office, with the responsible controller entity identified at netflix.com/legal/corpinfo.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data subject rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Access, correction, deletion, portability, objection, restriction, consent withdrawal, complaint to a supervisory authority, and the right not to be subject to solely automated decision-making, all set out without geographic limitation.

requiredDisclosures.name: Rights over automated decision-making
requiredDisclosures.note: Stated as a right not to be subject to a decision made solely by automated means where it would have a legal or similarly significant effect.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Notice is promised only as required by law, with continued use constituting acceptance — materially weaker than the one-month commitment in Netflix's own terms of use, which was last updated the same day.

requiredDisclosures.name: No sale of personal information
requiredDisclosures.note: Narrow but specific and unusual: Netflix states it does not share information about title selections of shows or movies you have watched, and uses contractual and technical measures to prevent its marketing providers from accessing that data. It makes no general no-sale statement.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Recipients are given as categories — Service Providers, Partners, Netflix Marketing Providers, Advertisers, Ad Service Providers, Ad Measurement Companies. None is named, and the Netflix family of companies is referenced by link.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: A cookie choices tool is linked from the statement and from the site footer, though Netflix states it does not respond to Do Not Track signals and describes no Global Privacy Control support.

requiredDisclosures.name: International transfer safeguards
requiredDisclosures.note: Describes contractual, technical and organisational measures, data protection agreements, and a practice of challenging disproportionate or unlawful government requests, with detail at a linked page.

requiredDisclosures.name: Minimum age
requiredDisclosures.note: 18 or the age of majority in the country of residence to subscribe; below that only with parental involvement, supervision and approval.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent withdrawal mechanism
requiredDisclosures.note: Withdrawal available at any time where processing rests on consent, with the usual carve-out that it does not affect prior processing or processing on other lawful grounds.

analyses.summary: OpenAI's privacy policy gives genuinely strong controls — training opt-out, memory control, data export, account deletion, a thirty-day deletion window, a named data protection officer. What sits alongside them is advertising: free and Go users have their ad history and interests collected, and OpenAI receives information from advertisers about purchases you make elsewhere. It also uploads your device address book if you connect contacts, and tracks the people in it who have not signed up.

exposures.title: Your chats feed advertising if you are on the free tier
exposures.whatItMeans: For Free and Go users, OpenAI collects ads history and interests — the type of ad content you view or engage with — and uses personal data to personalise the ads shown to you and measure their effectiveness.
exposures.whyItMatters: An assistant people use for medical questions, legal worries and money problems is also an advertising surface for the users who are not paying. The controls exist, but the default is on.

reference.label: 1. Personal Data we collect
reference.quote: For Free and Go users, we also may collect information about your ads history and interests, such as the type of ad content that you view or engage with.

exposures.title: Advertisers tell OpenAI what you bought from them
exposures.whatItMeans: OpenAI receives information from advertisers and data partners, expressly including information about purchases you make from those advertisers.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is inbound data about your activity on other companies' services, arriving without any action by you, and it is used to target ads back at you inside the assistant.

reference.label: Information We Receive from Other Sources
reference.quote: For example, we could receive information about purchases you make from these advertisers.

exposures.title: Connecting contacts uploads your address book, including people who never signed up
exposures.whatItMeans: If you connect device contacts, OpenAI uploads information from your address books, checks which contacts use the Services, and will notify you if a contact signs up later.
exposures.whyItMatters: Retaining information about non-users so they can be recognised on future signup means people who never agreed to anything are held in the system. The policy links a separate article on how it uses uploaded contact information of people who do not use the service.

reference.label: Contact Data
reference.quote: If any of your contacts aren’t yet using our Services, we’ll update you if they sign up for our Services later.

exposures.title: A work email address exposes your account to your employer
exposures.whatItMeans: Business account administrators may access and control your account including your Content, and creating an account with an employer's email address means OpenAI may share the fact of your account and details such as your email with that organisation.
exposures.whyItMatters: Conversations you treated as private become readable by an administrator, and the trigger is simply which address you signed up with.

exposures.title: Your content trains the models unless you find the setting
exposures.whatItMeans: Content may be used to improve the Services including to train the models, with the opt-out described in a linked help article.
exposures.whyItMatters: Deletion also behaves differently once training has happened: the policy notes deleted data may already have been de-identified and disassociated from your account, in which case it is not removed with the rest.

exposures.title: The privacy policy can change without advance notice
exposures.whatItMeans: Updates are made by publishing a new version and effective date on the page, unless another form of notice is legally required.
exposures.whyItMatters: The Terms of Use promise thirty days' notice of adverse changes; this policy promises none. The document governing your data is the one with the weaker commitment.

availableActions.action: Turn off model training in data controls
availableActions.howTo: Account settings carry a direct control over whether your Content is used to improve and train the models. It is one toggle and it applies going forward.

availableActions.action: Use the advertising controls if you are on Free or Go
availableActions.howTo: Account settings include advertising controls governing what data personalises the ads shown to you. Paid tiers above Go are not described as receiving ads at all.

availableActions.action: Use Temporary Chat for anything sensitive
availableActions.howTo: Temporary Chats do not appear in history, are not used to improve the models, and are deleted automatically within 30 days unless retained for safety or legal reasons.

availableActions.action: Do not connect your contacts
availableActions.howTo: Contact upload is opt-in. Declining it keeps your address book — and the people in it who are not users — out of the system entirely.

availableActions.action: Exercise data rights through the privacy portal or DPO
availableActions.howTo: Access, rectification, deletion, restriction, portability and consent withdrawal go through privacy.openai.com or dsar@openai.com; the data protection officer is dpo@openai.com. Inaccurate model output about you can be raised the same way.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named data controller
requiredDisclosures.note: OpenAI Ireland Limited for the EEA and Switzerland with a registered address; OpenAI OpCo, LLC elsewhere.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data protection officer contact
requiredDisclosures.note: dpo@openai.com is published alongside a dedicated DSAR address.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: Unusually specific for this corpus: 30 days from deletion, automatic deletion of Temporary Chats within 30 days, with named exceptions for legal holds, banned content and financial records.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data subject rights and complaint route
requiredDisclosures.note: The full set is listed, including the right to lodge a complaint with a local data protection authority.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children under 13
requiredDisclosures.note: Not directed to under-13s, with a reporting address and parent-guardian account linking for teens.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Changes take effect on publication with no notice period, in contrast to the 30 days the Terms of Use commit to for adverse changes.

analyses.summary: American Express's site rules bind you by the act of loading the page, reserve the right to change themselves without telling you, and take an unrestricted perpetual licence to any idea you post — explicitly including know-how and intellectual property — for sharing across the whole corporate group for any purpose. The document governs website use rather than your card agreement, which limits what is at stake, but the clauses themselves are among the most one-sided in this corpus.

exposures.title: Anything you post can be taken and used, including your ideas
exposures.whatItMeans: Postings on any message board or chat room are not confidential, and American Express may use and pass on anything in them — including ideas, concepts, know-how and other intellectual property — to its parent, subsidiaries and affiliates for any purpose it considers appropriate.
exposures.whyItMatters: There is no limit on purpose, no time limit, and no compensation. 'For any purpose whatsoever' combined with 'other intellectual property' is a broader grant than most content licences in this corpus, and it sits in a website-rules document rather than anywhere a user would look for it.

reference.label: 5. Confidentiality Of User Communications
reference.quote: American Express may use and provide information contained in any such postings (including any ideas, concepts, know-how or other intellectual property) to any of its parent company, subsidiaries and affiliates for any purpose whatsoever

exposures.title: You are bound by simply opening the page
exposures.whatItMeans: Acceptance is triggered by access itself — no checkbox, no button, no acknowledgement.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is browsewrap: you are treated as having agreed to terms you were never shown. Its enforceability is contested in many jurisdictions, but the document asserts it plainly.

reference.label: Rules and Regulations
reference.quote: By accessing the Site you indicate your acknowledgment and acceptance of these terms and conditions.

exposures.title: Terms can change without notice and you are deemed to know
exposures.whatItMeans: American Express may revise the rules at any time, and users are treated as informed of and bound by the changes as soon as they are posted.
exposures.whyItMatters: There is no notification, no effective date, no version history and no re-acceptance. The only way to know what you are bound by is to re-read the page yourself, and nothing tells you when it moved.

reference.label: 9. Changes to rules and regulations
reference.quote: users are deemed to be apprised of and bound by any changes to these Rules and Regulations

exposures.title: Your data may cross borders because you used the site
exposures.whatItMeans: Providing any personal information through the site is treated as consent to transmit it across international borders for processing under American Express's standard business practices.
exposures.whyItMatters: Consent to international transfer is inferred from use rather than asked for, and the destination is defined by internal practice rather than named.

reference.label: 8. Transmission of Personal Data
reference.quote: user consents to the transmission of such personal or proprietary user information over international borders as necessary for processing in accordance with American Express' standard business practices

exposures.title: Liability is disclaimed as far as the law allows, including for viruses
exposures.whatItMeans: All content is provided as-is with no warranty of accuracy or security, and liability is disclaimed for all categories of damage, expressly including harm from viruses that infect your computer.
exposures.whyItMatters: Naming viruses specifically is unusual: it disclaims responsibility for a harm originating on their infrastructure and landing on your machine.

reference.label: 4. Limitation of liability
reference.quote: including liability associated with any viruses which may infect a user's computer equipment

exposures.title: Linking to the site is prohibited without permission
exposures.whatItMeans: Caching, unauthorised hypertext links to the site, and framing of its content are all prohibited, and American Express reserves the right to disable them.
exposures.whyItMatters: It asserts control over ordinary web behaviour — linking — which is a restriction most readers would not expect and which sits oddly against how the web works.

availableActions.action: Do not post anything you would want to own
availableActions.howTo: The unrestricted IP grant attaches to message board and chat room postings. Keep ideas, business proposals and anything proprietary out of those surfaces entirely.

availableActions.action: Re-read the rules yourself before relying on them
availableActions.howTo: There is no notification of changes and no version history. If these terms matter to you, save a dated copy — the document expressly says the posted version governs.

availableActions.action: Check which country's Amex entity issued your card
availableActions.howTo: This site is published in India for Indian residents and covers only rupee-denominated cards issued in India. If your card was issued elsewhere, these rules and the benefits described may not apply to you.

reference.label: 14. JURISDICTION/GOVERNING LAW
reference.quote: The Web site is published in India for Indian citizens and residents in India, and relates only to Indian American Express-issued Cards

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Indian law is named, and the document is scoped to India-issued rupee cards.

requiredDisclosures.name: Designated DMCA agent
requiredDisclosures.note: A registered agent and contact address are published.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: No notification mechanism, effective date or version history. Users are deemed bound on posting, which means there is no way to detect that the terms moved.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: Indian IT Rules require a named grievance officer on intermediary websites. None appears in this document; American Express publishes a separate grievance redressal policy, analysed independently.

analyses.summary: American Express India's grievance policy is the strongest complaint document in this corpus and the clearest counterexample to the pattern of unnamed grievance contacts. It publishes a six-level escalation chain with three individuals named in full — Ms. Priyameet Kaur as Head of Customer Service, Ms. Garima Chandel as Nodal Officer, Mr. Ashish Pandey as Principal Nodal Officer — each with a direct phone number, an email address and the Gurgaon office address, plus the CEO's name and email. It commits to 30 days for complaints, 14 days for insurance grievances under IRDAI rules, and it sets out the RBI credit-information compensation framework with a 21-day correction window and payment credited within five working days. The costs are small and specific: everything above the 24x7 helpline runs Monday to Friday 8:30 to 5:00, the 30-day target is stated as an endeavour, and the compensation framework excludes complaints about how your credit score was computed and complaints you have already taken to a consumer forum.

exposures.title: Every escalation above the helpline is business hours only
exposures.whatItMeans: Level 1, the general helpline, is 24x7 toll-free. Levels 2 to 5 — the Executive Correspondence Unit, the Head of Customer Service, the Nodal Officer and the Principal Nodal Officer — each publish the same Monday-to-Friday 8:30 am to 5:00 pm window.
exposures.whyItMatters: The route that exists round the clock is the one that could not resolve your complaint. Escalation, which is where a named officer and a tracked commitment enter, is available for 42.5 hours a week.

reference.label: Level 5: Principal Nodal Officer
reference.quote: Call Us: +91 124 6702638 (Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 5:00 pm)

exposures.title: Thirty days is an endeavour, and it is also the gate to the regulator
exposures.whatItMeans: The bank states its endeavour is to resolve all complaints within 30 days of receipt. The same 30 days is the period you must wait before the RBI Integrated Ombudsman will hear you, and the clock only starts once the bank has received every piece of information it asks for.
exposures.whyItMatters: The one figure in the document does double duty as a service target and as the waiting period before an external remedy exists, so a complaint that drifts consumes the whole internal window before anyone outside the bank can look at it. A request for further information resets when the count begins.

reference.label: Level 6: Banking Ombudsman Scheme
reference.quote: The 30-day period will be reckoned after all the necessary information sought from the customer has been received

exposures.title: Disputes about how your credit score was calculated get no compensation
exposures.whatItMeans: The RBI compensation framework set out here pays for delay in correcting credit information reported to the credit bureaus, but expressly does not apply to grievances about the computation of the credit score or the scoring model.
exposures.whyItMatters: A wrong entry is compensable; a score you believe was calculated wrongly from correct entries is not. That is the harder of the two problems to detect and the one a consumer has no other route to challenge.

reference.label: The compensation framework shall not be applicable in the following cases
reference.quote: complaints pertaining to disputes/ grievances regarding the computation of the credit score/credit score model

exposures.title: Taking a complaint to a consumer forum first forfeits the compensation route
exposures.whatItMeans: The compensation framework does not apply to complaints that have been decided by, or are already pending in, other fora such as the Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, courts or tribunals.
exposures.whyItMatters: The order in which you use the channels changes what you can recover. A consumer who goes to the district commission before exhausting the bank's internal ladder loses the statutory delay compensation, and the document does not say so anywhere near the escalation instructions.

reference.label: The compensation framework shall not be applicable in the following cases
reference.quote: complaints that have been decided by or are already pending in other fora such as Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Courts, Tribunals, etc.

exposures.title: Credit-information disputes outside the compensation framework go to arbitration
exposures.whatItMeans: Disputes among credit information companies, the bank, borrowers and clients on credit information matters for which CICRA 2005 provides no remedy are to be settled by conciliation or arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the statute's own routing rather than the bank's drafting, but the effect on a consumer is the same as an arbitration clause: the residual category of credit-reporting dispute leaves the ombudsman and consumer-forum system altogether.

reference.label: The compensation framework shall not be applicable in the following cases
reference.quote: such disputes shall be settled by conciliation or arbitration as provided in the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996

availableActions.action: Escalate to a named officer rather than repeating the helpline call
availableActions.howTo: Level 3 is Ms. Priyameet Kaur, Head of Customer Service, +91 124 6702527, Head-Customerservicesindia@aexp.com. Level 4 is Ms. Garima Chandel, Nodal Officer, +91 124 6702386, AEBCNodalOfficer@aexp.com. Level 5 is Mr. Ashish Pandey, Principal Nodal Officer, +91 124 6702638, pnoindia@aexp.com. All three sit at American Express Banking Corp., Cyber City, Tower C, DLF Building No. 8, Sector 25, DLF City Phase II, Gurgaon 122002. Quote the complaint number the helpline generated.

reference.label: Level 3: Head of Customer Service / Level 4: Nodal Officer / Level 5: Principal Nodal Officer

availableActions.action: Go to the RBI Ombudsman once thirty days have passed
availableActions.howTo: File at https://cms.rbi.org.in or call 14448 (9:30 am to 5:15 pm), or write to the Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre, Reserve Bank of India, 4th Floor, Sector 17, Chandigarh 160017. You need the complete transaction details and the bank's response, or the absence of one.

deadline.description: Available only after 30 days from logging the complaint with the bank, counted from when the bank received all information it asked you for.

reference.label: Level 6: Banking Ombudsman Scheme
reference.quote: you may approach the Office of the Banking Ombudsman for grievance redressal

availableActions.action: Use the insurance channel for anything Amex sold you as a corporate agent
availableActions.howTo: Write to Insurance.complaints@aexp.com. IRDAI requires resolution in 14 days, and Amex commits to writing to you about the delay if it will miss that. If it is unresolved after 30 days, take it to IRDAI's grievance redressal mechanism at https://irdai.gov.in/grievance-redressal-mechanism1.

deadline.description: Insurance grievances carry a 14-day IRDAI resolution requirement, with escalation to IRDAI after 30 days.

reference.label: Insurance Complaints
reference.quote: Insurance complaints/Grievances will be resolved within 14 days as per IRDAI requirements.

availableActions.action: Claim compensation for a delayed credit-bureau correction
availableActions.howTo: If the bank fails to correct credit information with the credit information companies within 21 calendar days of being told, compensation is due, and it must be credited to your bank or card account within five working days of resolution. State your preferred account in the complaint form. If compensation is wrongly denied, that itself goes to the RBI Ombudsman.

deadline.description: The bank's correction window is 21 calendar days from being informed by you or a credit information company; compensation accrues for resolution beyond 30 days.

reference.label: Compensation framework
reference.quote: within twenty- one (21) calendar days of being informed by the complainant or a CIC

availableActions.action: Attend the monthly Grievance Redressal Day
availableActions.howTo: If the bank has missed its timeline, you can attend the monthly Grievance Redressal Day in person or join on Webex to put the complaint directly. Details are linked from this policy.

availableActions.action: Report mis-selling or harassment on the dedicated line
availableActions.howTo: Complaints about mis-selling or harassment by a bank representative go to Manager-Customerservicesindia@aexp.com or 0124-6702523, Monday to Friday 8:30 to 5:00 — a separate route from the ordinary escalation ladder.

reference.label: For any complaints related to mis-selling or harassment

availableActions.action: Read the published complaints analysis before you file
availableActions.howTo: The policy links complaints analyses for FY 2023-24, FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26. These are the bank's own volume and category data and are the only public evidence of how the ladder actually performs.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: The most complete instance in the corpus. Three individuals are named with direct phone, email and postal address — Ms. Priyameet Kaur (Head of Customer Service), Ms. Garima Chandel (Nodal Officer), Mr. Ashish Pandey (Principal Nodal Officer) — alongside the CEO Sanjay Khanna and ceoindia@aexp.com. RBI's grievance redressal directions require a nodal and principal nodal officer to be published; this document exceeds that with a six-level chain and stated hours for each.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer complaint route
requiredDisclosures.note: Six levels, each with its own contact: 24x7 toll-free helpline 1800 419 3646, in-app chat, branch complaint register, online form, then four escalation tiers, then the RBI Integrated Ombudsman with its own number, portal and Chandigarh address. Separate dedicated routes exist for insurance and for mis-selling or harassment.

requiredDisclosures.name: Error resolution procedure and timeframes
requiredDisclosures.note: A 30-day resolution endeavour with automatic complaint numbers and system-generated ageing reported to senior management; 14 days for insurance under IRDAI; 21 calendar days for credit-bureau corrections; compensation credited within five working days of resolution. Stated as an endeavour rather than a guarantee, but with figures attached, which most documents here do not manage.

requiredDisclosures.name: Company identification details
requiredDisclosures.note: American Express Banking Corp., Cyber City, Tower C, DLF Building No. 8, Sector 25, DLF City Phase II, Gurgaon 122002, Haryana, repeated at each escalation level, with the policy scoped to India-issued cards, India merchant accounts and vendors servicing India-issued accounts.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: The document carries a 'Last updated on August 3, 2026' line and nothing else. No notification mechanism, no version history, and no statement of what changed — which matters here because the named officers and their direct numbers are the substance of the policy and can be replaced silently.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer rights preservation
requiredDisclosures.note: The compensation framework excludes complaints already decided by or pending in a Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, court or tribunal, and excludes credit-score computation disputes entirely. Both exclusions come from the RBI framework rather than Amex drafting, but the document reproduces them without telling a consumer that choosing a forum first costs them the statutory compensation.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: This is a complaint-handling policy, not a data notice. It describes a complaints management tool that tracks complaint ageing but does not process personal data as its subject; retention for American Express India is addressed in its online privacy statement, analysed separately.

analyses.summary: Bank of America's online privacy notice reads calmly and gives away a great deal. It collects Social Security number, driver's licence number, CVV2, credit and income information, and — alongside these — keystrokes, mouse movements, swipes and gestures, plus voice-to-text queries from the mobile app. Account relationship, transaction information and where you bank are then used to target advertising, including prescreened offers of credit, on third-party sites. Consent is taken from use of the site rather than asked for. The sharpest clause is about account aggregators: if you give anyone your user ID and password, the bank will treat every transaction initiated with them as authorised by you, and disclaims responsibility for what happens next. Set against that, the notice honours browser opt-out preference signals as sale/sharing opt-outs and commits to deleting data as soon as legally permitted.

exposures.title: Sharing your password makes every resulting transaction yours
exposures.whatItMeans: If you give a third-party aggregator your Bank of America user ID and password, the bank will consider that you authorised any transaction or action taken with those credentials, and states it is not responsible for how that third party uses or discloses what it reaches.
exposures.whyItMatters: Account aggregation is a mainstream product that routinely asks for bank credentials, and this clause converts using one into accepting liability for anything done through it. The remedy the notice offers — change your password — only works after the fact.

reference.label: Additional Information — Third-Party Data Sharing
reference.quote: If you share your Bank of America user ID, password or other information about your accounts with others, we will consider that you have authorized any transaction or action initiated by using the access information you provide.

exposures.title: Your keystrokes, mouse movements and gestures are collected
exposures.whatItMeans: Beyond pages visited and links clicked, the notice lists unique and measurable patterns such as keystrokes, mouse clicks and movements, swipes and gestures, together with voice-to-text queries in the mobile app.
exposures.whyItMatters: These are behavioural biometrics: the way you type and move is identifying in itself and can persist across sessions and accounts. The notice groups them with ordinary device data and offers no separate control over them.

reference.label: Types of personal information we collect online
reference.quote: unique and measurable patterns such as keystrokes, mouse clicks and movements, swipes and gestures

exposures.title: What you bank and where is used to sell you credit
exposures.whatItMeans: The notice states that types of accounts, transactional information and the location in which you bank may be used to decide which advertisements and offers to show you, including prescreened offers of credit, both on Bank of America properties and on unaffiliated third-party sites.
exposures.whyItMatters: Transaction history is among the most revealing categories a bank holds, and using it for ad targeting puts it to a purpose entirely separate from running the account. Prescreened credit offers also mean the profile is being scored, not just segmented.

reference.label: Online Behavioral Advertising — How we tailor ads to you
reference.quote: We may use personal information about your relationship with us (such as types of accounts, transactional information or the location in which you bank) to help determine which advertisements or offers to present to you.

exposures.title: Consent is taken from the act of browsing
exposures.whatItMeans: The notice states that by using the sites and mobile apps you agree to it, and that where consent is not separately required, using the site is itself consent to collection, use and sharing.
exposures.whyItMatters: Nothing is signed or clicked. A person checking a branch location has consented to the same terms as someone opening an account, and there is no moment at which the choice is presented.

reference.label: Our Online Privacy Practices
reference.quote: We ask for your consent when required, otherwise by using our Site and Mobile Apps, you consent to the collection, use and sharing of your personal information

exposures.title: No retention period, only a promise to delete when allowed
exposures.whatItMeans: Retention is described as a period required by laws and regulations plus the necessary business purpose, with no duration stated for any category, though the notice does commit to secure deletion as soon as legally permitted.
exposures.whyItMatters: 'Necessary business purpose' is defined by the bank, so the commitment to delete has no fixed date attached to it. The categories at stake include Social Security number, driver's licence number and submitted account-opening documents.

reference.label: How do we use your personal information?
reference.quote: We retain personal information for a period of time as required by laws and regulations and the necessary business purpose. We securely delete personal information as soon as legally permitted.

exposures.title: Changes are published by editing a date
exposures.whatItMeans: When the notice changes, the only stated step is revising the Last updated date on the page. There is no notification, and users are told to review it whenever they have questions.
exposures.whyItMatters: A date change is not notice. Because consent here is taken from continued use of the site, a silent revision converts your next visit into agreement to terms you have not seen.

reference.label: Updates to this Notice
reference.quote: If we make changes to this Notice, we will revise the Last updated date on this page.

exposures.title: Opting out of ad targeting has to be redone constantly
exposures.whatItMeans: The behavioural advertising opt-out is stored in a cookie, so it requires cookies to be enabled to work, and must be repeated if you clear cookies, use a different browser, buy a new device or log in under a different screen name.
exposures.whyItMatters: An opt-out that resets on ordinary browser hygiene is one most people will never sustain, and the notice is explicit that opting out does not stop tailored content once you are logged in to online banking.

reference.label: Online Behavioral Advertising — Reminder
reference.quote: If you delete cookies, buy a new device, access our Sites and Mobile Apps or other sites from a different device, login under a different screen name, or change web browsers, you will need to opt out again.

exposures.title: Sharing across the Bank of America group, including Merrill
exposures.whatItMeans: Personal information may be shared with affiliates and subsidiaries such as Merrill, with contracted third-party providers, and with government agencies as laws require. Limiting is available only 'where appropriate' and through a separate preferences page.
exposures.whyItMatters: Affiliate sharing moves banking data into brokerage and vice versa, and the notice does not enumerate the affiliates. The control lives on another page rather than in the notice that describes the sharing.

reference.label: With whom do we share your personal information?

exposures.title: De-identified data is shared onward on the bank's own judgement
exposures.whatItMeans: Collected personal information may be aggregated or de-identified and then shared with third-party providers, both to tailor services and for Bank of America's own business purposes.
exposures.whyItMatters: The notice defines de-identification as removing details that identify you personally, which is a weaker standard than statutory de-identification, and once data is treated as de-identified it falls outside the protections the rest of the notice describes.

exposures.title: Social widgets report your browsing to their owners
exposures.whatItMeans: Share buttons embedded on Bank of America pages are owned by unaffiliated third parties, who may have access to information about your browsing on the pages where those widgets appear.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is collection by companies you have no relationship with, occurring on a banking site, and the notice states plainly that unaffiliated third-party sites and apps are not subject to Bank of America's privacy notices.

availableActions.action: Set a browser opt-out preference signal
availableActions.howTo: Enable Global Privacy Control or an equivalent signal in your browser. The notice states Bank of America captures opt-out preference signals and, where users have rights under applicable law, treats them as valid requests to opt out of sale and sharing at the browser level.

reference.label: How you can opt out of Online Behavioral Advertising

availableActions.action: Register your sharing and marketing choices
availableActions.howTo: Use the 'Control How We Can Share Your Data and Market To You' page linked from the notice. This is the route for limiting affiliate and marketing sharing.

availableActions.action: Opt out of interest-based ads at the industry level
availableActions.howTo: Use YourAdChoices.com/control (Digital Advertising Alliance) or the Network Advertising Initiative opt-out tool. Keep cookies enabled or the opt-out cannot be stored, and redo it after clearing cookies or changing device or browser.

reference.label: How you can opt out of Online Behavioral Advertising

availableActions.action: Never hand your banking credentials to an aggregator
availableActions.howTo: Where an aggregation service offers to take your information-sharing consent directly with Bank of America instead of your user ID and password, take that route. If you have already shared credentials, revoke through the Security Center in Online Banking and change your password — the notice recommends both.

availableActions.action: Correct inaccurate information through a human
availableActions.howTo: Use Contact Us on the site or app, call or write to the number and address on your account statements, or speak to a representative at a financial centre or your Financial Advisor.

reference.label: Making sure personal information is accurate

availableActions.action: If you are in California, use the separate CCPA notice
availableActions.howTo: The additional rights for California residents live in the California Consumer Privacy Act Notice, referenced twice from this document but not contained in it.

reference.label: How do we use your personal information?

availableActions.action: Withhold device permissions you do not need
availableActions.howTo: Geolocation and contact-list access are described as granted by you for specific features such as finding an ATM. Decline them at the operating-system level and the feature, not the account, is what stops working.

reference.label: How do we use your personal information?

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: The only stated mechanism is revising the Last updated date on the page. No notification is given, and consent is taken from continued use.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period for any category. Stated as the time required by law plus the necessary business purpose, though paired with a commitment to delete as soon as legally permitted.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: Browser opt-out preference signals are captured and treated as valid opt-out requests for sale and sharing, in addition to the DAA and NAI routes.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children under 13
requiredDisclosures.note: Sites are stated not to be marketed to under-13s; accounts with child access are owned by a parent or guardian and require specific consent. A separate Children's Privacy Policy is referenced.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Recipients are given only as categories — affiliates and subsidiaries, contracted third-party providers, government agencies. Merrill is the single named affiliate; the advertising companies are not named.

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of personal data collected
requiredDisclosures.note: Enumerated in detail, including Social Security number, driver's licence number, CVV2, credit and income information, device identifiers, geolocation and behavioural patterns.

requiredDisclosures.name: GLBA consumer privacy notice
requiredDisclosures.note: This is the online privacy notice, not the GLBA annual privacy notice, which Bank of America publishes as a separate document. Recording it absent here would be a claim about the wrong document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Sensitive personal information categories
requiredDisclosures.note: Social Security number, account credentials, precise geolocation and health information received at event registration are each identified, with health data handled under a dedicated paragraph.

requiredDisclosures.name: International transfer safeguards
requiredDisclosures.note: The notice covers U.S. online services for a U.S. audience and states information may be transferred to or processed in the U.S. Non-U.S. services are directed to their own policies.

analyses.summary: Booking.com's notice is well drafted — named data protection officer, Binding Corporate Rules, local representatives in four countries, call recordings deleted after 30 days by default, verification data not kept past verification. What it discloses inside that good drafting is a guest reputation score handed to every hotel you book: your cancellation percentage, your completed-booking count, and whether anyone has ever reported misconduct involving you. It also states that where a minor's data reaches the platform it may be retained to train AI systems, that public and social-media sources are searched about you when a complaint is raised, and that special-category data cannot be kept out of what that search returns. AI training runs on legitimate interest rather than consent, and no retention period is given for anything except call recordings.

exposures.title: The hotel is told your cancellation rate and whether anyone has reported you
exposures.whatItMeans: Alongside the reservation, Booking.com passes the trip provider a summary about you: whether your account is verified, whether you have booked with them before, how many reservations you have completed, the percentage you have cancelled, whether you leave reviews, and the absence of reports to Booking.com regarding misconduct involving you.
exposures.whyItMatters: That is a behavioural score on a traveller, disclosed to a business the traveller has no relationship with and cannot see the score from. The misconduct item is phrased as an absence, which means its non-appearance carries meaning too — a guest who has been reported has that fact communicated by omission.

reference.label: The trip provider you booked with
reference.quote: The absence of reports to Booking.com regarding misconduct involving you

exposures.title: A minor's data may be kept to train AI systems
exposures.whatItMeans: The service is not intended for under-18s and data collected about minors without valid parental consent is deleted on discovery. But where minors' data is provided, Booking.com states it may in limited circumstances retain and use it to test, train and improve its AI systems, under legal obligation or legitimate interest relating to content moderation.
exposures.whyItMatters: The deletion promise and the AI-training retention sit two paragraphs apart and point in opposite directions. A parent booking a family trip has no way to tell which applies to their child's record, and no consent is sought for the training use.

reference.label: How we treat personal data belonging to minors
reference.quote: we may in limited circumstances retain and use this personal data to test, train, and improve our AI systems

exposures.title: A complaint triggers a search of media and social media about you, and sensitive data comes back with it
exposures.whatItMeans: Where a safety or security concern arises, Booking.com may collect information about you from publicly available sources such as media reports or social media platforms and combine it with what it already holds. The notice adds that it cannot prevent some of that information containing special categories of personal data.
exposures.whyItMatters: Special categories means health, religion, sexual orientation, political opinion and the rest. The sentence is an unusually frank admission that an open-web search about a named traveller returns material the GDPR would otherwise require a specific lawful basis to touch — and the basis relied on is that the individual made it public themselves.

reference.label: Safety, security & fraud prevention
reference.quote: We cannot prevent that some of that information may contain special categories of personal data.

exposures.title: Your upcoming trip can be cancelled on Booking.com's own assessment
exposures.whatItMeans: Reservations may be stopped or held while an assessment runs, and where Booking.com has concerns about serious misconduct it may cancel your upcoming reservations and decline your future ones. The assessment draws on reports by others, public-source material and behavioural analysis.
exposures.whyItMatters: A cancelled hotel the night before a flight is a concrete loss, and the decision rests on a concern rather than a finding. No appeal route, evidence standard or notice period is described for it.

reference.label: Safety, security & fraud prevention
reference.quote: If we have concerns about serious misconduct, we may cancel your upcoming reservations or decline your future reservations via our platform.

exposures.title: AI training runs on legitimate interest, and objecting means writing in
exposures.whatItMeans: Training and optimizing AI models is listed as its own processing purpose, and it falls under the legitimate-interest basis rather than consent. If you want to object and no opt-out is available in your account settings, the notice directs you to contact the privacy team.
exposures.whyItMatters: Consent would mean the training does not happen until you agree; legitimate interest means it happens until you write in and win the argument. The contrast is inside the same document — AI memories are consent-based with a settings control, and model training is not.

reference.label: Legal bases for personal data processing
reference.quote: If you wish to object to the processing where we rely on legitimate interest and the use of AI systems and no opt-out mechanism is available to you directly... contact us

exposures.title: No retention period for anything except phone calls
exposures.whatItMeans: Retention is described by criteria — as long as necessary to provide services, detect fraud, meet accounting and tax law, and resolve claims. Actual periods appear only for call recordings and digital-assistant transcripts at 30 days by default, and insurance call recordings at up to 12 months.
exposures.whyItMatters: Reservation history, reviews, passport details added to an account and the behavioural profile built from browsing all fall under the criteria and none under a period. The two figures given show the drafters could state periods where they chose to.

exposures.title: Browsing is stitched across devices and sessions even when you are logged out
exposures.whatItMeans: For analytics and platform optimization, Booking.com may combine personal data collected during different visits, on different devices and on different Booking.com websites, expressly including when you are not logged in. Personalization separately links browsing activity across sessions and devices for account holders.
exposures.whyItMatters: Logging out is the control most people believe separates one session from the next. This says it does not, and the linking runs on legitimate interest rather than consent.

reference.label: Analytics, insights & market research
reference.quote: we may combine personal data we collect from you during different visits to our platform or visits on different devices or different websites of ours, even when you are not logged in

exposures.title: Your data moves across Agoda, Priceline and OpenTable for marketing
exposures.whatItMeans: Personal data is exchanged with other Booking Holdings companies — Agoda and OpenTable are named — for service delivery, fraud detection, analytics, personalized offers and marketing communications, relying on legitimate interest for most of those purposes.
exposures.whyItMatters: Booking a hotel on one brand feeds the marketing profile on brands the traveller may never have used, and the sharing basis for personalized offers is legitimate interest rather than the consent the marketing itself requires.

reference.label: Why we share personal data within the Booking Holdings Inc. group (BHI)

exposures.title: Your email and phone number are hashed and matched into advertisers' databases
exposures.whatItMeans: Identifiers such as email address and telephone number are hashed and shared with advertising partners so they can be matched against records those partners hold separately. Booking.com describes hashing as limiting what the recipient can do with the data.
exposures.whyItMatters: Hashing an email address does not de-identify it — it produces a stable key that matches the same person wherever else that address appears, which is precisely the point of the exercise. It is disclosed clearly, which is more than most peers manage.

exposures.title: You are made responsible for telling your travelling companions
exposures.whatItMeans: Booking for others means supplying their names, dates of birth and, for flights and some attractions, passport or national ID details. The notice places the duty to inform them on you.
exposures.whyItMatters: The people whose passport numbers are in the reservation never see this notice, have no account, and cannot exercise any of the rights it describes — the obligation to reach them is transferred to the person who booked.

reference.label: Personal data you give us about others
reference.quote: You're responsible for notifying others when you provide their information through our platform.

availableActions.action: Watch your cancellation rate — it follows you to the next hotel
availableActions.howTo: The percentage of reservations you have cancelled is passed to trip providers as part of the summary about you. Cancelling free-cancellation bookings speculatively is not costless in the way the refund suggests; it changes what the next property is told about you.

reference.label: The trip provider you booked with

availableActions.action: Manage or delete your AI memories, and withdraw consent for the feature
availableActions.howTo: AI memories are generated by a third-party model from your interactions and stored. Privacy settings let you view, manage and delete them and withdraw consent at any time — this is the one AI use in the notice with a direct control rather than an email request.

reference.label: AI memory: Remembering your key details to personalize your experience

availableActions.action: Object to AI training and other legitimate-interest processing in writing
availableActions.howTo: Where no setting exists, objection goes to the privacy team — which includes the Data Protection Officer — at dataprotectionoffice@booking.com, or by post to Oosterdokskade 163, Amsterdam. Ground transportation is a different controller with its own address at rentalcars.com. Include your country of residence.

availableActions.action: Decline analytical and marketing cookies, and expect to do it again elsewhere
availableActions.howTo: The option is offered through a cookie banner where required, so it may not appear in every jurisdiction. Browser settings work regardless. Functional cookies cannot be declined without losing sign-in and booking management.

availableActions.action: Do not add identification documents to your account for convenience
availableActions.howTo: Passport and ID details can be stored in the account so they need not be re-entered. Doing so puts them in a persistent record with no stated retention period, rather than in one reservation. Verification via passport and selfie is separate, and that data is stated not to be retained beyond verification.

availableActions.action: Unlink any social media account you connected
availableActions.howTo: Linking triggers data exchanges between Booking.com and the social platform in both directions. The notice states you can unlink at any time in account settings.

reference.label: Personal data and information about you we receive from other sources

availableActions.action: Unsubscribe from marketing across every channel it uses
availableActions.howTo: Marketing arrives by push notification, SMS, WhatsApp and other messaging apps, in-app notification and email. The unsubscribe link covers email; account settings cover the rest. Abandoned-booking reminders are part of this, not of transactional messaging.

availableActions.action: Use the Data Subject Request form, and escalate to a regulator if unsatisfied
availableActions.howTo: Access, correction, erasure, restriction, portability, consent withdrawal and objection are all offered, through account settings, the Data Subject Request form, email or post. Identity is verified by questions about past reservations. Booking.com is supervised by the Dutch Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens and the UK ICO, and names local representatives in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, South Korea and Turkey.

availableActions.action: Tell your travelling companions what you handed over
availableActions.howTo: The notice makes you responsible for informing them. For flights and some attractions this includes their passport or national ID details, which then travel to the trip provider and, for car rental pre-registration, to the rental company.

reference.label: Personal data you give us about others

availableActions.action: Decline car rental pre-registration — it is optional
availableActions.howTo: Pre-registration forwards your email, home address, phone, date and place of birth, passport and driver's licence to the rental company before you arrive. The notice states you can still collect the car without providing any of it.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: Criteria only for everything that matters — reservations, reviews, account data, stored identity documents, behavioural profiles. Actual periods are given only for customer-service call recordings and digital-assistant transcripts (30 days by default) and insurance call recordings (up to 12 months).

requiredDisclosures.name: Lawful basis for processing
requiredDisclosures.note: Set out as a table mapping each of ten purpose categories to contract, legitimate interest, legal obligation or consent, with the balancing test described and the legitimate interests enumerated.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data protection officer contact
requiredDisclosures.note: dataprotectionoffice@booking.com for Booking.com B.V. and Booking.com Distribution B.V., dataprotectionofficer@rentalcars.com for the ground-transportation controller, with postal addresses and named local representatives in four further countries.

requiredDisclosures.name: International transfer safeguards
requiredDisclosures.note: Binding Corporate Rules for intra-group transfers out of the EEA, Standard Contractual Clauses for third-party processors in non-adequate countries, equivalent mechanisms for the UK, and contract-necessity where the trip provider is outside the EEA.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automated decision-making rights
requiredDisclosures.note: States that no solely automated decision producing legal or similarly significant effects is currently made; where a decision could have significant effect — fraud monitoring is the example given — an automated system informs it but a person reviews and decides.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: Training and optimizing AI models is a legitimate-interest purpose with no opt-out mechanism described. Objection is possible but must be raised by contacting the privacy team. AI memories, by contrast, are consent-based with a settings control.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Where an update could significantly impact people, Booking.com states it will take steps to inform them before the change takes effect. No period is committed to, and lesser changes carry only a recommendation that you revisit the page.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: Analytical and marketing cookies can be declined via a banner, but only 'where required' — so the control is conditioned on jurisdiction rather than offered to everyone. Functional cookies are stated to be non-optional.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children's data
requiredDisclosures.note: Under-18 floor with deletion on discovery of processing without valid parental consent — qualified by the separate statement that minors' data may be retained to train AI systems in limited circumstances.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data subject rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Access, correction, erasure, restriction, portability, consent withdrawal and objection, with four routes to exercise them, identity verification by reservation history, and the supervisory authorities named.

analyses.summary: LinkedIn's user agreement is the most balanced set of terms in this corpus so far. There is no arbitration clause and no class-action waiver, changes cannot be retroactive and material ones come with notice and a chance to review, and the content licence ends when you delete the content. The costs are elsewhere: the licence is transferable and sublicensable while it lasts, Microsoft and GitHub are named affiliates receiving your data, an employer who bought your seat gets reports on your use, and everyone outside Europe litigates in Santa Clara County.

exposures.title: Your data flows to Microsoft and GitHub as named affiliates
exposures.whatItMeans: The licence you grant runs to LinkedIn 'and our Affiliates', and affiliates are defined to include Microsoft Corporation and any of its subsidiaries, with GitHub given as an example.
exposures.whyItMatters: Naming them is more transparent than most peers manage, but it means a professional profile sits inside the whole Microsoft group, not just LinkedIn.

exposures.title: An employer who bought your seat can monitor your use of it
exposures.whatItMeans: If a paid Service such as Recruiter or LinkedIn Learning was purchased for you by another party, that party has the right to control access to it and to get reports on your use of it. Your personal account remains yours.
exposures.whyItMatters: Course-taking and recruiting activity on an employer-funded seat is reportable to that employer, and the boundary between the paid seat and the personal account is easy to lose track of in daily use.

exposures.title: Expired cards keep being billed, and a backup card can be charged
exposures.whatItMeans: LinkedIn may store and continue billing your payment method even after it has expired, use it for other Services you buy, and automatically charge a secondary payment method if the primary one fails.
exposures.whyItMatters: Letting a card expire is how many people expect a subscription to end. This states that it will not, and that a spare card on file is a fallback for charges you did not direct to it.

exposures.title: The licence is transferable and sublicensable while it lasts
exposures.whatItMeans: You grant a worldwide, transferable and sublicensable right to use, copy, modify, distribute, publicly perform, display, host and process your content without further consent, notice or compensation.
exposures.whyItMatters: Deleting content ends the licence going forward, but not for anyone LinkedIn already sublicensed, anything others re-shared or stored, or anything it must retain by law.

exposures.title: Nothing you post is guaranteed to be kept
exposures.whatItMeans: LinkedIn states it is not a storage service and has no obligation to store, maintain or provide you a copy of any content you or others provide, beyond what law requires.
exposures.whyItMatters: Years of posts, articles and messages can disappear without recourse, and liability for loss of data is expressly excluded from the damages you could claim.

exposures.title: Liability is capped at fees paid or one thousand dollars
exposures.whatItMeans: Liability cannot exceed the greater of total fees you paid, if any, or US$1,000, and lost profits, lost business opportunities, reputational harm and loss of data are excluded entirely.
exposures.whyItMatters: Reputation and business opportunity are the specific things a professional network can damage, and both are named in the exclusion. The cap does not apply to death, personal injury, fraud, gross negligence or intentional misconduct.

exposures.title: Outside Europe, disputes go to Santa Clara County
exposures.whatItMeans: For everyone outside the Designated Countries — including all users outside the United States — California law governs exclusively and all claims may be litigated only in the federal or state courts of Santa Clara County, California.
exposures.whyItMatters: For a member in India or Brazil, the practical effect is similar to an arbitration clause: the forum is far enough away that most claims will not be brought. EU and EEA members keep their home courts and mandatory consumer protections.

exposures.title: Social actions can appear alongside advertising
exposures.whatItMeans: Ads may be served near your content, and your social actions — likes, comments, follows, shares — may be visible and included with ads. Your name or photo may be used to promote a feature within the Services.
exposures.whyItMatters: Your endorsement of something can be shown to your network as advertising context, though third-party sponsored content requires separate consent.
