availableActions.action: Delete content to end the licence on it
availableActions.howTo: Unlike Amazon's perpetual, irrevocable licence, LinkedIn's ends for specific content when you delete it, or generally when you close your account — subject to prior sublicensing, others' copies and legal retention.

availableActions.action: Cancel before the renewal date, and remove old cards
availableActions.howTo: Subscriptions charge automatically at the start of each period. Expired cards keep working, so cancelling is the only reliable stop; removing a secondary card prevents the fallback charge.

availableActions.action: Review changes during the notice window
availableActions.howTo: Material changes come with notice and an opportunity to review before they take effect, and the agreement states changes cannot be retroactive. Objecting means closing your account, but the window is real.

reference.label: 1.3 Changes
reference.quote: We agree that changes cannot be retroactive.

availableActions.action: Keep a personal account separate from any employer-purchased seat
availableActions.howTo: Reports on your use go to whoever paid for the paid Service. Your personal account is expressly outside their rights.

availableActions.action: If you are in the EU or EEA, sue at home
availableActions.howTo: Members in the Designated Countries may choose the courts of their country of habitual residence and keep their mandatory national consumer protections, rather than being routed to California.

requiredDisclosures.name: Arbitration clause
requiredDisclosures.note: There is none. Disputes go to courts — Santa Clara County for most of the world, home courts for EU and EEA members. No class-action waiver and no jury-trial waiver appear anywhere in the document, which makes this the least restrictive dispute posture in this corpus.

requiredDisclosures.name: Non-retroactivity of changes
requiredDisclosures.note: States plainly that changes cannot be retroactive, and commits to notice and an opportunity to review before material changes take effect.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named data controller
requiredDisclosures.note: LinkedIn Ireland Unlimited Company for the EU, EEA and Switzerland; LinkedIn Corporation elsewhere.

requiredDisclosures.name: Minimum age
requiredDisclosures.note: 16, raised where local law requires an older age for processing without parental consent.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automated decision-making disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: Recommendations, ranking and generative AI features are described, with a warning that generated content may be inaccurate and that the user is responsible for reviewing it.

analyses.summary: TikTok's terms take a perpetual, irrevocable, fully transferable licence to everything you post, waive your privacy, publicity and moral rights in it, and confirm you have no right to any income from it — while making you responsible for clearing the music rights and notifying your own performing rights organisation of the royalty-free licence you just granted on their behalf. Account deletion is irreversible and permanently destroys your content. Note this is the rest-of-world edition, which by its own terms does not cover India, the US, the EEA, the UK or Switzerland.

exposures.title: A perpetual, irrevocable licence to everything you post
exposures.whatItMeans: You grant an unconditional, irrevocable, non-exclusive, royalty-free, fully transferable, perpetual worldwide licence to use, modify, adapt, reproduce, make derivative works of, publish, transmit and distribute your content — and to authorise other users and third parties to do the same — in any format and on any platform, now known or hereafter invented.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the broadest content licence in the corpus. Irrevocable and perpetual means deleting the video does not end it; fully transferable means it can be sold to someone else; 'hereafter invented' means it covers formats that do not exist yet.

exposures.title: You waive your privacy, publicity and moral rights
exposures.whatItMeans: Posting content waives any right to prior inspection or approval of marketing or promotional material using it, waives all rights of privacy and publicity in connection with it, and commits you never to assert moral rights where they cannot be assigned.
exposures.whyItMatters: Your face and voice can appear in promotional material you never see beforehand, and the waiver of publicity rights removes the usual control a person has over commercial use of their likeness.

reference.label: Waiver of Rights to User Content

exposures.title: You clear the music rights, and you tell your PRO
exposures.whatItMeans: The licence expressly covers reproducing sound recordings and the musical works in them on a royalty-free basis, with no payment to labels, publishers, performing rights organisations, SoundExchange, unions, engineers or producers. If you are affiliated with a PRO you must notify it yourself; if you assigned rights to a publisher you must obtain its consent.
exposures.whyItMatters: The obligation to clear rights is pushed entirely onto the creator, including the duty to inform the organisation whose royalties you have just waived. The terms warn plainly that writing a song does not mean you have the right to grant this licence.

reference.label: Specific Rules for Musical Works and for Recording Artists

exposures.title: You cannot earn from your own content, here or anywhere
exposures.whatItMeans: TikTok may generate revenue from your use of the Services through advertising, sponsorships, promotions, usage data and Gifts, and you have no right to share in it. You also have no right to income from your own content, and are prohibited from monetising it on any third-party service — the terms use claiming your own video on YouTube as the example.
exposures.whyItMatters: The restriction reaches beyond TikTok's own platform to what you may do with your work elsewhere.

exposures.title: Your identity can be disclosed to anyone who complains
exposures.whatItMeans: TikTok reserves the right to disclose your identity to any third party claiming that content you posted violates their intellectual property or privacy rights.
exposures.whyItMatters: A claim is enough. There is no stated verification step, no notice to you, and no opportunity to contest before the disclosure.

reference.label: Waiver of Rights to User Content

exposures.title: Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone
exposures.whatItMeans: Account deletion goes through a support form rather than a setting, and once done you cannot reactivate the account or retrieve any content or information. Separately, TikTok may disable your account at any time in its sole discretion.
exposures.whyItMatters: The terms themselves recommend saving copies of your content locally, which is an admission that nothing on the platform is durable.

exposures.title: Content is analysed as it is sent, received and stored
exposures.whatItMeans: Automated systems analyse your content to provide customised search results, tailored advertising, and spam and malware detection, at the point of sending, receiving and storage.
exposures.whyItMatters: It covers content in transit as well as at rest, which includes material you sent to one person rather than published.

reference.label: 5. Your Access to and Use of Our Services

exposures.title: Notice of changes is best-effort only
exposures.whatItMeans: TikTok will use commercially reasonable efforts to generally notify users of material changes, but tells you to check the Terms regularly. Continued use after the new date is acceptance.
exposures.whyItMatters: 'Commercially reasonable efforts' to 'generally notify' is not a commitment to reach you, and the licence above is what you are re-accepting each time.

availableActions.action: Set your content to approved viewers only
availableActions.howTo: The privacy setting in the platform controls whether content is public or restricted to people you approve. It does not affect the licence you granted, but it limits who can extract and remix it.

availableActions.action: Keep local copies of everything you post
availableActions.howTo: The terms explicitly recommend this, because content can be removed or blocked with or without notice and deletion is irreversible.

availableActions.action: If you are a musician, check your PRO and publisher obligations first
availableActions.howTo: The terms place the duty on you to notify your performing rights organisation of the royalty-free licence and to obtain your publisher's consent before granting it. Posting first can put you in breach of your own contracts.

reference.label: Specific Rules for Musical Works and for Recording Artists

availableActions.action: Do not post anything you may want to monetise elsewhere
availableActions.howTo: The terms bar you from claiming your own uploaded content for monetisation on other platforms. Publish to the platform you intend to earn from first.

availableActions.action: Check which regional edition governs you
availableActions.howTo: This edition states it applies only if you are not in the US, EEA, UK, Switzerland or India. Jurisdiction-specific supplemental terms supersede these where they conflict, so the document you find first may not be the one that binds you.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Commits to commercially reasonable efforts to notify generally, plus a Last Updated date — weaker than a notice commitment but stronger than silence.

requiredDisclosures.name: Repeat infringer policy
requiredDisclosures.note: States accounts of repeat copyright infringers may be disabled or terminated in appropriate circumstances and at TikTok's discretion.

requiredDisclosures.name: Account deletion route
requiredDisclosures.note: Available, but through a support form rather than a self-service setting, and expressly irreversible with no content retrieval.

requiredDisclosures.name: Compensation for commercial use of content
requiredDisclosures.note: No compensation of any kind. The terms state TikTok may generate revenue from your content and that you have no right to share in it, and no right to income from the content itself.

requiredDisclosures.name: Right to contest identity disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: Identity may be disclosed to a third party on their claim alone, with no verification step, notice or opportunity to object described.

analyses.summary: Uber's rider privacy notice marks with an asterisk every data practice it does not perform in the EEA, UK or Switzerland — turning a two-tier privacy regime into a typographic convention. Among the asterisked items: buying enrichment data from data resellers, including your household income range, lifestyle, purchasing behaviour and streaming habits. It also collects facial verification biometrics, in-cabin video from autonomous vehicles, recordings of your calls, and dashcam footage that drivers submit about you.

exposures.title: An asterisk marks the privacy you do not get outside Europe
exposures.whatItMeans: The notice states that because of GDPR and related laws, Uber does not perform some of the described collections and uses in the EEA, UK or Switzerland, and that these are indicated with an asterisk. If you use Uber outside those regions, your data may be collected and used for every asterisked purpose.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the clearest statement of two-tier privacy in the corpus. It is not hidden — it is a documented convention, applied inline, so a reader anywhere else can count exactly which protections they are not receiving.

reference.label: European Economic Area, United Kingdom, and Switzerland
reference.quote: Uber does not perform some of the data collections and uses described in this notice in the EEA, UK or Switzerland. Such data collections and uses are indicated with an asterisk (*).

exposures.title: Outside Europe, your household income and streaming habits are bought in
exposures.whatItMeans: Among the asterisked practices: receiving data from data resellers, and enrichment data covering age range, household income range, gender, general interests and lifestyle, general purchasing behaviour, viewing preferences and streaming habits.
exposures.whyItMatters: A ride-hailing app knowing your household income bracket and what you stream has nothing to do with getting you across town, and it arrives from brokers rather than from you. Europeans are exempt from this by the notice's own convention.

reference.label: Marketing partners, advertisers, and service providers

exposures.title: Facial verification generates biometric data
exposures.whatItMeans: Identity verification collects government ID documents, user-submitted selfies and facial verification information — biometric data generated to confirm your identity, your age, or that the account is not being used by someone else. The selfie-versus-ID comparison is itself asterisked.
exposures.whyItMatters: A faceprint cannot be reissued after a breach, and the process is also used to check you are wearing a helmet when renting a bike, which extends biometric capture well past account security.

exposures.title: Cameras inside the car, and dashcams outside it
exposures.whatItMeans: In an autonomous vehicle, in-cabin cameras record video of you, and audio may be recorded when you contact support during a trip. Separately, Uber receives dashcam footage and Record My Ride videos of you submitted by drivers, and video shared by fleet partners.
exposures.whyItMatters: You are recorded inside a vehicle by two parties, one of which is another user whose submission you neither authorise nor see.

exposures.title: Your gender is inferred from your first name
exposures.whatItMeans: Demographic data includes gender or inferred gender, derived using your first name, collected to enable Women Rider Preference and for marketing and advertising.
exposures.whyItMatters: One of the two stated purposes is a safety feature; the other is advertising. The same unreliable inference serves both, and the marketing use is not separately consented to.

exposures.title: Precise location while the app is merely open
exposures.whatItMeans: Precise location is collected from the moment you request a ride or order until it is finished — and also whenever the Uber app is open on your phone's screen.
exposures.whyItMatters: Opening the app to browse restaurants, without ordering anything, is enough to log where you are.

exposures.title: People who never made an account are covered
exposures.whatItMeans: The notice applies to Guest Users — people receiving rides or deliveries booked by someone else, including through Uber Health, Uber for Business, gift cards or Uber Connect — and Uber receives their name, contact info, location and trip details from the account owner.
exposures.whyItMatters: A patient sent home from a clinic by Uber Health has a record created about them without ever agreeing to anything or having an account through which to object.

exposures.title: Calls and chats are recorded and transcribed
exposures.whatItMeans: Communications data includes audio recordings, recordings of phone calls, call transcripts and chat logs, covering both contact with support and messages with drivers and delivery people.
exposures.whyItMatters: Conversations with a driver, including about where you live and who you are visiting, are retained as transcribed text.

availableActions.action: Count the asterisks before deciding what to allow
availableActions.howTo: Every asterisked practice is one Uber has judged unlawful or inadvisable under GDPR. If you are outside Europe, they apply to you, and the notice makes them individually identifiable.

reference.label: European Economic Area, United Kingdom, and Switzerland

availableActions.action: Set location to 'while using', and close the app when you are done
availableActions.howTo: Precise location is collected whenever the app is open on screen, not only during a trip. Closing it fully is the difference between trip-scoped and browsing-scoped location history.

availableActions.action: In Quebec, demand human review of an automated decision
availableActions.howTo: Quebec residents may ask about the factors used in automated decision-making, request correction of the data behind it, and require review by Uber personnel. Elsewhere the notice offers no equivalent.

availableActions.action: Use your national data protection authority
availableActions.howTo: The notice names the regulator and route for Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Kenya, Saudi Arabia, Nigeria, Peru, South Korea, Taiwan, Türkiye and the EEA — a genuinely useful list of who to escalate to.

availableActions.action: Type your pickup address instead of sharing precise location
availableActions.howTo: The notice states you can use Uber without precise location; it is less convenient, not impossible.

requiredDisclosures.name: Jurisdiction-specific rights and regulators
requiredDisclosures.note: Eleven jurisdictions are addressed individually with named regulators and contact routes — the most thorough regional disclosure in this corpus.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data protection officer contact
requiredDisclosures.note: A DPO is named and contactable, with a Swiss representative additionally appointed under the Federal Act on Data Protection.

requiredDisclosures.name: Lawful basis for processing
requiredDisclosures.note: A dedicated section sets out legal bases, data controllers and the framework for international transfers.

requiredDisclosures.name: Equal treatment regardless of jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Expressly and systematically not equal. The asterisk convention marks each practice performed only outside the EEA, UK and Switzerland, including data-reseller enrichment and selfie-to-ID comparison.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automated decision-making rights outside Quebec
requiredDisclosures.note: The right to an explanation, correction and human review of automated decisions is set out for Quebec residents only; no equivalent is offered to users elsewhere.

requiredDisclosures.name: Biometric data retention
requiredDisclosures.note: Facial verification information is collected, but no retention period or deletion route specific to biometric data appears in the captured text.

analyses.summary: This is not a list of things Stripe does to you — it is a list of lawful businesses that cannot use Stripe, and the cost of being near a boundary is losing your payment processing. Both lists are declared non-exhaustive, the prohibited list ends with a catch-all for any business Stripe 'considers unfair, deceptive or predatory', and an approval granted after due diligence can be modified or revoked at any time. The India-specific list is the broadest of the eleven jurisdictions and prohibits charities, non-profits, religious organisations, lobby groups and political organisations outright — on the same page where Stripe says it does not restrict access based on political viewpoints. The document carries no date, no version history and no statement of what happens to settled funds when an account is closed.

exposures.title: Both lists are declared non-exhaustive, so compliance cannot be verified
exposures.whatItMeans: The prohibited and restricted lists are stated to be representative rather than complete. A business that appears on neither list still has no assurance it is permitted.
exposures.whyItMatters: You can read every word of this page, match nothing, build your product on Stripe, and still be found in breach. The standard you are held to is not the one published, which means the page cannot be used to make the decision it exists to inform.

reference.label: Prohibited Businesses
reference.quote: The types of businesses listed here are representative of prohibited categories, but this is not an exhaustive list.

exposures.title: A catch-all makes Stripe the sole judge of what is predatory
exposures.whatItMeans: The unfair-practices section closes with a category covering any other business Stripe considers unfair, deceptive or predatory towards consumers.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is a discretionary standard with no defined test, no examples bounding it and no review. Combined with the non-exhaustive framing, it means any account can be brought inside the prohibited list by a judgement made after the fact.

reference.label: Unfair, deceptive or abusive acts or practices
reference.quote: Any other businesses that Stripe considers unfair, deceptive or predatory towards consumers

exposures.title: Approval survives only as long as Stripe wants it to
exposures.whatItMeans: Restricted businesses go through additional due diligence and supply licences and business-model detail. The resulting approval is per service offer and can be modified or revoked by Stripe at any time.
exposures.whyItMatters: A pharmacy, a lender, a crowdfunding platform or a firearms dealer can complete Stripe's diligence, launch, and have the approval withdrawn later with no stated cause, notice period or appeal. The diligence buys entry, not stability.

reference.label: Restricted Businesses
reference.quote: the approval is specific to each service offer and it may be modified or revoked by Stripe at any time per the terms of the Stripe Services Agreement

exposures.title: In India the prohibited list covers charities, non-profits, religious and political organisations
exposures.whatItMeans: The India jurisdiction list — the one governing this /in/ edition of the page — prohibits charities, non-profit organisations, religious organisations, lobby groups and political organisations, alongside alcohol, dating services, currency exchange, vehicle sales, high-value goods and unlicensed financial institutions. It is the longest of the eleven jurisdiction lists at 22 categories.
exposures.whyItMatters: The page opens by saying Stripe does not restrict access based on political viewpoints or affiliation, and then bars an entire class of civic and religious organisations from the product in one country. Both statements are true as drafted, but a reader who stops at the stated principle will draw the wrong conclusion about whether Stripe will process their donations.

reference.label: Why this page exists
reference.quote: we do not restrict access to our services based on political viewpoints or affiliation

exposures.title: The list changes and the document carries no date
exposures.whatItMeans: The page opens with a banner announcing that the restricted and prohibited lists have been updated — in this capture, domestic charter air travel moving from prohibited to restricted in eight markets. There is no effective date, no version number, no change log beyond the current banner and no notice commitment for future moves.
exposures.whyItMatters: Movement in the other direction — restricted to prohibited — ends a business's ability to take payments. Nothing here says how much warning an existing merchant gets, or whether an account already operating in a category is grandfathered when the category moves.

reference.label: Update banner
reference.quote: We've made important updates to the list of restricted and prohibited businesses.

exposures.title: Twelve months of card inactivity closes a Stripe Issuing account automatically
exposures.whatItMeans: If no card on an Issuing account is used for twelve consecutive months, Stripe closes the Issuing account without any stated notice or reactivation route.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is a dormancy rule with account closure rather than a fee as the penalty. A business that issues cards seasonally, or holds a programme in reserve, loses it by doing nothing — and the document does not say what happens to balances or to cards in the field at closure.

reference.label: Prohibitions for Stripe Issuing products — Inactivity
reference.quote: If there is inactivity on all cards associated with an account for a period of 12 consecutive months, Stripe automatically closes your Issuing account.

exposures.title: Not updating your marketing copy fast enough can close the whole account
exposures.whatItMeans: Stripe's compliance teams may require changes to an Issuing user's marketing materials or user experience, and failure to comply within the requested timeframe may result in closure of the Stripe account — not just the Issuing product.
exposures.whyItMatters: The trigger is a missed deadline on a request whose timeframe Stripe sets, and the consequence reaches beyond the product the request concerned. A business using Stripe for its core payments as well as Issuing risks both on one compliance ticket.

reference.label: Prohibitions for Stripe Issuing products — Non-compliance
reference.quote: Failure to comply within the requested time frames might result in the closure of your Stripe account.

exposures.title: Individual creators are exempt from pre-approval but not from monitoring
exposures.whatItMeans: Content creators on approved platforms and those selling their own content do not need pre-approval, but remain bound by this list and are expressly subject to ongoing monitoring by Stripe for compliance.
exposures.whyItMatters: The exemption from paperwork is not an exemption from enforcement, and the prohibited categories it points back at include adult content — the largest single category of independent creator income. A creator whose work drifts across that line loses payment processing without ever having had an approval to revoke.

reference.label: Restricted Businesses — Content creation platforms
reference.quote: are subject to monitoring by Stripe to ensure compliance

availableActions.action: Read your country's list before the global one
availableActions.howTo: The Jurisdiction-specific prohibited businesses section overrides the general lists and differs sharply by country — India bars 22 categories, Thailand marks each as prohibited or restricted, the US bars only four. A business permitted in one Stripe market can be prohibited in yours.

availableActions.action: Get approval in writing before launching in a restricted category
availableActions.howTo: Restricted businesses are told to expect additional information requests — licences, business-model detail — at account creation. Raise it before you build rather than at the first transaction, and keep the approval and its scope, since it is granted per service offer.

reference.label: Restricted Businesses
reference.quote: you will be asked to provide additional information (such as proof of relevant licences or more details about your business model) to confirm your eligibility to use Stripe

availableActions.action: Keep your registered business details current
availableActions.howTo: The prohibited-uses section requires immediate notification of any change to personal or business information, and misdescribing the nature of the business is itself a prohibited use. Stale details are a breach independent of what you sell.

reference.label: Prohibited Uses of Stripe Products
reference.quote: If there are any changes to your personal and business information, you must notify Stripe immediately

availableActions.action: Find out what happens to your money before you need to
availableActions.howTo: This page states the grounds for closing an account and says nothing about settled funds, reserves or payout holds — those sit in the Stripe Services Agreement, which it repeatedly defers to. Read that document's fund-hold and reserve terms alongside this list, because they are the half that determines the cost of being on the wrong side of it.

availableActions.action: Use an Issuing card at least once a year to keep the programme open
availableActions.howTo: Twelve consecutive months with no activity on any card closes the Issuing account automatically. A single transaction inside the window prevents it.

reference.label: Prohibitions for Stripe Issuing products — Inactivity

availableActions.action: Keep a second processor available if you are near a boundary
availableActions.howTo: Restricted-category approval is revocable at any time and the list itself moves without notice. For a business in a restricted category the only real mitigation is not depending on a single acquirer, since neither the standard nor the timing is yours to control.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: The page announces that the lists have just changed and gives no effective date, no version history and no commitment to notify merchants before a category moves. Breach of the changed list is grounds for account closure, so the absence of a notice period converts an edit to a web page into an immediate compliance event for existing merchants.

requiredDisclosures.name: Non-retroactivity of changes
requiredDisclosures.note: Nothing states how a merchant already operating in a category is treated when that category moves from restricted to prohibited, or when the catch-all is applied to a model previously accepted. No grandfathering, transition period or wind-down route is offered.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer complaint route
requiredDisclosures.note: There is no appeal or review process for a prohibited or restricted determination. The only routes offered are a generic 'contact us' link and, for several restricted categories, 'contact our sales team' — a commercial channel, not a redress one. For a decision that ends a business's ability to take payments, no escalation path is published.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: This is the /in/ edition, and Stripe operates in India as a regulated payment intermediary. No grievance officer, nodal officer, address or response-time commitment appears anywhere in the document, which is the corpus's most common Indian-compliance absence.

requiredDisclosures.name: Treatment of funds on account termination
requiredDisclosures.note: New name — the payments_fintech fund-hold and reserve question, recorded against the document that creates the termination grounds. This page sets out every basis on which an account can be closed and states nothing about settled balances, reserves, payout holds or chargeback exposure after closure, deferring entirely to the Stripe Services Agreement it references but does not summarise.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: The document creates obligations enforceable by account closure and names no governing law, no forum and no Stripe contracting entity. It refers to 'the acquiring Stripe entity' in the cross-border acquiring prohibition without identifying which entity that is for an Indian merchant.

requiredDisclosures.name: Equal treatment regardless of jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: The page states a principle of not restricting access on political viewpoint or affiliation, then applies eleven country-specific prohibition lists that differ by an order of magnitude — India bars 22 categories including charities, non-profits, religious organisations, lobby groups and political organisations; the United States bars four, none of them civic. The principle is stated globally and the practice is not, and the document does not reconcile them.

analyses.summary: Amazon's privacy notice is broad by design: it covers physical stores using cameras and computer vision, Alexa voice recordings, synced Wi-Fi credentials, Social Security and driver's licence numbers, credit-bureau history, and your full click-by-click path through the site. Data is used to develop and deploy generative AI models, with no opt-out described. It carries one genuinely unusual commitment in the other direction — a promise never to weaken protections for past data without consent.

exposures.title: Your data develops Amazon's generative AI models, with no opt-out here
exposures.whatItMeans: Personal information is used with machine learning and artificial intelligence across products and services, expressly including developing and deploying generative AI models and services.
exposures.whyItMatters: Unlike several peers in this corpus, this notice describes no training opt-out. It points to a separate Generative AI Development Disclosure, so whether a control exists cannot be determined from the document that announces the practice.

reference.label: For What Purposes Does Amazon Use Your Personal Information?
reference.quote: This includes using data to develop or deploy our generative AI models and services.

exposures.title: Physical stores watch you with cameras and computer vision
exposures.whatItMeans: Amazon's physical stores may use cameras, computer vision, sensors and other technology to gather information about your activity in store, including which products and services you interact with. Collected examples include images or videos when you shop in Amazon stores or stores using Amazon Services.
exposures.whyItMatters: This extends the same profile from browsing into the physical world, and it reaches third-party stores that merely use Amazon's technology — where a shopper has no reason to expect Amazon is involved at all.

exposures.title: Government ID numbers, credit history and Wi-Fi credentials
exposures.whatItMeans: Collected information includes Social Security and driver's licence numbers, credit history from credit bureaus, corporate and financial information, and device Wi-Fi credentials if you sync them across Amazon devices.
exposures.whyItMatters: Credit history is also used for scoring methods to assess and manage credit risk, so a retail relationship carries a credit assessment. Synced Wi-Fi credentials mean Amazon holds the password to your home network.

exposures.title: Every scroll, click and mouse-over is recorded
exposures.whatItMeans: Automatic collection includes the full URL clickstream to, through and from Amazon's websites with dates and times, products viewed or searched, page response times, length of visits, and page interaction such as scrolling, clicks and mouse-overs.
exposures.whyItMatters: Clickstream from before and after your visit means the record extends beyond Amazon's own pages, and interaction-level detail is closer to session recording than to page analytics.

exposures.title: Hashed identifiers link you to ad companies
exposures.whatItMeans: Ad companies receive an advertising identifier — a cookie, a device identifier, or a code derived by applying irreversible cryptography to information such as your email address — plus an estimated value of the ads shown to you. Some of those companies use it to serve you ads from other advertisers.
exposures.whyItMatters: A hashed email is still a stable identifier for the same person across services, so 'we never share your name' and 'you are identifiable' can both be true at once.

exposures.title: Changes are your responsibility to notice
exposures.whatItMeans: The notice states the business changes constantly, so the privacy notice will change too, and you should check the websites frequently. Unless stated otherwise, the current notice applies to all information already held about you.
exposures.whyItMatters: There is no notification and the new version applies retroactively to data already collected — though the commitment below meaningfully limits how far that can go.

reference.label: Conditions of Use, Notices, and Revisions

exposures.title: Privacy disputes go to Washington law and the damages caps in the Conditions of Use
exposures.whatItMeans: Any dispute over privacy is subject to the Conditions of Use, including its limitations on damages, dispute resolution provisions, and Washington state law.
exposures.whyItMatters: The privacy notice does not stand alone: the remedies for a privacy failure are whatever the separate Conditions of Use allow.

reference.label: Conditions of Use, Notices, and Revisions

availableActions.action: Sign out and block cookies to browse unlinked
availableActions.howTo: The notice states that signing out of your account and blocking cookies lets you browse without the history being linked to your account. That is an explicit, documented route most peers do not offer.

availableActions.action: Edit browsing history and turn items off for recommendations
availableActions.howTo: Improve Your Recommendations lets you remove individual items from personalisation with a per-item toggle, and Your Browsing History is directly editable.

availableActions.action: Adjust Your Ads Privacy Choices
availableActions.howTo: The notice links a dedicated page for personalised and cross-context behavioural advertising opt-out, separate from browser cookie settings.

availableActions.action: Do not sync Wi-Fi credentials across devices
availableActions.howTo: Automatic Wi-Fi credential synchronisation is opt-in per device. Turning it off keeps your network password out of the collection described here.

availableActions.action: Use Data Privacy Queries to request access or deletion
availableActions.howTo: Where applicable law provides the right, access and deletion requests go through the Data Privacy Queries page. The notice warns some services may be limited afterwards.

requiredDisclosures.name: Commitment not to weaken protections retroactively
requiredDisclosures.note: A genuinely strong and uncommon commitment: Amazon states it will never materially change its policies to be less protective of information already collected without the consent of affected customers.

requiredDisclosures.name: EU-US Data Privacy Framework participation
requiredDisclosures.note: Participation in the EU-US framework plus the UK Extension and the Swiss-US framework is declared.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children under 13
requiredDisclosures.note: States no knowing collection from under-13s without parental consent, with a separate Children's Privacy Disclosure.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No retention period is stated for any category. The notice adds that when you update information a copy of the prior version is usually kept.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: Use of personal data to develop and deploy generative AI models is disclosed, but no opt-out or control appears in this document. A separate Generative AI Development Disclosure is referenced.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: The notice states Amazon is not in the business of selling personal information, but no sale-or-share opt-out link appears here; it is deferred to Your Ads Privacy Choices and the state-specific disclosures.

analyses.summary: Eternal's policy covers Zomato, Blinkit, District and Hyperpure, and reaches further into your phone than any other document in this corpus. It collects which other applications are present or absent on your device, accesses metadata for photographs, audio, video and your address book, states plainly that the mobile identifiers it uses instead of cookies cannot be deleted, names data brokers among its sources, and makes you indemnify the company if the contacts you uploaded did not consent.

exposures.title: It records which other apps are on your phone
exposures.whatItMeans: Across Zomato, Blinkit, District and Hyperpure, the company may collect information about the presence, the absence, and details of other applications on your mobile phone.
exposures.whyItMatters: Your installed-app list describes your finances, health, politics, dating life and religion more precisely than your food orders ever could. The stated justification is enabling payment and UPI links, which needs far less than presence-and-absence of everything.

reference.label: Mobile status
reference.quote: we may collect information about the presence and/ or absence and/ or details pertaining to other applications on your mobile phone

exposures.title: The identifier used to track you cannot be deleted
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy states that on mobile it may use device IDs rather than cookies to recognise you, store preferences and track your use — and that, unlike cookies, mobile device IDs cannot be deleted.
exposures.whyItMatters: It is a rare admission that the tracking mechanism is deliberately chosen for being outside your control. Clearing data, clearing cookies and reinstalling do not reset it.

reference.label: Computer and device information
reference.quote: Unlike cookies, mobile device IDs cannot be deleted.

exposures.title: You indemnify the company for the contacts it collected from you
exposures.whatItMeans: If you upload or grant access to your contact list, you warrant that you obtained explicit informed consent from every person in it, and you agree to indemnify Eternal against any claim arising from your failure to do so.
exposures.whyItMatters: Nobody obtains written consent from their whole address book before tapping allow. The company collects the data and the legal exposure for collecting it lands on the user.

exposures.title: Your photos, audio and address book metadata are reachable
exposures.whatItMeans: The applications may access metadata and other information associated with files stored on your mobile device, including photographs, audio and video clips, personal contacts and address book information.
exposures.whyItMatters: Photo metadata carries location and timestamps for places you have been that have nothing to do with ordering food.

exposures.title: Data brokers are a named source
exposures.whatItMeans: Information may be obtained from business partners, marketing and advertising partners, data enrichment services, data brokers, analytics providers, researchers, publicly available sources and other users — and the company expressly reserves the right to combine all of it with what it collects from you directly.
exposures.whyItMatters: Most policies in this corpus avoid the phrase. Naming data brokers as an input, and reserving the right to merge that with your order history to 'identify potential new customers', is unusually direct.

exposures.title: Precise GPS is tied to your device ID
exposures.whatItMeans: Location-enabled services collect GPS latitude, longitude and altitude with timestamps, and the policy states this location data may be associated with your device ID and other information held about you.
exposures.whyItMatters: Combined with the undeletable device identifier above, a continuous location history attaches to a key you cannot reset.

exposures.title: CCTV at offices and events, including vehicle details
exposures.whatItMeans: Images and video of individuals attending events or visiting office premises are collected via CCTV, capturing images, vehicle information and other identifying details, plus photographs and video at events for promotional use.
exposures.whyItMatters: It extends the same profile into physical spaces, and event attendees are not generally told a food-delivery company's privacy policy governs the footage.

exposures.title: Refusing any of it can mean no service
exposures.whatItMeans: Using the services is agreement and informed consent to everything described, and if you do not provide the information required, Eternal and its platforms may decline to provide services to you. Changes take effect on continued use, with no notice.
exposures.whyItMatters: Consent is a precondition rather than a choice, and the document it consents to can change silently.

availableActions.action: Deny contacts permission — and protect yourself from the indemnity
availableActions.howTo: The contact-book indemnity only attaches if you upload or grant access. Declining at the operating-system level keeps both your contacts and your legal exposure out of it.

availableActions.action: Reset your advertising ID at the device level
availableActions.howTo: The policy is correct that mobile device IDs cannot be deleted, but Android and iOS both let you reset the advertising identifier, which breaks continuity for ad targeting even where the hardware ID persists.

availableActions.action: Set location to 'while using the app', never 'always'
availableActions.howTo: Precise GPS is only needed while you are ordering. Restricting it stops the continuous history that would otherwise attach to a non-resettable identifier.

availableActions.action: Deny photo and file access
availableActions.howTo: File metadata for photos, audio and video is reachable through app permissions. Ordering food does not require it.

availableActions.action: Do not use Google or Facebook sign-in
availableActions.howTo: Third-party authentication hands over your third-party user ID, profile picture, and contacts or friend lists subject to permissions. An email registration avoids that entirely.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data of minors
requiredDisclosures.note: Unusually careful: a minor's data provided by an adult is limited to the specific purpose and expressly not used to build a profile, market to, or otherwise secondarily process the minor.

requiredDisclosures.name: Scope of covered individuals
requiredDisclosures.note: States the policy covers customers, merchant partners, delivery partners, event participants, employees, contractors and interns — broader and clearer than most.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: Not present in the captured text. India's IT Rules require a named officer with contact details; the policy refers to 'grievance redressal mechanisms' without naming one.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Changes take effect on continued use with no notification; the policy tells you to check it periodically.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent withdrawal mechanism
requiredDisclosures.note: Consent is given by use and required for service, but no route to withdraw it for the device, location, contacts or data-broker processing appears in the captured text.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period appears in the captured text for any category, including CCTV footage and location history.

analyses.summary: American Express India's KYC page handles Aadhaar better than any other document in this corpus: it is one of six equally acceptable officially valid documents, never the default, and all ten places it is listed instruct you to mask the first eight digits. Around that good handling the page has three problems. It asks its own question — what if I have no officially valid document with my current address — and answers it by reprinting the same list, so a tenant without a passport, licence, voter ID or Aadhaar has no route at all. It tells you to email certified copies of those identity documents to addresschange@aexp.com from your registered address, an ordinary mailbox, while the secure upload portal is offered only in a different section. And it discloses that Amex failed to collect address proof for changes made between February 2019 and April 2020, then asks the affected customers to fix it. Nothing on the page states how long the documents are kept, who receives them, or what happens to your card if you do not send them.

exposures.title: Identity documents are collected by ordinary email
exposures.whatItMeans: For address changes and for the 2019-2020 remediation, the stated submission route is emailing a certified or self-attested copy of an officially valid document from your registered email address to addresschange@aexp.com, with post or courier as the alternative. A secure upload portal at americanexpress.com/in/docupload exists but is offered only in the current-address-collection section.
exposures.whyItMatters: Passport, driving licence, voter ID and Aadhaar scans are the exact material identity fraud runs on, and email delivers them in plain text through servers neither party controls, leaving a permanent copy in your sent folder and in the recipient mailbox. The bank has a secure channel and does not route these submissions through it.

reference.label: KYC documents required for address change — How do I submit the required documents?
reference.quote: You may send the certified copy of the Officially Valid Document (OVD) from your registered email ID to addresschange@aexp.com

exposures.title: The question about having no valid document is answered with the same list
exposures.whatItMeans: The page asks 'If I do not have any Officially Valid Document (OVD) containing current address, can I submit any other alternate documents?' and answers by restating that an OVD is mandatory under the RBI Master Directions and reprinting the same six documents. Utility bills and bank statements are refused, twice, in their own separate question.
exposures.whyItMatters: Renters, people who have recently moved, and people whose documents carry an old address are exactly who asks that question, and the page has no answer for them. RBI's Master Direction on KYC treats certain other documents, a recent utility bill among them, as a deemed officially valid document for proof of address for a limited period pending an OVD update. That route is not mentioned, so the page reads as a closed door where the regulation leaves one ajar.

reference.label: KYC documents required for address change — question 3
reference.quote: As per the RBI Master Directions, an Officially Valid Document (OVD) is a mandatory requirement for making any change to the Current Residential address.

exposures.title: Amex asks customers to repair its own records gap
exposures.whatItMeans: A dedicated section states that address changes requested between 13 February 2019 and 15 April 2020 were processed without address proof being collected, and asks those customers to now send a self-attested officially valid document.
exposures.whyItMatters: The failure to collect the document was the bank's, and the work of correcting it — locating the document, attesting it, emailing it, waiting fourteen days — falls entirely on the customer, with no statement of what happens to the account if they do not. It is a candid disclosure, and the burden it creates is one-directional.

reference.label: KYC documents required for address change remediation
reference.quote: Our records indicate that you had requested a change of address between 13th February 2019 and 15th April 2020 for which address proof was not collected.

exposures.title: Provisional address proof expires in three months and the page never says what follows
exposures.whatItMeans: Where a card was approved on provisional residence documents, those are valid for only three months from approval and a current-address OVD must be submitted. The page states the requirement and gives the upload route, but nowhere states the consequence of not completing it.
exposures.whyItMatters: RBI permits regulated entities to restrict operation of an account where periodic KYC updating is not completed. A cardholder reading this page learns there is a deadline but not that missing it can freeze the card, so the one fact that would make them act is the one omitted.

reference.label: KYC documents required for current address collection
reference.quote: You previously provided us with provisional documents (residence address proof) which are valid only for a period of 3 months from the date of approval for your Card.

exposures.title: A representative may come to inspect your original documents
exposures.whatItMeans: A single footnote states that an American Express representative may contact you in order to see and verify the original of the document you uploaded.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the only description of what happens after submission, it appears as an unnumbered footnote, and it commits you to an in-person or telephone verification by someone the page does not identify, at a time it does not bound.

reference.label: Footnotes
reference.quote: An American Express Representative may contact you in order to see and verify the original OVD uploaded by you.

exposures.title: The page carries no date and no version
exposures.whatItMeans: There is no last-updated line, no effective date and no version marker anywhere in the document, though it cites an RBI circular from 2015-16 and describes a remediation exercise for 2019-2020.
exposures.whyItMatters: The document tells you which identity papers a bank will accept, which is exactly the kind of list that moves when the regulator moves. With no date there is no way to tell whether you are reading the current requirement or one superseded years ago.

availableActions.action: Use a non-Aadhaar document — the page treats all six equally
availableActions.howTo: Passport (first and last pages), driving licence (front and back), Voter ID from the Election Commission, NREGA job card signed by a state government officer, or a National Population Register letter are each accepted on their own. Aadhaar is listed as one option among six and is never required.

reference.label: What are the KYC documents required to apply for a Credit/Charge Card?

availableActions.action: Mask the first eight digits if you do submit Aadhaar
availableActions.howTo: Every mention of Aadhaar on this page instructs masking the first eight digits, which is what the RBI Master Direction requires of a redacted proof of possession. Redact before you send, not after.

reference.label: Officially Valid Document list
reference.quote: Proof of possession of Aadhaar (please Mask first 8 digits of the Aadhaar number)

availableActions.action: Send documents through the upload portal instead of email
availableActions.howTo: americanexpress.com/in/docupload takes TIF, TIFF, JPEG, BMP, GIF or PNG up to 10 MB and needs the reference number from the Amex email titled 'Please submit KYC documents'. The page recommends it for faster processing; use it for address changes too rather than the addresschange@aexp.com mailbox.

reference.label: KYC documents required for current address collection — How do I submit the required documents?

availableActions.action: Declare no change instead of resubmitting documents at KYC refresh
availableActions.howTo: Where nothing about your KYC, demographic or financial information has changed, you can give a declaration to that effect rather than sending documents again. Call 1800 180 1188 toll-free or +91 124 2801188, Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 5:00 pm.

reference.label: Can I provide Self-Declaration to the Bank for completing my KYC refresh

availableActions.action: Skip the document entirely for a correspondence address at your office
availableActions.howTo: Updating a correspondence address to an office address needs no officially valid document — call the helpline number on the back of the card. Only the current residential address triggers the OVD requirement.

reference.label: If I would like to change/update my correspondence address to my office address

availableActions.action: Expect fourteen days, and chase after that
availableActions.howTo: A maximum of 14 calendar days from receipt of the document is stated for updating the residential address, with a confirmation sent if the document met the requirement. If no confirmation arrives, escalate through the published grievance ladder rather than resubmitting.

deadline.description: Fourteen calendar days from receipt of the officially valid document for the address to be updated on file.

reference.label: What is the time taken for the Address to be updated?
reference.quote: A maximum of 14 Calendar Days from the date of receipt of Officially Valid Document (OVD) will be taken to update the Current Residential Address on File.

availableActions.action: Carry a marriage certificate or gazette notification if your name changed
availableActions.howTo: A document remains an officially valid document after a name change only if supported by a state-issued marriage certificate or a gazette notification. The page makes this mandatory for address changes, so assemble it before submitting rather than after a rejection.

requiredDisclosures.name: Aadhaar Act compliance and alternatives
requiredDisclosures.note: The best handling in the corpus. Aadhaar appears as one of six officially valid documents in every list, never as the default and never alone, and all ten of its appearances carry the instruction to mask the first eight digits — the redacted proof-of-possession form the RBI Master Direction and the Aadhaar Act permit a bank to hold. Five genuine non-Aadhaar alternatives are offered, including the NREGA job card and the National Population Register letter, which are the routes available to people without a passport or licence.

requiredDisclosures.name: Identity verification and KYC documents
requiredDisclosures.note: Enumerated separately for five scenarios — new application, periodic updation, address change, current address collection and the 2019-2020 remediation — each with the acceptable document list, the submission channel and, for address changes, a fourteen-day turnaround. PAN or Form 60 and a photograph are stated for applications. The RBI circular relied on is cited by number (DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16).

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period is stated for any of it. The page collects passport, licence, voter ID and Aadhaar copies and says nothing about how long the copies are held, where, or when they are destroyed. RBI's Master Direction requires KYC records to be kept for five years after the relationship ends; the customer is told none of that.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: The page does not name or describe a single recipient of the documents it collects. RBI-regulated entities are required to upload KYC records to the Central KYC Records Registry, so these documents leave the bank by regulation, and nothing on the page says so.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: The document carries no last-updated line, no effective date and no version marker at all — a stronger absence than the stale dates elsewhere in this corpus, since there is nothing to compare against. Its subject is a regulator-driven document list that changes when the Master Direction changes.

requiredDisclosures.name: Company identification details
requiredDisclosures.note: American Express Banking Corp., DLF Cyber City, DLF Building No. 8, Tower C, DLF City Phase II, Gurgaon 122002, with the toll-free 1800 180 1188 and landline +91 124 2801188 and their Monday-to-Friday 8:30 to 5:00 hours repeated at the foot of each section.

requiredDisclosures.name: Error resolution procedure and timeframes
requiredDisclosures.note: Partially. Fourteen calendar days is committed for the address update itself, with confirmation sent when the document meets the requirement. There is no stated route or timeframe for a rejected document, and no statement of what a customer does when their only address proof is one of the refused types.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: This page is a document checklist and gives a helpline rather than a grievance contact. American Express India publishes a dedicated grievance redressal policy naming a Head of Customer Service, Nodal Officer and Principal Nodal Officer with direct contacts, captured separately in this corpus as 887b98bf. Recording an absence here would be a claim about the wrong document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer complaint route
requiredDisclosures.note: Nothing on the page tells a customer what to do if their document is refused or their address is not updated within fourteen days. The only contacts given are a general helpline and a submission mailbox, and the separately published grievance ladder is not linked from here.

analyses.summary: Dropbox publishes the most specific cookie disclosure in this corpus: a table giving, per category, the exact data elements collected, the expiry range, and the third parties involved by name. That specificity is also what makes two things visible that most policies hide — cookies classified as strictly necessary can last five years, and the 'performance and functionality' bucket collects your email address and prior support-chat history.

exposures.title: Cookies called strictly necessary can last five years
exposures.whatItMeans: The strictly-necessary category — the one that cannot be refused — has expiry times ranging from 30 days up to 5 years.
exposures.whyItMatters: A five-year identifier is a durable way to recognise the same browser long after any session ended. Because the category is exempt from consent, this is the longest-lived tracking you cannot decline.

reference.label: Strictly necessary cookies
reference.quote: These cookies are set to expire after times ranging from 30 days to 5 years.

exposures.title: Functionality cookies collect your email and past chat history
exposures.whatItMeans: The performance and functionality category collects website usage data, previous help centre or chat history, email address, and a unique ID.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is directly identifying data sitting in a category most people accept as harmless convenience, and it is shared with a third party, SnapEngage.

reference.label: Performance and functionality
reference.quote: Categories of data collected for these purposes include website usage data, previous help center or chat history, email address, and unique ID.

exposures.title: Cross-website tracking data goes to advertising partners
exposures.whatItMeans: Marketing cookies collect cross-website tracking data and advertisement conversion data, with Adobe, Marketo and Google named; social advertising cookies involve Facebook, X and LinkedIn.
exposures.whyItMatters: Your browsing beyond Dropbox informs the advertising you see, and the recipients include the three largest social advertising networks.

reference.label: General marketing and advertising
reference.quote: Categories of data collected for these purposes include cross-website tracking data, browser information, version data, and advertisement conversion data.

exposures.title: Do Not Track signals are ignored
exposures.whatItMeans: Dropbox states its systems do not respond to DNT:1 signals from browsers, citing the absence of an agreed standard.
exposures.whyItMatters: A browser-level refusal has no effect here. The policy does honour Global Privacy Control, which is the signal with legal force in several US states, so the practical gap is narrower than it first reads.

reference.label: Browser settings
reference.quote: our systems currently don’t respond to DNT:1 signals from browsers visiting our websites

exposures.title: One policy covers four different products
exposures.whatItMeans: The article applies to Dropbox, Dropbox Sign, DocSend and FormSwift websites, each of which has its own separate privacy policy.
exposures.whyItMatters: Cookie practice is unified while the privacy commitments are not, so what happens to the data afterwards depends on which of four documents governs the product you used.

availableActions.action: Turn on Global Privacy Control in your browser
availableActions.howTo: Dropbox states it recognises and respects GPC. Unlike Do Not Track, which it ignores, this one takes effect and needs no account.

availableActions.action: Use the Cookies & CCPA Preferences link
availableActions.howTo: Linked in the page footer under Support and throughout the site, this is a real per-category consent control — not an email request.

availableActions.action: Contact the Data Protection Officer for the underlying data
availableActions.howTo: privacy@dropbox.com is published for questions about data collected through cookies.

requiredDisclosures.name: Cookie categories, data elements, retention and recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: The strongest disclosure in this corpus: per-category tables giving purpose, exact data elements, expiry ranges and named third-party providers.

requiredDisclosures.name: Granular consent control for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: The Cookies & CCPA Preferences link provides per-category consent from the footer of every page.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: An opt-out is offered through the same preferences link, alongside a statement that personal information is not sold.

analyses.summary: This is the same Meta privacy policy that governs Facebook, served to Instagram in US English rather than British English. The substance is identical — collection from people with no account, message content and metadata, camera-roll and voice input, public content used to develop AI at Meta for Meta and third parties, and retention decided case by case with no period for anything. It is a separate document only because 'Centre' became 'Center'.

exposures.title: Information is collected about you with no account at all
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy states that when you use Meta products, some information about you is collected even if you do not have an account, and that content others share or reshare about you is processed.
exposures.whyItMatters: Every control this policy offers — Privacy Checkup, ad preferences, download, delete — requires an account. Collection and remedy are not offered to the same set of people.

reference.label: What information do we collect?
reference.quote: When you use our Products, we collect some information about you even if you don't have an account.

exposures.title: Your public content develops Meta's AI, and third parties' too
exposures.whatItMeans: Information used to develop and improve AI at Meta includes public content that you or others create or share, and your interactions with AI features and their metadata. The stated purpose covers Meta Products and third parties.
exposures.whyItMatters: Photos and captions posted long before generative AI existed are training material now, and no opt-out appears in the policy text.

reference.label: Developing and improving AI at Meta

exposures.title: Message content and metadata are processed
exposures.whatItMeans: Messages you send and receive, including their content, and metadata about content and messages are used for personalisation, product provision and safety — each qualified with 'subject to applicable law'. Manual human review is used in some cases.
exposures.whyItMatters: Direct messages are named alongside public posts as an input, and the limit is whatever local law imposes rather than a commitment made here.

exposures.title: One Accounts Centre merges your WhatsApp identity
exposures.whatItMeans: Adding a WhatsApp account to an Accounts Centre with other Meta accounts associates them and shares your information with WhatsApp. Information, infrastructure and systems are shared across the Meta Companies.
exposures.whyItMatters: The separation people assume between a photo-sharing account and an encrypted messenger is a settings choice, presented as a convenience.

exposures.title: Behavioural signals down to mouse movement
exposures.whatItMeans: Device information includes what you are doing on your device — whether the app is in the foreground, whether your mouse is moving — plus device identifiers, signals, GPS location and network information.
exposures.whyItMatters: The stated purpose is distinguishing humans from bots, but it is a continuous behavioural record held against your identity.

exposures.title: Camera roll, voice and support selfies
exposures.whatItMeans: Collected content includes what you provide through the camera feature or camera-roll settings, through voice-enabled features, and a photo or video selfie supplied when contacting support.
exposures.whyItMatters: A selfie given to recover an account enters the same processing described for personalisation and safety, with no separate handling or retention stated.

exposures.title: Retention is case by case, with no period for anything
exposures.whatItMeans: Information is kept as long as needed, decided case by case, and in some instances kept for an extended period.
exposures.whyItMatters: Not one category — messages, AI interactions, the support selfie — has a stated end date, and every criterion is defined by Meta.

reference.label: How long do we keep your information for?

availableActions.action: Run Privacy Checkup
availableActions.howTo: A guided walkthrough of the privacy settings, linked from the policy. Fastest route to the settings that change what is collected and shown.

availableActions.action: Keep WhatsApp out of your Accounts Centre
availableActions.howTo: The merge is opt-in. Not adding WhatsApp to an Accounts Centre with your Instagram account is what keeps the identities separate.

availableActions.action: Download your information before deleting anything
availableActions.howTo: Port, download and delete tools are linked from the policy. Download first — deletion is not reversible and extended retention applies in some cases.

reference.label: Port, download or delete your information

availableActions.action: Review connected apps and websites
availableActions.howTo: Integrated partners receive information about you and your activity, and can always access what is public. Connections are revoked here.

availableActions.action: Use the material-change notice window
availableActions.howTo: Meta commits to notice before material changes with an opportunity to review before continuing — a real window, better than most peers here.

reference.label: How will you know that the Policy has changed?

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Notice before material changes with an opportunity to review the revised policy before continuing.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data subject tools
requiredDisclosures.note: Access, portability, download and deletion offered as in-product tools rather than email requests.

requiredDisclosures.name: No sale of personal information
requiredDisclosures.note: States it does not sell any information to anyone and never will.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period for any category; retention decided case by case with unspecified extended preservation.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: Public content and AI-feature interactions develop AI at Meta for Meta and for third parties, with no opt-out described in the policy text.

analyses.summary: At 213,097 characters this is the largest document in the corpus, and its size buys real disclosure: it names its third-party ad and analytics recipients, names a Data Protection Officer with a postal address and phone number, extends its data-subject rights to everyone regardless of location, and promises prominent notice before a material change takes effect. What it does not do is state a single retention period for anything general — the section gives criteria and then says periods 'can vary significantly'. It buys demographic data and contact information from data brokers, says it may use your data to train and fine-tune its AI models including LLMs with no opt-out attached to that statement, and targets ads on your Copilot conversations 'including files you share'. If your account came from an employer, a school, or your cable company, that party can read the contents of your files and communications and change your privacy settings above your head — and creating a personal Microsoft account with a work email address extends the employer's reach to the personal account too. In 213,097 characters the word 'sell' appears exactly once, in a promise not to sell K-12 student data; the statement never says whether adult consumer data is sold.

exposures.title: Your employer or school reads your files and sets your privacy settings
exposures.whatItMeans: For any Microsoft product used with a work or school (Microsoft Entra ID) account, the organization can access and process the interaction data, diagnostic data, and the contents of the communications and files associated with the account. On a managed Windows device the organization additionally uses centralized management tools to control device settings including privacy settings, device policies, software updates and data collection.
exposures.whyItMatters: Every control described in the rest of this 213,097-character statement can be switched off above your head by your employer, and the statement routes your privacy requests to that administrator rather than to Microsoft. Microsoft states expressly that it is not responsible for the organization's privacy or security practices.

reference.label: Windows — managed devices
reference.quote: your organization may use centralized management tools provided by Microsoft or others to access and process your data (including your interaction data, diagnostic data, and the contents of your communications and files), and to control device settings (including privacy settings)

exposures.title: A personal account made with a work email is reachable by the employer
exposures.whatItMeans: The Microsoft account section states that if you use a work or school email address to create a Microsoft account — a personal account, not an Entra ID one — your organization may access the data associated with it.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the employer-administrator category reaching past the boundary a user thinks they drew. Someone who deliberately keeps a separate personal Microsoft account, but registered it with the address they had at the time, has no notice of this anywhere in the product. The document also warns that changing employers can cost you access to products or content bought with that account.

reference.label: Microsoft account — work or school account
reference.quote: If you use a work or school email address to create a Microsoft account, your organization may access your data associated with your Microsoft account.

exposures.title: Your cable company can hold and delete your Microsoft account
exposures.whatItMeans: A 'third-party account' is a Microsoft account created by you or by a service provider such as a cable or internet provider, tied to an email address on that provider's domain. The statement says the service provider has control over the account, including the ability to access it or delete it.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the reseller arm of the administrator category, and it is longer here than at Google or Zoom: the party holding the account is an ISP the user chose for broadband, is not named anywhere, and its powers include deletion. Microsoft's only instruction is to go read that provider's own terms.

reference.label: Microsoft account — third-party account
reference.quote: Your service provider has control over your account, including the ability to access or delete your account.

exposures.title: For enterprise products, a contract you have never seen overrides this statement
exposures.whatItMeans: Where an organization's agreement with Microsoft for Enterprise and Developer Products conflicts with this privacy statement, the agreement controls. That covers Microsoft 365, Azure, Dynamics 365, Intune and the professional services sold alongside them.
exposures.whyItMatters: The employee whose data is processed is not a party to that agreement and cannot read it. For the products most working adults use every day, this document is a default that a private contract can displace in any direction, and the user has no way to find out which terms actually govern their data.

reference.label: Enterprise and developer products
reference.quote: In the event of a conflict between our privacy statement and the terms of any agreement(s) between a customer and Microsoft for Enterprise and Developer Products, the terms of those agreement(s) will control.

exposures.title: AI training is stated broadly; the opt-out is scoped to Copilot and to some markets
exposures.whatItMeans: The How we use personal data section says Microsoft may use your data to develop, train and fine-tune its AI models including large language models, with no opt-out attached. A narrower opt-out appears in the Copilot section, covering conversation data only and qualified as available 'in some markets'.
exposures.whyItMatters: The broad statement and the narrow control do not line up. A user who finds and uses the Copilot opt-out has stopped one input in one product in some countries; the general training permission over 'your data' across Windows, Office, Bing, Edge and Xbox is unaffected, and whether the Copilot control exists at all depends on where you live.

reference.label: How we use personal data — Product development / Artificial Intelligence and Copilot capabilities
reference.quote: In some markets, this data can help train our AI models in Microsoft Copilot unless you opt out.

exposures.title: Ads are targeted on your Copilot conversations and the files you share into them
exposures.whatItMeans: Microsoft commits that it does not use email, human-to-human chat, video calls, voice mail, or your documents and photos in storage to target ads. The Advertising section then lists Copilot conversations, expressly including files you share, among the current interactions ads may be shown against.
exposures.whyItMatters: The reassurance and the practice sit four paragraphs apart. A document uploaded to Copilot for help with a draft is a file, and the not-for-ads promise about files stops at the storage boundary rather than at the file. There is no separate control for it; it falls under general personalized-ads opt-out.

reference.label: Advertising
reference.quote: Ads may be shown that relate to the current interaction you are having with us, such as your Copilot conversations (including files you share)

exposures.title: No general retention period anywhere in 213,097 characters
exposures.whatItMeans: The retention section lists three criteria — purpose, sensitivity of the data, and legal obligations — and then states that actual periods vary significantly and defers the numbers to product documentation outside this statement.
exposures.whyItMatters: Nothing in the general section is falsifiable. Four narrow features do carry a number — deleted Outlook.com mail for roughly 7 plus 30 days, the Bing Experience Improvement Program at 18 months, Edge cross-web search activity at one year, and a closed account at 60 days — which shows Microsoft can state a period when it chooses to, and did not for anything covering the bulk of the collection.

reference.label: How we use personal data — Our retention of personal data
reference.quote: actual retention periods can vary significantly.

exposures.title: Microsoft buys data about you from data brokers
exposures.whatItMeans: The list of third-party sources Microsoft receives data from opens with data brokers, from which it purchases demographic data and contact information to supplement what it collects directly. The list also includes user-generated content services, publicly available academic and commercial data sets, and joint-marketing partners.
exposures.whyItMatters: None of the in-product controls the statement describes reaches a purchase made from a third party — you cannot opt out of a transaction you were not part of. It is disclosed plainly, which makes it countable, and it puts Microsoft in the same category the corpus already found at Uber.

reference.label: Personal data we collect — third-party sources
reference.quote: Data brokers from which we purchase demographic data and contact information to supplement the data we collect.

exposures.title: Teams holds a record on you if any user has you in their address book
