exposures.whatItMeans: Under 'Notice to non-user contacts', if your details appear in the device or Outlook address book of a Teams user who enables contact syncing, Microsoft processes your data to determine whether you are a Teams user, stores your information on its servers for as long as that user keeps syncing, and periodically re-checks whether you have since joined.
exposures.whyItMatters: This builds and maintains a record about a person who has never used Microsoft Teams, never agreed to this statement, and has no account through which to see or delete it. The record's lifetime is controlled by a third party's phone settings. It is the pattern the corpus already found at Robinhood, OpenAI and Flipkart, here running on a contact list rather than a signup form.

reference.label: Microsoft Teams — Notice to non-user contacts
reference.quote: your information will be stored on our servers, and we will periodically process your information as a part of the Teams user’s contact syncing experience to check whether you have subsequently joined Teams.

exposures.title: Clearing your Bing history does not clear Microsoft's search logs
exposures.whatItMeans: The privacy dashboard and Bing Settings let you review and clear your search terms and clicked results. The statement says plainly that this removes them from your search history and does not delete the information from Microsoft's search logs, which are retained and de-identified.
exposures.whyItMatters: The control that looks like deletion is a view-clearing control. The user is told, which is more than most, but the disclosure sits one sentence after the paragraph describing the control, and nothing in the dashboard UI carries it.

reference.label: Bing — Managing search history
reference.quote: does not delete information from our search logs, which are retained and de-identified as described above

exposures.title: The search-suggestion control does not exist in the Windows search box
exposures.whatItMeans: Search suggestions send the characters you type and what you click to Microsoft as you type. The statement gives instructions to turn the feature off in Bing and in Microsoft Edge, then states it cannot be turned off in the search box in Windows 10 and Windows 11.
exposures.whyItMatters: Keystroke-level transmission from the operating system's own search box is not optional, on the OS most of these users cannot leave. A control offered in the browser and withheld in the OS is a narrower version of the same asymmetry the enterprise-contract clause creates.

reference.label: Bing — Search suggestions
reference.quote: Search suggestions cannot be turned off in the search box in Windows 10 and Windows 11.

exposures.title: A voice-activated app answers to anyone in the room, on a locked device
exposures.whatItMeans: Voice activation can run while the device is locked and the screen is off. Once an app is woken by its keyword it may keep listening, and the statement says it may be activated by anyone speaking near the device with the same capabilities and information available as when the device is unlocked. Separately, it states that turning voice activation off does not stop third-party desktop apps from listening to the microphone.
exposures.whyItMatters: The lock screen is the boundary most people rely on, and this says a voice keyword crosses it for whoever is standing there. The residual disclosure — that the off switch does not bind third-party desktop apps — means the control the statement offers does not describe the state of the machine.

reference.label: Speech, Voice Activation, Inking, and Typing — Voice activation
reference.quote: The app may be activated by anyone who speaks near the device and have access to the same set of capabilities and information as when the device is unlocked.

exposures.title: Xbox hands game publishers a broad profile, and uninstalling is the only way to stop it
exposures.whatItMeans: Any publisher of a game or network-connected app you use gets your Xbox user identifier, gamertag, country and age range, data about your in-game communications, any Xbox enforcement activity against you, gameplay sessions, presence, time played, rankings, avatars, friends lists, club memberships, and anything you create in the app. The stated way to stop it is to remove the game from every device you installed it on.
exposures.whyItMatters: Your moderation record travels to third parties you have no relationship with, and the remedy is to stop playing the game. Publishers process this under their own policies, which the statement tells you to go and read separately. A partial revocation route at microsoft.com/consent is offered for 'some' publisher access, without saying which.

reference.label: XBOX — data shared with game and apps publishers and developers
reference.quote: To stop sharing game or app data with a publisher, remove its games or app from all devices where you have installed them.

exposures.title: Your gamertag and leaderboard scores are public and cannot be hidden
exposures.whatItMeans: Xbox privacy settings let you limit who sees your activity, content and statistics, but the statement carves out gamertag and leaderboard scores as public with no setting to hide them. Other players' game clips can capture your in-game character, gamertag and, depending on their settings, your audio chat; and if any party member enables voice-to-text captioning, all voice in the party is captioned.
exposures.whyItMatters: A persistent public handle plus a public score is a durable identifier a user cannot retract, and the capture and captioning features mean another participant's setting determines whether your speech is recorded or transcribed.

reference.label: XBOX — data viewable by others
reference.quote: Your gamertag and scores that show on game leaderboards are considered public and cannot be hidden.

exposures.title: Xbox safety review covers voice, video and in-game conversations
exposures.whatItMeans: To enforce the Community Standards for Xbox, Microsoft may collect and review voice, text, images, videos and in-game content, including uploaded clips, conversations you have, and posts in clubs and games. Elsewhere the statement describes hash-matching scanning across products and sharing with NCMEC and law enforcement.
exposures.whyItMatters: Voice chat between friends is inside the review surface, not outside it. The purpose is one most users support; the scope is broader than 'reported content' and carries no stated retention or appeal route.

reference.label: XBOX — Safety
reference.quote: we may collect and review voice, text, images, videos and in-game content

exposures.title: Family Safety records how you drive
exposures.whatItMeans: Enabling Drive Safety uses your location to record driving habits — whether you stay within speed limits, whether you use your phone while driving, and whether you accelerate or brake suddenly — and uploads those reports to the cloud, where they can be shared with the family group.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is telematics of the kind insurers buy, generated inside a family-controls product and typically enabled by the account organizer rather than the driver. The statement retains only the last known location for Location Sharing, but says nothing about how long drive reports persist.

reference.label: Microsoft Family Safety
reference.quote: your location will be used to record your driving habits, such as whether you are driving within the speed limits, if you’re using your phone while driving, and if you accelerate or brake suddenly.

exposures.title: Your disk encryption key is escrowed to your Microsoft account by default
exposures.whatItMeans: When Windows device encryption is on, the BitLocker recovery key generated for a personal device is automatically backed up online and tied to your personal Microsoft account. Microsoft states it does not use individual recovery keys for any purpose.
exposures.whyItMatters: Full-disk encryption whose key is held by the vendor has a different threat model from full-disk encryption whose key is held only by you: the key is reachable by anyone who can compel or compromise the Microsoft account. The commitment not to use the keys is a promise about Microsoft's own conduct, not about who else can reach them.

reference.label: Security and safety features — Device encryption
reference.quote: The BitLocker recovery key for your personal device is automatically backed up online and associated with your personal Microsoft account.

exposures.title: Optional diagnostics can send parts of the file you had open when something crashed
exposures.whatItMeans: Optional (Full) diagnostic data adds enhanced error reporting, which includes the memory state of the device at the moment of a system or app crash — which the statement notes may unintentionally contain user content, such as parts of a file you were using. It also adds Edge browsing history and search terms, and which programs run and for how long.
exposures.whyItMatters: The setting is presented as helping Microsoft fix bugs, and does that; the disclosure that document contents can ride along is inside a parenthesis in a bullet list. Required diagnostic data cannot be turned off at all, and on a managed device your organization decides the level.

reference.label: Windows — Diagnostics, optional diagnostic data
reference.quote: which may unintentionally contain user content, such as parts of a file you were using when the problem occurred

exposures.title: Anyone sharing your saved card can see what you bought
exposures.whatItMeans: If a payment method is saved to an account used by you and other Microsoft account holders, your purchase receipts may be available to anyone else who uses that payment method to buy from Microsoft.
exposures.whyItMatters: A shared family card turns your purchase history into a household record without any setting having been changed. For gifts, medical or personal purchases, and for anyone in a controlling relationship, that visibility is the whole exposure.

reference.label: Reasons we disclose personal data
reference.quote: your purchase receipts may be available to anyone else who uses and has access to the same payment method to make a purchase from Microsoft.

exposures.title: A device administrator can locate the machine even after you refused location to every app
exposures.whatItMeans: Find my device lets an administrator of a Windows device locate it from account.microsoft.com, and the statement says it works even if other users on that device have denied location access to all their apps. The user sees a notification when a lookup happens. Separately, emergency calls share precise location regardless of your location settings, and desktop apps have no per-app precise-location control at all.
exposures.whyItMatters: On a shared or family PC the person who set the machine up outranks the person using it on the one setting most people believe is theirs. The notification is after the fact.

reference.label: Location services — Find my device
reference.quote: This feature will work even if other users have denied access to location for all their apps.

exposures.title: Feedback you submit can reach your administrator, or the public
exposures.whatItMeans: Feedback Hub submissions made with a work or school account may be associated with your organization and viewable by its administrators. The statement then adds that regardless of which account you use, your feedback may be publicly accessible depending on your organization's settings, and that Microsoft may share feedback and related data with device manufacturers and firmware developers.
exposures.whyItMatters: The second sentence detaches the exposure from the account choice: a personal-account submission can still be made public by settings held by an organization. Bug reports routinely contain screenshots, file paths and, on HoloLens, camera and microphone capture.

reference.label: Feedback Hub
reference.quote: your feedback may be publicly accessible depending on your organization’s settings.

exposures.title: Several ad protections depend on where you live, and one depends on keeping a cookie
exposures.whatItMeans: Microsoft honours the Global Privacy Control signal 'in certain jurisdictions'. Turning off Personalized offers in Windows also stops cross-product data being used for those offers only 'in some regions such as the European Economic Area' — elsewhere you must separately visit the ads page. Cookie consent is obtained 'where required'. And a signed-out ad opt-out is stored as a browser cookie valid for five years that dies when you clear cookies.
exposures.whyItMatters: The same product gives materially different privacy outcomes to two users who did the same thing, and a user cannot tell from the document which side of the line they are on. The cookie-based opt-out is the sharper case: routine browser hygiene silently re-enables personalized advertising, and nothing tells you.

reference.label: Advertising — Opting Out / Windows Personalized offers
reference.quote: In some regions such as the European Economic Area, turning off Personalized offers on Windows also stops the use of data from other Microsoft products to personalize tips, ads, and recommendations in Windows.

exposures.title: OneDrive contents are indexed, and a shared link is transferable by whoever receives it
exposures.whatItMeans: Microsoft indexes the contents of your OneDrive documents so they are searchable. Content stored in a folder inherits that folder's sharing permissions, and a share link forwarded by its recipient gives the next person access to your content even though you never chose to share it with them.
exposures.whyItMatters: Content-level indexing of a private drive is a broader processing claim than storage, and the link behaviour means access control is delegated to the good behaviour of every recipient. Revocation exists but requires you to notice.

reference.label: OneDrive
reference.quote: we index the contents of your OneDrive documents so that you can search for them later.

availableActions.action: Keep your personal life off any work, school or ISP-issued account
availableActions.howTo: An Entra ID work or school account gives the organization your files and communications and control of your privacy settings; a provider-issued account gives your ISP the power to access or delete it. Neither has a user-side override. Also avoid creating a personal Microsoft account with a work email address — the statement says the employer may reach that account's data too.

reference.label: Microsoft account — work or school account, third-party account

availableActions.action: Opt out of personalized ads in two separate places, while signed in
availableActions.howTo: The Personalized ads and offers page covers Microsoft's own personalization; the Third-party ad settings page is a separate opt-out covering sharing with partners including Xandr, Yahoo, Facebook and The Trade Desk. Sign in first: a signed-out opt-out is stored as a cookie that is lost whenever you clear cookies. In Windows, also turn off the advertising ID in Settings, which is a distinct control from both.

availableActions.action: Turn off the Copilot AI-training opt-out if your market has one
availableActions.howTo: The Copilot section says conversation data may train Microsoft's AI models 'in some markets' unless you opt out, with the control described in the Copilot FAQ and the privacy dashboard. Note that this reaches Copilot conversation data only; the general statement that Microsoft may use your data to train and fine-tune its models has no opt-out attached.

availableActions.action: Send required diagnostic data only
availableActions.howTo: In Windows Settings under Diagnostics & feedback, decline optional (Full) diagnostic data — that is the level that adds Edge browsing history and search terms, which programs you run, and crash memory dumps that can contain parts of open files. Required data cannot be turned off. The Diagnostic Data Viewer shows exactly what your device sends.

availableActions.action: Turn off online speech recognition and voice activation, and check what is left
availableActions.howTo: Both are Windows privacy settings. Device-based recognition still powers captions, Narrator and voice access without sending audio to Microsoft. The statement warns that third-party desktop apps may still listen to the microphone after voice activation is off, so also review per-app microphone permissions in Windows Settings.

reference.label: Speech, Voice Activation, Inking, and Typing

availableActions.action: Use the privacy dashboard, and know what it does not reach
availableActions.howTo: The dashboard covers browsing, search, location and Copilot activity tied to your Microsoft account, and lets you view, export and delete. It does not delete Bing search logs, does not reach data held under an organization's contract, and the statement says plainly that not all personal data Microsoft processes is controllable through these tools — for the rest you must use the privacy support and requests page.

reference.label: How to access and control your personal data

availableActions.action: Cut the Xbox publisher and visibility exposure where you can
availableActions.howTo: Set Xbox online safety and privacy settings on the console or Xbox.com to limit what is shared with the public and with friends; try microsoft.com/consent to revoke some publisher access. Accept that gamertag and leaderboard scores are public with no setting, and that the only complete way to stop a publisher receiving your data is to uninstall its game everywhere.

reference.label: XBOX — data viewable by others; data shared with publishers

availableActions.action: Turn off Family Safety location features, including Drive Safety
availableActions.howTo: Location Sharing, Drive Safety, Share Drives, Places and Location Alerts are each switchable in Family Safety settings, and device location data can be managed on the privacy dashboard. Drive Safety is the one that generates a driving-behaviour record.

availableActions.action: Decide deliberately about the BitLocker recovery key
availableActions.howTo: Windows device encryption backs the recovery key up to your Microsoft account automatically. If you do not want Microsoft holding a key to your disk, remove the escrowed key from your account devices page and store it yourself — accepting that losing it means losing the data.

reference.label: Security and safety features — Device encryption

availableActions.action: Export before you close, and use the 60-day grace period
availableActions.howTo: Download OneDrive files, Outlook.com mail from Privacy and data settings, Skype chat history by request, and Teams data via the export page. After you request closure the account is marked for deletion and permanently deleted 60 days later, so the window to change your mind is fixed and finite. Authenticated deletion requests are processed within 30 days.

deadline.description: A closed Microsoft account is marked for deletion and permanently deleted 60 days later; that is the window to recover it or retrieve anything not already exported.

reference.label: Collection of data from children — account closure

availableActions.action: Contact the Data Protection Officer, or go over Microsoft's head
availableActions.howTo: The privacy support and requests page carries a 'Contact the Microsoft privacy team or the Microsoft Data Protection Officer' route, with a 30-day response commitment. Postal contacts are given for Microsoft Corporation in Redmond and Microsoft Ireland Operations Limited in Dublin, plus a US toll-free number, a Brazilian LGPD route and a Swiss representative. You can also complain directly to your data protection authority, and DPF complaints Microsoft cannot resolve go to the relevant EU/UK/Swiss authority or to binding arbitration.

reference.label: How to contact us
reference.quote: We will respond to questions or concerns within a period of no longer than 30 days

availableActions.action: Withdraw consent, and object to legitimate-interest processing
availableActions.howTo: The statement grants these rights regardless of your location: withdraw any consent at any time, object at any time to direct marketing, and object to or restrict processing done in the public interest or under legitimate interests. Cookie consent is withdrawn via 'Manage cookies' in the website footer.

reference.label: How to access and control your personal data
reference.quote: Microsoft provides you with the following data protection rights regardless of your location

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No general period is stated. The retention section gives three criteria and says actual periods 'can vary significantly', deferring durations to product documentation outside this document. GDPR Art 13(2)(a) allows criteria where a period is not possible, but Microsoft states a period elsewhere when it chooses to — Outlook.com deleted mail (~7 days in the folder, up to 30 days after), Bing Experience Improvement Program (18 months), Edge cross-web search activity (one year), closed accounts (60 days) — which shows the general silence is a choice.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: Present but doubly scoped: it covers Copilot conversation data only, and only 'in some markets'. The broader statement that Microsoft 'may use your data to develop, train, and fine-tune our AI models, including large language models (LLMs)' sits in How we use personal data with no opt-out and no market qualifier. Copilot Health is the counter-example — data uploaded there is expressly not used to train generative AI models and not used for advertising.

requiredDisclosures.name: No sale of personal information
requiredDisclosures.note: The word 'sell' occurs exactly once in 213,097 characters, in the K-12 education commitment 'not sell or rent student personal data'. The statement never says whether adult consumer personal data is sold or shared for value; the CCPA-facing answer is deferred to a separate U.S. State Data Privacy Notice not covered by this document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: No 'Do Not Sell or Share' link or mechanism appears in this document. The nearest thing is a 'Share my data with third parties for personalized ads' toggle honoured on receipt of a Global Privacy Control signal 'in certain jurisdictions'. US state rights are routed to a separate U.S. State Data Privacy Notice with its own notice-at-collection details.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Unusually strong for this corpus, and the opposite of Google's posture. Advertising recipients are named — Xandr, Yahoo, Facebook, The Trade Desk, Media.net, Outbrain, Taboola — as are eleven analytics providers with opt-out links (Adjust, AppsFlyer, Clicktale, Flurry, Google Analytics, Kissmetrics, Mixpanel, Nielsen, Acuity Ads, WebTrends, Optimizely), alongside a maintained third-party cookie inventory. Vendors, affiliates and game publishers remain categories.

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of personal data collected
requiredDisclosures.note: Enumerated at length: name and contact, credentials, demographics, payment, subscription, interactions, device and usage, error reports, bot usage, interests, content consumption, searches and commands, voice, text and inking, images, contacts and relationships, traffic data, social data, location, biometric, other input, file and message content, and video/audio recordings at Microsoft premises — then extended per product across roughly forty product sections.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Among the stronger commitments in the corpus: the last-updated date is revised, changes are described on a Change history page, and for material changes — including a change of processing purpose inconsistent with the original — Microsoft commits to 'provide prominent notice of the change before it takes effect', rather than the continued-use-is-acceptance model used almost everywhere else.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named data controller
requiredDisclosures.note: Microsoft Corporation, and for the EEA, UK and Switzerland, Microsoft Ireland Operations Limited, both with postal addresses and telephone numbers. Microsoft Schweiz GmbH is named as the Swiss Art. 14 representative.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data protection officer contact
requiredDisclosures.note: A named DPO route exists — 'Contact the Microsoft privacy team or the Microsoft Data Protection Officer' on the privacy support page — plus a postal address addressed to the Data Protection Officer at Microsoft Ireland Operations Limited, Dublin, with a phone number, and a 30-day response commitment. The individual is not named, which is the only gap.

requiredDisclosures.name: International transfer safeguards
requiredDisclosures.note: The most detailed in the corpus: nineteen data-centre countries named, standard contractual clauses cited by name, EU-U.S. DPF, UK Extension and Swiss-U.S. DPF certifications with onward-transfer liability accepted, adequacy decisions referenced, escalation to the relevant EU/UK/Swiss authority for unresolved complaints, binding arbitration for residual DPF complaints, and FTC enforcement jurisdiction acknowledged.

requiredDisclosures.name: Lawful basis for processing
requiredDisclosures.note: Consent, necessity for the products used, contractual and legal obligations, security and safety, and legitimate interests — with an express statement that legitimate interests are balanced against the individual's rights and freedoms and dropped where outweighed.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent withdrawal mechanism
requiredDisclosures.note: Stated as a right held regardless of location: 'If Microsoft obtained your consent to use your personal data, you can withdraw that consent at any time.' Cookie consent is withdrawn through 'Manage cookies' in the site footer; marketing consent through the communication permissions page or a web form for people without an account.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data subject rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Information, access, erasure, rectification, portability, objection and restriction, granted 'regardless of your location' rather than only to EU residents. The stated limits are legal ones and, materially, organizational ones: where an employer, school or service provider administers your account, the statement routes you to them instead.

requiredDisclosures.name: Equal treatment regardless of jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Present for data-subject rights, which are extended to everyone regardless of location — rare in this corpus. It does not hold for three controls: the Global Privacy Control signal is honoured only 'in certain jurisdictions'; turning off Personalized offers in Windows also stops cross-product personalization only 'in some regions such as the European Economic Area'; and the Copilot AI-training opt-out exists only 'in some markets'. Cookie consent is obtained 'where required'.

requiredDisclosures.name: Sensitive personal information categories
requiredDisclosures.note: No categories of sensitive personal information are defined and no right to limit their use appears. The single statement is advertising-scoped and negative — Microsoft Advertising does not process data qualifying as 'sensitive data' under US state law for personalized advertising — while the document elsewhere describes collecting biometric data, precise geolocation, uploaded personal health records and wearable data in Copilot Health, and voice recordings. Contrast Google, which defines the categories in its key terms.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automated decision-making rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Automated processing is disclosed in several places — personalization, ad targeting, fraud and piracy detection, automated safety and content-removal decisions, and age-appropriate experience gating that can 'change your settings or access to certain features' if age verification fails. No right to human review, explanation, or contest of an automated decision is stated anywhere, and Xbox enforcement activity is disclosed to game publishers.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children under 13
requiredDisclosures.note: Parental or guardian consent required below 13 or a higher local age, revocable at any time; child accounts auto-joined to the consenting adult's family group; parental view and delete of browsing, search, location and app usage on the privacy dashboard; Xbox child accounts default to the most restrictive settings with optional diagnostics off; no personalized advertising to anyone under 18; authenticated deletion requests processed within 30 days.

requiredDisclosures.name: Biometric data consent
requiredDisclosures.note: Collection is stated to depend on the products used and on consent. Windows Hello stores a derived template rather than the image of a face, fingerprint or iris; the verification data never leaves the device and is user-deletable in Settings. HoloLens iris sign-in stays on the headset. Photos legacy face grouping is on-device and off unless enabled.

requiredDisclosures.name: Biometric data retention
requiredDisclosures.note: Windows Hello biometric verification data 'remains on your device until you remove it', with a re-confirmation prompt after a significant period of inactivity — a retention rule expressed as a condition rather than a number, and one of the few retention statements in the document that is actually operative.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: Consent is obtained before placing optional cookies that are not strictly necessary or communication-facilitating, separated by purpose (advertising, analytics, social media), withdrawable via 'Manage cookies' in the footer. Qualified throughout by 'where required', so the mechanism's availability tracks jurisdiction. Named cookies with purposes are listed, including NAP, which holds an encrypted country, postal code, age, gender, language and occupation.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer complaint route
requiredDisclosures.note: A 30-day response commitment, an express right to complain to a data protection authority, DPF escalation to the EU/UK/Swiss authorities with binding arbitration for residual complaints, FTC oversight acknowledged, a US toll-free number for state privacy rights, an LGPD route for Brazil, a Telecommunications Business Act notice for Japan, and a next-of-kin route for deceased users' accounts.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: This capture is the US/Canada edition of the statement (sourceUrl is the en-us Privacy Statement; the chooser landed on the Canadian page). The Indian IT Rules 2021 grievance-officer requirement is not engaged by this document, so its absence is not a finding here.

analyses.summary: HDFC Bank invents a category — 'Derivative Data' — for the credit scores, behavioural projections and algorithmic profiles built about you, and then treats those outputs exactly like the data you supplied: shareable, further shareable, and covered by a consent taken from the act of using any product. Anyone who hands the bank data about you is deemed to have been authorised by you to do it. Customer data may be given to prospective vendors as sample material for proof-of-concept testing, justified as the bank's legitimate interest. No retention period is stated anywhere, and the policy takes effect as soon as it is posted with no notice you can rely on. The Indian policy offers review and correction; the EU notice on the same page offers erasure, portability, objection and restriction. Real positives sit alongside all of that: a Consent Connect dashboard, a consent-withdrawal form with a 30-business-day commitment, and an explicit promise not to take biometrics without consent.

exposures.title: The profile the bank builds about you is defined as your data, and shared like it
exposures.whatItMeans: 'Derivative Data' is defined to include credit scores, behavioural projections, profiling, analytical results and reports produced by algorithms, analytics, software or automation — whether from your information alone or combined with data sourced from any other person or database. It is folded into the single defined term 'Data', so every sharing, processing and consent provision in the policy applies to it identically.
exposures.whyItMatters: The inference is often more consequential than the input: a behavioural projection determines whether you get a loan. Defining it as data the bank may share with credit bureaus, fintech entities and co-lenders means a machine's opinion of you circulates with the same freedom as your address.

reference.label: Data
reference.quote: any derivative thereof ("Derivative Data") like any credit scores or behavioural projections, profiling, analytical results, reports

exposures.title: Anyone who gives the bank data about you is deemed to have had your permission
exposures.whatItMeans: By accepting the policy or using any product — including a UPI transfer where your account is not even with HDFC and it is only the payment service provider bank — you agree that any person who submits data about you, or from whom the bank sources it, shall be deemed to have been authorised by you to do so, and you authorise the bank's processing of it.
exposures.whyItMatters: This constructs your consent for collections you had no part in and cannot enumerate. It also reaches people whose only connection to HDFC is that the other side of their transaction banks there.

reference.label: When and how your Data is collected?
reference.quote: any person who submits any Data or part thereof to us or from whom we source the same (including Derivation), shall be deemed to have been authorised by you to submit such Data to us

exposures.title: Your banking data may be handed to prospective vendors as demo material
exposures.whatItMeans: Under legitimate interests, the policy permits sharing your data — as a sample, or specifically, or generally — with any potential or actual service provider, consultant or vendor so they can run a proof of concept. That party may combine it with its own or externally sourced data, run or pilot the proposed solution on it, and return the results together with the data.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is live customer banking data used to evaluate a sales pitch. The counterparty is by definition not yet contracted, which is also the point at which the policy's promise to restrict processing by contract does not yet apply.

reference.label: Purposes of processing Data
reference.quote: sharing of your Data either as part of a sample or specifically or generally with any potential or actual service provider or consultant or vendor or third party or Processing Entity, for the purposes of testing of proof of concept

exposures.title: The onward-sharing chain has no end, and the contractual limit only covers direct contracts
exposures.whatItMeans: Data goes to subsidiaries, co-branding partners, co-lenders, co-originators, credit bureaus, fintech entities, the Central KYC Records Registry and payment-system participants. Each of those may share it onward with their own service providers, agents, affiliates, distributors, marketing agents, merchants, aggregators, lead generators, sourcing entities and 'other players/intermediaries in any ecosystem'. The commitment to restrict processing by contract is expressly limited to entities the bank contracts with directly.
exposures.whyItMatters: Lead generators and aggregators are named recipients, which is how a bank relationship becomes marketing inventory. Beyond the first hop nothing in this document constrains what happens to the data.

reference.label: Who we share your Data with?
reference.quote: [Wherever the Data is shared with any Processing Entity (with whom we have direct contract), we will through such contracts restrict the processing by them of such Data for the aforesaid purposes.]

exposures.title: EU customers are made to consent in advance to purely automated decisions
exposures.whatItMeans: Automated profiling and decision-making determines eligibility and credit decisions, and automated anti-money-laundering and sanctions checks may decide you present a fraud or laundering risk. In the EU notice, you expressly acknowledge that the automated decision is necessary for the contract and/or explicitly consent to it — and therefore, in the policy's own words, are subject even to decisions based solely on automated processing.
exposures.whyItMatters: Article 22 of the GDPR gives a right not to be subject to solely automated decisions with legal effect, subject to exceptions for necessity and explicit consent. This clause asserts both exceptions at once, in advance, so the protection is disclaimed by the same document that describes the processing.

reference.label: Automated processing
reference.quote: You expressly acknowledge that the automated decision is necessary for entering into or performance of contract and/or you explicitly consent to such automated decision making, hence you subject to even the decisions which are solely based on automated processing.

exposures.title: The policy changes the moment it is posted, and using your account is acceptance
exposures.whatItMeans: You are made responsible for apprising yourself of the policy and any change on each use of the website, app or platform, or when applying for or using any product or making any service request. The changed policy is effective as soon as it is published. Notification is optional — the bank says it may update you through app notifications, a banner, SMS, email or social media.
exposures.whyItMatters: For a current account, 'each use' means every login and every transaction. This makes continued use of your own bank account into rolling acceptance of terms that can change without any notice you are entitled to rely on.

reference.label: Changes to this Privacy Policy
reference.quote: The changed Privacy Policy shall be effective as soon as it is published/posted/hosted on our website/respective Apps/platforms.

exposures.title: No retention period, and retention expressly outlives your account
exposures.whatItMeans: Data is kept on the bank's systems or with third parties for as long as required for the stated purposes, and expressly beyond the expiry of the transactional or account-based relationship, where needed for legal and regulatory obligations, legal claims, the policy's own purposes, or specific consents. Withdrawing consent likewise leaves the bank retaining what it says it must.
exposures.whyItMatters: One of the four grounds for keeping data past the end of the relationship is the policy itself, which makes the limit circular. Closing the account ends the banking; it does not end the file, and nothing here says when it would.

reference.label: Period of storage of the Data

exposures.title: Which rights you have depends on whether you bank in India or the EU
exposures.whatItMeans: The Indian policy offers a right to review data you provided and to correct or amend it 'as feasible', plus consent withdrawal by form. The EU notice on the same page sets out the full GDPR set — objection, access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability — with lawful bases stated per purpose and a route to a supervisory authority.
exposures.whyItMatters: Same bank, same systems, same Derivative Data. The Indian customer has no erasure right, no portability and no right to object to legitimate-interest processing, including the proof-of-concept sharing above. This is the third document in the corpus where protection is decided by geography, after Uber and LinkedIn.

exposures.title: Data goes to authorities without your consent or knowledge, on a broad ground
exposures.whatItMeans: The bank may share data without obtaining consent or intimating you with government, statutory, regulatory, law-enforcement, investigating and judicial bodies that ask for it, and with any person where disclosure is necessary for compliance with a legal or regulatory obligation. It states it has no control over how those recipients process the data afterwards.
exposures.whyItMatters: The second limb is wider than compulsion by order or warrant — necessity for compliance is judged by the bank. Combined with the no-intimation clause, the disclosure is invisible to the customer at the time and afterwards.

reference.label: Who we share your Data with?

exposures.title: Biometrics, contact lists, CCTV and recorded conversations are all in scope
exposures.whatItMeans: Collected categories include biometric data and fingerprints, the IMEI of your device, contact lists where specific permission is obtained, CCTV images at branches, offices and ATMs, and conversations during meetings, calls and correspondence with bank staff. Sensitive personal data is separately enumerated to include health condition, sexual orientation, medical records and biometrics.
exposures.whyItMatters: Enumerating sensitive categories explicitly is better practice than most peers, and biometrics carry a clear promise of explicit consent. The exposure is the concentration: a single institution holding biometrics, device identifiers, contact lists and recorded conversations alongside the complete financial record.

reference.label: Data
reference.quote: We will not collect your biometric information without your explicit consent.

availableActions.action: Use Consent Connect to see and change what you have consented to
availableActions.howTo: HDFC operates a self-service dashboard for viewing and managing consents for communications and product or service preferences. It is the only standing consent-management surface in this corpus's finance documents — check what is switched on there before assuming any default.

availableActions.action: Withdraw consent by the prescribed form, and expect it to be partial
availableActions.howTo: Complete the Consent Withdrawal Form and email it from your registered address to privacy@hdfc.bank.in. After verification the bank commits to processing it within 30 business days. It will keep data needed for legal and regulatory obligations, and withdrawal may affect the products you currently hold.

deadline.description: The bank commits to processing a verified consent-withdrawal request no later than 30 business days after receipt.

availableActions.action: Refuse contact-list permission — it is one of the few that is genuinely optional
availableActions.howTo: The policy states contact lists are collected only in some cases where specific permission is obtained. Unlike the account data, this is a device permission you can decline without losing the banking relationship, and it protects people who are not customers.

availableActions.action: Withhold consent to cross-selling, which is separately gated
availableActions.howTo: Selling, cross-selling, distributing and referring products to you is stated to be subject to your specific consent, as is participation in surveys, contests and market research. These are distinct from the general consent taken by using a product, so they can be refused separately.

availableActions.action: Exercise the review-and-correct right — accuracy is made your obligation
availableActions.howTo: The policy makes it mandatory for you to ensure the accuracy and completeness of all data disclosed, and states the bank is not responsible for the authenticity of what you supplied. Ask via privacy@hdfc.bank.in for the prescribed correction process, and check what credit bureaus hold too, since scores flow back into the bank's Derivative Data.

availableActions.action: EU customers: use the GDPR rights the Indian policy does not offer
availableActions.howTo: The EU notice provides objection, access, rectification, erasure, restriction and portability, states the lawful basis for each processing purpose, and offers a copy of the safeguards applied to transfers outside the EEA on request. Ask for those safeguards in writing — the notice acknowledges destination countries may have less stringent confidentiality laws.

reference.label: How to exercise your information rights (including the right to object)?

availableActions.action: Ask about automated decisions rather than accepting the outcome
availableActions.howTo: Credit decisions, eligibility and AML checks may be fully automated, and an automated finding that your behaviour is consistent with fraud or laundering can follow you. The EU notice states rights exist in relation to automated decision-making and directs you to contact the bank; there is no equivalent statement for Indian customers, so ask through the privacy contact.

availableActions.action: Read the product terms as well — this policy expressly does not limit them
availableActions.howTo: The policy states that each product's terms cover additional matters and that this policy does not limit them or any other consent you have given. Consents signed on an application form therefore survive independently of anything here.

availableActions.action: Reach the Privacy Contact at privacy@hdfc.bank.in
availableActions.howTo: This is the only contact route the policy provides for privacy questions, corrections, consent withdrawal and security concerns. No individual officer is named, so ask for the name and designation of the person handling your request when you write.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period for any category. Retention runs for as long as required and expressly beyond the end of the account relationship, with the policy's own purposes listed as one of the grounds for extending it.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: Only a generic 'Privacy Contact' mailbox at privacy@hdfc.bank.in. No named officer, no designation, no postal address for privacy grievances and no response timeline, in a document that otherwise cites Indian law throughout.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: The revised policy is effective on publication. Notification through app notifications, banners, SMS, email or social media is expressly optional, and the customer is made responsible for checking on each use of any product or platform.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent withdrawal mechanism
requiredDisclosures.note: A dated Consent Withdrawal Form emailed from the registered address to privacy@hdfc.bank.in, with a stated 30-business-day processing commitment after verification — one of the few concrete timelines in the document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Sensitive personal information categories
requiredDisclosures.note: Enumerated as required by India's SPDI Rules: passwords, financial account and card details, physical, physiological and mental health condition, sexual orientation, medical records and history, and biometric information, with the public-domain carve-out stated.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automated decision-making rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Disclosed but disclaimed. The EU notice has the customer acknowledge in advance that automated decisions are contractually necessary and/or explicitly consent to them, concluding that they are therefore subject to solely automated decisions. No equivalent right, and no statement of rights, appears in the Indian policy.

requiredDisclosures.name: Lawful basis for processing
requiredDisclosures.note: Set out per purpose in the EU notice — contract, legal obligation, legitimate interests and consent — with a statement that the balancing test is applied before collection. The Indian policy states no bases and takes consent from use.

requiredDisclosures.name: International transfer safeguards
requiredDisclosures.note: Data is stored in India; transfers outside the EEA are made with adequate safeguards and a copy is available on request. The notice is unusually candid that destination countries may afford less confidentiality and that data may become subject to their disclosure requirements.

requiredDisclosures.name: Biometric data consent
requiredDisclosures.note: An express commitment not to collect biometric information without explicit consent — a rare unqualified promise on this category in the corpus, though no retention period attaches to it.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Indian law, with disputes arising out of the privacy policy subject to the courts and tribunals of Mumbai.

analyses.summary: Google's privacy policy pairs the widest collection in the corpus with its most developed control surface, and the two do not cancel out. It commits to things few others do — it will not reduce your rights without your explicit consent, it does not run personalised ads on sensitive categories or on the content of Gmail, Drive or Photos, and a general-area search is widened to at least 3 square kilometres or a thousand people. Against that: it collects publicly available information from across the web to train its AI models, with no opt-out anywhere in the document; it records your voice plus a few seconds before the wake word; service providers listen to samples of saved user audio; health data from Fitbit and Pixel Watch includes sleep, heart rate and skin temperature; and over two million non-Google sites feed activity back. It states plainly that Chrome Incognito does not stop any of that third-party sharing. If your account is managed by an employer or school, that administrator — and the reseller who manages it — can read your email, change your password, and restrict your ability to edit your own privacy settings. No retention period appears in the document at all.

exposures.title: Public information about you trains Google's AI models, with no opt-out
exposures.whatItMeans: Google states it may collect information that is publicly available online or from other public sources to help train its AI models and build products including Google Translate, Gemini Apps and Cloud AI capabilities.
exposures.whyItMatters: This reaches people who have never used a Google service — the pattern the corpus already found at Robinhood, OpenAI and Flipkart, here applied to model training rather than record-building. The policy offers controls over activity, ads and history, and none of them touches this collection, because it does not depend on you having an account.

reference.label: Additional Context — publicly accessible sources
reference.quote: we may collect information that's publicly available online or from other public sources to help train Google's AI models and build products and features like Google Translate, Gemini Apps, and Cloud AI capabilities

exposures.title: Incognito mode does not stop Google collecting from the sites you visit
exposures.whatItMeans: Sites and apps that integrate Google services such as ads and analytics share information with Google regardless of which browser or browser mode you use. The policy states this expressly for Chrome Incognito, which it describes as keeping browsing private from other people using your device.
exposures.whyItMatters: Private browsing is widely understood as preventing collection, and this says the opposite in terms. Over two million non-Google sites and apps partner with Google for advertising, so the surface it applies across is most of the web.

reference.label: Additional Context — Activity on 3rd-party sites and apps that use our services
reference.quote: although Incognito mode in Chrome can help keep your browsing private from other people who use your device, third party sites and apps that integrate our services still share information with Google when you visit them

exposures.title: Your administrator can stop you changing your own privacy settings
exposures.whatItMeans: For accounts managed by a school or employer, the domain administrator and the resellers who manage the account can access and retain information stored in the account including email, view usage statistics, change the password, suspend or terminate access, hand the account over to satisfy a legal request, and restrict your ability to delete or edit your information or your privacy settings.
exposures.whyItMatters: Every control the rest of the policy describes can be switched off above your head, and by a reseller as well as by your employer. The reseller is a company the user has no relationship with and is not named anywhere.

reference.label: When Google shares your information — With domain administrators
reference.quote: Restrict your ability to delete or edit your information or your privacy settings

exposures.title: Voice recording starts before you say the wake word
exposures.whatItMeans: When a device detects an activation command such as 'Ok Google', Google records your voice and audio plus a few seconds before the activation. Separately, service providers are used to analyse and listen to samples of saved user audio to improve audio recognition technologies.
exposures.whyItMatters: The pre-roll captures whatever was being said before anyone intended to address the device, and human review by contractors means those samples can be heard by people. Both are disclosed plainly, which is more than most, but neither carries a stated retention period.

reference.label: Additional Context — Media (like images, files, audio, and video) from your interactions

exposures.title: Sleep, heart rate and skin temperature
exposures.whatItMeans: Through Fitbit, Pixel Watch, Nest and Google Fit, Google collects height and weight you provide plus sleep patterns, heart rate, skin temperature, calories burned and steps taken.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is health data held under a general consumer privacy policy rather than a health-specific regime. The policy's protection is that personalised ads are not shown on sensitive categories including health — a limit on advertising use, not on collection, retention or sharing.

reference.label: Additional Context — Similar information related to your physical or mental health

exposures.title: No retention period appears in the policy
exposures.whatItMeans: Retention is described in four tiers — data you can delete, data anonymised automatically after a set period, data kept until you delete your account, and data kept longer for legitimate business or legal purposes — but no actual period is given for any of them. The durations are deferred to a separate page.
exposures.whyItMatters: The tiers describe a policy shape without stating a single number, so nothing in the document is falsifiable. The user-facing remedy is the auto-delete setting, which puts the period in the user's hands for activity data and leaves the rest unstated.

exposures.title: Merchants upload their loyalty-card data into Google
exposures.whatItMeans: Google receives information from partners to provide advertising and research services on their behalf, and gives the example of merchants uploading data from their loyalty-card programmes so they can include loyalty information in search or shopping results or measure ad performance.
exposures.whyItMatters: Your in-store purchase history arrives at Google from the shop, under the shop's decision rather than yours, and is then matched to you. The safeguard offered is that advertisers receive only aggregated reports, which constrains the output rather than the ingestion.

reference.label: Additional Context — advertising and research services on their behalf

exposures.title: Call and message metadata across Gmail, Meet, Chat, Voice and Fi
exposures.whatItMeans: For services used to make calls or send messages, Google may collect your phone number, calling and receiving party numbers, forwarding numbers, sender and recipient email addresses, times and dates, call durations, routing information, and the types and volumes of calls and messages.
exposures.whyItMatters: Communications metadata reveals the shape of a person's relationships even where content is untouched, and the list here spans six services including a full phone plan. The policy separately notes it uses this to infer the people who matter most to you online.

exposures.title: Your name and photo can appear in advertising
exposures.whatItMeans: When signed in and interacting with services — leaving a YouTube comment or reviewing an app in Play — your name and photo appear next to that activity, and Google may also display it in ads depending on your Shared Endorsements setting.
exposures.whyItMatters: An ordinary review becomes advertising content carrying your identity, shown to people you did not choose. There is a specific control, but it is on by default in the sense that the setting must be found and changed.

reference.label: Sharing your information — When you share your information

exposures.title: Android phones report installed apps and device state on a schedule
exposures.whatItMeans: An Android device with Google apps periodically contacts Google servers with device type, carrier name, crash reports, which apps you have installed, and — depending on device settings — other information about how you use the device.
exposures.whyItMatters: The list of installed applications is itself revealing, covering health, dating, religious and political apps, and the reporting is periodic rather than triggered by anything the user does.

reference.label: Information we collect as you use our services — Your apps, browsers & devices

availableActions.action: Set activity data to auto-delete
availableActions.howTo: In My Activity you can delete items individually or choose to have activity deleted automatically after a set period. This is the only mechanism in the policy that attaches an actual duration to retention, and it is the user who sets it.

availableActions.action: Run Privacy Checkup, then go deeper
availableActions.howTo: Privacy Checkup walks the main settings. Beyond it: My Activity and Personalisation Settings for Web & App Activity, Search Services History and YouTube History; My Ad Center for ad personalisation; About You for what other people can see; Shared Endorsements to keep your name and photo out of ads.

availableActions.action: Turn off Shared Endorsements specifically
availableActions.howTo: It has its own setting, separate from ad personalisation, and it is what governs whether your name and photo appear beside your reviews and recommendations inside advertisements.

availableActions.action: Manage signed-out settings too
availableActions.howTo: Google stores data against browser and device identifiers when you are not signed in. Signed-out search customisation, YouTube Search and Watch History, and Ad Settings each have separate signed-out controls.

reference.label: Your privacy controls — When you're signed out

availableActions.action: Do not rely on Incognito to stop Google collection
availableActions.howTo: The policy states third-party sites and apps integrating Google services share information regardless of browser mode. The controls that do bite are the Web & App Activity subsetting covering activity on other sites and apps, and the 'sites and apps that use Google services' setting.

reference.label: Additional Context — Activity on 3rd-party sites and apps

availableActions.action: Export everything with Takeout before you delete anything
availableActions.howTo: You can export a copy of your account content, and separately delete content from specific services, delete specific items via My Activity, delete individual Google products, or delete the entire account.

availableActions.action: Set up Inactive Account Manager
availableActions.howTo: It lets you nominate someone to receive access to parts of your account if you become unexpectedly unable to use it, and to set what happens to the account. It is the only succession mechanism the policy describes.

availableActions.action: Keep personal data out of a managed account
availableActions.howTo: If your account is administered by an employer or school, the administrator and the reseller managing it can read stored information including email, change the password, and restrict your ability to edit your privacy settings. No user-side control overrides that.

reference.label: When Google shares your information — With domain administrators

availableActions.action: Turn off device location services at the OS level
availableActions.howTo: Android device settings control GPS, sensors and the scanning of nearby Wi-Fi access points, cell towers and Bluetooth devices. Timeline is separately opt-in. Where a general area is used for search, Google widens it to at least 3 square kilometres or the area covering 1,000 people.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: Google states publicly available information is collected to train its AI models for Translate, Gemini Apps and Cloud AI. No opt-out is described, and the collection does not depend on having an account.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: Four retention tiers are described and not one carries a stated duration; the periods are deferred to a separate page outside this document. Auto-delete puts a period on activity data only, and only if the user sets it.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Among the strongest in the corpus: Google states it will not reduce your rights under the policy without your explicit consent, publishes archived versions, and gives more prominent notice for significant changes including email for certain services.

requiredDisclosures.name: Non-retroactivity of changes
requiredDisclosures.note: The explicit-consent commitment operates as a non-retroactivity guarantee for rights reductions, matching LinkedIn's posture rather than the continued-use-is-acceptance model used almost everywhere else.

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of personal data collected
requiredDisclosures.note: Enumerated across account information, content, device and app data, activity, location, health data from fitness products, and communications metadata, with a worked server-log example.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Recipients are categories — affiliates, trusted businesses, service providers, measurement companies, over two million advertising partners. Only Lumen, for content-removal transparency, and the EU consumer-service affiliates are named.

requiredDisclosures.name: Sensitive personal information categories
requiredDisclosures.note: Defined in the key terms as medical facts, racial or ethnic origins, political or religious beliefs and sexuality, with commitments not to run personalised ads on those categories, to require the same of advertisers, and to seek explicit consent before sharing sensitive personal information.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data subject tools
requiredDisclosures.note: My Activity, Google Dashboard, Personal Info, Privacy Checkup, My Ad Center, Takeout export, per-product and whole-account deletion, and Inactive Account Manager — the most developed self-service control surface in the corpus.

requiredDisclosures.name: International transfer safeguards
requiredDisclosures.note: States information may be processed on servers outside your country, that the same protections apply regardless, and that Google complies with certain legal transfer frameworks and works with local data protection authorities on complaints it cannot resolve directly.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data protection officer contact
requiredDisclosures.note: No DPO or privacy contact is named in this document. Users are directed to a general contact link and to the EU affiliate entities listed in the key terms.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: This policy is served on the Indian country version alongside terms that name none either, though the IT Rules 2021 require a published grievance officer for significant social media intermediaries.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children under 13
requiredDisclosures.note: Handled by reference rather than in the body: separate notices are listed for Google Accounts managed with Family Link for children under 13, YouTube Kids, Google Workspace for Education, and voice and audio collection from children's features on the Assistant.

analyses.summary: Walmart's notice is the most complete disclosure document in the corpus and what it discloses is extraordinary. It collects biometric identifiers including voice prints, iris and retina imagery, face geometry and palm prints; background checks and criminal convictions; household income, family health, ethnicity, citizenship and number of children; and inferences it describes as covering intelligence and aptitudes. Appendix 1 then states, category by category, that all of it is sold or shared — including financial account numbers and criminal conviction data — with business partners that receive it for their own independent use rather than to provide services to Walmart. Automated licence plate readers operate in the car parks and in-store cameras at checkout. Against that sits a control set that is also among the best here: Global Privacy Control is honoured and extends to the account and to linked VIZIO televisions, cross-company marketing and sensitive processing are opt-in rather than opt-out, biometrics carry a real destruction schedule, VIZIO viewing data stays separate unless you opt in, and there is an appeal if a request is refused. The grade is High rather than Very High because those controls are specific and operative, not because the collection is ordinary.

exposures.title: Financial account numbers and criminal convictions go to business partners for their own use
exposures.whatItMeans: Appendix 1 lists every category of personal information as sold or shared. For Financial Information — credit and debit card numbers and financial account numbers — and for Background Information, which includes background checks and criminal convictions, the recipients include business partners described as receiving data for their own independent use and not to provide services to a Walmart entity.
exposures.whyItMatters: Independent use is the distinction that separates a processor from a recipient with its own purposes. These are the two categories where onward use is hardest to undo: a card number cannot be un-disclosed, and a conviction record circulating among unnamed business partners can affect decisions the notice's own no-significant-effect-profiling promise does not reach, because that promise binds Walmart and not them.

reference.label: Appendix 1 — Financial Information; Background Information
reference.quote: Business partners, including those that receive data for their own independent use and not to provide services to a Walmart entity.

exposures.title: Biometric identifiers across face, eye, hand and voice
exposures.whatItMeans: The collected categories include voice prints, imagery of the iris or retina, face geometry, and palm prints or fingerprints. Virtual try-on for eyeglasses and makeup uses facial scanning to measure unique features.
exposures.whyItMatters: Biometrics cannot be reissued after a breach the way a card can. Walmart is unusually specific about the limits — eyeglass biometrics deleted within 48 hours and never sold or shared, makeup images not stored, voice used for transcription rather than biometric analysis — but the collected-categories list is broader than those three named uses account for.

reference.label: What Personal Information Do We Collect? — Biometric Information

exposures.title: Inferences about your intelligence
exposures.whatItMeans: The Inferences category covers individual preferences and characteristics drawn from shopping patterns and behaviours, and the notice names intelligence and aptitudes among them. Inferences are marked as used for targeted advertising and as sold or shared with business partners for independent use.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is a judgement about a person rather than a record of what they did, it is derived rather than provided so there is nothing to correct at source, and it is in the subset that leaves Walmart for third parties' own purposes.

reference.label: What Personal Information Do We Collect? — Inferences
reference.quote: inferences drawn from and related to shopping patterns and behaviors, intelligence, and aptitudes

exposures.title: Household income, family health and children, collected as demographics
exposures.whatItMeans: Demographic Information is defined to include age, gender, citizenship, ethnicity, date of birth, family or marital status, household income, education, employment, family health, number of children, number of cars owned and virtual assets owned.
exposures.whyItMatters: Family health and ethnicity are sensitive categories in most US state privacy statutes, and they sit in a bucket marked as used for targeted advertising and as sold or shared. The notice carves sensitive personal information out of targeted advertising and requires consent where law demands it, but the carve-out is a parenthetical inside the appendix rather than a limit on the category itself.

reference.label: What Personal Information Do We Collect? — Demographic Information

exposures.title: Licence plate readers and cameras across the property
exposures.whatItMeans: Automated licence plate readers may operate on Walmart properties where law permits, and cameras and automated technologies operate in-store and outside on Walmart property, capturing images at checkout and to deter theft.
exposures.whyItMatters: Neither is consented to in any meaningful sense — driving into a car park is enough — and a licence plate is a durable identifier that links a person to a place and time. This collection reaches people who never enter the shop and never hold an account.

reference.label: How Do We Collect Personal Information? — Collected Through Automated Means

exposures.title: Your content is used to train Walmart's AI
exposures.whatItMeans: Among the listed uses is undertaking activities to verify or maintain the quality or safety of services or devices and to improve, upgrade or enhance them, given as 'such as training our AI'. Communications with the AI chatbots, including Sparky, are a collected category.
exposures.whyItMatters: No opt-out from AI training is offered anywhere in the notice. The interest-based advertising and sale/sharing opt-outs are the only controls provided, and neither reaches a use characterised as service improvement.

reference.label: How Do We Use Personal Information?
reference.quote: Undertaking activities to verify or maintain the quality or safety of our services or devices and to improve, upgrade, or enhance them, such as training our AI.

exposures.title: The app listens for a wake word whenever it is open
exposures.whatItMeans: With microphone and speech-recognition consent, the Walmart shopping voice assistant has access to the microphone whenever the app is open and continually listens for 'Hey, Walmart'. Walmart states it retains nothing before recognising that phrase.
exposures.whyItMatters: Continuous listening is disclosed plainly and gated on consent, which is the right way to do it, but the retention promise is a statement about Walmart's practice rather than a technical limit a user can verify.

reference.label: How Do We Collect Personal Information? — Provided Directly by You

exposures.title: Walmart is paid for insights built from your shopping history
exposures.whatItMeans: Walmart offers insights and related services to companies including its suppliers, derived by combining shopping history from many customers, and states it may receive payment for these insights.
exposures.whyItMatters: The notice says these insights do not directly identify you, which leaves indirect identification unaddressed, and the commercial incentive is disclosed without any control attached — the sale/sharing opt-out is described elsewhere and is not tied to this practice.

reference.label: Who Do We Disclose to and Why? — Walmart Suppliers and Other Third Parties

exposures.title: No retention period, and the limit is partly Walmart's own policy
exposures.whatItMeans: Personal information is kept as long as necessary for the notice's purposes, but no longer than required or permitted under applicable law or internal Walmart policy. Only biometrics carry a schedule: destroyed when the purpose is satisfied, within three years of last interaction, or as law requires.
exposures.whyItMatters: An outer bound set by internal policy is one the company can move, and 'permitted' rather than 'required' by law is the widest possible framing. The biometric schedule shows Walmart can state a period when it chooses to.

reference.label: How Long Do We Retain Your Personal Information?

exposures.title: You are told to check the notice yourself for changes
exposures.whatItMeans: Walmart commits to giving notice of significant updates, then asks you to check the notice periodically for changes, with the last-updated date posted at the top.
exposures.whyItMatters: 'Significant' is Walmart's judgement and no period or delivery method is committed to. The version analysed shows how narrow an update can be — the stated change is the addition of voice-interaction information — which is precisely the kind of change a periodic reader would miss.

reference.label: How Will I Know if this Privacy Notice Changes?

exposures.title: Opting out of interest-based ads takes at least three separate actions
exposures.whatItMeans: The opt-out must be done in the Walmart account, again in mobile device settings, and again through the NAI and DAA industry tools. It requires cookies enabled, applies only to the current browser on the current computer, and must be redone after clearing cookies. A previous Walmart.com opt-out does not cover Walmart ads on other sites without resubmitting on the Ad Preferences page.
exposures.whyItMatters: Four places, per browser, per device, reset by ordinary cookie clearing. The Global Privacy Control route is far better and covers sale and sharing including targeted advertising, but it is described further down in a region-specific section rather than here.

reference.label: How Can You Set Your Preferences? — Interest-Based Advertising

availableActions.action: Send a Global Privacy Control signal, logged in
availableActions.howTo: Enable GPC in your browser and then sign in to your Walmart account. The notice states that a GPC signal sent while logged in extends the opt-out to your whole account, including VIZIO OS products linked to it, rather than to that browser alone. Walmart displays a confirmation, and processing of already-stored data takes up to 15 days.

deadline.description: Immediately effective for data collected during that interaction; up to 15 days for other data already held.

reference.label: Region-Specific Disclosures and Privacy Rights — US State Privacy Rights

availableActions.action: Use Your Privacy Choices to access, correct, delete and opt out
availableActions.howTo: The 'Your Privacy Choices' link in the website footer or the app settings covers access, correction, deletion, opting out of targeted advertising, and opting out of sale or sharing. In California, Texas and Nebraska a second route is required — call 1-800-925-6278 and say 'Privacy'.

reference.label: Region-Specific Disclosures and Privacy Rights — US State Privacy Rights

availableActions.action: Appeal a refused privacy request
availableActions.howTo: If Walmart declines to act, use the privacy request page with your Privacy Request ID and Zip Code and select the appeal option. The notice also commits to no discrimination or retaliation for exercising rights.

reference.label: Region-Specific Disclosures and Privacy Rights — US State Privacy Rights

availableActions.action: Leave VIZIO viewing data unlinked
availableActions.howTo: VIZIO maintains viewing, activity, mobile app and streaming data separately from your Walmart account unless you opt in to combine them. The switch is at VIZIO.com/account and can be turned off at any time. Signing in to a VIZIO television with a Walmart account is enough to start the account-level data flow even without this combination.

reference.label: When Does this Privacy Notice Apply to VIZIO Related Information?

availableActions.action: Keep the higher-consent marketing channels off
availableActions.howTo: Automated phone and text messages, and disclosure to companies outside the Walmart corporate family for their own direct marketing, are opt-in — do not consent and they do not happen. Email, push and postal mail are opt-out via Communication Preferences & Alerts; allow up to 10 days for email, 30 for calls and texts, and six to ten weeks for postal mail.

reference.label: How Can You Set Your Preferences? — Marketing

availableActions.action: Stop prescreened credit offers separately
availableActions.howTo: Walmart's marketing consent standards expressly do not apply to co-branded credit card offerings through associated financial institutions. Use optoutprescreen.com or 1-888-567-8688, which is the credit reporting industry route rather than Walmart's.

reference.label: How Can You Set Your Preferences? — Marketing

availableActions.action: Withhold camera, microphone, contacts and precise location
availableActions.howTo: All four require permission and can be revoked in device settings at any time. Precise geolocation is consent-based; imprecise location inferred from IP address is not. Bluetooth settings separately control in-store location sharing.

reference.label: How Do We Collect Personal Information?

availableActions.action: Decline virtual try-on rather than the store
availableActions.howTo: Eyeglass and makeup try-on collect biometric information and you are offered the choice to consent or decline before the camera is used. Makeup try-on shares measurements and images with Perfect Corp; eyeglass biometrics are deleted within 48 hours and are not sold or shared.

reference.label: How Do We Collect Personal Information? — Provided Directly by You

availableActions.action: Delete the account from the app
availableActions.howTo: The Account section of the Walmart app has a Delete Account link. The notice also allows deletion through Contact Us, subject to the exceptions defined by law.

reference.label: How Can You Access and Update Your Personal Information?

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of personal information sold or shared
requiredDisclosures.note: Appendix 1 gives a category-by-category table of what is sold or shared, to which recipient types, and whether it is used for targeted advertising. The most complete such table in the corpus, and the reason the severity of the disclosure practice can be established at all.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: Available through Your Privacy Choices, through GPC — which extends to the account and to linked VIZIO devices when signed in — and by phone in California, Texas and Nebraska. Effective immediately for the current interaction and within 15 days for stored data.

requiredDisclosures.name: Sensitive personal information categories
