requiredDisclosures.note: Biometric, financial, geolocation, background and demographic categories are each enumerated, with sensitive personal information processed only with consent where law requires and excluded from targeted advertising.

requiredDisclosures.name: Biometric data retention
requiredDisclosures.note: A real schedule: destruction at the first of purpose satisfied, three years from last interaction, or as law requires. Eyeglass try-on biometrics are separately committed to deletion within 48 hours and are not sold or shared.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period for anything other than biometrics. The outer bound is what is required or permitted by law or by internal Walmart policy, which is self-defined.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: Training Walmart's AI is a named use, and chatbot communications including Sparky are a collected category, but no opt-out from that use is offered.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Only a commitment to notice of significant updates, with no period or delivery method, plus a request that users check the notice periodically.

requiredDisclosures.name: Rights over automated decision-making
requiredDisclosures.note: Walmart states it does not engage in profiling in furtherance of decisions producing legal or similarly significant effects, and Canadian users may email globalprivacy@wal-mart.com to obtain information about automated processing used to render a decision.

requiredDisclosures.name: International transfer safeguards
requiredDisclosures.note: Discloses processing in the United States and India, with information management agreements required of each processor and, where law requires, prior consent before transferring outside the user's jurisdiction.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children under 13
requiredDisclosures.note: Sites are for a general audience and not directed to children under 13 or 14 depending on region; any child-directed service will say so and post a separate notice.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Recipients are given as categories — advertisers, publishers, social media platforms, ad technology providers, data technology vendors, business partners. Only Google Analytics, Perfect Corp, Sam's Club, One Finance and VIZIO are named.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent withdrawal mechanism
requiredDisclosures.note: Marketing consent can be withdrawn through Communication Preferences & Alerts with stated processing times, device permissions revoked in settings, and Canadian users may withdraw consent to collection, use and disclosure subject to legal and contractual restrictions.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: Provided for Canada through 'Manage Cookie Settings' in the homepage footer. The US sections offer interest-based advertising opt-outs and GPC rather than a cookie consent interface.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: No individual is named. Contact is the Walmart Corporate Privacy Office at Bentonville and a general feedback page; Canada references a Senior Vice President by title only.

analyses.summary: Zoom makes the clearest AI commitment in the corpus — it states twice that it does not use your audio, video, chat, screen sharing, attachments or other communications content to train its own or third-party AI models — and pairs it with a real two-year deletion limit on facial geometry and voiceprints, on-device processing for video effects, and Global Privacy Control support. The exposure is not Zoom. It is the account owner. Depending on settings, whoever owns the account can read Team Chat direct messages, meeting recordings and transcripts, whiteboards and files, and email and calendar content — expressly including Zoom Emails that are end-to-end encrypted. Archiving reaches further still: if a guest in someone else's meeting is subject to archiving, that guest's own account owner receives the meeting group chat and the direct messages sent to them. And if the account was bought through a reseller, that reseller may be able to access personal data and content including meetings, webinars and messages, from a company the participant has no relationship with at all.

exposures.title: The account owner can read encrypted Zoom Email
exposures.whatItMeans: Zoom Email is end-to-end encrypted by default between active Zoom Email users, and the statement says account owners or designated administrators may control the encryption key. Depending on settings, account owners and administrators can access email and calendar content sent to and from users on their accounts, expressly stated to apply even if those Zoom Emails are encrypted.
exposures.whyItMatters: End-to-end encryption normally means the content is unreadable to anyone but the participants. Here it means unreadable to Zoom while remaining readable to your employer, which is a materially different guarantee from the one the phrase usually conveys.

reference.label: Who Can See, Share, and Process My Personal Data — Other Collaborative Feature Content
reference.quote: account owners and designated account administrators can access email and calendar content sent to and from users on their Zoom Email or Zoom Calendar accounts, even if those Zoom Emails are encrypted

exposures.title: Archiving follows you into meetings you are only a guest at
exposures.whatItMeans: If a participant is subject to archiving, their account owner receives messages sent to Everyone in the meeting and the direct messages sent to that participant. The statement extends this to guests: a guest subject to archiving means that guest's own account owner receives the meeting group chat messages and the direct messages sent to them.
exposures.whyItMatters: The organisation capturing the messages is not the one hosting the meeting. Joining an external meeting from a work account can route a private message sent to you by someone at another company into your employer's archive, and neither sender nor recipient is told at the time.

reference.label: Who Can See, Share, and Process My Personal Data — In-Meeting/Webinar Messages

exposures.title: A reseller you never dealt with may reach your meeting content
exposures.whatItMeans: Where an account owner licensed or purchased Zoom through a third-party reseller, the statement says that reseller may be able to access personal data and content for users, including meetings, webinars and messages hosted by the account owner.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is content access, not billing data, held by an intermediary that participants have no relationship or contract with and are never told about. It is listed first among the sharing circumstances and carries none of the contractual limits Zoom describes for its vendors.

reference.label: How Do We Share Personal Data? — Resellers
reference.quote: the reseller may be able to access personal data and content for users, including meetings, webinars, and messages hosted by the account owner

exposures.title: Keystrokes and mouse movements are usage data
exposures.whatItMeans: Usage information includes mouse movements, clicks, keystrokes and actions such as mute or video toggling, along with when participants join and leave, whom they message, and which features they use. Some of this is optional and controlled by the Diagnostic Data Preferences setting.
exposures.whyItMatters: Keystroke and pointer telemetry inside a work tool is behavioural data about attention and activity, and much of it is also visible to the account owner as product usage — including how long each participant stayed in a meeting.

reference.label: What Personal Data Do We Receive? — Usage Information

exposures.title: Third-party apps approved by your employer can receive everything
exposures.whatItMeans: Depending on settings, personal data and content may be shared with apps and integrations approved by account owners, which the statement says may include all of the personal data categories listed — account and profile information, participant lists, settings, content, product usage, device information and third-party emails shared with the app. That data is then governed by the developer's privacy policy rather than Zoom's.
exposures.whyItMatters: The decision to install is the account owner's and the consequences fall on every participant, including guests who never agreed to that developer's terms. Zoom's own protections stop at the point of transfer.

reference.label: Who Can See, Share, and Process My Personal Data — Apps and Integrations

exposures.title: Automated scanning of backgrounds, images, files and inbound email
exposures.whatItMeans: Zoom states it uses advanced tools to automatically scan certain content — virtual backgrounds, profile images, incoming emails to Zoom Email from non-Zoom-Email senders, and files uploaded or exchanged through chat — to detect violations of its terms and illegal or harmful activity.
exposures.whyItMatters: The scanning is for safety rather than advertising and its scope is stated narrowly, which is better than most. But it is content inspection that applies regardless of account owner settings, and inbound email from outside the encrypted path is inside it.

reference.label: How Do We Use Personal Data? — Authentication, Integrity, Security, and Safety

exposures.title: Feedback you give Zoom becomes Zoom's
exposures.whatItMeans: The category of communications with Zoom includes feedback provided by users about Zoom's products and services, described parenthetically as owned by Zoom.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the eighth appearance of the ideas-become-ours clause in the corpus and the first found in a privacy statement rather than terms of service — an ownership claim placed in the document a user reads to understand data handling, not rights transfer.

reference.label: What Personal Data Do We Receive? — Communications with Zoom

exposures.title: Retention has criteria but no periods
exposures.whatItMeans: Personal data is retained as long as required for the uses described, with four stated criteria — the ongoing relationship, whether account owners or users delete information, legal obligations, and Zoom's legal position including statutes of limitations. Only facial geometry and voiceprints carry a period, of two years from last interaction.
exposures.whyItMatters: Naming the criteria is more than most documents in the corpus do, but none of them produces a date. Meeting recordings, transcripts and chat content are all inside the general regime, and deletion depends in part on the account owner acting rather than on you.

exposures.title: Enrichment data is bought about you from third parties
exposures.whatItMeans: Zoom obtains information about account owners and their users from market data enrichment services, including company size, industry, contact information and activity of certain enterprise domains, and from advertising partners including whether you clicked an ad.
exposures.whyItMatters: Enrichment attaches employer and role information to a profile from sources the individual never interacted with, and it applies to users under an account rather than only to the purchasing organisation.

reference.label: What Personal Data Do We Receive? — Information from Partners

availableActions.action: Assume the account owner can see it
availableActions.howTo: Recordings, transcripts, whiteboards, files, poll and Q&A responses, Team Chat content including direct messages where archiving is on, and Zoom Email and Calendar content including encrypted email are all listed as accessible to account owners depending on their settings. Ask your administrator which of these are enabled rather than inferring from the encryption label.

reference.label: Who Can See, Share, and Process My Personal Data

availableActions.action: Submit Q&A and feedback anonymously
availableActions.howTo: The statement says account owners can see who provided responses to polls, Q&A and post-meeting feedback together with the responses, unless the responses are submitted anonymously. The same applies to questions asked during a webinar Q&A.

reference.label: Who Can See, Share, and Process My Personal Data — Account Owner

availableActions.action: Turn down Diagnostic Data Preferences
availableActions.howTo: Zoom states some usage data collection is optional and controlled by this setting. It is the only user-side control offered over the mouse, keystroke and interaction telemetry.

reference.label: What Personal Data Do We Receive? — Usage Information

availableActions.action: Set Global Privacy Control where your state supports it
availableActions.howTo: Residents of California, Colorado, Connecticut, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire and Texas can set GPC to opt out of sale or sharing for targeted advertising. Otherwise use Cookies Settings or Your Privacy Choices — and note those are stored in a cookie, so they must be set per browser and per device and reset if you clear cookies.

reference.label: California & Other U.S. State Privacy Rights

availableActions.action: Decline the enhanced features that take biometrics
availableActions.howTo: Facial geometry and voiceprint processing requires your consent and is separate from the on-device video effects, which Zoom states never leave the device and are not retained. If you do consent, the data is deleted when no longer needed or two years after your last interaction, whichever comes first.

reference.label: How Do We Use Personal Data? — Enhanced Features

availableActions.action: Appeal a refused request, and use the phone route
availableActions.howTo: Zoom acknowledges requests within 10 business days and responds substantively within 45 calendar days, extendable to 90 with notice. A denial can be appealed by replying to it or emailing privacy@zoom.us. Requests can also be made by phone on +1-888-799-0566.

deadline.description: Receipt acknowledged within 10 business days; substantive response within 45 calendar days, extendable to a total of 90 with written notice.

reference.label: California & Other U.S. State Privacy Rights

availableActions.action: Contact the DPO or the EU/UK representative directly
availableActions.howTo: privacy@zoom.us reaches the Data Protection Officer at Zoom Communications, 55 Almaden Blvd, San Jose. The EU representative is Workvivo Limited in Cork and the UK representative is ZVC UK Ltd in London, both named with full addresses.

availableActions.action: Check which apps your account owner has approved
availableActions.howTo: Apps added to the account may receive all listed categories of personal data and are then governed by the developer's own policy. Other participants can see which app you are using in a meeting if it is receiving content.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: The strongest such statement in the corpus, and made twice: Zoom does not use audio, video, chat, screen sharing, attachments or other communications-like Customer Content, including poll results, whiteboards and reactions, to train its own or third-party AI models. Intelligent features process content solely to provide those features.

requiredDisclosures.name: Biometric data retention
requiredDisclosures.note: Facial geometry and voiceprints for enhanced features are deleted when no longer necessary or two years after the last interaction with Zoom, whichever comes first. On-device video effects data never leaves the device and is not retained.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period for general personal data. Four retention criteria are listed, which is more than most documents give, but none of them yields a date.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: Cookies Settings and Your Privacy Choices, plus Global Privacy Control for residents of California, Colorado, Connecticut, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire and Texas. Zoom states it does not sell in the conventional sense but that its advertising and analytics services may constitute sale or sharing.

requiredDisclosures.name: Rights over automated decision-making
requiredDisclosures.note: Zoom states it does not engage in profiling producing legal or similarly significant effects, and does not use or disclose sensitive personal information to infer characteristics or in any way triggering the CCPA right to limit.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data protection officer contact
requiredDisclosures.note: privacy@zoom.us and a postal address in San Jose, with separately named EU and UK representatives — Workvivo Limited in Cork and ZVC UK Ltd in London.

requiredDisclosures.name: Lawful basis for processing
requiredDisclosures.note: Five bases set out with the specific purposes each covers: contract, revocable consent for advertising cookies, legal obligation, vital interests including CSAM detection, and enumerated legitimate interests.

requiredDisclosures.name: International transfer safeguards
requiredDisclosures.note: EU-U.S., UK Extension and Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework certification with FTC jurisdiction and DPA panel cooperation named, plus standard contractual clauses for transfers to non-adequate countries.

requiredDisclosures.name: EU-US Data Privacy Framework participation
requiredDisclosures.note: Certified for Zoom Communications, Zoom Voice Communications and Solvvy, with liability retained for third-party agents processing inconsistently with the Principles and binding arbitration available for residual complaints.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: For material changes Zoom commits to notify and provide an opportunity to review before you choose to continue using the products. Update notes are published at the foot of the statement — the analysed version lists six.

requiredDisclosures.name: Minimum age
requiredDisclosures.note: Under 16 may not sign up for a Zoom account; a separate Children's Educational Privacy Statement covers under-18s at educational organisations.

requiredDisclosures.name: Shine the Light disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: California residents may request the names of third parties receiving personal information for their own direct marketing, by emailing privacy@zoom.us with the statement 'Shine the Light Request'.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Recipients are categories — resellers, vendors, marketing and analytics partners, corporate affiliates, third-party developers. Only Zoom Voice Communications, Solvvy and Apple's TrueDepth technology are named; the reseller with content access is not identified to participants at all.

analyses.summary: Canva's terms are written to be readable — every section carries a plain-English box — and the plain English is not where the cost sits. Ideas and feedback you send are assigned to Canva outright, the second outright assignment in the corpus after Paytm. Liability is capped at the greater of $100 or a year's subscription fees, and that cap is expressly disapplied to your indemnity and your breach of the use restrictions, so Canva's exposure is limited and yours is not. Arbitration is mandatory under AAA consumer rules with a class action and jury waiver and no opt-out of any kind, each side paying its own arbitration fees. Termination for a Violation deletes the account and everything in it, bars export, refunds nothing, still requires you to pay out the rest of the subscription, and bans you from making another account. Against that, the AI training control is real and sits in Privacy Settings, price rises need 30 days or a renewal, and Canva Education content is excluded from AI training.

exposures.title: Your ideas are assigned to Canva, not licensed
exposures.whatItMeans: Any suggestions, ideas, enhancement requests or other feedback you give Canva about the Service or its products are assigned to Canva, and Canva owns everything it develops in connection with the Service.
exposures.whyItMatters: Assignment transfers title; a licence would only permit use. This is the sixth appearance of the ideas-become-ours clause in the corpus and the second that assigns rather than licenses, after Paytm — the rest, including Netflix and Dropbox, take a licence or merely disclaim obligation.

reference.label: 10. Canva's Intellectual Property
reference.quote: You assign to Canva any suggestions, ideas, enhancement requests, or other feedback you provide to Canva relating to the Service or Canva's products.

exposures.title: The liability cap protects Canva and is switched off for you
exposures.whatItMeans: Aggregate liability is capped at the greater of $100 or the subscription fees you paid in the preceding twelve months. The same paragraph states the cap does not apply to liabilities arising out of your indemnification obligations or your breach of the Restrictions on Use of the Service.
exposures.whyItMatters: The cap is written as mutual and then unwound on the two routes by which a user would actually owe money. Canva's maximum exposure to a free user is $100; the user's exposure under the indemnity is uncapped.

reference.label: 14. Limitation of Liability
reference.quote: These limitations will not apply to liabilities arising out of your indemnification obligations or your breach of the section entitled 'restrictions on use of the service.'

exposures.title: Mandatory arbitration with no opt-out and no fee relief
exposures.whatItMeans: Claims go to binding AAA arbitration under the Consumer Arbitration Rules, brought only individually, with class and representative proceedings barred and the right to a jury trial expressly waived. Each party pays its own AAA filing, administrative and arbitrator fees.
exposures.whyItMatters: No opt-out is offered at any point, which places Canva alongside Amazon at the closed end of the corpus's arbitration spectrum and below Dropbox, which offers 30 days, and OpenAI, which reopens the window on every update. Dropbox also reimburses fees on claims under $75,000; Canva does not, so the filing cost can exceed the value of a consumer design subscription dispute.

reference.label: 16.d Dispute Resolution
reference.quote: All Claims must be brought in the parties' individual capacity, and not as a plaintiff or class member in any purported class or representative proceeding.

exposures.title: Termination for a violation costs you the work, the money, and the account
exposures.whatItMeans: Where Canva determines in its reasonable discretion that a Violation occurred it may delete the account with all Designs and User Content, permanently ban you, and disclose the content to government authorities or law enforcement. You get no refund, must immediately pay outstanding fees for the remaining subscription period, lose the ability to export, and may not open a new account without written permission.
exposures.whyItMatters: Every consequence lands at once and on Canva's own determination. The obligation to keep paying for a service you have been banned from is the unusual part — cancellation by you forfeits prepaid fees, and termination by Canva accelerates the unpaid ones.

reference.label: 15.c Effect of Termination
reference.quote: In the event of a termination of your subscription due to a Violation by you, you will not receive any refund and will immediately pay any outstanding fees for the remaining period of your subscription.

exposures.title: Signing up with a work email hands your employer the account
exposures.whatItMeans: Using an employer or organisation email address makes the account an Administered Account, binds that organisation to the terms, and lets Canva share your email, name and account information with it and give it control. The administrator can then access, transfer and control the account and all content and designs, change billing and privacy settings, and delete it.
exposures.whyItMatters: The trigger is the email address, not a decision to join a team, and the takeover can happen to an account you already had. Canva promises only reasonable efforts to give advance notice so you can move content to a personal account first.

reference.label: 1.b Signing up with a managed email address
reference.quote: the Admin Entity's admin may be able to access, transfer and control your Administered Account and all content and designs associated with it

exposures.title: You indemnify Canva for anything you upload
exposures.whatItMeans: You must defend and indemnify Canva and its affiliates, officers, directors, agents, licensors and employees against all claims, costs, damages, losses, liabilities and expenses including attorneys' fees, resulting from your violation of the terms or from your User Content.
exposures.whyItMatters: The trigger for the User Content limb is the content existing, not you being at fault — a third-party claim about an image you uploaded in good faith is within it. Read with the limitation-of-liability section, this is the obligation the $100 cap explicitly does not limit.

exposures.title: Teammates can take ownership of what you made
exposures.whatItMeans: A Team Owner or Administrator may control access to, delete, or re-assign ownership of the User Content you upload and Designs you create on a Team account, and Canva states it is not responsible for anything they do.
exposures.whyItMatters: The terms' own advice is to keep personal work on a personal account, which is an admission that ownership inside a Team is not stable. Content included in a shared Design also remains available in that Design after your subscription ends.

exposures.title: Canva does not promise to keep your data
exposures.whatItMeans: The warranty disclaimer states expressly that Canva does not warrant it will preserve or maintain your data without loss, alongside the usual as-is and as-available disclaimers.
exposures.whyItMatters: For a platform whose purpose is storing and editing your designs, the absence of any data-preservation warranty means the $100 cap is the measure of what losing all of it is worth.

reference.label: 11. Warranty Disclaimer
reference.quote: Canva does not warrant that it will review your data for accuracy or that it will preserve or maintain your data without loss.

exposures.title: Creating an account is consent to marketing
exposures.whatItMeans: By creating a Canva account you consent to receiving offers, updates and marketing communications by email, phone number or other contact details provided, with withdrawal available through Message Preferences or an unsubscribe link.
exposures.whyItMatters: Consent is bundled into account creation rather than asked for separately, so the default is on and the burden of switching it off is the user's. The opt-out is genuine and free, which is what keeps this from being worse.

exposures.title: Seats are billed by default unless removed in time
exposures.whatItMeans: Under the Pay as You Grow model, seats added to a Team are billed on the next Billing Date unless removed first, with three days' email notice to the billing contact. No refund or credit is given for removing seats already paid for.
exposures.whyItMatters: Three days' notice to a single billing contact is a narrow window to catch seats added by someone else on the team, and annual subscribers are billed for seat changes every three months rather than at renewal.

reference.label: 9.b Pricing for Additional Seats on your Team

exposures.title: Canva can hand the contract to someone else without telling you
exposures.whatItMeans: Canva may transfer or assign its rights and obligations in whole or in part at any time, with or without notice. You may not assign without Canva's written consent, except to a successor by merger or change of control.
exposures.whyItMatters: The asymmetry is explicit, and the clause that would normally require notice of a change in counterparty says the opposite. Your designs and the AI-training settings attached to them travel with the assignment.

availableActions.action: Turn off AI training on your content and usage data
availableActions.howTo: Open Privacy Settings. The terms state these settings control whether your general usage data and User Content may be used by Canva and its trusted partners to develop and improve AI-powered features, and that you can review and update them at any time.

availableActions.action: Never sign up with your work email address
availableActions.howTo: Use a personal address. An organisation-provisioned address makes the account an Administered Account, binds your employer to these terms, and permits Canva to hand over control of the account and everything in it on the employer's request.

reference.label: 1.b Signing up with a managed email address

availableActions.action: Keep personal work off Team accounts
availableActions.howTo: The terms advise this directly: do not upload User Content or create Designs on a Team account if you do not want to potentially transfer ownership or disclose them. Administrators can re-assign ownership and delete content.

availableActions.action: Export before you cancel, and long before any dispute
availableActions.howTo: Download or export User Content and Designs using the Service's own functionality prior to expiry or termination. This route is available unless the account was terminated for a Violation, in which case the terms remove it entirely.

availableActions.action: Cancel a free trial before it converts
availableActions.howTo: At the end of a free trial Canva charges the next billing cycle's subscription fee to your nominated payment method unless you cancel first. Cancellation is in account settings.

deadline.description: Before the free trial or pilot period ends, otherwise the subscription fee for the next billing cycle is charged automatically.

availableActions.action: Use the price-rise window
availableActions.howTo: A price increase does not apply until your next renewal or thirty days after notice, whichever is later. Cancel within that period if you do not want the new price.

deadline.description: A price increase takes effect at the next renewal or 30 days after notice, whichever is later.

availableActions.action: Adjust marketing preferences after signing up
availableActions.howTo: Account creation is itself the consent. Use Message Preferences or the unsubscribe link in any marketing message — the terms confirm withdrawal is free and that service and legally required messages continue regardless.

availableActions.action: Remove Team seats before the Billing Date
availableActions.howTo: Seats are billed on the next Billing Date unless removed first, and Canva emails the billing contact three days beforehand. For annual subscriptions the Billing Date recurs every three months from the subscription start, not just at renewal.

deadline.description: Notice of additional seats and their fees is emailed to the billing contact three days before the Billing Date; removals after that are billed with no refund.

reference.label: 9.b Pricing for Additional Seats on your Team

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: A genuine control in Privacy Settings covering both general usage data and User Content, reviewable at any time, with Canva Education content excluded from AI training outright. The terms do not state whether the default is on or off.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Reasonable advance notice, but only for changes Canva reasonably determines materially adversely affect your rights, delivered in-service or by email. Continued use constitutes agreement.

requiredDisclosures.name: Advance notice of fee changes
requiredDisclosures.note: Price increases apply at the next renewal or 30 days after notice, whichever is later, with cancellation available instead.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automatic renewal disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: Subscriptions renew automatically each billing cycle with notice before auto-renewal, and free trials convert to a paid subscription unless cancelled first.

requiredDisclosures.name: Refund and cancellation rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Disclosed and adverse: cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing cycle with no refund of fees already paid except where required by law, and outstanding fees become immediately due.

requiredDisclosures.name: Arbitration opt-out right
requiredDisclosures.note: None is offered. Arbitration is mandatory from acceptance, with a class action waiver and an express jury trial waiver, and each party bearing its own AAA fees.

requiredDisclosures.name: Pre-arbitration dispute procedure
requiredDisclosures.note: Users are directed to contact Canva first so it can attempt to resolve the dispute, but no notice period or form is specified and no fee consequence attaches to skipping it.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: California law, with US court filings in the Northern District of California or Santa Clara County. The contracting entity depends on billing address — Canva US, Inc, Canva UK Operations Ltd, or Canva Pty Ltd in Australia for everywhere else, including India.

requiredDisclosures.name: Company identification details
requiredDisclosures.note: All three contracting entities are named with full legal notice addresses in Austin, London and Surry Hills.

requiredDisclosures.name: Designated DMCA agent
requiredDisclosures.note: The terms state Canva responds to DMCA-compliant notices and refer to an Intellectual Property Policy, but name no designated agent or address in this document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Minimum age
requiredDisclosures.note: Under 13, or the local minimum age for consent to data processing, may not use the Service except through Canva Education, which is certified COPPA and FERPA compliant by iKeepSafe.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: This is the en_in edition and names no grievance officer or response timeline, directing complaints to the Trust Centre and a general contact form.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer rights preservation
requiredDisclosures.note: States the terms do not affect consumer rights that cannot lawfully be waived, and that no limitation applies to gross negligence, fraud or wilful misconduct.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period is stated. The only deletion commitment is on termination, where Canva may delete all data unless legally prohibited.

analyses.summary: Google's dispute terms are among the best in the corpus — no arbitration, no class action waiver, no indemnity or liability cap for consumers, advance notice and an appeal before an account is suspended, and Takeout export if a service is withdrawn. What it takes instead is the content. The licence over everything you put into Gmail, Drive, Photos and Docs is worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable to contractors, includes modification and derivative works, and is granted for a purpose that expressly includes developing new technologies and services for Google. It lasts as long as the content is protected by copyright, not until you delete it — deleting stops public availability, not the licence. Content is analysed automatically as it is sent, received and stored. Nothing in the terms offers an opt-out from that development use, while the rules for you forbid using Google's AI output to build models of your own. Indian users contract with Google LLC in Delaware, under California law in Santa Clara County courts, with Google's Indian entities expressly excluded from the definition of Google.

exposures.title: The licence over your content outlives your deletion of it
exposures.whatItMeans: The licence lasts for as long as your content is protected by intellectual property rights — for a photo or a document, the life of copyright. Removing content commits Google only to stop making it publicly available within a reasonable time.
exposures.whyItMatters: Most users read deletion as ending the arrangement. Here the two are separate: what ends is public visibility, not the worldwide, sublicensable right to host, reproduce, modify and create derivative works. The clause states no mechanism by which the licence itself is ever terminated.

reference.label: Licence — Duration
reference.quote: This licence lasts for as long as your content is protected by intellectual property rights.

exposures.title: Your content is licensed for developing new Google technologies
exposures.whatItMeans: The stated purposes of the licence are operating and improving the services, promoting the services with content you shared publicly, and developing new technologies and services for Google.
exposures.whyItMatters: The first two purposes are bounded by the service you are using; the third is not bounded by anything. Read with the separate statement that Google uses artificial intelligence and machine learning across its services, this is the clause that would carry model development, and the terms name no opt-out from it anywhere.

reference.label: Licence — Purpose
reference.quote: developing new technologies and services for Google consistent with these terms

exposures.title: Everything is analysed in transit and at rest
exposures.whatItMeans: Automated systems and algorithms analyse your content for spam and malware, to recognise patterns, and to customise services including personalised search results, content and ads. The terms state this analysis occurs as content is sent, received and while it is stored.
exposures.whyItMatters: The defined scope of 'your content' includes emails you send and receive through Gmail, videos in Drive, and documents you create. Only the advertising element is described as adjustable, through Ads Settings; the pattern-recognition and customisation analysis is not presented as optional.

reference.label: Licence — Purpose
reference.quote: This analysis occurs as the content is sent, received, and when it is stored.

exposures.title: Google may build models from your content; you may not build models from its output
exposures.whatItMeans: Users are prohibited from using AI-generated content from Google's services to develop machine learning models or related AI technology, and from reverse engineering Google's machine learning models. Google's own licence over user content extends to developing new technologies.
exposures.whyItMatters: The same activity is permitted in one direction and forbidden in the other, in a single document. The asymmetry is what makes the absence of any AI training opt-out consequential rather than incidental.

reference.label: Do not abuse our services
reference.quote: using AI-generated content from our services to develop machine learning models or related AI technology

exposures.title: Indian users contract with a Delaware company, and Google's Indian entities are excluded
exposures.whatItMeans: This is the India country version, but the service provider is Google LLC in Mountain View, the definition of Google excludes any local entities based in India, and disputes go to the state or federal courts of Santa Clara County, California under California law.
exposures.whyItMatters: For an Indian consumer the practical forum is a US court, and the local Google entity is defined out of the agreement. The terms preserve local courts only to the extent applicable local law prevents the California forum, which puts the burden on the user to establish that first.

reference.label: Settling disputes, governing law, and courts
reference.quote: These disputes will be resolved exclusively in the federal or state courts of Santa Clara County, California, USA

exposures.title: The licence is sublicensable to contractors you never see
exposures.whatItMeans: Google may sublicense its rights over your content to other users where the service requires it, and to contractors who have signed agreements consistent with these terms, for the limited purposes in the Purpose section.
exposures.whyItMatters: The contractors are not named or categorised, and the purposes they inherit include developing new technologies. The protection is contractual and internal to Google's supply chain rather than something a user can inspect or refuse.

exposures.title: Services use your data allowance while you are not using them
exposures.whatItMeans: Google states its services frequently use the internet when you are not actively engaged with them or your device, for purposes including software updates, security, user experience, Google's operations and advertising, and that you are responsible for the resulting network costs.
exposures.whyItMatters: Advertising is named among the purposes for background data use, and on metered mobile plans the cost of that lands on the user. The terms offer no way to limit it beyond checking your own device and network settings.

reference.label: Mobile, Wi-Fi, and other Network Connection Costs
reference.quote: Google uses the Internet in this way for a wide variety of purposes—for example, to provide software updates and to improve Google's services, security, user experience, and/or Google's operations, including advertising.

exposures.title: Breaking the law can mean your identity goes to the victims
exposures.whatItMeans: If you violate applicable law, Google states it may report certain offences to the authorities and that your identity may be disclosed to the victims, in addition to content removal and account termination.
exposures.whyItMatters: Disclosure of identity to a private party is a step beyond reporting to authorities, and the trigger is Google's assessment of a legal violation rather than a finding by a court.

reference.label: Taking action in case of problems
reference.quote: you may be subject to penalties or punishment under applicable law, and your identity may be disclosed to the victims

exposures.title: An organisation's administrator can reach or disable your account
exposures.whatItMeans: Where an organisation's administrator assigns you a Google Account, that administrator may require additional rules and may be able to access or disable the account.
exposures.whyItMatters: The same sentence covers a school and an employer, and the terms place no limit on what the administrator may access. This is the same exposure Dropbox creates for team accounts, stated more briefly.

reference.label: Using Google services on behalf of an organisation or business

exposures.title: Notice of material change is 'reasonable', with carve-outs
exposures.whatItMeans: Material changes carry reasonable advance notice and an opportunity to review, except when Google launches a new service or feature, or in urgent situations such as preventing abuse or responding to legal requirements. Disagreeing means removing your content and closing the account.
exposures.whyItMatters: 'Reasonable' is Google's judgement rather than a stated period — Netflix and Dropbox both commit to a specific month or thirty days. The new-service carve-out matters because new services are where new terms usually arrive.

availableActions.action: Turn off ad personalisation
availableActions.howTo: Use Ads Settings. The terms name this as the control for the customisation limb of the content analysis — recommendations, personalised search results, content and ads. It does not stop the spam, malware and pattern-recognition analysis.

availableActions.action: Export everything with Takeout before you need to
availableActions.howTo: Google Takeout is named in the terms as the export route, and is committed to when Google makes material changes that negatively affect you or stops offering a service. Running it periodically means an account suspension does not have to be the first time you try.

reference.label: Develop, improve, and update Google services

availableActions.action: Appeal a suspension rather than accepting it
availableActions.howTo: The terms state that if you believe your account has been suspended or terminated in error you can appeal, and that Google will normally give advance notice, a reason, and an opportunity to address the issue first.

reference.label: Suspending or terminating your access to Google services

availableActions.action: Sue in your local court where local law allows it
availableActions.howTo: There is no arbitration clause and no class action waiver. Where applicable local law prevents a dispute being resolved in California, the terms permit filing in your local courts, and where local law prevents California law applying, local law governs.

reference.label: Settling disputes, governing law, and courts

availableActions.action: Treat what you upload as licensed for the life of its copyright
availableActions.howTo: Deletion stops public availability but the licence text is tied to the duration of your intellectual property rights, not to deletion. For material you would not want used in developing new Google technologies, the decision point is upload, not deletion.

availableActions.action: Check the country version attached to your account
availableActions.howTo: Sign in and view the terms to see which country your account is associated with. That association determines which Google affiliate provides the service, processes your data, and which version of the terms governs — for India it is Google LLC, with local Indian entities excluded.

availableActions.action: Limit background data at the device level
availableActions.howTo: The terms make you responsible for network usage occurring when you are not actively using the services, and suggest checking your mobile or internet plan and your device and network settings. Restricting background data for Google apps is the only lever named.

reference.label: Mobile, Wi-Fi, and other Network Connection Costs

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Reasonable advance notice and an opportunity to review for material changes, but with no stated period and with carve-outs for new services or features and for urgent situations.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: California law, exclusive jurisdiction in Santa Clara County, with a preserved fallback to local courts and local law where applicable local law requires it.

requiredDisclosures.name: Arbitration clause
requiredDisclosures.note: There is none, and no class action waiver either. Disputes go to courts. The third document in the corpus with this posture, after LinkedIn and Netflix.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: No opt-out is offered. The content licence expressly covers developing new technologies and services for Google, and the terms separately state Google uses artificial intelligence and machine learning across its services, while prohibiting users from developing models from Google's AI output.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: This is the India country version and names no grievance officer, address or response timeline, though the IT Rules 2021 require significant social media intermediaries to publish one. Users are directed to a general contact page.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period appears in the terms. The only duration stated is the content licence's, which runs for as long as the content is protected by copyright.

requiredDisclosures.name: Repeat infringer policy
requiredDisclosures.note: Google states it suspends or closes the accounts of repeat copyright infringers, with detail referred to the Copyright Help Centre. No DMCA agent is named in this document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer indemnity
requiredDisclosures.note: The indemnity is expressly limited to business users and organisations, and carves out liability caused by Google's own breach, negligence or wilful misconduct. Consumers owe no indemnity under these terms.

requiredDisclosures.name: Limitation on indemnity
requiredDisclosures.note: For business users the cap is the greater of US$500 or 125% of fees paid in the preceding 12 months. No monetary cap is applied to consumers, and liability for fraud, death or personal injury by negligence, gross negligence and wilful misconduct is excluded from every limitation.

requiredDisclosures.name: Minimum age
requiredDisclosures.note: Stated by reference rather than by number — the age required to manage your own Google Account, with parental permission below it and additional service-specific age requirements.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer rights preservation
requiredDisclosures.note: Opens the About these terms section by stating that rights which cannot be limited by contract are not restricted, and repeats the carve-out for local consumer forums and local governing law.

requiredDisclosures.name: Company identification details
requiredDisclosures.note: Google LLC, organised under Delaware law, 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California 94043, with EU consumer-service affiliates named in the definitions.

analyses.summary: MakeMyTrip's cookie policy is better than most of its peers on the things that are easy to get wrong: it states explicit consent as the lawful basis, renews that consent every twelve months, and honours browser Do Not Track by automatically disabling advertising cookies. Where it costs the user is the exit — withdrawing consent requires emailing the data protection officer rather than clicking anything, and the opt-out only works if you allow the third-party cookies you are trying to avoid.

exposures.title: Opting out requires allowing third-party cookies
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy states that for the opt-out to work, your browser must permit third-party cookies.
exposures.whyItMatters: The mechanism used to remember that you refused tracking is the same mechanism used to track. A privacy-hardened browser that blocks third-party cookies silently loses the opt-out, and nothing tells you it has stopped working.

reference.label: How Do I Turn Off Cookies or Withdraw Consent?
reference.quote: for the opt-out to work for you, your browser must allow third-party cookies

exposures.title: Withdrawing consent is an email, not a setting
exposures.whatItMeans: Consent is granted by clicking a button in the product, but revoking it requires writing to dpo@makemytrip.com.
exposures.whyItMatters: The asymmetry is the point: one click in, one email and an unspecified wait out. There is no stated response time and no in-product control.

reference.label: How Do I Turn Off Cookies or Withdraw Consent?
reference.quote: If you wish to revoke your consent for use of cookies, please reach out to us at dpo@makemytrip.com

exposures.title: Data gathered before you opt out is kept and used
exposures.whatItMeans: Disabling a cookie stops further collection but does not undo what was already collected.
exposures.whyItMatters: Opting out is forward-looking only. The policy is explicit about this, which is more honest than most, but it means a late opt-out does not recover the history.

reference.label: How Do I Turn Off Cookies or Withdraw Consent?
reference.quote: we may still use information collected from cookies prior to your disabled preference being set

exposures.title: Tracking pixels on third-party sites measure ad exposure
exposures.whatItMeans: Web beacons and action tags count visitors who arrive after seeing a MakeMyTrip banner elsewhere.
exposures.whyItMatters: It links your presence on unrelated sites to your arrival here, though the policy states the result is aggregated and not used to access personal information.

reference.label: What is a Cookie?
reference.quote: a visitor identification technology such as “web beacons”, or “action tags”, which count visitors who have come to the website after being exposed to an MMT banner ad on a third-party site

exposures.title: Cookie data feeds marketing contact, not just ads
exposures.whatItMeans: Information collected via cookies may be used to communicate with you, send newsletters, seek feedback and send promotional material.
exposures.whyItMatters: It crosses from shaping what you see into contacting you directly, which most readers would treat as a separate decision from accepting cookies.

reference.label: How We use Cookie?
reference.quote: We may use information collected via cookies to communicate with you, for sending newsletters, seeking your opinion and feedback and providing you services and promotional materials.

availableActions.action: Turn on Do Not Track in your browser
availableActions.howTo: The policy states that if it detects Do Not Track it will automatically disable advertising and targeting cookies. That is a one-time browser setting requiring no contact with the company.

reference.label: How Do I Turn Off Cookies or Withdraw Consent?
reference.quote: If we detect that you have enabled the do not track setting in your browser, we will automatically disable advertising/ targeting cookies.

availableActions.action: Email the DPO to withdraw consent
availableActions.howTo: Write to dpo@makemytrip.com. This is the only stated route to revoke consent; no in-product toggle is described.

reference.label: How Do I Turn Off Cookies or Withdraw Consent?

availableActions.action: Expect to be asked again within twelve months
availableActions.howTo: Consent is renewed annually from the date it was given, so a refusal is not permanent and the prompt will return.

reference.label: Basis for Lawful Processing
reference.quote: We seek to renew your consent every 12 months from the date of obtaining the consent.

requiredDisclosures.name: Lawful basis for cookie processing
requiredDisclosures.note: Explicit consent is named as the basis, with an annual renewal cycle — materially better than the peers captured alongside it, most of which state no basis at all.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent withdrawal mechanism
requiredDisclosures.note: A route exists, but it is an email to the DPO rather than an in-product control, and no response time is stated.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data protection officer contact
requiredDisclosures.note: dpo@makemytrip.com is published for both consent withdrawal and rights requests.

requiredDisclosures.name: Cookie categories and retention periods
requiredDisclosures.note: First-party vs third-party and persistent vs session are distinguished, though persistent cookies are described only as lasting 'a pre-defined period' without naming it.

analyses.summary: Snap's cookie policy is unusually forthcoming about who receives data — it names eleven advertising partners outright, including Facebook, Google, LinkedIn, Reddit, PayPal and The Trade Desk. What it asks in return is that you accept tracking that runs in both directions across the open web, and that you set your preferences separately on each of seven different Snap domains. Essential cookies may be active before you have chosen anything.

exposures.title: Snap tracks you on other companies' websites
exposures.whatItMeans: Snap places cookies on third-party services and collects your activity there, using it to target and measure advertising.
exposures.whyItMatters: This runs outside Snapchat entirely. Managing it inside the app does not reach it, and the policy points you to a separate Advertising Preferences page rather than controlling it here.

reference.label: Provided by Us
reference.quote: We may collect information about your activity on third-party services that use cookies provided by us.

exposures.title: Other companies combine your Snap activity with data from elsewhere
exposures.whatItMeans: Partners allowed to set cookies on Snap's services may build a profile over time and merge it with information gathered from other services and companies.
exposures.whyItMatters: The result is a cross-company profile that neither you nor Snap fully controls, and the policy discloses the practice without limiting it.

reference.label: Provided by Others
reference.quote: These companies may collect information about how you use our services over time and combine it with similar information from other services and companies.

exposures.title: Essential cookies run before you make any choice
exposures.whatItMeans: Cookies classified as essential may be active from the moment you access the site, and in some jurisdictions that includes session cookies used to understand how you browse.
exposures.whyItMatters: Analytics-shaped use is placed in the category that does not wait for consent. The policy does say these expire within 24 hours and are then anonymised, and that they can be disabled — but only after the fact.

reference.label: Essential
reference.quote: Because they are essential, they may be active from the moment you access the website.

exposures.title: Preferences must be set separately on seven domains
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy lists distinct cookie-settings pages for snap.com, snapchat.com, spectacles.com, yellowla.com, snapfoundation.org, arcadiacreativestudio.com and pixy.com.
exposures.whyItMatters: One decision does not carry across Snap's own properties. A refusal recorded on snapchat.com leaves the other six untouched, and nothing in the flow tells you that.

exposures.title: Stopping app collection requires uninstalling
exposures.whatItMeans: For the mobile app, the policy offers device identifier settings and, failing that, uninstalling Snapchat.
exposures.whyItMatters: Uninstalling is offered as a privacy control, which is another way of saying there is no in-app setting that stops the collection this policy describes.

reference.label: Device Identifier Settings
reference.quote: if your mobile device offers an uninstall process, you can always stop us from collecting information through the app by uninstalling the Snapchat app

availableActions.action: Set cookie preferences on every Snap domain you use
availableActions.howTo: The policy links a separate cookie settings page for each of seven Snap sites. Setting them on one does not affect the others.

availableActions.action: Use the device-level advertising ID opt-out
availableActions.howTo: iOS and Android both allow limiting ad tracking at the operating-system level, which reaches the app collection that in-app settings do not.

availableActions.action: Review the named advertising partners
availableActions.howTo: The policy names eleven — Bing, Facebook, Google Analytics, Hubspot, LinkedIn, Pardot, PayPal, Pinterest, Reddit, The Trade Desk, Twitter. Each has its own opt-out, and the disclosure is specific enough to act on.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Eleven advertising partners are named individually — materially more specific than the category-level descriptions most peers in this corpus give.

requiredDisclosures.name: Cookie duration and purpose detail
requiredDisclosures.note: Purposes are categorised and a separate Cookie Information Page is said to list each cookie with its purpose and lifetime.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: Settings pages exist, but the policy states essential cookies may run from first access and describes browser and site settings as after-the-fact controls rather than a prior consent gate.

analyses.summary: Zerodha's terms cap the broker's total liability at one hundred rupees — roughly a dollar — for a business that holds its customers' securities portfolios. Around that sit the terms that make the cap matter. Every order placed with your credentials is yours whether or not the person entering it was authorised, and Zerodha states it assumes no responsibility for unauthorised access at all. Securities lodged as margin can be sold at Zerodha's sole choice of which ones, to cover debts owed not only by you but by any member of your 'Group' as defined in your account-opening schedule, and can be re-pledged onward to any institution Zerodha deems fit. Errors in a contract note must be raised within 24 hours or the note is deemed accepted, and Zerodha reserves the right to reject the objection anyway. The terms change without notice or communication of any kind. And the client indemnifies Zerodha against losses caused by technical issues at Zerodha's own end. Two things run the other way, and both are real: a grievance officer is named for each entity with a 24-hour acknowledgement and 15-day disposal commitment, and arbitration is genuinely mutual. The contrast with Zerodha's own privacy policy, which is the mildest finance document in the corpus, is the sharpest within-site split found so far.

exposures.title: Total liability is capped at one hundred rupees
exposures.whatItMeans: The terms state that in any event Zerodha's liability arising out of them shall not exceed INR 100, alongside the usual exclusion of indirect, consequential, special and exemplary damages including loss of business, revenue, profits and goodwill.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the lowest absolute liability cap in the corpus — below Dropbox's $20 and Canva's $100, and unlike Paytm's it is a flat figure rather than one that scales with what you paid. The counterparty is a SEBI-registered broker and depository participant holding the client's demat holdings, so the gap between the cap and the value at risk is the entire portfolio.

reference.label: 24.7 Miscellaneous
reference.quote: In any event, the liability of Zerodha arising out of the Terms shall not exceed INR 100 (Indian Rupees One Hundred Only).

exposures.title: Trades made by someone who stole your credentials are still yours
exposures.whatItMeans: Clients are solely responsible for all orders and transactions executed with their login credentials, expressly irrespective of whether the person executing them was authorised to do so, and Zerodha states it assumes no responsibility whatsoever for liabilities arising out of unauthorised access to a password or 2FA credentials.
exposures.whyItMatters: The terms elsewhere acknowledge the risk of third parties hacking the account and routing orders, and then place the entire consequence on the client. Combined with the INR 100 cap, a compromised account producing losses has no recourse against the broker even where the compromise involved Zerodha's systems.

reference.label: 4.7 Account security and passwords
reference.quote: Clients shall solely be responsible for all orders entered and transactions executed on the Platform using their login credentials, irrespective of whether the person actually executing such transactions were authorised to do so or not.

exposures.title: Your securities can be sold to cover someone else's debts
exposures.whatItMeans: Zerodha has an irrevocable right at its sole discretion to set off margin — by appropriating cash or by selling or transferring securities — against dues of the Client or of any member of the Client's Group, defined as the individuals, group companies, firms and entities listed in the schedule to the Member Client Agreement signed at account opening. Where securities are sold, the choice of which ones is solely Zerodha's.
exposures.whyItMatters: A default by a company or family member listed in a schedule you signed years ago can be settled out of your portfolio, and you do not choose which holdings are liquidated. Most clients will not recall what that schedule contained.

exposures.title: Margin securities are re-pledged onward at Zerodha's discretion
exposures.whatItMeans: Any securities or cash placed as margin may in turn be placed as margin by Zerodha with exchanges, banks, clearing corporations or any other institutions Zerodha deems fit, and the client authorises all acts necessary to do so.
exposures.whyItMatters: The open-ended category — any other institutions Zerodha may deem fit — means the set of parties holding an interest in your securities is not knowable from the contract, and the client's authorisation is given in advance for all of them.

exposures.title: You indemnify Zerodha for Zerodha's own technical failures
exposures.whatItMeans: The client indemnifies Zerodha, its affiliates, partners, directors, employees and agents against losses suffered by Zerodha, its other customers, or third parties arising from — among other things — bank delays or any technical issue at Zerodha's end that delays fulfilment of a mutual fund order and changes the NAV at which it is placed.
exposures.whyItMatters: An indemnity normally covers harm the indemnifying party caused. Limb (c) covers harm caused by the indemnified party's own systems, and extends to losses suffered by Zerodha's other customers, which is a liability of unknown size arising from something entirely outside the client's control.

reference.label: 18.1 Indemnities
reference.quote: in case of bank delays or any technical issue at Zerodha's end that may lead to the delay of the fulfilment of an order and the resultant change in the NAV at which the order is placed

exposures.title: The terms change without notice, and using the account is agreement
exposures.whatItMeans: The terms state the information is subject to change without notice, and that the client agrees to any and all changes without specific communication from Zerodha, by continuing to use the platform or hold an account.
exposures.whyItMatters: There is no notification, no effective date, and no version comparison. Holding an existing account is enough to accept terms you were never told changed — and the version analysed was last updated in December 2023, so there is no way for a client to know what has moved since.

reference.label: 1.3 General Terms
reference.quote: You agree to any and all changes to the Terms without specific communication from Zerodha, by Your continuing usage of the Platform and/or continuing to hold an account with Zerodha.

exposures.title: Twenty-four hours to find an error, and Zerodha can reject the objection
exposures.whatItMeans: Errors in reports, statements or contract notes — including wrong execution prices, wrong scrips or wrong quantities — must be notified in writing by email within 24 hours of receipt, and the terms state Zerodha has the right to accept or reject the objection. Anything not objected to within 24 hours is deemed accepted.
exposures.whyItMatters: Contract notes arrive by email within 24 hours of the trade, so the window can expire while a client is away from their inbox for two days. It applies to the exact category of error a client is least likely to spot quickly, and the final say on a timely objection still rests with Zerodha.

exposures.title: Consent to calls and messages that overrides the national DND registry
exposures.whatItMeans: The client authorises Zerodha, its affiliates and representatives to contact them by phone call and SMS notwithstanding the client's registration under Do Not Disturb.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the fourth document in the corpus to take consent that expressly supersedes a user's DND or NCPR registration, after PhonePe, MakeMyTrip and Paytm. A national consumer-protection register is being contracted away in a single sentence buried in a miscellaneous clause, and it extends to affiliates and representatives rather than Zerodha alone.

reference.label: 24.4 Miscellaneous
reference.quote: The Client hereby authorizes Zerodha, its affiliates and representatives to contact them via phone calls and SMS, notwithstanding the Client's registration under DND.

exposures.title: Trading can be restricted at any time with no notice and no liability
exposures.whatItMeans: Zerodha may at any time, at sole discretion and without prior notice, prohibit or restrict a client's ability to place orders or trade in any securities, vary exposure and turnover limits, and impose client-specific surveillance. It states it may be unable to inform the client in advance and is not liable for losses resulting.
exposures.whyItMatters: Being unable to exit a position during volatility is when losses occur, and the terms disclaim exactly that scenario. Section 9.7 goes further: trading may be suspended because of margin shortfalls by other clients, and no client may claim damages for that.

exposures.title: Notice can be given by nailing it to your door
exposures.whatItMeans: Permitted modes of service include affixing the notice on the door at the last known address, oral communication to an answering machine, advertising in a daily newspaper circulating in the area of the last known address, and posting on Zerodha's own notice board if no address is known. Communication returned unclaimed, refused or undelivered is deemed properly served.
exposures.whyItMatters: Deemed service by newspaper advertisement or by a notice on the broker's own board means a client can be bound by a communication they had no realistic chance of receiving, in a relationship where 24-hour objection windows apply.

exposures.title: Account opening fees are not refunded, and reinstatement is final
exposures.whatItMeans: Account opening charges and document pickup charges are non-refundable, with refunds available only where Zerodha fails to open the account within 10 days of complete documentation, or on a case-by-case basis if the account was never activated. Separately, where services are suspended or terminated, Zerodha's decision on reinstatement is stated to be final.
exposures.whyItMatters: The refund carve-outs are reasonable and specific, which makes the finality clause stand out: a client who believes a suspension was wrong has the grievance route but no appeal from the outcome.

availableActions.action: Escalate to the named grievance officer
availableActions.howTo: The Compliance Officer is the grievance officer — Pankathi H Jain for Zerodha Broking Limited and Ashmy Narayanan for Zerodha Commodities. Complaints are acknowledged within 24 hours and disposed of within 15 days, and the officer reports directly to the Board.

deadline.description: Acknowledgement within 24 hours of the complaint; disposal within 15 days of receipt.

availableActions.action: Read every contract note within 24 hours
availableActions.howTo: Contract notes arrive by email within 24 hours of a trade. Errors in price, scrip or quantity must be raised in writing by email within 24 hours of receipt, and anything unchallenged is deemed accepted. Set a filter so these are never missed.

deadline.description: 24 hours from receipt of any report, statement or contract note, after which its correctness is deemed accepted.

availableActions.action: Find out who is in your 'Group'
availableActions.howTo: The schedule to the Member Client Agreement signed at account opening defines the individuals, companies, firms and entities whose dues Zerodha may set off against your margin. Request a copy and check who is listed.

availableActions.action: Use physical Power of Attorney to keep the TPIN requirement, or the reverse
availableActions.howTo: Where the Online DIS route is used, the CDSL TPIN must be entered for every debit or sell transaction from your holdings — a genuine second gate on outgoing securities. It does not apply if you submitted a physical Power of Attorney instead.

availableActions.action: Keep the margin buffer yourself
availableActions.howTo: You must monitor the market value of securities pledged as margin continuously and replenish any shortfall, and the terms state this applies whether or not Zerodha tells you about the shortfall. Failure lets Zerodha liquidate positions of its own choosing.

availableActions.action: Set up authenticator-based 2FA rather than SMS
availableActions.howTo: Zerodha supports TOTP through Authy, Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator as an alternative to SMS or email OTP. Because unauthorised trades remain your responsibility regardless of authorisation, the strength of this factor is doing more work here than in most services.

availableActions.action: Re-read the terms yourself, periodically
availableActions.howTo: There is no notification of any kind when the terms change, and continued account holding is agreement. The last-updated date at the foot of the page is the only signal available.

availableActions.action: Attempt amicable settlement before arbitration
availableActions.howTo: The terms require both parties to try to settle a dispute within 30 days in good faith, after which written notice refers it to a sole arbitrator appointed mutually, or by the Mumbai Centre for International Arbitration if the parties cannot agree. Seat and venue are Bangalore, in English, with a written reasoned award.

deadline.description: A 30-day good-faith settlement period precedes any referral to arbitration.

reference.label: 27. Governing Law, Jurisdiction and Dispute Resolution

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: Both entities' compliance officers are named — Pankathi H Jain and Ashmy Narayanan — with an email route, a 24-hour acknowledgement commitment, a 15-day disposal commitment, and direct reporting to the Board. One of only a handful in the corpus to name a person.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Expressly disclaimed. The terms are subject to change without notice and the client agrees to all changes without any specific communication, by continuing to hold the account.

requiredDisclosures.name: Advance notice of fee changes
requiredDisclosures.note: In contrast to the terms themselves: changes to brokerage, transaction charges, commissions and fees are notified by email and/or SMS to the registered address and number, with the dates they become effective.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Indian law, arbitration by a sole arbitrator under Mumbai Centre for International Arbitration rules seated in Bangalore, and exclusive jurisdiction of the Bangalore courts.

requiredDisclosures.name: Arbitration clause
requiredDisclosures.note: Genuinely mutual, unlike Paytm's, where arbitration is an election the company alone holds. Preceded by a 30-day amicable settlement period, with the arbitrator mutually appointed or named by MCIA, and no class action waiver in the document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Refund and cancellation rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Account opening and document pickup charges are non-refundable, with a full refund if Zerodha fails to open the account within 10 days of complete documentation, a duplicate-payment refund route, and case-by-case consideration where the account was never activated.

requiredDisclosures.name: Company identification details
requiredDisclosures.note: Both entities with full SEBI registration numbers — INZ000031633 for Zerodha Broking, INZ000038238 and MCX 46025 for Zerodha Commodities, CDSL depository participant IN-DP-431-2019 — plus CIN and registered office.

requiredDisclosures.name: Limitation on indemnity
requiredDisclosures.note: The client indemnity is uncapped and extends to losses suffered by Zerodha's other customers and by third parties, including from technical issues at Zerodha's own end. Zerodha's own liability is capped at INR 100.

requiredDisclosures.name: Minimum age
requiredDisclosures.note: Clients warrant they are at least 18 and not barred by law from accessing the platform.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent withdrawal mechanism
requiredDisclosures.note: The DND override at clause 24.4 is granted with no stated mechanism for withdrawing it, and it extends to affiliates and representatives.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No retention period appears in the terms. The privacy policy does not state one either.

analyses.summary: PayPal's India user agreement puts almost every decision that matters about your money inside PayPal's sole discretion, and says so plainly. Funds can be held for 180 days or longer; reserves are set on confidential criteria PayPal has no obligation to explain; Buyer Protection is decided by PayPal and its first decision is final. You cannot close the account while any of that is running, though PayPal may end the relationship at will. Sellers additionally accept $2,500 per violation as pre-agreed damages, deductible from any PayPal account they control, and give up control of how their own checkout presents payment options. Smaller things worth knowing: your card details are refreshed from third-party sources without you acting, changes that reduce your rights need only 14 days' notice, and PayPal takes over your claim against a recipient whenever it reverses your payment. The one place it reads better than its peers is disputes — arbitration is your option rather than a requirement, and there is no class-action waiver.

exposures.title: PayPal decides your Buyer Protection claim, and its first answer is the final one
exposures.whatItMeans: PayPal alone determines whether a claim qualifies for Buyer Protection. The original determination is treated as final. An appeal is possible only if you have new or compelling information that was unavailable at the time, or you believe the process itself erred.
exposures.whyItMatters: The protection people rely on when paying a stranger online is adjudicated by the same company that operates the payment, with no neutral reviewer, and 'I disagree with the outcome' is expressly not a ground for a second look.

reference.label: PayPal's Buyer Protection Program
reference.quote: PayPal determines, in its sole discretion, whether your claim qualifies for the Buyer Protection program. PayPal's original determination is considered final

exposures.title: Your money can be held for 180 days, and longer than that under legal process
exposures.whatItMeans: If PayPal believes you engaged in a restricted activity, it may hold your funds for up to 180 days, and the hold may run past 180 days where a court order or regulatory requirement applies. Risk-based holds on incoming payments run up to 21 days and extend to 180 if a transaction is disputed.
exposures.whyItMatters: Half a year without access to your own balance ends most small businesses, and the trigger is PayPal's belief rather than any finding by anyone else.

reference.label: Actions We May Take if You Engage in Any Restricted Activities
reference.quote: Hold your funds for up to 180 days if reasonably needed to protect against the risk of liability

exposures.title: You cannot close the account while PayPal is looking at it
exposures.whatItMeans: Closure is blocked while you are under investigation, while a transaction, dispute or claim is open, while the balance is negative, and while any hold, limitation or reserve is in place. Any funds held at closure are paid out at PayPal's discretion.
exposures.whyItMatters: Walking away is the ordinary remedy when a service turns against you. Here the conditions that would make you want to leave are the same conditions that prevent it. The exit is one-sided in the other direction too: PayPal reserves sole discretion to suspend or terminate for any reason at any time.

reference.label: Closing Your PayPal Account
reference.quote: In certain cases, you may not close your PayPal account, including: To evade an investigation.

exposures.title: Reserves and limitations are set on criteria PayPal will not disclose
exposures.whatItMeans: Holds, limitations and reserves may rest on confidential criteria and proprietary risk models, and PayPal states it has no obligation to explain them.
