A rolling reserve withholds a percentage of every payment for a set period; a minimum reserve requires a floor balance you cannot withdraw.
exposures.whyItMatters: You cannot correct a decision whose basis you are not told, and you cannot price a business around a reserve percentage that can be re-set whenever PayPal's assessment of you changes.

reference.label: What are holds, limitations and reserves?
reference.quote: We have no obligation to disclose the details of our risk management or security procedures to you.

exposures.title: $2,500 per violation, pre-agreed, taken from any account you control
exposures.whatItMeans: For Acceptable Use Policy violations tied to fraud or counterfeit goods, you agree in advance that $2,500 per violation is a reasonable minimum estimate of PayPal's damages, and that PayPal may debit it directly from the balance of any PayPal account you control.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is a penalty you consented to before any dispute, calculated per violation, collected by self-help from accounts other than the one involved — no demand, no proof of loss, no court. Where you hold more than one account, a negative balance in either may be set off against the other.

reference.label: Actions We May Take if You Engage in Any Restricted Activities
reference.quote: PayPal may deduct such damages directly from any existing balance in any PayPal account you control

exposures.title: An irrevocable worldwide licence to your content, with your moral rights waived
exposures.whatItMeans: Content you provide or post through PayPal Services is licensed to PayPal and its partners on a non-exclusive, irrevocable, royalty-free, transferable and worldwide basis, to improve, operate and promote current services and develop new ones. You are not compensated, and you agree to waive your moral rights and not assert them against PayPal.
exposures.whyItMatters: Irrevocable means the licence outlives your account. A moral-rights waiver additionally gives up attribution and objection to derogatory treatment — rights that in India are statutory and normally personal to the author.

reference.label: License grant from you to PayPal; intellectual property warranties
reference.quote: you agree to waive your moral rights and promise not to assert such rights against PayPal

exposures.title: A credit report is pulled on business accounts, and again whenever PayPal perceives risk
exposures.whatItMeans: Opening or converting to a business account is consent to PayPal obtaining your personal and/or business credit report from a credit reporting agency — at that moment, and on any later occasion PayPal reasonably believes risk has increased.
exposures.whyItMatters: The second half is open-ended: consent given once at signup covers an unlimited number of future pulls, triggered by an internal risk judgment you are never shown.

reference.label: Business accounts
reference.quote: at account opening or conversion and whenever we reasonably believe there may be an increased level of risk associated with your business PayPal account

exposures.title: You release PayPal from claims you do not yet know you have
exposures.whatItMeans: In any dispute with another account holder you release PayPal from all claims and damages of every kind, known and unknown, and expressly waive the protections that would otherwise confine such a release to claims you knew or suspected existed.
exposures.whyItMatters: The waiver of unknown claims is the operative half. It disposes of causes of action that have not surfaced yet — including ones arising from facts PayPal knows and you do not.

reference.label: Release of PayPal
reference.quote: you expressly waive any protections that would otherwise limit the coverage of this release to include only those claims which you may know or suspect to exist in your favor

exposures.title: Sellers pay a dispute fee even when the buyer never contacts PayPal
exposures.whatItMeans: The Dispute fee applies when a buyer claims with PayPal, charges back with their card issuer, or reverses with their bank. It is set from your claims-to-sales ratio over the preceding three months; at 1.5% or more with over 100 transactions it becomes the High Volume rate. Engaging in any Restricted Activity lets PayPal charge the High Volume rate on all current and future disputes regardless of your actual ratio.
exposures.whyItMatters: A chargeback filed at a bank is outside the seller's control and often outside their knowledge, yet it counts toward the ratio that prices every later dispute. The Restricted Activity override converts the fee from cost recovery into a penalty of indefinite duration.

reference.label: Dispute Fee
reference.quote: Paypal may charge the High Volume Dispute fees for all current and future disputes irrespective of your dispute ratio or sales volumes

exposures.title: Sellers may not steer customers away from PayPal, or show another method first
exposures.whatItMeans: No surcharging PayPal. PayPal marks must get placement, position and payment-flow treatment at least equal to any other method, and no other payment mark may appear upstream of PayPal's in the checkout. You may not discourage a customer from using PayPal or express a preference for alternatives.
exposures.whyItMatters: These are restrictions on how a merchant designs their own checkout and talks to their own customers, and they block passing PayPal's higher cost on to the transaction that incurs it.

reference.label: Presentation of PayPal
reference.quote: you must not present any payment method or mark upstream (or at an earlier point in the checkout experience) from the presentment of any of PayPal's services

availableActions.action: Report an unauthorised transaction within 60 days of the statement
availableActions.howTo: Tell PayPal at once through customer service. Reporting within 60 days after the statement showing transfers you did not make earns 100% protection for the unauthorised amount; a good reason such as a hospital stay may extend the window. Note that letting someone use your login is expressly excluded.

deadline.description: 60 days after PayPal provides the account statement showing the transfers you did not make.

availableActions.action: Business accounts: check fees against the statement within 60 days
availableActions.howTo: You have 60 days from when statement or account activity information becomes available to notify PayPal in writing of pricing or fee errors. After that you are treated as having accepted the figures and PayPal has no obligation to correct them.

deadline.description: 60 days from the account statement or activity information being made available to you.

reference.label: Your responsibility to notify PayPal of pricing or fee errors

availableActions.action: Appeal a Buyer Protection decision, but only on new information or process error
availableActions.howTo: The original determination is final unless you have information that was not available at the time, or you can point to an error in how the decision was made. Gather the new evidence before filing rather than restating the original claim.

availableActions.action: Choose your card issuer for currency conversion instead of PayPal
availableActions.howTo: PayPal's rate includes its own currency conversion fee. Where your card and network allow it, you can have the issuer convert instead — the choice is offered per card, in account settings or at the transaction. Note it may be unavailable when a backup payment method is in play.

availableActions.action: Elect arbitration for claims under ₹700,000 — it is your option, not an obligation
availableActions.howTo: For non-injunctive claims below ₹700,000 you may choose binding arbitration through a mutually agreed ADR provider, conducted by telephone, online or on written submissions, with the manner chosen by you and no personal appearance. There is no mandatory arbitration clause and no class-action waiver in this agreement, so the courts remain open.

availableActions.action: Remove the card if you do not want PayPal refreshing its details
availableActions.howTo: The agreement names removal of the payment method as the only way to stop automatic updates from third-party sources. Removing it also clears the preference settings attached to that card.

reference.label: Link or Unlink a Payment Method

availableActions.action: Opt out of marketing email and of autodialed or pre-recorded calls
availableActions.howTo: Marketing email opts out at signup, in account preferences on paypal.in, or via the unsubscribe link — allow up to 10 business days. Autodialed and pre-recorded marketing calls require your prior express written consent in the first place, and can be declined in account settings or through customer support. Factual account messages continue either way.

availableActions.action: Sellers: keep the balance swept to your bank and hold a buffer against reversals
availableActions.howTo: You are liable for the full amount plus fees whenever a payment is later invalidated, and a shortfall becomes a negative balance PayPal may collect from other accounts or later receipts. Withdrawing promptly limits what a hold can freeze; a reserve outside PayPal limits what a reversal can overdraw.

reference.label: Payments that are invalidated and reversed

availableActions.action: Log in at least once every two years
availableActions.howTo: PayPal may close an account that has not been logged into for two or more years. A single sign-in resets it.

availableActions.action: Escalate content and personal-information complaints to the Grievance Officer
availableActions.howTo: The agreement points complaints about your personal information or content to PayPal's Grievance Officer under the Information Technology Act 2000. The document describes the role but does not name the officer or give contact details, so ask customer service for them in writing.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: India's IT Rules require a grievance officer identified by name with contact details. This document refers to the role and its statutory basis but names no officer and gives no address, email or phone.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: At least 14 days, and only where the change reduces your rights or increases your responsibilities; other revisions take effect on posting. The shortest such period among the Indian financial documents in this corpus.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Indian law, with the courts of Mumbai named for disputes. Arbitration is offered as the user's election below ₹700,000 rather than imposed, and no class-action waiver appears.

requiredDisclosures.name: Error resolution procedure and timeframes
requiredDisclosures.note: Notification within 60 days of the first statement showing the error; determination within 10 business days, extendable to 45, or 90 for new accounts, point-of-sale and foreign-initiated transfers, with provisional credit while investigating and a written explanation if no error is found.

requiredDisclosures.name: Liability limit for unauthorised transactions
requiredDisclosures.note: 100% cover for unauthorised transactions reported within 60 days of the statement, subject to cooperating with the investigation. Transactions by someone you gave your login to are expressly outside it.

requiredDisclosures.name: Identity verification and KYC documents
requiredDisclosures.note: Acceptable documents are enumerated, and the agreement discloses that information and its terms may be shared with the Authorised Dealer Bank and the Reserve Bank of India for the bank's KYC obligations.

requiredDisclosures.name: Fee schedule
requiredDisclosures.note: Disclosed by reference rather than by amount — Merchant Services Fees, Micropayment Fees, Dispute fee and currency conversion fee tables all live on separate pages incorporated into the agreement, so no rate in force can be read from this document alone.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: A user agreement rather than a privacy notice; data retention is deferred to PayPal's separate Privacy Statement, which is analysed under its own hash.

analyses.summary: This is a NYDFS conflict-of-interest disclosure, and it is unusually candid: two tables listing every asset Coinbase supports in New York against whether Coinbase holds it and whether Coinbase has a commercial relationship with it or its issuer. The numbers are stark — Coinbase holds all 209 assets New York customers can trade on its own balance sheet, and 163 of those 209 also carry a commercial engagement, which the document defines broadly enough to include Coinbase Ventures investments in the issuer. What the document does not contain is any policy for managing those conflicts, anything about how custodied assets are held or treated in insolvency, or any statement of insurance status; the holdings shown are as of 31 March 2026 against a quarterly update commitment, and the page is expressly for United States customers only despite being served from the /en-in/ path.

exposures.title: Coinbase holds a position in every one of the 209 assets you can trade
exposures.whatItMeans: Of the 209 assets listed as available for trading in the US including New York, the table records 'Yes' under Coinbase Holding for all 209 — Coinbase carries each of them on its own balance sheet.
exposures.whyItMatters: The venue setting the listing, the spread and the availability of an asset is also long that asset. There is no asset on the New York menu where Coinbase's own position is neutral, so a customer cannot pick a trade that avoids the conflict.

reference.label: Introduction
reference.quote: Coinbase holds on our balance sheet many of the assets that we support for trading

exposures.title: 163 of the 209 tradable assets also carry a commercial engagement with the issuer
exposures.whatItMeans: Roughly four in five tradable assets are marked 'Yes' for Commercial Engagement, a term the document defines broadly enough to cover Coinbase Ventures investments in the issuer, custody arrangements, and other business relationships with the asset or an affiliated party.
exposures.whyItMatters: Listing a token is a decision worth a great deal to its issuer, and in 163 of 209 cases the exchange making that decision has a financial or business relationship with the party who benefits. The document says the relationship may have started either before or after the listing, which is the disclosure that matters and the one most venues omit.

reference.label: Introduction
reference.quote: construed broadly to capture business activities such as financial engagements (e.g., Coinbase Ventures agreements)

exposures.title: The same pattern runs through Prime custody, at 384 assets
exposures.whatItMeans: The Coinbase Custody Trust Company table lists 384 assets: 327 are held by Coinbase, 277 carry a commercial engagement, and 241 carry both. Only 21 assets in the custody list carry neither.
exposures.whyItMatters: Custody is the service where a customer most expects the provider to be a neutral bailee rather than a counterparty. On this list the custodian holds its own position in 85 percent of what it safeguards.

exposures.title: The conflicts are disclosed and nothing says how they are managed
exposures.whatItMeans: The document identifies conflicts asset by asset and stops there. It contains no information barrier, no restriction on Coinbase trading against customer flow, no listing-committee independence statement, and no policy on how a Ventures position is walled off from a listing decision.
exposures.whyItMatters: Disclosure without mitigation transfers the whole problem to the customer, who has no way to act on it beyond not trading. Reading this page tells you the conflict exists on almost every asset and gives you no basis for deciding whether it is controlled.

exposures.title: The figures are two quarters old against a quarterly update commitment
exposures.whatItMeans: The document promises quarterly updates and states holdings as of 31 March 2026. This page was captured on 4 September 2026, by which point the 30 June figures had not been published here.
exposures.whyItMatters: A conflict disclosure is only as good as its date. Assets added and positions taken since March are not reflected, so a reader in September is checking a token against a picture of the balance sheet that is five months old.

reference.label: Introduction
reference.quote: Coinbase will update these disclosures on a quarterly basis

exposures.title: The Indian URL serves a document that says it is for United States customers only
exposures.whatItMeans: This page sits at coinbase.com/en-in/legal/digital-asset-disclosures but covers only assets supported in New York, is stated to be hosted in and directed to the United States, and closes with the New York State Department of Financial Services licence.
exposures.whyItMatters: An Indian customer who follows Coinbase's own India-localised legal menu to 'Digital Asset Disclosures' reaches a document that disclaims applicability to them and discloses nothing about the assets, holdings or conflicts on the service they actually use. The equivalent disclosure for that user does not exist at this address.

reference.label: Site footer
reference.quote: This Site is hosted in the United States and is intended for and directed to customers in the United States only.

availableActions.action: Look up any token you intend to buy in the trading table before you buy it
availableActions.howTo: The two columns tell you whether Coinbase holds the asset and whether it has a commercial engagement with the issuer. For New York trading assets the holding answer is always yes, so the column that varies is Commercial Engagement — 46 of the 209 are marked No.

availableActions.action: Read the underlying positions rather than the yes/no flags
availableActions.howTo: The document points to investor.coinbase.com for the Crypto Assets Held footnotes in the financial statements, and to coinbase.com/ventures/portfolio for the Ventures holdings. Those give sizes; this page only gives a flag.

availableActions.action: Check the as-of date before relying on it
availableActions.howTo: The holdings date is stated in the third paragraph. If it is more than a quarter old, the page is behind its own commitment and newly listed assets may not appear at all.

reference.label: Introduction
reference.quote: Coinbase Holdings are provided as of March 31, 2026.

availableActions.action: Outside the United States, do not treat this page as your disclosure
availableActions.howTo: It covers New York only and says so. Custody terms, insurance status and asset risk for a non-US account are governed by the Coinbase User Agreement and the local entity's terms, not by this document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named regulators and legal bases for disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: The New York State Department of Financial Services is named and the Virtual Currency Business Activity licence is stated in the footer, which identifies the regime this disclosure is made under (NYDFS Part 200 and the associated coin-listing guidance).

requiredDisclosures.name: Scope of covered individuals
requiredDisclosures.note: Scope is stated plainly and narrowly: assets supported for trading and/or custody in New York, for customers in the United States only. The disclosure is honest about its scope; the problem is that Coinbase serves it from an India-localised path where the scope excludes the reader.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: A quarterly update cadence is committed to in writing, and the as-of date is stated on the face of the document. Recorded as present on the commitment; the captured figures were 31 March 2026 against a 4 September 2026 capture, so the commitment and the artefact do not agree.

requiredDisclosures.name: Conflict of interest management policy
requiredDisclosures.note: New name — narrower than anything in the existing vocabulary, and specific to venues that both list and hold. The document identifies conflicts on 163 of 209 tradable assets and states no mitigation: no information barrier between Coinbase Ventures and listing decisions, no restriction on proprietary trading against customer flow, no independent listing review.

requiredDisclosures.name: Custody and segregation of customer assets
requiredDisclosures.note: New name. Coinbase Custody Trust Company heads a 384-asset table and the document says nothing about how those assets are held — omnibus or segregated, on-chain or with a sub-custodian, and whether customer assets are separated from the corporate holdings the same table records. NYDFS Part 200.9 requires a custodian to hold virtual currency for the benefit of the customer; this page does not state it.

requiredDisclosures.name: Treatment of customer assets in insolvency
requiredDisclosures.note: New name, kept distinct from custody because it is the separate question a customer needs answered. Nothing in this document says whether custodied digital assets would be property of the customer or of the bankruptcy estate if Coinbase failed, which is the risk that the balance-sheet holdings disclosed here make concrete.

requiredDisclosures.name: FDIC insurance status of investment products
requiredDisclosures.note: Existing canonical name, applied to digital assets. The document makes no insurance statement of any kind — no FDIC, no SIPC, no private crime-insurance disclosure and no disclaimer that digital assets are uninsured. On a page whose subject is what Coinbase holds and how, the omission of the sentence saying these holdings are not insured is the notable one.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: Captured from the /en-in/ path served to Indian users. The IT Rules 2021 require a named grievance officer with contact details on Indian-facing pages. This document names no officer and offers no contact route at all — not even a support link.

analyses.summary: Netflix's Indian terms are among the more restrained subscription contracts in the corpus, and the reason is notice: material changes and price changes both carry a one-month advance commitment, there is no arbitration clause, and cancellation is self-service and effective at the end of the billing period. What you give up sits in narrower places. A class action waiver applies wherever the law permits it. Payments are non-refundable for partial periods and unused content. Any payment method on the account may be charged if the primary one fails. Anything you send Netflix as feedback is licensed to it worldwide and in perpetuity for free, with moral rights waived. And the plans described as being without commercial interruptions carry an explicit carve-out for live events, replays and linear programming — the second document in the corpus to keep advertising on a service sold as ad-free.

exposures.title: Ads remain on the plans sold as uninterrupted
exposures.whatItMeans: Subscription plans are described as designed for an experience without commercial interruptions, and then advertising is expressly permitted during live or special events including replays, as part of linear programming, or where streaming rights or other obligations require it.
exposures.whyItMatters: The absence of advertising is the thing the higher-priced plans are sold on, and the carve-out is broad enough to cover exactly the programming — live sport and events — where ad load is heaviest. JioHotstar's terms do the same thing, which makes this a pattern rather than one company's drafting.

reference.label: 2.4 Advertisements and Commercial Content
reference.quote: While our subscription plans are designed to provide an experience without commercial interruptions, there may be some occasions when you may see advertisements — for example, during certain live or special events (including replays), as part of linear programming

exposures.title: Any card on the account can be charged when one fails
exposures.whatItMeans: You authorise Netflix to charge any payment method associated with the account if the primary method is declined or unavailable, and Netflix may also update stored payment details itself using information from payment providers.
exposures.whyItMatters: A card you added once for a single purpose remains a live billing instrument indefinitely, and card-updater services mean cancelling or replacing the card does not necessarily stop the charge. You stay responsible for uncollected amounts either way.

reference.label: 2.2 Payment Methods
reference.quote: You authorize us to charge any Payment Method associated with your account in case your primary Payment Method is declined or no longer available to us for payment of your subscription fee.

exposures.title: Nothing is refundable, including time you paid for and did not use
exposures.whatItMeans: Cancellation takes effect at the end of the billing period, and to the extent the law permits, payments are non-refundable with no credits for partial subscription periods or unused content.
exposures.whyItMatters: Cancelling on day two of a monthly cycle costs the same as cancelling on day thirty. The qualifier 'to the extent permitted by the applicable law' preserves Indian consumer remedies, but the default the contract sets is no refund.

reference.label: 2.6 Cancellation
reference.quote: payments are non-refundable and we do not provide refunds or credits for any partial subscription periods or unused Netflix content

exposures.title: Class actions are waived wherever the law allows it
exposures.whatItMeans: You and Netflix agree to bring claims only in an individual capacity, and courts may not consolidate claims or preside over representative or class proceedings, in each case where applicable law permits.
exposures.whyItMatters: Streaming disputes are small in value and identical across millions of subscribers — a wrongly applied price rise costs each person a few hundred rupees. Individual claims are the one format in which such a case is not worth bringing.

reference.label: 6. Class Action Waiver
reference.quote: YOU AND NETFLIX AGREE THAT EACH MAY BRING CLAIMS AGAINST THE OTHER ONLY IN YOUR OR ITS INDIVIDUAL CAPACITY, AND NOT AS A PLAINTIFF OR CLASS MEMBER IN ANY PURPORTED CLASS OR REPRESENTATIVE PROCEEDING

exposures.title: Feedback you send is Netflix's to use forever, for free
exposures.whatItMeans: Any comments, ideas, concepts, reviews or techniques you send — including questionnaire responses and postings on the service — may be used by Netflix worldwide and in perpetuity for any purpose, with no compensation or acknowledgement, and you agree not to enforce moral rights.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the fifth appearance of the ideas-become-ours clause in the corpus, after HDFC Bank, American Express India, Zomato and Paytm. Netflix's is at the milder end — a perpetual licence to use feedback, not an assignment of ownership, and section 7.2 states Netflix does not accept unsolicited content ideas at all — but the moral-rights waiver still applies to anything you do send.

reference.label: 7.3 Feedback
reference.quote: Netflix is free to use any comments, information, ideas, concepts, reviews, or techniques or any other material contained in any communication you may send to us ("Feedback") ... worldwide and in perpetuity without further compensation, acknowledgement or payment to you for any purpose whatsoever

exposures.title: Anyone you let onto the account is acting as you
exposures.whatItMeans: By allowing others to access the account you agree they act on your behalf and that you are bound by changes they make, expressly including changes to subscription plans. Account access also carries access to the viewing history.
exposures.whyItMatters: A household member upgrading the plan binds the Account Owner to the higher price, and the viewing record of everyone on the account is visible to anyone with access. Netflix simultaneously restricts sharing outside the household, so the risk sits with the sharing it does permit.

reference.label: 4. Account Access
reference.quote: you agree that such individuals are acting on your behalf and that you are bound by any changes that they may make to the account, including changes to subscription plans

exposures.title: Support can ask for full access to your computer
exposures.whatItMeans: Customer Service may assist through a remote access support tool that the terms describe as giving Netflix full access to your computer. Consent is required and the terms state alternative assistance is available if you decline.
exposures.whyItMatters: Full remote access reaches everything on the machine, not the Netflix account, and the request arrives mid-problem when a user wants the issue fixed. The terms are unusually direct about what it grants, which is what makes declining possible.

reference.label: 7.4 Customer Support
reference.quote: Customer Service may best be able to assist you by using a remote access support tool through which we have full access to your computer

exposures.title: Offer eligibility is Netflix's decision alone, and it can claw the offer back
exposures.whatItMeans: Eligibility for promotional offers is determined at Netflix's sole discretion using device ID, payment method or contact information, and Netflix reserves the right to revoke an offer and place the account on hold if it decides you were not eligible.
exposures.whyItMatters: Device ID and payment method are used to link you to a past or existing household account, so an offer accepted in good faith can be withdrawn and access suspended on Netflix's own determination, with no stated review.

reference.label: 1.3 Offers
reference.quote: Offer eligibility is determined by Netflix at its sole discretion and we reserve the right to revoke an Offer and put your account on hold in the event that we determine you are not eligible.

exposures.title: The agreement can be transferred to someone else
exposures.whatItMeans: Netflix may assign or transfer the agreement, including its rights and obligations, at any time, and you agree to cooperate with the transfer.
exposures.whyItMatters: The counterparty you contracted with can change without your consent, which matters most for the data held under the agreement and for who the one-month notice commitments then bind.

reference.label: 7.6 Changes to these Terms and Assignment

availableActions.action: Turn off test participation
availableActions.howTo: Go to the Account page and change the 'Test participation' setting. The terms state you can do this at any time, and it removes you from the interface and feature experiments Netflix runs continuously.

availableActions.action: Cancel before the renewal date, not after
availableActions.howTo: Cancel on the Account page; it takes effect at the end of the current billing period, and the end date is shown there. Because partial periods are not refunded, cancelling immediately after a renewal costs a full cycle.

deadline.description: Before each billing date. The subscription renews automatically until cancelled, and no refund is given for the unused remainder of a cycle already charged.

availableActions.action: Act on the one-month price-change notice
availableActions.howTo: Netflix commits to notifying you at least one month before any price change or plan change takes effect. That window is enough to cancel before the new price is charged.

deadline.description: At least one month's notice is given before a price or plan change applies, and the same one-month commitment covers material changes to the terms.

reference.label: 2.7 Changes to the Price and Subscription Plans

availableActions.action: Refuse the remote access tool
availableActions.howTo: Tell Customer Service you do not consent to remote access support. The terms state Netflix will assist you through other means.

availableActions.action: Cancel through the third party if you subscribed through one
availableActions.howTo: Where Netflix was bought through an app store or telecom bundle, cancelling on the Netflix Account page may not be enough — turn off auto-renew or unsubscribe in that third party's account instead.

availableActions.action: Keep the account limited to people you would let change the plan
availableActions.howTo: Anyone with account access is treated as acting on your behalf and can bind you to plan changes, and can see the account's viewing activity. Use separate profiles and keep the Account Owner's credentials off shared devices.

availableActions.action: Send Netflix nothing you would want to own
availableActions.howTo: Section 7.2 states Netflix does not accept unsolicited materials or ideas for content, and section 7.3 licenses anything you do send in perpetuity without payment. Treat questionnaire responses and postings the same way.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: At least one month's advance notice for material changes, and separately at least one month before any price or subscription plan change takes effect. Among the strongest change-notice commitments in the corpus.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automatic renewal disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: States the subscription continues until terminated, that failing to cancel before the billing date authorises the next cycle's charge, and that the next payment date is shown on the Account page. A pre-authorisation of up to one month of service at signup is also disclosed.

requiredDisclosures.name: Refund and cancellation rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Disclosed and adverse: self-service cancellation effective at period end, with no refunds or credits for partial periods or unused content, subject to non-waivable consumer law.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Laws of India. The contracting party is named as Netflix Entertainment Services India LLP and identified as the consumer point of contact.

requiredDisclosures.name: Arbitration clause
requiredDisclosures.note: There is none. Disputes go to the courts under Indian law, with only a class action waiver limiting their form — the same posture as LinkedIn's user agreement.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: No grievance officer, contact address or response timeline is named, though the IT Rules 2021 require publishers of online curated content in India to appoint one. Users are directed to the Help Centre.

requiredDisclosures.name: Minimum age
requiredDisclosures.note: 18 to create an account or become an Extra Member; minors may use the service only under adult supervision.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer rights preservation
requiredDisclosures.note: The liability section states the terms will not limit non-waivable warranties or mandatory consumer protection rights, and the class action waiver and non-refundability are both qualified by what applicable law permits.

requiredDisclosures.name: Advance notice of fee changes
requiredDisclosures.note: At least one month before a price change becomes effective.

requiredDisclosures.name: Electronic record status
requiredDisclosures.note: Account notices — payment authorisations, invoices, contact and payment method changes, confirmations — are sent in electronic form only.

analyses.summary: eBay's payments terms govern five regulated entities across five jurisdictions, and the protections they give a seller depend heavily on which one you get. The general structure is consistent, though. Money eBay holds for you is not a deposit — for the US, Australian and Canadian entities it is an unsecured claim against eBay, which may pool your funds with other sellers', invest them, and keep the interest, with any beneficial interest you might have in that yield assigned away. Funds can be held for up to 30 days for being a new or dormant seller and up to 190 days after you close the account, and a rolling reserve can withhold a fixed percentage of daily proceeds. Under the US entity you irrevocably assign to eBay all rights in any accounts receivable, payments of money and general intangibles owed in your favour, to secure whatever you owe. In Europe you assign every current and future receivable against your buyers, and defective ones are assigned back with an obligation to repay immediately. Leaving is not a real option — terminating these terms means you can no longer sell on eBay at all. Against that: genuine financial regulation by the CSSF, FCA and AUSTRAC, a real trust arrangement in Canada, consumer forum rights preserved in Luxembourg, notice periods of up to two months, and an arbitration opt-out that comes with eBay paying the fees on claims of $10,000 or less.

exposures.title: Your money is an unsecured claim, pooled and invested, and eBay keeps the interest
exposures.whatItMeans: Funds received on your behalf do not constitute deposits. Where held by the US, Australian or Canadian entity they represent an unsecured claim for payment against eBay. eBay may combine your funds with those of other customers and invest them; you have no ownership interest in those investments, eBay retains any interest earned, and you assign to eBay any beneficial interest you might have in it.
exposures.whyItMatters: Unsecured means that if the entity fails you rank behind secured creditors for money that was the proceeds of your own sales. The yield on your balance is eBay's by assignment, and the assignment is stated rather than offered. Canada is the exception — there a statutory trust under the Retail Payment Activities Act applies, though eBay keeps the interest there too and funds in transit are outside the trust and uninsured.

reference.label: Part I, Section 5 — Settlement of Funds and Payouts; Part IV, Section 3 — RPAA Trust Arrangement

exposures.title: You assign eBay every receivable owed to you, not just eBay's
exposures.whatItMeans: Under the terms for the US entity, to the extent permitted by law you irrevocably sell, assign, grant, convey and transfer to eBay and its affiliates all of your rights, title and interests in any and all accounts receivable, payments of money, and general intangibles owed in your favour, to satisfy any obligations you owe eBay in connection with Managed Payments.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is not limited to money arising from eBay sales. As drafted it is a blanket security assignment over the seller's receivables generally, given in advance and irrevocably, in a document a person accepts to start selling used goods.

reference.label: Part II, Section 3 — Authorization for Collection of Owed Amounts
reference.quote: you hereby irrevocably sell, assign, grant, convey and transfer to eBay and its Affiliates, as applicable, all of your rights, title, and interests in any and all accounts receivable, payments of money, and general intangibles owed in your favor

exposures.title: In Europe your claim against the buyer is sold on before you are paid
exposures.whatItMeans: Where a buyer uses a Specific Payment Method such as direct debit, invoice or instalments, you assign all current and future claims against your buyers — with ancillary rights including security interests, insurance claims and rescission rights — to eBay, which assigns them to an acquirer such as Adyen and on to a payment partner. You irrevocably authorise eBay, with power of sub-delegation, to notify the buyer and exercise those rights in its own name, including rights that cannot normally be transferred.
exposures.whyItMatters: The chain assignment does transfer the buyer's non-payment risk away from you, which is a real benefit. But defective receivables come back: a return, an eMBG claim you cannot evidence, or a refund makes it a Defect Receivable, reassigned to you with an obligation to repay the purchase price without undue delay, set off against anything eBay owes you next.

reference.label: Part I, Section 7 — Purchase and Assignment of Seller Receivables

exposures.title: Holds and reserves can withhold your proceeds for a month, or a percentage indefinitely
exposures.whatItMeans: Holds of up to 30 days apply to new, dormant and infrequent sellers, to previously restricted or suspended sellers, to unusual selling patterns including an unexpected surge in sales or a change in average selling price, and during authenticity verification — longer where delivery times are extended. Separately, a rolling reserve may withhold a set percentage of daily proceeds, sized on factors including your personal and business credit history.
exposures.whyItMatters: The triggers include succeeding — a surge in sales is listed alongside suspicion of fraud — and the seller has already shipped the goods. Reserves are also set partly on credit history, so a seller's borrowing record shapes how much of their own sales revenue they can access.

reference.label: Part I, Section 5 — Holds and Reserves

exposures.title: Money can be kept for 190 days after you close the account
exposures.whatItMeans: Where the payout entity is the US, Australian or Canadian company, eBay may keep a portion of your funds after account closure to cover refunds or disputes, returning unused amounts to your linked account within 190 days of closure unless the law requires otherwise.
exposures.whyItMatters: Just over six months is a long time to hold a former user's money, and 190 days is the outer commitment rather than a target. Closing the account is also the only way most sellers can terminate, since termination by any other route is not offered outside Luxembourg and the UK.

exposures.title: Leaving the payments terms means leaving eBay entirely
exposures.whatItMeans: Selling on eBay requires continued registration for Managed Payments. Terminating these terms means you cannot continue selling or using the other eBay services, affiliates may terminate your User Agreement accordingly, and terminating with one eBay payment entity terminates with all of them.
exposures.whyItMatters: It removes the possibility of rejecting these terms while remaining a seller, which is what makes the assignment, hold and reserve provisions unavoidable rather than negotiable. The right to terminate free of charge when terms change is real, but the price of exercising it is the business.

reference.label: Part I, Section 10 — Effect of Termination

exposures.title: Owed Amounts can be taken from any payment method eBay or its affiliates hold
exposures.whatItMeans: You authorise eBay to collect amounts owed by deducting from pending settlements, charging your linked financial account by direct debit mandate, charging any other payment method stored with eBay or its affiliates, deducting from a stored value account, or using a collections agency. Outside the EU and UK you waive, so far as the law allows, any right to advance notice of a particular pre-authorised charge.
exposures.whyItMatters: The waiver of advance notice is the sharp part: a card you saved for buying something can be charged for a dispute you lost, without warning. EU and UK sellers keep three days' notice on SEPA and BECS mandates; everyone else does not.

reference.label: Part I, Section 8 — Collection of Fees and Other Amounts You Owe

exposures.title: Arbitration in Utah for the US entity, and for most of the world
exposures.whatItMeans: Claims against the US entity go to binding AAA arbitration under Utah law, with class, representative and private attorney general actions barred and relief limited to the individual — the terms state any relief awarded cannot affect other users. The US entity is also the payout entity for every country not assigned to one of the other four, so this reaches sellers far outside the United States.
exposures.whyItMatters: A seller in Brazil or Nigeria contracts into Utah law and Salt Lake County courts. The opt-out is real but must be posted, personally signed, within 30 days of first accepting the terms — and it is offered to new users of the payment services only.

exposures.title: Statutory payment protections are switched off for business sellers
exposures.whatItMeans: Business sellers using the Luxembourg entity agree that named articles of the 2009 Luxembourg payment services law and its Title III do not apply, including the provisions on non-execution and defective execution. Sellers using the UK entity who are not micro-enterprises, charities or consumers agree that Part 6 and a list of regulations of the Payment Services Regulations 2017 do not apply, and must report unauthorised transactions within 60 days.
exposures.whyItMatters: These are the rules that make a payment provider answerable for money that goes missing, and they are disapplied by agreement for anyone above a small-business threshold. The corpus has seen protections vary by geography; here they vary by the size of the customer.

reference.label: Part III, Sections 4 and 10; Part VI, Section 1

exposures.title: A failed debit costs a fee, and eBay disclaims all consequences
exposures.whatItMeans: Canadian sellers are charged CDN$7.00 and Australian sellers AUD 8.00 by separate debit for every debit transaction that is unsuccessful or returned unpaid, and in both cases the terms state eBay has no liability whatsoever caused by a dishonoured debit. Canadian sellers also waive all pre-notification requirements under the Payments Canada rules for variable debits.
exposures.whyItMatters: The fee applies per attempt, and eBay chooses the collection method and timing. Waiving pre-notification means the debit can arrive without warning, which is also what makes it more likely to fail.

reference.label: Part IV, Section 2 and Part V, Section 2

availableActions.action: Opt out of arbitration within 30 days, by post
availableActions.howTo: Mail a completed and signed Opt-Out Notice, postmarked no later than 30 days after you first accept these terms, to eBay Inc., Attn: Litigation Department, Re: Opt-Out Notice, 339 W. 13490 S., Ste. 500, Draper, UT 84020. It must include your name, full address, and the user IDs and email addresses it applies to. The terms state this is the only way to opt out.

deadline.description: Postmarked within 30 days of first accepting the Payments Terms of Use. Offered to new users of the payment services.

availableActions.action: Ask eBay to pay the arbitration fees
availableActions.howTo: If you followed the Notice of Dispute procedure and the relief sought is $10,000 or less, eBay will on request pay all administration and arbitrator fees. Submit the request by mail to the AAA with your Demand for Arbitration. Claims under $25,000 are decided on documents alone unless the arbitrator orders a hearing.

reference.label: Part II, Section 4.2 — Costs of Arbitration

availableActions.action: Send the Notice of Dispute correctly and wait out the 30 days
availableActions.howTo: Download the Notice of Dispute form, complete every field, sign it personally, and send it by certified mail to eBay Inc., Attn: Litigation Department, 339 W. 13490 S., Ste. 500, Draper, UT 84020. Arbitration may be initiated 30 days after eBay receives it. Doing this properly is also the precondition for the fee waiver.

deadline.description: Arbitration may be initiated 30 days after eBay receives a valid Notice of Dispute.

availableActions.action: Terminate free of charge when terms change
availableActions.howTo: Advance notice is 2 months if your payout entity is eBay Sarl, 2 months for eCUK consumers, micro-enterprises and charities, 30 days for the Australian entity and 14 days for everyone else. You may terminate at no cost before the effective date. German consumers must give explicit consent to material changes, and consumers with eBay Sarl or eCUK can reject changes rather than being deemed to accept them.

deadline.description: Between 14 days and 2 months of notice depending on payout entity, with a free termination right before the effective date.

availableActions.action: Escalate to the financial regulator
availableActions.howTo: These are supervised entities, which most documents in this corpus are not. eBay Sarl is licensed in Luxembourg under CSSF licence 33/19 and complaints can be escalated to the CSSF at cssf.lu; eBay Commerce UK is FCA-authorised as an electronic money institution, firm reference 1028611; eBay Commerce Australia is registered with AUSTRAC.

reference.label: Introduction — eBay Payment Entity contact information; Part III, Section 10 — Complaints

availableActions.action: As an EU or UK consumer, sue where you live
availableActions.howTo: Consumers dealing with eBay Sarl may bring proceedings in the courts of their own residence or in Luxembourg, and eBay Sarl may only enforce against a consumer in the consumer's own jurisdiction. Mandatory consumer protections in your country apply over the Luxembourg choice of law where they are more favourable.

reference.label: Part III, Section 10 — Governing Law and Jurisdiction

availableActions.action: Report unauthorised transactions immediately, and watch the deadline
availableActions.howTo: Notify eBay as soon as you notice an unauthorised, delayed or incorrect payment; notification is free and telephone notice may need written confirmation. With eBay Sarl the outer limit for an incorrectly executed transaction is 13 months. With eCUK, business sellers who are not micro-enterprises or charities have 60 days from the debit date or eCUK is not liable.

deadline.description: 60 days from the debit date for eCUK business sellers; up to 13 months after execution for incorrectly executed transactions with eBay Sarl.

reference.label: Part I, Section 6 — Security; Part III, Section 4; Part VI, Section 1

availableActions.action: Keep a second payment method on file, deliberately
availableActions.howTo: If eBay cannot debit your linked financial account for Owed Amounts, it may withhold payouts until you supply another valid method. Choosing which method sits on file — and setting your preferred collection method in your account — is better than having eBay choose among everything stored with it and its affiliates.

requiredDisclosures.name: Company identification details
requiredDisclosures.note: The most complete in the corpus: five entities with registered addresses, plus eBay Sarl's Luxembourg RCS number B164557, VAT ID and CSSF licence 33/19; eCUK's FCA firm reference 1028611; and eCA's AUSTRAC registration, each with the regulator's verification website.

requiredDisclosures.name: Arbitration opt-out right
requiredDisclosures.note: Thirty days from first acceptance, by signed written notice posted to Draper, Utah, with the form provided. Amendments to the arbitration agreement carry 30 days' notice and do not apply to claims already filed.

requiredDisclosures.name: Pre-arbitration dispute procedure
requiredDisclosures.note: A personally signed Notice of Dispute by certified mail with a downloadable form, a 30-day resolution period, and eBay paying administration and arbitrator fees on request where the relief sought is $10,000 or less.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Set out per entity: Utah for eCI, Luxembourg for eBay Sarl, Ontario or Quebec for eCCA, New South Wales for eCA. Consumer forum rights are preserved in Luxembourg and mandatory local consumer protections prevail over the choice of law.

requiredDisclosures.name: Advance notice of fee changes
requiredDisclosures.note: Amendment notice of 2 months for eBay Sarl and for eCUK consumers, micro-enterprises and charities, 30 days for eCA and 14 days for others, with a free termination right before the effective date.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer rights preservation
requiredDisclosures.note: German consumers must explicitly consent to material changes; EU, UK and Australian consumers and Australian small businesses keep court rights over disputes; Luxembourg consumers keep their home forum. These are the strongest consumer carve-outs in the corpus.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer complaint route
requiredDisclosures.note: Complaints to eBay Sarl may be escalated to the CSSF as the competent out-of-court authority for Luxembourg payment institutions, with a published Complaints Procedure.

requiredDisclosures.name: Error resolution procedure and timeframes
requiredDisclosures.note: Free notification of unauthorised, delayed or incorrect payments; a 13-month outer limit for incorrectly executed transactions with eBay Sarl; a 60-day limit for eCUK business sellers; monthly transaction statements at no cost via Seller Hub.

requiredDisclosures.name: Identity verification and KYC documents
requiredDisclosures.note: Enumerated for individuals and businesses, including beneficial owners, directors and officers, with the anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing purpose stated and a typical two-business-day assessment period.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Adyen N.V. is named as an acquirer, and the specific regulatory recipients are identified by instrument — DSA, DAC7, CESOP, the US INFORM Consumers Act, and Article 19 of the German Trademark Act for IP rights holders.

requiredDisclosures.name: Limitation on indemnity
requiredDisclosures.note: The seller indemnity covers reversals, chargebacks, claims, costs, losses, damages, fees, fines and penalties arising from any transaction processed for an item you listed, including the accuracy of your item description, with no cap.

requiredDisclosures.name: FDIC insurance status of investment products
requiredDisclosures.note: Stated in the negative and clearly: funds are not deposits, represent an unsecured claim against eBay for the US, Australian and Canadian entities, and in Canada are held in trust but are not CDIC-insured at beneficiary level, with in-transit funds outside the trust entirely.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: Partially, and unusually concrete: up to 190 days retention of funds after account closure, and inactivity defined as six consecutive years without access plus three without transactions before an account may be closed.

analyses.summary: X's terms grant a worldwide, sublicensable, royalty-free licence over everything you post and say in terms what most platforms leave to a privacy policy: the licence includes training X's machine learning and AI models, generative or otherwise, with no opt-out anywhere in the document. The licence section survives termination, so ending your account does not end it. There is no arbitration and no user indemnity, but there is a class-action waiver enforced in two named Texas counties, a $100 liability cap, and liquidated damages of $15,000 per million posts you view in a day — a penalty for reading that is 150 times what X can ever owe you. This one page carries two different contracts: the US/rest-of-world edition withholds three protections the EU/UK edition grants.

exposures.title: The content licence expressly covers training AI models, and no opt-out exists
exposures.whatItMeans: The licence you grant on posting is worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free, sublicensable, for any purpose, in any media now known or later developed — and it states in terms that this includes use with and training of X's machine learning and artificial intelligence models, whether generative or another type. Both editions say it. Neither offers a setting, a form, or any other way to withhold it.
exposures.whyItMatters: Most platforms in this corpus either stay silent on training or bury it in the privacy policy. X puts it inside the IP grant, which means refusing it is refusing to post at all. The only control the document describes is not posting.

reference.label: 3. Content on the Services — Your Rights and Grant of Rights in the Content
reference.quote: for use with and training of our machine learning and artificial intelligence models, whether generative or another type

exposures.title: The licence outlives your account without ever being called perpetual
exposures.whatItMeans: The words perpetual and irrevocable appear nowhere. The survival clause does the same work: on termination or deactivation everything ends except sections 2, 3, 5 and 6 — and section 3 is the content licence.
exposures.whyItMatters: Deleting your account ends your right to use X and does not end X's right to use, sublicense and train on what you posted. The result matches TikTok's expressly perpetual licence while reading as a milder document.

reference.label: 4. Using the Services — Ending These Terms
reference.quote: the following sections shall continue to apply: 2, 3, 5, 6

exposures.title: $15,000 in liquidated damages for reading too much
exposures.whatItMeans: Requesting, viewing or accessing more than 1,000,000 posts in any 24-hour period makes you jointly and severally liable for $15,000 per million posts (EUR 15,000 in the EU/UK edition). The clause states these are a reasonable estimate of X's damages and not a penalty, and does not limit X's other remedies.
exposures.whyItMatters: The trigger is viewing, not scraping or reselling, and joint and several liability reaches anyone who induced or knowingly facilitated it. Set against a $100 cap on X's own liability, the two clauses put a 150-to-1 ratio between what you can owe X and what X can ever owe you.

reference.label: 5. Disclaimers and Limitations of Liability — Liquidated Damages
reference.quote: you will be jointly and severally liable to us for liquidated damages as follows for requesting, viewing, or accessing more than 1,000,000 posts

exposures.title: X's total liability is capped at $100
exposures.whatItMeans: Aggregate liability cannot exceed the greater of $100 or what you paid in the past six months for the service giving rise to the claim, across every theory including negligence, and expressly even where the remedy fails of its essential purpose. Lost data, deleted content and unauthorised access to your transmissions are all named as things X is not liable for.
exposures.whyItMatters: A free account's ceiling is $100. A Premium subscriber's is whatever six months of subscription came to. The EU/UK edition drops the number entirely and limits liability only to the maximum permissible locally, so the same company offers a hard cap in one market and a legal one in another.

reference.label: 5. Disclaimers and Limitations of Liability — Limitation of Liability
reference.quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL THE AGGREGATE LIABILITY OF THE X ENTITIES EXCEED THE GREATER OF ONE HUNDRED U.S. DOLLARS

exposures.title: Outside the EU and UK, your account can be ended for no reason
exposures.whatItMeans: The US/rest-of-world edition lists five grounds for suspension and then adds a sixth that swallows them: X may terminate or stop serving you for any other reason or no reason at its convenience. The EU/UK edition contains no such sentence — there, the five enumerated grounds are the whole list.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the same document, split by where you live. A US user's account is terminable at will; an Irish user's is not. Notice is only reasonable efforts by email or on your next login attempt, and there is no stated way to retrieve content afterwards.

reference.label: 4. Using the Services — Ending These Terms (US/rest-of-world edition)
reference.quote: we may also terminate your account or cease providing you with all or part of the Services for any other reason or no reason at our convenience

exposures.title: A promise to respect restricted-audience posts that only EU and UK users get
exposures.whatItMeans: The EU/UK licence adds one sentence the US/rest-of-world licence does not have: if you have used X's features to limit distribution of your content to a restricted community, X will respect that choice. The US edition's licence runs to the identical breadth with no such carve-out.
exposures.whyItMatters: Protected posts and restricted communities are a product feature everywhere, but a contractual commitment to honour them only in Europe. Outside the EU/UK, the licence to make your content available to the rest of the world reads over your audience setting rather than under it.

reference.label: 3. Content on the Services — Your Rights and Grant of Rights in the Content (EU/EFTA/UK edition)
reference.quote: if you have chosen via our features to limit the distribution of your Content to a restricted community, we will respect that choice

exposures.title: A class-action waiver with no arbitration to justify it, in two named Texas counties
exposures.whatItMeans: There is no arbitration clause anywhere in either edition. Disputes go to court — but exclusively to the federal or state courts of Wichita County or Tarrant County, Texas, under Texas law, and you separately waive the right to be a plaintiff or class member in any class, collective or representative action. X reserves, at its sole discretion, the right to sue you in your own country instead.
exposures.whyItMatters: The usual trade is that you give up class actions and get a cheap arbitration forum in exchange. Here you give up class actions and get a courthouse in north Texas. Every small claim is individually uneconomic and must be filed thousands of miles from most users, while X keeps the option of coming to you.

reference.label: 6. General
reference.quote: shall be brought and must proceed exclusively in the federal or state courts located in Wichita County or Tarrant County, Texas

exposures.title: Your claim expires in one year, X's does not
exposures.whatItMeans: Federal claims must be brought within one year of the events, state claims within two, and anything later is permanently barred. The EU/UK edition shortens everything to one year. The clause runs only against you; nothing shortens X's time to sue.
exposures.whyItMatters: Harms from a platform — a suppressed account, a data exposure, a content misuse — are often discovered long after they happen. A one-year bar running from the occurrence rather than the discovery can expire before you know there was anything to sue about.

reference.label: 6. General
reference.quote: you must initiate any proceeding or action asserting a federal claim within one (1) year of the date of the occurrence

exposures.title: Thirty days' notice of changes in the EU, best efforts everywhere else
exposures.whatItMeans: The EU/UK edition commits to 30 days' advance notice of changes affecting the rights or obligations of either party, other than new functions or legal changes. The US/rest-of-world edition says only that X will try to notify you of material revisions. Both make continued use acceptance, and both state the changes will not be retroactive.
exposures.whyItMatters: The same sentence, one market apart, is the difference between a month to read a new AI-training clause and finding out afterwards. The non-retroactivity commitment is real and rarer than it should be, but it protects only conduct that already happened.

reference.label: 6. General
reference.quote: we will notify you 30 days in advance of making effective changes to these Terms that impact the rights or obligations of any party

exposures.title: Everything you type into X's AI features is Content under the licence
exposures.whatItMeans: Content is defined to include any inputs, prompts, outputs and information obtained or created through the Services, and you are made responsible for all of it. The same section prohibits jailbreaking and prompt engineering or injection as misuse of the Services.
exposures.whyItMatters: Prompts you write to an assistant and what it writes back fall inside the same worldwide sublicensable licence as a public post, including the training grant. Nothing distinguishes a private prompt from a published one.

reference.label: 3. Content on the Services
reference.quote: including any inputs, prompts, outputs, and/or information obtained or created through the Services

exposures.title: Sign in with X depends on an account X can end without notice, and the terms say nothing about what happens then
exposures.whatItMeans: Sign in with X appears once, as a developer feature that pulls the developer into a separate Developer Agreement. Nothing in either edition addresses what becomes of your logins to third-party sites when X suspends, terminates or reclaims your account — and X may reclaim usernames, in the US edition expressly without liability to you.
exposures.whyItMatters: Every third-party service you signed into with X inherits an account you do not control and cannot appeal beyond a Help Center form. A reclaimed username with no stated protection for downstream authentication is an account-takeover risk against sites that never heard about the suspension.

reference.label: 4. Using the Services
reference.quote: suspend or terminate users, and reclaim usernames without liability to you

availableActions.action: Check which of the two editions binds you before relying on anything in it
availableActions.howTo: One page carries two contracts. The EU/EFTA/UK edition (effective 15 January 2026) is with X Internet Unlimited Company in Dublin under Irish law; the other (effective 10 April 2026) is with X Corp. in Bastrop, Texas. Termination grounds, the liability cap, change notice and the restricted-community promise all differ.

reference.label: X Terms of Service — edition headings

availableActions.action: Treat every post as training data, because the terms give you no way to withhold it
availableActions.howTo: The AI-training right sits inside the content licence, not in a privacy setting, so it attaches the moment you post. The only control the document describes is what you choose not to post.

reference.label: 3. Content on the Services — Your Rights and Grant of Rights in the Content

availableActions.action: Use restricted-audience features, knowing the promise to honour them is EU/UK-only
availableActions.howTo: Protected posts and restricted communities limit who can see and reuse content in practice everywhere. Only the EU/EFTA/UK edition contractually commits X to respect that limit against its own licence.

availableActions.action: Avoid bulk-reading tools and high-volume third-party clients
availableActions.howTo: The liquidated damages clause triggers on requesting, viewing or accessing over a million posts in 24 hours, and reaches anyone who induces or knowingly facilitates it. Research tooling, archivers and automated clients can cross that line without scraping anything for resale.

availableActions.action: Appeal a termination through the account-access form, and in the EU or UK escalate outside X
availableActions.howTo: Both editions point to help.x.com/forms/account-access/appeals. UK users may additionally complain through the internal process or bring a claim in a competent court under the Online Safety Act 2023; EU users may use out-of-court dispute settlement under the Digital Services Act.

availableActions.action: File any claim within a year of the event, not a year of finding out
availableActions.howTo: The clock runs from the occurrence of the facts, not from discovery. Two years for US state-law claims, one year for federal claims and for everything under the EU/UK edition; after that the claim is stated to be permanently barred.

deadline.description: One year from the occurrence of the event for federal and EU/UK claims, two years for US state-law claims, after which claims on those facts are permanently barred.

availableActions.action: Leave by deactivating, and keep your own copies first
availableActions.howTo: You may end the agreement at any time by deactivating and discontinuing use. The content licence, the privacy section, the liability limits and the misuse provisions all survive, so deactivation ends your rights and not X's.

reference.label: 4. Using the Services — Ending These Terms

availableActions.action: Re-point any third-party logins that use Sign in with X onto an email address
availableActions.howTo: Nothing in these terms preserves your access to services you authenticated through X if the account is suspended or the username reclaimed. Adding a password or an email login on those services removes the dependency before it matters.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: Both editions grant training rights over user content expressly, and neither describes any opt-out, setting or objection route. The privacy policy agrees that X trains on collected and publicly available information and likewise names no control. Recorded absent from the document text, not from a broken capture: the licence paragraph is complete in both editions.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Split by market. EU/EFTA/UK: 30 days' advance notice of changes affecting either party's rights, excluding new functions and legally required changes. US/rest-of-world: X will try to notify you of material revisions. Continued use is acceptance in both.

requiredDisclosures.name: Non-retroactivity of changes
requiredDisclosures.note: Both editions state changes will not be retroactive and that the current version at x.com/tos governs. One of only a handful of documents in this corpus to commit to this.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Stated precisely and asymmetrically. Texas law with exclusive venue in Wichita or Tarrant County for the US/rest-of-world edition; Irish law and Irish courts for the EU/UK edition. In both, X reserves sole discretion to sue you in your own country of residence instead.

requiredDisclosures.name: Arbitration clause
requiredDisclosures.note: There is none, in either edition — the word does not appear. Notable because the class-action waiver survives on its own: X takes the waiver without offering the arbitration forum that is usually its justification.

requiredDisclosures.name: Limitation on indemnity
requiredDisclosures.note: These terms impose no indemnity obligation on the user at all, in either edition. Among the social platforms in this corpus that is unusual and runs in the user's favour.

requiredDisclosures.name: Minimum age
requiredDisclosures.note: At least 13 in both editions, stated in the summary and again in section 1, with an express mechanism for an adult to bind a minor.

requiredDisclosures.name: Designated DMCA agent
requiredDisclosures.note: Named in both editions: X Corp., Attn: Copyright Agent, 865 FM 1209 Building 2, Bastrop TX 78602, with copyright@x.com and the help.x.com/forms/ipi reporting form.

requiredDisclosures.name: Repeat infringer policy
requiredDisclosures.note: Not in this document. Copyright removal and appeal processes are delegated to Help Center pages; the terms state no standard or consequence for repeat infringement, which US safe-harbour practice normally puts in the terms themselves.

requiredDisclosures.name: Refund and cancellation rights
requiredDisclosures.note: X sells paid subscriptions, and this document contains no refund, cancellation or renewal terms at all — it routes paid users to a separate Terms for Paid Services at legal.x.com/purchaser-terms that is not part of this capture. A subscriber reading the terms of service learns nothing about their money.

requiredDisclosures.name: Company identification details
requiredDisclosures.note: Both contracting entities are identified with registered offices: X Corp., Bastrop TX, and X Internet Unlimited Company, Dublin, with Irish company number 503351 and VAT number IE9803175Q.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer complaint route
requiredDisclosures.note: For UK users, an internal complaints process plus a court claim under the Online Safety Act 2023; for EU users, internal process or out-of-court dispute settlement under the Digital Services Act. Users elsewhere get the Help Center appeals form and nothing beyond it.

requiredDisclosures.name: Effect of termination on connected third-party sign-ins
requiredDisclosures.note: A new name, narrower than anything in the existing vocabulary and specific to identity providers. Sign in with X is offered and referenced in these terms, but neither edition says what happens to a user's logins at third-party services when the X account is suspended, terminated or its username reclaimed — and the US edition reclaims usernames expressly without liability.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: X operates in India, where the IT Rules 2021 require a named Resident Grievance Officer with contact details in the terms. This document has two editions, neither of them Indian, and names no grievance officer.

analyses.summary: TikTok's Intellectual Property Policy, effective April 2025, gives rightsholders a working takedown route and gives users an appeal that is weaker than the statute it invokes. Removed content is deleted after a period the policy never states, cannot be reinstated once deleted, and even a successful appeal restores it only 'at TikTok's sole discretion' — where the US DMCA obliges a provider to put content back within 10 to 14 business days. The appeal, including your contact details, is forwarded whole to the person who reported you, and the policy states plainly that they may use it to sue you. No designated copyright agent, postal address or email appears anywhere in the document.

exposures.title: Removed content is deleted on an unstated clock and is then gone permanently
exposures.whatItMeans: Content taken down after a copyright report is deleted after 'a period of time' that the policy does not quantify, and after deletion it cannot be restored even if the report was wrong.
exposures.whyItMatters: The appeal only works if you file it before an undisclosed deadline you were never told. A creator who is travelling, ill, or simply slow to open the app loses the work outright, and there is no export of removed content.

reference.label: Information for Users: Copyright Infringement Appeal
reference.quote: We delete the removed content after a period of time in accordance with applicable laws and our data retention policy. After the deletion, your content can no longer be reinstated.

exposures.title: Winning the appeal does not get your video back
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy says TikTok may reinstate content where it does not infringe or where the claimant has not gone to court, then makes the decision discretionary regardless.
exposures.whyItMatters: Under 17 U.S.C. § 512(g) a provider that receives a valid counter-notification must replace the material in 10 to 14 business days unless the claimant sues. This policy converts that obligation into a choice, so a user with a good defence still has no entitlement to restoration.

reference.label: Information for Users: Copyright Infringement Appeal
reference.quote: The decision to reinstate any content is at TikTok’s sole discretion.

exposures.title: Your whole appeal, with your contact details, goes to the person who reported you
exposures.whatItMeans: TikTok forwards the entire appeal including any contact information to the original reporter, and states that the reporter may use it to bring a lawsuit or seek a court order keeping the content down.
exposures.whyItMatters: Contesting a takedown means handing your address details to an adversary who has already acted against you. The document is candid about the consequence, which makes the choice between losing a video and being identifiable to a claimant an explicit one.

reference.label: Information for Users: Copyright Infringement Appeal
reference.quote: The copyright claimant may use this information to file a lawsuit against you.

exposures.title: The repeat-infringer threshold is undefined and a single report can end the account
exposures.whatItMeans: A repeat infringer policy is asserted with the trigger 'in appropriate circumstances', and a separate sentence reserves immediate bans for cases TikTok considers severe.
exposures.whyItMatters: No strike count, no window and no appeal route for the ban itself is published. An account representing years of audience can be closed on one report that TikTok grades as severe, and the user cannot tell in advance where the line is.

reference.label: Removal of Content; Account Bans
reference.quote: We may exercise our discretion to immediately ban any account in cases of severe copyright violations.

exposures.title: A ban extends to any account you open afterwards
exposures.whatItMeans: TikTok reserves the right to refuse a new account to anyone whose previous account was used for improper activities.
exposures.whyItMatters: Termination is not a reset. The consequence follows the person rather than the account, and 'improper activities' is broader than the copyright infringement the policy is about.

reference.label: Removal of Content; Account Bans
reference.quote: We reserve the right to refuse any account holder whose account was used for improper activities from opening a new TikTok account.

exposures.title: No designated copyright agent, address or email is published
exposures.whatItMeans: Every route in the document — report, appeal, EU authorisation request — runs through a TikTok web form or the app. No agent is named and no postal or email contact appears anywhere.
exposures.whyItMatters: Both sides of a copyright dispute are confined to TikTok's own intake forms, with no addressable human and no channel outside the product. If the form rejects a submission for missing information, which the policy warns it may, there is nowhere else to send it.

reference.label: Information for Rightsholders
reference.quote: Failure to include necessary information may limit our ability to investigate your claims and may result in your report being denied.

exposures.title: Music is handled exactly like video, and the only sound-specific route is EU-only and for rightsholders
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy names music as an example of a protected work and then applies one identical process to everything. The single audio-specific mechanism — asking that music or audiovisual works be made unavailable — is an Article 17 route for rightsholders in the EU, not a user remedy.
exposures.whyItMatters: On a platform built on sound, a user cannot learn from this document whether an audio claim mutes the track or removes the whole video, and there is no partial remedy: the outcomes described are removal, ban, and LIVE restriction.

reference.label: EU Copyright Directive
reference.quote: If you want to request that your music or audiovisual works are made unavailable in the EU, we need you to file this form.

exposures.title: EU and non-EU users are told different amounts about what happens next
exposures.whatItMeans: The EU appeal section explains the quotation, criticism, parody and pastiche exceptions users may rely on. The non-EU section omits those and instead carries the forwarding warning and the sole-discretion sentence.
exposures.whyItMatters: A user's understanding of both their defences and their risk depends on which paragraph applies to them, and neither section cross-references the other.

reference.label: If you are a user located in the European Union

availableActions.action: Appeal from the in-app notification without waiting
availableActions.howTo: The appeal is reachable only from the in-app notification about the removal. Because the deletion clock is unstated and deletion is final, treat the notification as the start of a deadline you cannot see.

reference.label: Information for Users: Copyright Infringement Appeal
