availableActions.action: Ask the rightsholder for a retraction before appealing
availableActions.howTo: The policy suggests contacting the copyright owner directly for a retraction. This is the one route that does not put your contact details in front of a claimant who may sue.

reference.label: Information for Users: Copyright Infringement Appeal
reference.quote: you can reach out to the copyright owner directly to request a retraction

availableActions.action: If you are in the EU, name the exception you are relying on
availableActions.howTo: The policy sets out quotation, criticism, review, caricature, parody and pastiche as available exceptions and gives the fairness test — no longer than necessary, acknowledged source, no unreasonable harm. Address those three points in the appeal.

reference.label: If you are a user located in the European Union

availableActions.action: Keep your own master copy of anything you post
availableActions.howTo: There is no export or recovery of removed content and reinstatement is discretionary, so the platform copy cannot be treated as storage.

reference.label: Information for Users: Copyright Infringement Appeal

availableActions.action: Take an out-of-court or court route if the in-app process fails
availableActions.howTo: The general note acknowledges that users and rightsholders may use out-of-court dispute settlement or court proceedings under their own national law. It names no body, so the route has to be located independently.

reference.label: General Note
reference.quote: Users or rightholders may have other ways to seek resolution, such as out-of-court dispute settlement processes or in-court proceedings under laws in their countries.

requiredDisclosures.name: Designated DMCA agent
requiredDisclosures.note: 17 U.S.C. § 512(c)(2) requires a service provider claiming safe harbour to designate an agent and make that agent's name, address, phone and email available on its website. This policy names no agent and gives no address, phone or email; all reporting is routed through an online form. LinkedIn's equivalent policy publishes a named agent and postal address.

requiredDisclosures.name: Counter-notice procedure
requiredDisclosures.note: An in-app appeal exists and is described as the route for a compliant counter-notification, but the § 512(g) elements are not set out, no 10-to-14-business-day restoration window is stated, and the put-back obligation is replaced by 'TikTok's sole discretion'.

requiredDisclosures.name: Repeat infringer policy
requiredDisclosures.note: Adopted and communicated as § 512(i) requires, separately for copyright and trademark. No threshold, strike count, decay window or appeal route for the ban is disclosed — only 'in appropriate circumstances' plus a discretionary immediate ban for severe cases.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: The interval between removal and permanent deletion is the clock that decides whether an appeal can still restore content, and it is given only as 'a period of time in accordance with applicable laws and our data retention policy'. No figure appears in this document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Released 27 March 2025 and effective 26 April 2025 — a 30-day gap between publication and effect, which is better practice than most documents in this corpus. There is no clause governing how future changes will be notified.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer complaint route
requiredDisclosures.note: The general note acknowledges out-of-court dispute settlement and national court proceedings, which tracks the shape of the EU Digital Services Act. No settlement body, regulator or contact is named.

analyses.summary: Walmart's California notice gives Californians the fullest rights set in this corpus — access, deletion, correction, opt-out of sale and sharing, a limit on sensitive information, and both access to and opt-out from automated decision-making — all reachable from one Your Privacy Choices link or one phone call, with Global Privacy Control honoured and carried across devices when you are signed in. The table underneath is what those rights are for. Every collected category is marked as sold or shared for cross-context behavioural advertising, biometric information and criminal-conviction background checks included, and for all but biometrics the recipients include business partners that take the data for their own independent use rather than to serve Walmart. Walmart's own sensitive-information list has only three entries — government identifiers, account and payment credentials, precise geolocation — so voice prints, iris and retina imagery, face geometry and palm prints sit outside it and inside the sold-or-shared table. Training Walmart's AI is a named purpose with no opt-out, and no retention period is stated for anything.

exposures.title: Biometric identifiers are in the sold-or-shared table
exposures.whatItMeans: Biometric information is defined here as voice prints, imagery of the iris or retina, face geometry, and palm prints or fingerprints, and it appears as its own row in the table of categories Walmart may sell or share for cross-context behavioural advertising, to vendors described as including advertising networks, marketplace sellers and analytics providers.
exposures.whyItMatters: A face or a palm print cannot be reissued after it leaves. Walmart's own definition of sensitive personal information in this notice lists only government identifiers, account log-in and payment details, and precise geolocation, so biometrics are not covered by the sensitive-information protections the notice elsewhere describes, including the promise that sensitive information is kept out of targeted advertising.

reference.label: What Are the Categories of Personal Information Collected?
reference.quote: Biometric Information, such as voice prints, imagery of the iris or retina, face geometry, and palm prints or fingerprints.

exposures.title: Criminal convictions go to business partners for their own use
exposures.whatItMeans: Background Information is defined as background checks and criminal convictions, and its row in the sale and sharing table lists both vendors for business operations and business partners that receive data for their own independent use and not to provide services to a Walmart entity.
exposures.whyItMatters: A criminal record is the single category most likely to cost someone a job, a tenancy or a loan, and 'business partners for their own independent use' is a recipient class with no contractual limit stated and no name attached. Once it is transferred for a partner's own purposes, Walmart's deletion right does not reach it.

reference.label: Sale and Sharing of Personal Information
reference.quote: Business partners, including those that receive data for their own independent use and not to provide services to a Walmart entity.

exposures.title: Sensitive information is used to build inferences that sell you things
exposures.whatItMeans: One sentence states that sensitive personal information is used for every purpose listed above it and, additionally, to make inferences about customers which Walmart may use to promote certain products or services.
exposures.whyItMatters: Inferring characteristics from sensitive personal information for marketing is precisely the use the CCPA limit right exists to stop. Walmart does offer that right, which is to its credit, but it is opt-out: until you find Your Privacy Choices and use it, government identifiers, payment credentials and precise geolocation are feeding a marketing profile.

reference.label: What Are the Purposes for Collecting Personal Information?
reference.quote: We use sensitive personal information for each of the purposes described above and to make inferences about customers, which we may use to promote certain products or services.

exposures.title: Training Walmart's AI is a listed purpose with no opt-out
exposures.whatItMeans: Among the purposes for collecting personal information is verifying, maintaining, improving, upgrading or enhancing services and devices, 'such as training our AI'. Communications — the content of emails, text messages and interactions with Walmart's AI assistant chatbots — is a collected category, and the rights list contains no objection to this use.
exposures.whyItMatters: Every other right in this notice has a route attached to it; this use has none. What you typed to a shopping chatbot becomes training material, and the only lever the document offers is deletion, which also closes your account and disables in-store functions.

reference.label: What Are the Purposes for Collecting Personal Information?
reference.quote: such as training our AI

exposures.title: The pre-use notice says Walmart may make significant decisions about you automatically
exposures.whatItMeans: A pre-use notice states Walmart may use Automated Decision-Making Technologies to help make decisions that could have a significant impact on you, and that if implemented, notice will be given and rights will be exercisable through Your Privacy Choices.
exposures.whyItMatters: Walmart's main privacy notice states it does not engage in profiling in furtherance of decisions producing legal or similarly significant effects. This document says it may. Two documents from the same company, both current, describe the same practice in opposite directions, and only one of them carries the rights.

reference.label: Automated Decision-Making Technologies Pre-Use Notice
reference.quote: We may use Automated Decision-Making Technologies to help us make decisions that could have a significant impact on you.

exposures.title: The retention limit is partly Walmart's own internal policy
exposures.whatItMeans: Personal information is kept as long as necessary for the stated purposes, but no longer than required or permitted under applicable law or internal Walmart policy, and disposed of in accordance with Walmart's retention policies and procedures. No period is given for any category, including biometrics.
exposures.whyItMatters: One half of the outer bound is a document the reader cannot see and Walmart can change. The main Walmart privacy notice does publish a biometric destruction schedule — purpose satisfied, three years from last interaction, or as law requires — and that schedule does not appear here, so the biometric data this notice puts in the sold-or-shared table has no stated life in this document.

reference.label: How Long Do We Retain Your Personal Information?
reference.quote: but no longer than as required or permitted under applicable law or internal Walmart policy

exposures.title: Deletion closes your account and reaches into the store
exposures.whatItMeans: Exercising the deletion right may affect your ability to use the websites and online features, including closure of your online account, and limit your use of in-store functions that require personal information.
exposures.whyItMatters: The consequence is disclosed honestly, and it is still a price on a statutory right: order history, saved prescriptions and membership benefits sit on the account the request closes. The notice does not say which in-store functions stop working, so the cost cannot be assessed in advance.

reference.label: Delete My Personal Information
reference.quote: including closure of your online account

exposures.title: How you type is collected to tell you apart from a bot
exposures.whatItMeans: Internet and other network activity information expressly includes keystroke patterns, given as the example of how Walmart determines whether it is you or a bot interacting with it.
exposures.whyItMatters: Typing rhythm is a behavioural biometric that identifies a person across sessions and accounts, and it is placed here in the ordinary network-activity category rather than the biometric one — so it inherits none of the protections attached to biometrics, and that whole category is marked as sold or shared.

reference.label: What Are the Categories of Personal Information Collected?
reference.quote: keystroke patterns which help us determine if it is you or a bot

exposures.title: Access requests are capped at two a year
exposures.whatItMeans: Requests to access personal information may be submitted up to two times in a rolling twelve-month period. Identity verification requires name, address and, optionally, email and phone, with third-party identification services and a one-time passcode possible, and unverified requests are not processed.
exposures.whyItMatters: The cap is what the CCPA allows, so it is not a deviation — but combined with a category list that changes as Walmart's services change, two snapshots a year is the whole visibility a consumer gets into a dataset that includes biometrics and background checks.

reference.label: Request to Access My Personal Information
reference.quote: Requests to access your personal information may be submitted up to two times in a rolling 12-month period.

exposures.title: Nobody is named on the receiving end
exposures.whatItMeans: Every recipient in the sale and sharing table is a category — vendors for business operations, advertising networks, marketplace sellers, analytics providers, cloud storage providers, and business partners. No company is named anywhere in the document.
exposures.whyItMatters: The opt-out stops future sharing; it does not tell you who already holds the data or let you approach them. With criminal-conviction and biometric categories in the same table, the identity of the recipient is the fact that determines the consequence, and it is the one fact withheld.

reference.label: Sale and Sharing of Personal Information

availableActions.action: Use one link for all seven rights
availableActions.howTo: The Your Privacy Choices link in the website footer or the app settings section covers access, deletion, correction, opt-out of sale and sharing, the limit on sensitive personal information, and both automated decision-making rights. The phone alternative is 1-800-925-6278, press one, say 'Privacy'.

reference.label: What Are Your California Privacy Rights?

availableActions.action: Send Global Privacy Control and sign in once
availableActions.howTo: Walmart honours GPC for the browser or device that sends it, and when you then log in from that device the opt-out extends to your whole account. Signing in while opted out is what makes the choice follow you to other devices, so do both.

deadline.description: Immediately effective for data collected during that interaction; up to 15 days for data already held in Walmart's systems.

reference.label: Stop Selling or Sharing My Personal Information
reference.quote: it may take up to 15 days from receipt of your request to process the opt-out

availableActions.action: Limit the use of your sensitive personal information
availableActions.howTo: Ask Walmart to limit use and disclosure of sensitive personal information to the purposes law permits, through Your Privacy Choices. Once processed, the same page confirms the preference, so you can verify it took effect rather than assuming it did.

reference.label: Limit the Use and Disclosure of SPI

availableActions.action: Opt out of automated decisions before they are made about you
availableActions.howTo: Walmart states you can ask that significant decisions not be made about you using Automated Decision-Making Technologies, and can request access to decisions already made that way, both via Your Privacy Choices. Take this as available now rather than waiting for a notice, since the pre-use notice does not say when implementation begins.

availableActions.action: Ask for the Shine the Light list
availableActions.howTo: California residents can request the categories of personal information disclosed to third parties for those third parties' own direct marketing in the preceding calendar year, and the identity of those third parties. Write to the Walmart Privacy Office, MS #0160, 811 Excellence Dr, Bentonville, AR 72716-0160. This is the only route in the document that produces named recipients.

availableActions.action: Withhold consent for precise location
availableActions.howTo: Geolocation is described as imprecise by default, inferred from your IP address, and precise only if you provide consent. Declining the device location permission keeps it at the imprecise level rather than switching the service off.

reference.label: What Are the Categories of Personal Information Collected?

availableActions.action: Send an authorised agent with a signed letter
availableActions.howTo: An agent can use the same links. Walmart requires a power of attorney or a letter signed by you, uploadable at submission or within 10 business days after, and emailable to consumerprivacy@wal-mart.com if you filed by phone.

reference.label: How Do I Submit a Request Using an Authorized Agent?

availableActions.action: Read the Spanish edition or the request metrics
availableActions.howTo: The notice is published in Spanish, and Walmart links its count of California privacy requests fulfilled last year. Both sit at the top and bottom of this page and neither is reproduced inside it.

reference.label: Number of Requests Fulfilled Last Year

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of personal information sold or shared
requiredDisclosures.note: A twelve-row table naming, for each category, the recipient types. Complete and damaging to read: biometric information, background checks and criminal convictions, communications content, and financial information all appear, and every row but biometrics lists business partners receiving data for their own independent use.

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of personal data collected
requiredDisclosures.note: Thirteen categories with worked examples, including vehicle make, model, year, odometer reading and VIN from Auto Care Centers, household income, family health, number of children and cars owned, citizenship and ethnicity, criminal convictions, keystroke patterns and inferences about intelligence and aptitudes.

requiredDisclosures.name: Sensitive personal information categories
requiredDisclosures.note: Present but narrow: government-issued identifiers, account log-in and financial information, and precise geolocation — three entries. Biometric information is defined elsewhere in the notice as voice prints, iris and retina imagery, face geometry and palm prints, and is not among them, so the sensitive-information protections and the limit right do not reach it. Bank of America's CCPA notice in this corpus does classify biometric processing as sensitive.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: Your Privacy Choices link, phone line, and Global Privacy Control, with the opt-out propagating from browser to account on sign-in and to other devices when logged in. Immediately effective for the current interaction, up to 15 days for stored data, and a footer notification confirms the signal was received. Among the better opt-out implementations in the corpus.

requiredDisclosures.name: Right to limit use of sensitive personal information
requiredDisclosures.note: Offered explicitly, with confirmation of the preference on the same page where it was set. It matters here because the notice states outright that sensitive personal information is used to make inferences used to promote products, which is the use the right exists to stop.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automated decision-making rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Both access to and opt-out from Automated Decision-Making Technologies, plus a pre-use notice that such technologies may be used for decisions with significant impact. Notable because Walmart's main privacy notice states the opposite — that it does not engage in profiling in furtherance of decisions producing legal or similarly significant effects — and carries no such rights.

requiredDisclosures.name: Data subject rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Seven rights, each with its own section, its verification requirements, and its consequences. Non-retaliation is stated in operative terms — no denial of goods, different prices, or different quality — with the honest caveat that programmes requiring personal information may stop working.

requiredDisclosures.name: Shine the Light disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: The annual right under California Civil Code section 1798.83 to a list of categories disclosed for third parties' direct marketing and the identity of those third parties, exercisable by writing to the Bentonville privacy office.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period for any category. The outer bound is what law requires or permits, or internal Walmart policy — half of it unpublished and unilaterally changeable. The biometric destruction schedule that appears in Walmart's main privacy notice is not carried across into this document.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: Training Walmart's AI is named as a purpose for collecting personal information, and chatbot interactions are a collected category, but the seven-item rights list contains no objection or opt-out for that use. The same absence was recorded against Walmart's main privacy notice.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: No company is named anywhere. Recipients are given as vendors for business operations, advertising networks, marketplace sellers, analytics providers, cloud storage providers, and business partners. The Shine the Light request is the only route in the document that would produce identities.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Weakly but genuinely: the notice opens with a 'We Recently Updated Our Privacy Notice' block listing what changed — here, updated Contact Us information — alongside an Updated date of February 16, 2026. There is no commitment to notify anyone or any advance period, but a stated change log is more than Walmart's main privacy notice or either Bank of America notice provides.

requiredDisclosures.name: Children under 13
requiredDisclosures.note: Walmart states it does not knowingly sell or share for cross-context behavioural advertising the personal information of consumers under 16. It also discloses collecting information about children under 13 in connection with certain purchases and services, giving tobacco purchases as the example, and refers to the main privacy notice for the rest.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named Grievance Officer
requiredDisclosures.note: No individual is named. The contact is the Walmart Corporate Privacy Office, MS #0160, 811 Excellence Dr, Bentonville, AR 72716-0160, plus the customer service team and consumerprivacy@wal-mart.com for agent documentation. The same absence was recorded against Walmart's main privacy notice, so it holds across both documents.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer complaint route
requiredDisclosures.note: The notice says Walmart will notify you with reasons if it cannot comply with a request, and then stops. There is no appeal, no escalation, and no reference to the California Privacy Protection Agency or the Attorney General as the complaint route. Walmart's main privacy notice does describe an appeal where a request is refused; this one does not.

analyses.summary: OpenAI's terms give up more to the user than most in this corpus — you own the output, you can opt out of model training, price rises need thirty days' notice, and the indemnity applies only to businesses, not consumers. What they take is your day in court: mandatory arbitration, a class-action waiver and a jury-trial waiver, applied retroactively to claims that arose before these terms existed. There is a thirty-day window to opt out of arbitration, and it starts when you create the account.

exposures.title: Arbitration, no class actions, no jury — and it reaches backwards
exposures.whatItMeans: All disputes go to binding arbitration before a sole arbitrator, class and representative actions are prohibited, jury trial is waived, and the clause covers claims 'regardless of when the claim arose, even if it was before these Terms existed'.
exposures.whyItMatters: Class actions are the only practical route for a harm that is small per person and large in aggregate — precisely the shape of most consumer AI harms. The retroactive reach means agreeing today can capture a claim you already had.

reference.label: MANDATORY ARBITRATION
reference.quote: resolve any claims arising out of or relating to these Terms or our Services, regardless of when the claim arose, even if it was before these Terms existed

exposures.title: Mass claims are batched fifty at a time
exposures.whatItMeans: If 25 or more claimants with similar counsel file substantially similar disputes within 90 days, they are administered in batches of up to 50 with one arbitrator, one set of fees and one hearing per batch.
exposures.whyItMatters: Batching is the answer to mass arbitration, which was itself the answer to class waivers. It means fifty separate grievances get one hearing and one decision-maker.

exposures.title: Liability capped at what you paid, or one hundred dollars
exposures.whatItMeans: Aggregate liability cannot exceed the greater of what you paid for the service that gave rise to the claim in the previous twelve months, or US$100. Indirect, incidental, special, consequential and exemplary damages, including lost profits and lost data, are excluded entirely.
exposures.whyItMatters: For a free ChatGPT user the cap is one hundred dollars for any harm the service causes, and the excluded categories cover most of what an AI error actually costs someone.

exposures.title: A work email address can hand your account to your employer
exposures.whatItMeans: An account created with an organisation-owned email address may be added to that organisation's business account, after which the administrator can control the account, access your Content, and restrict or remove your access.
exposures.whyItMatters: Everything you typed into a personal-feeling chat becomes readable by your employer's administrator. Notice is promised — unless your organisation already told you it may monitor and control the account.

reference.label: Corporate domains
reference.quote: the organization’s administrator will be able to control your account, including being able to access Content (defined below) and restrict or remove your access to the account

exposures.title: Payments are not refundable
exposures.whatItMeans: You can cancel a paid subscription at any time, but payments are non-refundable except where required by law.
exposures.whyItMatters: Cancelling mid-period ends renewal, not the charge. The terms do preserve mandatory local cancellation rights, which matters in the EU and UK.

exposures.title: Your content trains the models unless you opt out
exposures.whatItMeans: Content may be used to provide, maintain, develop and improve the Services. A separate opt-out exists for model training, reached through a linked help article.
exposures.whyItMatters: The default is in, and the control lives outside the terms in a help article rather than as a setting the terms describe. The terms also warn opting out may limit how well the service handles your use case.

availableActions.action: Opt out of arbitration within 30 days
availableActions.howTo: Fill out the opt-out form linked in the arbitration section. The window is 30 days from account creation, and a fresh 30 days opens after any update to the arbitration terms. If you opt out of an update, the previously agreed arbitration terms continue to apply.

deadline.description: 30 days from account creation, or 30 days after any update to the arbitration terms takes effect.

reference.label: MANDATORY ARBITRATION
reference.quote: You may opt out of arbitration within 30 days of account creation or of any updates to these arbitration terms within 30 days after the update has taken effect

availableActions.action: Turn off model training on your content
availableActions.howTo: The terms link an article with the opt-out instructions. It is a real control, but it is off the terms page and defaults to on.

availableActions.action: Use a personal email, not a work one
availableActions.howTo: An account on an organisation-owned domain can be absorbed into that organisation's business account, giving its administrator access to your conversations. A personal address avoids that entirely.

availableActions.action: Use small claims court instead of arbitration
availableActions.howTo: Individual claims in small claims court are expressly carved out of both the informal-resolution requirement and arbitration.

availableActions.action: Cancel within 30 days of a price rise
availableActions.howTo: Price increases require at least 30 days' notice and take effect on your next renewal, so there is a real window to cancel before paying more.

requiredDisclosures.name: Arbitration opt-out right
requiredDisclosures.note: A 30-day opt-out is offered with a linked form, and re-opens on each update to the arbitration terms — considerably clearer than the norm.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: At least 30 days' notice by email or in-product notification for changes that materially adversely affect you.

requiredDisclosures.name: Ownership of AI output
requiredDisclosures.note: OpenAI assigns its right, title and interest in Output to the user, with the caveat that output may not be unique.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer indemnity
requiredDisclosures.note: The indemnity is expressly limited to businesses and organisations. Individual consumers are not asked to indemnify — a meaningful contrast with Apple and Chase in this corpus.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automatic renewal disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: States the payment method is charged automatically on each periodic renewal until cancelled, with cancellation available at any time.

analyses.summary: Amazon's cookie notice is short and readable, and it makes one thing explicit that most do not: refusing cookies does not degrade the service, it removes it. You cannot add to cart, check out, or use anything requiring sign-in. It was last updated in January 2020 and offers no consent choice at all — only browser-level blocking, which it describes as breaking the site.

exposures.title: Refusing cookies removes the ability to buy anything
exposures.whatItMeans: Blocking Amazon's cookies means no shopping cart, no checkout, and no access to any signed-in service.
exposures.whyItMatters: There is no middle setting. Consent to the full cookie set, including the advertising ones, is bundled with the ability to transact at all — so 'choice' here is use-it-or-leave-it rather than a preference.

reference.label: Cookies
reference.quote: if you block or otherwise reject our cookies, you will not be able to add items to your Shopping Cart, proceed to Checkout, or use any Amazon products and services that require you to sign in

exposures.title: Advertising follows you onto third-party sites
exposures.whatItMeans: Cookies are used to deliver interest-based ads both on Amazon and on sites that are not Amazon.
exposures.whyItMatters: Your shopping behaviour becomes an input to advertising you see elsewhere, and the notice points to a separate Interest-Based Ads document rather than setting the limits here.

reference.label: Cookies
reference.quote: Delivering content, including ads, relevant to your interests on Amazon sites and third-party sites

exposures.title: Third parties including social networks set their own cookies
exposures.whatItMeans: Search engines, analytics providers, social media networks and advertising companies may set cookies when you use Amazon.
exposures.whyItMatters: The set of parties receiving data is described by category, not by name, so you cannot determine who actually holds it or review their terms.

reference.label: Cookies
reference.quote: Approved third parties may also set cookies when you interact with Amazon services.

exposures.title: Last updated January 2020
exposures.whatItMeans: The document carries a 2020 date and does not reference any consent framework introduced since.
exposures.whyItMatters: A cookie notice that has not moved in six years, on a service that has changed substantially, is weak evidence about current practice.

reference.label: Cookies
reference.quote: Last updated: January 1, 2020

availableActions.action: Turn off interest-based ads in Your Account
availableActions.howTo: The notice states advertising preferences are set through Your Account. This limits ad personalisation without breaking checkout.

reference.label: Cookies
reference.quote: You may set your preferences through Your Account.

availableActions.action: Block third-party cookies only, not all cookies
availableActions.howTo: Blocking all cookies disables cart and checkout. Blocking only third-party cookies in your browser targets the advertising channel and leaves the first-party ones the notice says are essential.

availableActions.action: Check the mobile setting separately
availableActions.howTo: The notice warns that mobile operating systems apply their own limits and that your Amazon choices do not override them — so a preference set on desktop does not follow you to the app.

reference.label: Cookies
reference.quote: your choices do not override those more limited settings on such mobile devices

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: The notice describes advertising and analytics cookies but offers no consent choice — only browser blocking, which it states breaks core functionality. No lawful basis is stated in this document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: Not present in this document. The page footer links 'Your Ads Privacy Choices' and 'Additional State-Specific Privacy Disclosures'; this analysis covers only this document's text.

requiredDisclosures.name: Purposes for which cookies are used
requiredDisclosures.note: Eight purposes are enumerated, including advertising, research and reporting.

analyses.summary: Zoom's terms carry the most engineered dispute-resolution architecture in the corpus. Claims must be filed within one year or are permanently barred. Arbitration is mandatory with a class and mass action waiver, and the opt-out window ran for thirty days from April 2023 or from account creation, with a clause stating expressly that later versions never reopen it. Reject a settlement offer and fail to beat it and you pay Zoom's costs from that point, attorneys' fees included. If fifty similar claims are filed within 180 days, only sixteen proceed and the rest are held in abeyance. Liability is capped at what you paid in the preceding twelve months — nothing, for a free user — and unauthorised access to, loss of, deletion of or alteration of Customer Content is excluded by name, so a breach of your recordings is outside the cap rather than inside it. Feedback is irrevocably assigned to Zoom and then treated as Zoom's confidential information until Zoom decides otherwise, which is the only clause in the corpus that takes your idea and silences you about it. Set against that, the AI training commitment from the privacy statement is repeated here in the contract itself, and thirty days of post-termination access to retrieve your content is guaranteed.

exposures.title: One year to bring any claim, or it is gone
exposures.whatItMeans: Notwithstanding any other statute of limitations, any claim or cause of action under the agreement must be filed within one year of arising or it is permanently barred. Only intellectual property disputes are excluded.
exposures.whyItMatters: Statutory limitation periods for contract and consumer claims typically run three to six years. Harms of the kind this agreement concerns — a data breach, a billing practice, a wrongful termination of service — are often not discovered inside twelve months, and the clock runs from when the claim arose rather than from discovery.

reference.label: 27.10 Requirement to File Within One Year
reference.quote: any claim or cause of action under this Agreement ... must be filed within one (1) year after such claim or cause of action arose, or else that claim or cause of action will be permanently barred

exposures.title: Losing a settlement offer makes you pay Zoom's legal costs
exposures.whatItMeans: Either party may serve a written offer of judgment at least ten days before the arbitration hearing. If you decline and then fail to obtain a more favourable award, you recover none of your post-offer costs and must pay Zoom's costs from the time of the offer, which may include reasonable attorneys' fees up to the amount of damages awarded.
exposures.whyItMatters: This converts pressing a valid but modest claim into a financial risk. Winning less than Zoom offered leaves you worse off than accepting, so the practical effect is to make Zoom's first number close to final for any consumer without counsel.

reference.label: 27.8 Settlement Offers and Offers of Judgment

exposures.title: Fifty similar claims become sixteen, and the rest wait
exposures.whatItMeans: Where fifty or more substantially similar arbitration demands are brought against either party with the assistance of the same law firms or organisations within 180 days, sixteen are selected to proceed as Bellwether Arbitrations and the remainder are held in abeyance and may not be filed, processed or adjudicated until those conclude and a global mediation has been attempted.
exposures.whyItMatters: The class action is waived and mass individual arbitration — the remaining route for many people with the same complaint — is throttled to sixteen at a time. Zoom pays the bellwether costs and limitation periods are tolled, which softens it, but a claimant not selected waits on a process they cannot influence.

exposures.title: Loss of your meeting content is excluded from liability entirely
exposures.whatItMeans: Zoom's aggregate liability is capped at what you actually paid in the twelve months preceding the claim, and unauthorised access to, loss of, deletion of, or alteration of system data, Customer Content or Customer Data is separately listed as a category for which Zoom will not be liable at all. The warranty section adds that Zoom does not assume any responsibility for retention of any data.
exposures.whyItMatters: The excluded category names exactly what a customer of a recording and messaging platform would sue over. For a free account the cap is zero regardless, and for a paying customer the breach exclusion sits outside the cap rather than being limited by it.

reference.label: 26. Limitation on Liability
reference.quote: UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS TO, LOSS OF, DELETION OF, OR ALTERATION OF SYSTEM DATA, CUSTOMER CONTENT, OR CUSTOMER DATA

exposures.title: Your ideas are assigned to Zoom and then made Zoom's secret
exposures.whatItMeans: Feedback — including ideas, know-how, concepts, and suggested features — is owned by Zoom, and you unconditionally and irrevocably assign all right, title and interest in it, undertaking to make your employees, contractors, agents and end users do the same. All feedback is then treated as Zoom Confidential Information until Zoom in its sole discretion decides otherwise.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the ninth appearance of the ideas-become-ours clause in the corpus and the most severe: assignment of title, no compensation or attribution, extended to people you must bind on Zoom's behalf, and combined with a confidentiality obligation that stops you discussing your own idea afterwards. No other document adds the silence.

reference.label: 16.1 Feedback
reference.quote: All Feedback is and will be treated as Zoom Confidential Information until Zoom, in its sole discretion, chooses to make any specific Feedback non-confidential.

exposures.title: The arbitration opt-out closed in 2023 and never reopens
exposures.whatItMeans: Arbitration under NAM rules, or ADR Services for California residents, with class, collective, representative and mass action waivers and a jury trial waiver. The opt-out required an individualised email within thirty days of 1 April 2023 for existing users, or thirty days of account creation for new ones, and the modifications section states that changes to the agreement do not create a renewed opportunity to opt out.
exposures.whyItMatters: It also reaches backwards: disputes are defined to include facts occurring before this or any prior version of the agreement, and this arbitration agreement supersedes all previous versions. Anyone who held an account in April 2023 and did not act within thirty days is bound, including for earlier events.

exposures.title: Confidentiality runs one way
exposures.whatItMeans: Zoom Confidential Information covers anything you learn in connection with the services — business information, roadmaps, pricing, processes — whether or not marked confidential, and anything you reasonably should understand to be confidential. Your confidential information covers only what law requires to be kept confidential, plus sensitive security and technical information you clearly and conspicuously mark. Customer Content is expressly not Customer Confidential Information.
exposures.whyItMatters: Unmarked information flowing to you is protected by default; information flowing from you is not protected unless you marked it, and your meetings and files are excluded from the definition regardless. Pricing you were quoted is Zoom's confidential information.

exposures.title: Termination for no reason, and charges are kept
exposures.whatItMeans: Zoom may suspend immediately or terminate effective immediately for any non-compliance with the agreement or any referenced policy, and may terminate for any reason or no reason on thirty business days' notice. All charges are non-cancelable and non-refundable for the term, Zoom may retain charges already paid on termination, and you remain liable for charges accruing during a suspension.
exposures.whyItMatters: Paying for a period you were suspended from is the sharp end. The counterweight is real and worth naming: thirty calendar days of access after termination to retrieve your Customer Content, which several other documents in this corpus do not offer at all.

exposures.title: Policies can change with no notice at all
exposures.whatItMeans: Changes to the terms are posted with an effective date and you are told to check regularly and save copies; continued use after the effective date is agreement. Separately, Zoom may modify, delete and add to its guides, statements, policies and notices with or without notice to you, by posting an updated version.
exposures.whyItMatters: The Acceptable Use Guidelines are incorporated into the agreement and breaching them permits immediate termination, yet they sit in the category that can change silently. Keeping your email address current is made your responsibility for notices Zoom is not committed to sending.

exposures.title: Your logo becomes Zoom marketing material automatically
exposures.whatItMeans: You grant Zoom permission to identify you as a customer and use your logo across its marketing materials — website, emails, presentations, brochures. Case studies require your written approval; the logo use does not.
exposures.whyItMatters: The customer-reference right is granted by accepting the terms rather than negotiated, and for an organisation the fact of using a particular vendor can itself be sensitive.

exposures.title: Tax authorities can be told without notice, before or after
exposures.whatItMeans: Notwithstanding Zoom's other notice obligations and its Government Request Guide, Zoom may disclose customer information including Customer Confidential Information to a tax authority without notice to you either before or after the disclosure.
exposures.whyItMatters: Elsewhere Zoom commits to notifying you before compelled disclosures unless prohibited or unsafe. This clause removes that commitment for one recipient category entirely, including retrospectively.

availableActions.action: Send the Pre-Arbitration Demand properly, and use the sixty days
availableActions.howTo: Mail an individualised, signed demand with your name, phone, mailing and account email address, and a description of the dispute, to ATTN: Litigation Department, Zoom Communications, 55 Almaden Blvd, San Jose, CA 95113. Compliance is a condition precedent — the arbitrator must dismiss an arbitration filed without it — and either side may arbitrate after sixty days.

deadline.description: Arbitration may be brought sixty calendar days after a Pre-Arbitration Demand. Limitation periods are tolled while this process runs.

availableActions.action: Bring it in small claims court instead
availableActions.howTo: Small claims actions on an individual basis are excluded from arbitration, as are intellectual property claims. Electing small claims before an arbitrator is appointed closes the arbitration administratively.

availableActions.action: Act inside one year, whatever else happens
availableActions.howTo: Any claim not filed within one year of arising is permanently barred. Send the Pre-Arbitration Demand early, since the limitation period is tolled only once that informal process has begun.

deadline.description: One year from when the claim arose, after which it is permanently barred. Tolled during the informal dispute resolution process.

reference.label: 27.10 Requirement to File Within One Year

availableActions.action: Ask for an arbitration cost waiver
availableActions.howTo: If your gross monthly income is less than 300% of the federal poverty guidelines you may be entitled to a waiver of certain arbitration costs. Zoom also pays the provider's costs for the sixteen Bellwether Arbitrations in a mass filing.

availableActions.action: Cancel before the renewal notice period closes
availableActions.howTo: Renewal is automatic unless either party gives written notice at least thirty calendar days before the next term, through the billing portal or by email to renewals@zoom.us. Payments are non-cancelable and non-refundable once a term begins.

deadline.description: At least 30 calendar days before the next Renewal Term begins, or the period applicable law requires.

availableActions.action: Retrieve everything within thirty days of termination
availableActions.howTo: Zoom provides access to retrieve Customer Content for thirty calendar days after expiry or termination, after which it is deleted under Zoom's scheduled deletion protocols. This window applies regardless of why the agreement ended.

deadline.description: Thirty calendar days following expiration or termination to retrieve Customer Content.

reference.label: 14.5 Deletion and Access to Customer Content After Termination

availableActions.action: Use the Rate Change Notice window
availableActions.howTo: Price changes carry at least thirty calendar days' notice and take effect at the next renewal. You must terminate or modify the affected services within that notice period, or you are deemed to have accepted the change.

deadline.description: Not less than 30 calendar days' Rate Change Notice; failing to terminate or modify within it is deemed acceptance.

availableActions.action: Mark anything sensitive you send as confidential
availableActions.howTo: Your information is only Customer Confidential Information if law requires confidentiality or if it is sensitive security and technical information clearly and conspicuously marked confidential. Anything unmarked has no protection under the confidentiality section.

availableActions.action: Remove a backup payment method you do not want charged
availableActions.howTo: Adding a backup payment method authorises Zoom to charge it when the primary is declined, and Zoom may also use updated card details supplied by your issuing bank to charge a card that has been replaced.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: The commitment from the privacy statement is repeated in the contract itself: Zoom does not use audio, video, chat, screen sharing, attachments or other communications-like Customer Content, including poll results, whiteboards and reactions, to train Zoom or third-party AI models. Putting it in the terms makes it a contractual promise rather than a policy statement.

requiredDisclosures.name: Arbitration opt-out right
requiredDisclosures.note: Disclosed with its limits: thirty days from 1 April 2023 for existing users or from account creation for new ones, by individualised email to opt-out@zoom.us, and expressly not reopened by any later version of the agreement. Effectively closed for anyone with an account before mid-2023.

requiredDisclosures.name: Pre-arbitration dispute procedure
requiredDisclosures.note: A signed, individualised Pre-Arbitration Demand by post with specified contents, a sixty-day resolution period, and compliance made a condition precedent that the arbitrator must enforce by dismissal.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: California law with exclusive jurisdiction in Santa Clara County state courts and the Northern District of California, the FAA governing arbitration, and preserved non-derogable consumer protections for EU, EEA and UK consumers.

requiredDisclosures.name: Company identification details
requiredDisclosures.note: Zoom Communications, Inc., 55 Almaden Blvd, Suite 600, San Jose, CA 95113, with ZVC India Pvt. Ltd. named as the contracting entity for accounts with an Indian bill-to or sold-to address.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: No notice is committed to. Changes are posted with an effective date, users are told to check regularly and keep their own copies, and continued use is agreement. Guides and policies incorporated into the agreement may change with or without notice.

requiredDisclosures.name: Automatic renewal disclosure
requiredDisclosures.note: Renewal is automatic unless notice is given at least thirty days before the next term, with the termination route named, and a reminder notice promised where applicable law requires one.

requiredDisclosures.name: Advance notice of fee changes
requiredDisclosures.note: Not less than thirty calendar days' Rate Change Notice, effective at the next renewal, with a reminder of termination rights where law requires. Taxes and fees, by contrast, may be changed without notice.

requiredDisclosures.name: Refund and cancellation rights
requiredDisclosures.note: Disclosed and adverse: non-cancelable and non-refundable for the term, charges retained on termination, and liability for charges during a suspension. Statutory withdrawal and cooling-off rights are expressly preserved with a pro rata refund where they apply.

requiredDisclosures.name: Minimum age
requiredDisclosures.note: Sixteen, unless through a School Subscriber using Zoom for Education (K-12).

requiredDisclosures.name: Limitation on indemnity
requiredDisclosures.note: The customer indemnity is uncapped and covers use of the services, breach, IP violations, disputes between you and your own end users, and third-party personal injury or property damage. Zoom's own liability is capped at twelve months of fees with data loss excluded outright.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer rights preservation
requiredDisclosures.note: Liability limits apply only where not prohibited by law, EU, EEA and UK consumers keep non-derogable local protections, and withdrawal and cooling-off rights are preserved.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period is stated. Deletion after termination follows Zoom's regularly scheduled deletion protocols, and the warranty section disclaims any responsibility for retention of data at all.

analyses.summary: OpenAI's cookie policy is the most itemised in this corpus: roughly 130 cookies listed by name, source, duration and domain, updated August 2026. What that itemisation makes visible is that marketing-measurement cookies from six outside advertising networks — Meta, Google, Microsoft Bing, Reddit, TikTok and LinkedIn — run on chatgpt.com itself, not just the marketing site, with lifetimes up to 400 days. Consent is offered only where local law requires it, and the document contains no Do Not Sell or Share link, no Global Privacy Control statement, and no sentence distinguishing signed-in users from logged-out visitors.

exposures.title: Six advertising networks measure your use of chatgpt.com
exposures.whatItMeans: The Marketing Performance table lists cookies set by Meta, Google, Bing, Reddit, TikTok and LinkedIn on chatgpt.com and openai.com, with durations including Meta's datr and sb at 400 days and Google's IDE at 24 months.
exposures.whyItMatters: These are the same identifiers those networks use to build advertising profiles elsewhere. They are present on the domain where people type their questions, so the fact that you use ChatGPT — and when — is measurable by six advertising businesses that have nothing to do with the product.

reference.label: Marketing Performance cookies
reference.quote: These cookies help us support and understand the efficacy of our marketing efforts

exposures.title: Cookie choice exists only where the law compels it
exposures.whatItMeans: The Managing cookies section conditions the entire control surface on jurisdiction rather than offering it to everyone.
exposures.whyItMatters: Two people using the same product get different rights depending on where they live. A user outside the EU, UK or a US state with a privacy statute is told only to use browser settings.

reference.label: Managing cookies
reference.quote: Depending on applicable law, you may be able to choose which cookies are used when using our Services.

exposures.title: The un-refusable Necessary bucket carries third-party vendor cookies for up to a year
exposures.whatItMeans: The Necessary table — explicitly not disableable — includes Intercom device IDs lasting 270 days to 1 year, Cloudflare cf_clearance at 1 year, Stripe __stripe_mid at 1 year, Auth0 identifiers at 14 days to 1 year, and a Google cookie at 6 months.
exposures.whyItMatters: Everything in this category is set without consent and cannot be turned off, and it is not limited to OpenAI's own servers — six outside companies receive durable per-device identifiers on that basis.

reference.label: Managing cookies
reference.quote: Cookies listed as “Necessary” are required for the Services to function and cannot be disabled.

exposures.title: Nothing distinguishes a signed-in user from someone who never had an account
exposures.whatItMeans: The policy scopes itself to cookies used 'in connection with our Services' and never states whether the advertising and analytics cookies apply before sign-in, after sign-out, or to visitors who never register.
exposures.whyItMatters: The advertising cookies are listed against openai.com and ads.openai.com, which anyone can reach without an account, so the practical answer appears to be that they do apply — but the document does not say so, which leaves the most privacy-relevant question about a public marketing site unanswered.

reference.label: Cookie policy
reference.quote: This Cookie Policy describes what kinds of cookies and similar technologies OpenAI uses in connection with our Services

exposures.title: No CCPA opt-out route and no Global Privacy Control statement
exposures.whatItMeans: The document that discloses cross-context advertising cookies offers no Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information link, no statement on Global Privacy Control, and no statement on Do Not Track.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the document a US resident would read to find the opt-out, and it points them at browser settings instead. Peers with far weaker cookie disclosure — Dropbox and Zoom — both state a GPC position here.

exposures.title: Preferences must be set again on every browser and device
exposures.whatItMeans: Cookie settings do not follow the account; they are stored per browser.
exposures.whyItMatters: Someone who declines marketing cookies on their laptop is still counted on their phone, and the consent cookies themselves expire after six months to a year, so the choice has to be remade.

reference.label: Managing cookies
reference.quote: Cookie settings are device- and browser-specific, so you will need to set cookie preferences for each device’s browser.

availableActions.action: Open cookie settings on each OpenAI site you use
availableActions.howTo: The policy says settings are reachable directly on the sites where your jurisdiction allows the control. Repeat it per browser and per device, and again after roughly six months when the consent cookie expires.

availableActions.action: Block third-party cookies in the browser to cut the advertising networks
availableActions.howTo: Every cookie in the Marketing Performance table is third-party. Browser-level blocking removes them without touching sign-in, which depends on first-party OpenAI cookies.

availableActions.action: Know that the Necessary category cannot be declined
availableActions.howTo: That bucket includes Cloudflare, Stripe, Auth0, Intercom and Google identifiers lasting up to a year. Deleting cookies clears them; declining them is not offered.

availableActions.action: Ask privacy@openai.com for the cookie-related data
availableActions.howTo: The policy gives one contact address for cookie questions and refers all other processing to the privacy policy.

reference.label: Additional information
reference.quote: You can send any questions to privacy@openai.com.

requiredDisclosures.name: Categories of cookies and their purposes
requiredDisclosures.note: Three categories — Necessary, Analytics, Marketing Performance — each with a table naming every cookie, its source, duration, purpose and the domain it is set on. Among the most complete cookie disclosures in this corpus.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: A duration is given per cookie rather than per category, ranging from session and 10 minutes to 400 days and 24 months.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Twelve third parties are named: Auth0, Cloudflare, Stripe, Intercom, Datadog, Swoogo, Google, LinkedIn, Reddit, TikTok, Meta and Bing.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consent mechanism for non-essential cookies
requiredDisclosures.note: On-site cookie settings are offered, but only 'depending on applicable law' and 'if you are in a jurisdiction that allows for that control'. The consent is real where it exists; it is not offered universally.

requiredDisclosures.name: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
requiredDisclosures.note: No opt-out link, no Global Privacy Control statement and no Do Not Track statement appear anywhere in the document, although it discloses cookies from six advertising networks used for cross-context behavioural advertising — the processing CPRA treats as sharing.

requiredDisclosures.name: Scope of covered individuals
requiredDisclosures.note: The policy never says whether it applies to logged-out visitors or to people who have never created an account, even though the advertising cookies are listed against openai.com and ads.openai.com, which are reachable without one.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: The document carries a 'Last updated' date of August 14, 2026 but no clause stating how or whether users will be told when the cookie set or the policy changes.

analyses.summary: To bring a claim against Walmart you must post a physical letter to Bentonville, Arkansas by first-class mail, FedEx or UPS, bearing an original personal signature — the terms state expressly that digital, scanned, electronic, copied and facsimile signatures do not count — from you and separately from your lawyer, verified under penalty of perjury. That is the entry point to a mandatory arbitration with no opt-out of any kind, a class action waiver, a rule that the arbitration's existence and its award are confidential, and a bellwether mechanism that reduces twenty-five similar claims to ten while the rest wait for every appeal to finish. Decline a settlement offer and lose, and you pay Walmart's costs including expert fees. Anything that reaches court goes to Collin County or the Eastern District of Texas, and the terms say inconvenience to the parties cannot be argued against the transfer. Liability is capped at fees paid in the preceding six months, with theft, destruction and unauthorised access to data excluded outright. Your reviews and photos are licensed perpetually and irrevocably with moral rights waived, your chatbot inputs and purchase history train Walmart's models with no opt-out, and you indemnify Walmart even for claims that are groundless or false.

exposures.title: A claim requires a wet-ink signature sent by courier
exposures.whatItMeans: An arbitration demand must be delivered only by first-class mail, FedEx or UPS to Walmart's legal department in Bentonville, and must carry the original personal signature of the claimant and of any lawyer representing them. The terms define original personal signature to exclude digital, scanned, electronic, copied or facsimile signatures, and the signature verifies the factual statements under penalty of perjury.
exposures.whyItMatters: The entire relationship this governs is electronic — an account, an app, an order confirmation by email — and the only route to a remedy is made physical. No other document in the corpus imposes a wet-ink requirement, and it functions as a filter on claims rather than as a safeguard against anything.

reference.label: 20.3 Initiating a Demand for Arbitration
reference.quote: For purposes of this paragraph, "original personal signature" does not include any digital, scanned, electronic, copied, or facsimile signature.

exposures.title: Mandatory arbitration with no opt-out, and the award is secret
exposures.whatItMeans: All disputes go to individual arbitration before a single arbitrator with a class action waiver and no opt-out offered anywhere. Everything about the arbitration — its existence, the discovery exchanged, and the award itself — is confidential, and using an award in another arbitration is permitted only in narrow circumstances with the opposing party's identity redacted.
exposures.whyItMatters: Confidentiality over the fact of the arbitration and the award means no claimant can learn that others won on the same facts. Combined with the express statement that awards have no preclusive effect even against the same counsel on the same issues, each claimant starts from zero. Walmart sits alongside Amazon and Canva at the no-opt-out end of the corpus's arbitration spectrum.

exposures.title: Twenty-five similar claims become ten, and the rest wait for every appeal
exposures.whatItMeans: Where twenty-five or more demands involving common questions are brought by claimants represented by the same firm or coordinated firms, each side selects five for a total of ten Bellwether Demands. Remaining demands may not be filed until ninety days after all bellwethers have been arbitrated and any appeals exhausted.
exposures.whyItMatters: The threshold is lower and the throttle tighter than Zoom's fifty-to-sixteen, and the wait runs through the appeals of other people's cases. Since the class action is already waived, coordinated individual arbitration was the remaining route for many people harmed the same way.

exposures.title: Everything goes to two Texas courthouses, and inconvenience is not an argument
exposures.whatItMeans: Texas law governs, and any case in court must be brought exclusively in the Eastern District of Texas, Sherman Division, or the state courts of Collin County. Cases filed elsewhere are transferred or dismissed, and the terms state that transfer or dismissal cannot be denied on grounds of inconvenience to the parties, piecemeal adjudication, risk of inconsistent findings, or the presence of non-parties.
exposures.whyItMatters: Walmart serves customers in every state and confines them to one county. Pre-emptively removing inconvenience as a ground goes beyond choosing a forum — it forecloses the argument a court would normally weigh on behalf of a distant consumer.

exposures.title: You indemnify Walmart for claims that are groundless or false
exposures.whatItMeans: You must defend, at Walmart's option, and indemnify Walmart and its suppliers, vendors, contractors and licensors against all liabilities, claims, damages, costs and expenses — including electronically stored information costs, expert fees and attorneys' fees — arising from your misuse of the sites or any breach of the terms, and you agree to do so regardless of whether the matters are groundless, fraudulent or false, and regardless of the cause or alleged cause.
exposures.whyItMatters: Indemnity normally follows fault. Here it attaches to allegations that are admitted to be baseless, and 'regardless of the cause' removes even the requirement that the claim relate to something you actually did. It is uncapped, while Walmart's own liability is capped at six months of fees.

reference.label: 19. Indemnification
reference.quote: regardless of whether such matters are groundless, fraudulent, or false, and regardless of the cause or alleged cause thereof

exposures.title: Liability is capped at six months of fees, with data loss excluded
exposures.whatItMeans: No Walmart entity will be liable for damages exceeding the fees you paid in connection with your use of the Walmart Sites during the six months preceding the claim. The excluded categories are listed separately and include theft, destruction, unauthorised access to, alteration of, and loss of use of any record or data, along with loss of data generally.
exposures.whyItMatters: Six months is the shortest lookback in the corpus, and 'fees paid in connection with your use of the Walmart Sites' is not obviously the same thing as what you spent on merchandise. Data breach — the harm the privacy notice's collection makes possible — is placed outside the cap rather than limited by it.

exposures.title: Your chatbot inputs and purchase history train the model, with no opt-out
exposures.whatItMeans: Inputs to the Generative AI Features may not be kept confidential and are collected, used and retained by Walmart to answer questions from you and from other users. Your content including inputs, your purchasing history, your use of promotions and your personal information may be used to enhance and improve the features and the underlying model. Outputs are owned by Walmart, though you may use them.
exposures.whyItMatters: No opt-out is offered anywhere, and the mitigation offered is an instruction not to share sensitive or personal data with a shopping assistant. Meanwhile users are separately prohibited from using any Walmart material to develop, train or improve any AI model — the same one-way asymmetry Google's terms contain.

reference.label: 16.J Chatbots and Use of Generative AI
reference.quote: any of your Content (including but not limited to the Inputs), as well as your purchasing history from the Walmart Sites, your use of promotions as well as personal information, may be used to further enhance and improve the Generative AI Features, the underlying model

exposures.title: Reviews and ideas are licensed perpetually and irrevocably, with your name attached
exposures.whatItMeans: You grant Walmart a royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, unlimited, non-exclusive licence to use, reproduce, create derivative works from, modify, publish, edit, translate, distribute, perform and display any content you make available, sublicensable through multiple tiers. Walmart owes no confidentiality, no compensation, no response and no attribution, and may use any name associated with the content.
exposures.whyItMatters: This is the tenth appearance of the ideas-become-ours family in the corpus. It is a licence rather than an assignment, but perpetual, irrevocable and unlimited, with multi-tier sublicensing and a right to attach your name — a combination no other licence-form document here matches.

reference.label: 3.B Walmart's Rights to Use Content and Ideas

exposures.title: Uploading a family photo waives your moral rights in it
exposures.whatItMeans: By uploading photos to the Walmart Digital Photo Center you agree to waive all moral rights in those images and grant a sublicensable worldwide licence covering, among other purposes, developing new technologies and services for Walmart. Loss, deletion or alteration of your photos — even where caused by Walmart's negligence — entitles you only to replacement with a like amount of storage and processing.
exposures.whyItMatters: Photographs are the category people are least able to replace and the fourth licensed purpose is open-ended technology development. Walmart may also delete, move and edit photos for any reason without notice, and deletes accounts not accessed for a year.

exposures.title: Your mobile carrier hands over your device identifiers
exposures.whatItMeans: You authorise your wireless operator to disclose to Walmart and its third-party service providers your mobile number, name, address, email, network status, customer type, customer role, billing type, and the IMSI and IMEI device identifiers, for the duration of the business relationship.
exposures.whyItMatters: IMSI and IMEI are permanent hardware and SIM identifiers that survive app deletion and account closure. The authorisation is granted by accepting the terms rather than at any point where the carrier asks, and it runs for as long as the relationship lasts.

exposures.title: An order can be cancelled after confirmation and after shipping notice
exposures.whatItMeans: An order confirmation does not constitute acceptance of an order, and Walmart reserves the right to cancel orders containing pricing or availability errors with no further obligation, expressly even after you receive an order confirmation or a shipping notice. Accounts may also be restricted or terminated for any reason at Walmart's sole discretion.
exposures.whyItMatters: The point at which a purchase becomes binding is moved past every signal a customer would read as confirmation. For a mispriced item this is a unilateral cancellation right that persists after dispatch.

availableActions.action: Send the arbitration demand exactly as specified
availableActions.howTo: Post it by first-class mail, FedEx or UPS to Walmart Inc. Legal Department, 1 Customer Drive, Mailstop 0215, Bentonville, AR 72716. It must carry your original ink signature, your counsel's original ink signature if you have counsel, your contact details, the legal claims and their factual basis, the remedy sought, and a good-faith calculation of the amount in controversy. A scan or an e-signature does not satisfy this.

deadline.description: A compliant Demand tolls the statute of limitations for 90 days. Filing with the AAA is only permitted 60 or more days after the Demand is initiated, so the window between those two points is narrow.

availableActions.action: Use small claims court instead
availableActions.howTo: Small claims actions are excepted from arbitration if brought individually, within that court's jurisdiction, and not removed or appealed to a court of general jurisdiction. For most consumer-sized disputes this avoids the wet-ink demand, the 60-day wait and the bellwether queue entirely.

availableActions.action: Complain to a regulator, which the terms preserve
availableActions.howTo: Nothing in the terms prevents raising issues with federal, state or local government agencies, and where the law allows those agencies may seek relief against Walmart on your behalf. California residents can reach the Complaint Assistance Unit of the California Department of Consumer Affairs at (800) 952-5210.

reference.label: 20.2 Class Action Waiver and 24. How to Contact Us

availableActions.action: Treat the chatbot as public
availableActions.howTo: The terms instruct you not to share sensitive, personal, proprietary or confidential information with the Generative AI Features and state that inputs may not be kept confidential. There is no opt-out from inputs being used to improve the model, so restraint at the point of typing is the only control.

reference.label: 16.J Chatbots and Use of Generative AI

availableActions.action: Keep your own copies of anything in the Photo Center
availableActions.howTo: The terms make you responsible for monitoring and creating backups, provide the service under no warranty, cap all liability for loss at replacement storage, and permit deletion of accounts not accessed for one year.

deadline.description: Failure to access the Walmart Digital Photo Center account for one year is a stated ground for termination and deletion of all photos.

availableActions.action: Opt out of card account updater services at your bank
availableActions.howTo: Walmart participates in bank account updater services that automatically refresh your stored card number and expiry date when they change. The terms direct you to your issuing bank to opt out — Walmart offers no control over it.

availableActions.action: Check who is actually selling before you buy
availableActions.howTo: Marketplace Retailers handle their own processing, delivery, returns and customer service, and Walmart disclaims responsibility and liability for them, their products and their representations. Returns go to that retailer under its own policy, shown on its Seller Information page.

availableActions.action: Rely on the non-retroactivity of terms changes
availableActions.howTo: Changes do not apply to any dispute arising before the revised terms were posted or you were otherwise notified. If something has already gone wrong, the version in force at the time is the one that governs it.

requiredDisclosures.name: Arbitration opt-out right
requiredDisclosures.note: None is offered at any point. Arbitration is mandatory from first use, with a class action waiver, confidentiality over the award, and a bellwether process that holds most claims in abeyance.

requiredDisclosures.name: Pre-arbitration dispute procedure
requiredDisclosures.note: Disclosed in full and unusually onerous: a courier-delivered demand bearing original ink signatures from the claimant and their counsel, verified under penalty of perjury, followed by a 60-day wait before filing with the AAA.

requiredDisclosures.name: Governing law and jurisdiction
requiredDisclosures.note: Texas law, with the FAA governing arbitration, and exclusive court jurisdiction in the Eastern District of Texas, Sherman Division, or the state courts of Collin County — with inconvenience expressly unavailable as a ground to resist transfer.

requiredDisclosures.name: Non-retroactivity of changes
requiredDisclosures.note: A genuine protection and rare in this corpus: changes do not apply to any dispute arising before the revised terms were posted or notified.

requiredDisclosures.name: Notice of changes to terms
requiredDisclosures.note: Notice is by any reasonable means including simply posting a revised version. Users are told it is their responsibility to check regularly, and continued use is acceptance.

requiredDisclosures.name: AI training opt-out
requiredDisclosures.note: Chatbot inputs, purchasing history, promotion usage and personal information are used to improve the Generative AI Features and the underlying model, with no opt-out. Users are separately barred from using Walmart materials to train any model of their own.

requiredDisclosures.name: Limitation on indemnity
requiredDisclosures.note: The customer indemnity is uncapped and applies expressly to groundless, fraudulent or false claims and regardless of cause, covering ESI costs, expert fees and attorneys' fees. Walmart's own liability is capped at six months of fees.

requiredDisclosures.name: Designated DMCA agent
requiredDisclosures.note: The terms link a DMCA procedure page but name no designated agent or address in this document.

requiredDisclosures.name: Refund and cancellation policy
requiredDisclosures.note: Return and refund rules live in separate linked policies. The terms state only that returning an item in unused condition is the sole remedy where a product is not as described, and that all Pickup and Delivery refunds are at Walmart's discretion.

requiredDisclosures.name: Minimum age
requiredDisclosures.note: Users must be of legal age to contract or have parental or guardian consent, with the parent or guardian consenting on their behalf. Age-restricted products are self-certified at the point of order.

requiredDisclosures.name: Consumer complaint route
requiredDisclosures.note: The California Department of Consumer Affairs Complaint Assistance Unit is named with postal address and two phone numbers, and the class action waiver expressly preserves the right to raise issues with government agencies.

requiredDisclosures.name: Named third-party recipients
requiredDisclosures.note: Only Worldpay, for LocalFinds alcohol transactions, is named. Marketplace Retailers, restaurants, delivery contractors and generative AI providers are all referred to by category.

requiredDisclosures.name: Retention period
requiredDisclosures.note: No period appears in the terms. The only duration stated anywhere is the one-year inactivity threshold for deleting a Digital Photo Center account.

analyses.summary: One of the least restrictive documents in this corpus. Liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud, and for gross negligence or wilful misconduct is expressly not limited; the terms state outright that mandatory consumer protection law overrides them where they conflict; European consumers may sue in their own country's courts while Booking.com may only sue them there; material changes get advance notice and existing bookings stay governed by the terms in force when booked. The exposures are narrower. Breaching the terms can mean a cancelled booking with no refund and no explanation. Non-European consumers get exclusive Amsterdam or England and Wales jurisdiction rather than their home courts. And Booking.com forbids AI-powered browser assistants from making bookings on your behalf, states that unauthorised use causes it irreparable harm, and says it watches every visit for the pattern.

exposures.title: AI assistants are forbidden from booking on your behalf, on pain of an injunction
exposures.whatItMeans: You may not use robots, scrapers, other automated means, or automated assistants — the clause names AI-powered assistants that operate by interacting with your browser — to access anything on the platform without express written permission, and Booking.com states it does not authorise their use to make bookings. You further acknowledge that monetary damages are not an adequate remedy for such use, that it may cause Booking.com irreparable harm, and that it is entitled to injunctive relief.
exposures.whyItMatters: This reaches a tool running in the user's own browser, acting on the user's own instruction, on pages the user is entitled to see. The pre-agreed acknowledgement of irreparable harm is the operative part: it is drafted to make an injunction easier to obtain rather than to describe a loss.

reference.label: Intellectual property rights
